### `POST /api/create-project` — Create a New Saved Project

#### Synopsis

Creates a brand-new saved-project document owned by the authenticated principal. The request body must carry at least a `project_name` string; an optional `project_description` string and an optional `collaborators` array of e-mail addresses may additionally be supplied. Upon success the handler validates each field into domain value objects, assembles a canonical document body (owning account, rendered collaborators, a fixed five-folder scaffold, and a creation timestamp), persists it into the `saved_projects` collection, and returns a small acknowledgement object echoing the generated identifier and the validated name.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is a textbook resource-creation operation and, as such, it is bound to the `POST` verb rather than to `PUT`. The distinction is not academic hair-splitting: `POST` is neither *safe* nor *idempotent*, and both of those properties are exactly what we want to forfeit here. The handler mints a fresh, universally-unique project identifier on every single invocation via `Uuid::new_v4()`, which means that submitting the identical request body ten times will conjure ten distinct project documents into existence. A caller must never assume that a retried `POST /api/create-project` is a no-op; it is emphatically the opposite. Because the server — not the client — chooses the resource's location (the identifier), `PUT` would be semantically dishonest, and so `POST` it remains, world without end.

Viewed through a Domain-Driven Design lens, the handler occupies the thin HTTP adapter layer and is scrupulous about not letting primitive obsession leak inward. Raw JSON strings are refused entry to the domain until they have been transmuted into first-class value objects: a `project_name` becomes a `ProjectName` via `ProjectName::parse`, and every collaborator string becomes an `Email` via `Email::parse`. The persistence itself is delegated across a `UnitOfWork` port to a `document_collection` abstraction, so the handler never so much as glimpses the underlying datastore. The result is an application service whose only job is orchestration — extract, validate, assemble, persist, acknowledge — with all of the genuinely interesting business invariants pushed down into the domain where they belong.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This endpoint sits behind the full type-state request pipeline and consumes an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That type parameter is a compile-time proof: the handler body simply *cannot* be reached unless the request has already traversed validation, authentication, and authorization. Two headers drive that pipeline.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7f3a1c2e-9b4d-4f8a-a1e2-0c9d8e7f6a5b` | Correlation identifier (`CORRELATION_IDENTIFIER_HEADER_NAME`) threaded through the pipeline for tracing/logging. Its absence does not by itself reject the request, but supplying it is strongly advised so that a given creation can be correlated across logs. |
| `x-account-email` | **Yes** | `x-account-email: researcher@university.edu` | The authenticated account e-mail (`AUTHENTICATED_ACCOUNT_HEADER_NAME`). This is the sole source of the principal. If missing, the pipeline raises `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` (401); if present but not a parseable e-mail, `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` (401). The parsed value becomes the `owning_account` stamped onto the new document. |
| `Content-Type` | **Yes** | `Content-Type: application/json` | The body is extracted via axum's `Json<Value>` extractor and must be valid JSON. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The request advances through a sequence of zero-sized marker types — `RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated`, `RequestHasBeenValidated`, `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`, and finally `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` — each of which is an uninhabited enum used purely as a phantom stage marker. First the raw request is **Validated** (structural checks). Next it is **Authenticated**: the `x-account-email` header is read and parsed into an `Email`; missing header ⇒ `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, unparseable value ⇒ `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Finally it is **Authorized**, at which point the principal is known-good and callable via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()`, which returns a `&Email`. Because this handler's signature demands `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, the Rust type system guarantees at compile time that no unauthenticated or unauthorized request can ever execute a line of the handler body — there is no runtime `if authenticated { ... }` to forget.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

The body is extracted as a free-form `serde_json::Value`, and the handler then reaches into it field by field. It is **not** deserialized into a fixed struct, so unknown/extra fields are silently ignored rather than rejected. The handler reads exactly the following three fields.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_name` | string | **Yes** | Must be present and must be a JSON string (a non-string value ⇒ 400). Must additionally pass `ProjectName::parse` (e.g. a blank/whitespace-only name is rejected ⇒ 400). | — | The human-readable name of the project. Stored verbatim (as parsed) into the document body. |
| `project_description` | string | No | Only a JSON string is honored; the value is `trim()`-ed and an empty result is discarded. Any non-string value is ignored. | `None` (absent) | An optional free-text description. **Note:** the handler reads and validates this field into a local, but the current code binds it to `_optional_description` and does **not** persist it in the stored document body. See Edge Cases. |
| `collaborators` | array of string | No | Must be a JSON array when present; each element is inspected, non-string elements are ignored, string elements are `trim()`-ed, empties are dropped. Every surviving string must pass `Email::parse` — the first malformed address short-circuits the whole request ⇒ 400. | `[]` (empty) | Initial list of collaborator e-mail addresses. Rendered into the document as `{ "collaborator_email": <email> }` objects. |

The handler itself takes `Json<Value>`, but a faithful struct mirror of what it reads would be:

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns `200 OK` with a small acknowledgement object built by `build_project_creation_acknowledgement`. Note that this acknowledgement is **not** the full stored document — it contains only the three fields below.

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string | Yes | The server-generated UUID v4 identifying the new project. |
| `project_name` | string | Yes | The validated project name (echoed back exactly as parsed). |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Yes | A constant status string; always the literal `"project created"`. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` into a `SerializedErrorBody` with exactly two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The table below enumerates every `HttpError` variant and precisely when this endpoint can emit it.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `project_name` absent; `project_name` not a string; `ProjectName::parse` fails (e.g. blank name); any collaborator string fails `Email::parse`; or a downstream `DomainInvariantViolated` on insert. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the \`project_name\` field is required"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | Raised earlier in the pipeline when the `x-account-email` header is entirely absent. The handler body never runs. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"the x-account-email header was not provided"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | Raised earlier in the pipeline when `x-account-email` is present but not a parseable e-mail address. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the x-account-email header was not a valid e-mail"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | The datastore insert returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied`, mapped by `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` to a denied-authorization HTTP error. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"the authenticated principal is not authorized to create this project"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | The insert returns `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`. Uncommon for a pure create, but mapped defensively. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from the document collection (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure { "disk full" }`) — the catch-all `other_failure` arm. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the document collection failed: disk full"}` |

**Full serialized error body example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "the `project_name` field must be a string"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler is deliberately decomposed into small, single-purpose helpers. In invocation order:

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request` — reads the authorized principal `Email` off the request and returns it as an owned `String`.
2. `extract_proposed_project_name_field` — pulls `project_name` from the JSON body, erroring (400) if missing or non-string.
3. `validate_proposed_project_name` — parses the raw name into a `ProjectName` value object, mapping domain errors to 400.
4. `extract_project_description_field` — reads the optional `project_description`, trimming and discarding empties (result currently unused downstream).
5. `extract_initial_collaborator_email_list` — collects the raw collaborator strings from the `collaborators` array, ignoring non-strings and empties.
6. `validate_each_collaborator_email` — parses each raw address into an `Email`, short-circuiting on the first malformed one.
7. `build_canonical_folder_scaffold_names` — returns the fixed five-folder scaffold: `Documents`, `Literature`, `Figures`, `Drafts`, `Exports`.
8. `generate_project_identifier` — mints a fresh UUID v4 string for the new project.
9. `assemble_new_project_document_body` — combines name, owning account, rendered collaborators, folders, and a creation timestamp into the stored JSON body.
10. `render_collaborator_emails_as_json` — (called by #9) maps each `Email` into a `{ "collaborator_email": ... }` object.
11. `stamp_project_created_timestamp` — (called by #9) produces a `"<unix-seconds>Z"` creation timestamp from the system clock.
12. `build_new_project_stored_document` — wraps the body into a `StoredDocument` with its identifier and owning account.
13. `insert_new_project_document` — persists the document into `SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME` (`"saved_projects"`) via the `document_collection` port, mapping failures through #15.
14. `build_project_creation_acknowledgement` — builds the `{ document_identifier, project_name, acknowledgement }` response.
15. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` — translates an `ApplicationError` from the insert into the correct `HttpError` variant (denied/not-found/malformed/upstream).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`project_description` is validated then thrown away.** The handler binds it to `_optional_description` and never includes it in `assemble_new_project_document_body`. Clients may send it, but it will not appear in the stored document. Do not rely on it being persisted.
- **`created_at` is not real RFC-3339.** Despite the docstring calling it "RFC-3339-style," `stamp_project_created_timestamp` emits `format!("{seconds_since_epoch}Z")`, i.e. a bare Unix-seconds integer with a `Z` glued on (e.g. `"1751846400Z"`). It is not parseable by standard ISO-8601 parsers.
- **The folder scaffold is fixed and non-configurable.** Every project is created with exactly `Documents`, `Literature`, `Figures`, `Drafts`, `Exports`. There is no request field to override, extend, or suppress this list.
- **Malformed collaborators fail the entire request.** A single bad e-mail among ten valid ones rejects the whole creation with 400 — it does not skip the bad entry. However, non-string array elements (numbers, nulls) and empty/whitespace strings are silently dropped *before* validation, so those never trigger an error.
- **Non-idempotent by design.** Every call generates a new UUID and inserts a new document. Retrying after a timeout may create a duplicate project. There is no dedup key and no upsert.
- **Extra/unknown body fields are ignored.** Because the body is parsed as a loose `serde_json::Value`, sending arbitrary additional keys neither errors nor gets stored — they are simply never read.
- **The success response is a stub, not the document.** Callers wanting the folders, collaborators, or `owning_account` back must issue a subsequent read; the 200 body carries only identifier, name, and a constant acknowledgement string.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I sent `project_description` and it vanished. Is that a bug?**
A: It is a feature that behaves like a bug. The field is read and trimmed, then bound to `_optional_description` and never persisted. Your description went to a better place. Do not send it if you expect it back.

**Q: Can I make this idempotent by sending the same identifier twice?**
A: No. You do not get to send an identifier at all — the server generates one with `Uuid::new_v4()` on every call. Two identical requests yield two different projects. If you need idempotency, deduplicate on your side before calling.

**Q: Is `created_at` an ISO-8601 timestamp I can feed to `Date.parse`?**
A: Absolutely not, and we admire your optimism. It is the number of seconds since the Unix epoch with a lonely `Z` appended for decorative purposes. Strip the `Z`, parse the integer as seconds, and multiply by 1000 for JavaScript.

---

### `POST /api/create-subfolder` — Create a Subfolder Under a Project Folder

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts a small JSON envelope naming a parent project, a parent folder path, and a proposed subfolder name, and — after an exhaustive gauntlet of validation — persists a brand-new subfolder document into the `project_folders` document collection, owned by the authenticated principal. It generates a fresh UUID identifier for the subfolder, composes a slash-delimited qualified path that locates the subfolder inside its parent, and returns a compact acknowledgement echoing back the newly minted identifier and the qualified path. It is a creation endpoint in the classical sense: you hand it a name, it hands you back an identity.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a strict REST standpoint this is a resource-creation operation, and it is modeled as a `POST` precisely because it is neither safe nor idempotent: each successful invocation mints a *new* UUID via `Uuid::new_v4()` and inserts a *new* document, so submitting the identical body twice yields two distinct subfolder documents rather than converging on a single canonical resource. This is the textbook justification for preferring `POST` over `PUT` here — `PUT` carries an implicit contract of idempotency against a client-chosen URI, whereas this handler reserves identity assignment for the server and therefore cannot honor that contract. The endpoint sits at a slightly unusual, non-hierarchical URL (`/api/create-subfolder`) rather than a nested collection path, a legacy affordance that trades RESTful purity for call-site convenience; the more orthodox nested routes (`/api/projects/:project_identifier/folders/...`) live elsewhere in the same router.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, the HTTP handler is deliberately anemic at the boundary and thick in the interior: it performs presentation-layer concerns (header extraction, JSON field plucking, name hygiene, reserved-name and traversal rejection) inline, then delegates the single act of persistence to the `document_collection` port through the `insert_document` call. The only genuine domain value object invoked is `NonEmptyText`, which enforces the invariant that a subfolder name is a non-empty piece of text; everything else — the `resource_kind: "subfolder"` tag, the opaque `created-<uuid>` timestamp token, the qualified path composition — is presentation-layer bookkeeping assembled directly into a `serde_json::Value` rather than promoted into a first-class domain aggregate. This is a pragmatic, transport-shaped handler, not a rich domain command, and the documentation below reflects the code exactly as written.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request to this endpoint is funneled through the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor before the handler body ever runs. That extractor reads exactly two headers:

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | **Yes** | `x-account-email: owner@example.com` | The authenticated principal. Must be present, must be valid UTF-8 text, and must parse via the `email_string_prism` into a valid `Email`. Absence → `401 authentication_credentials_were_missing`. Non-text (bad bytes) or unparseable email → `401 authentication_credentials_were_invalid`. This value becomes the `owning_account` on the persisted subfolder document. |
| `x-request-id` | No (soft) | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a2e-1b44-4d90-9e2a-abc123456789` | Correlation identifier for tracing. If omitted, the extractor substitutes the literal string `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"`. Note the subtlety: because a default is always supplied, the validation stage (which rejects an *empty* correlation identifier) never actually fails on a merely-absent header. Not echoed in the response body. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated → Authenticated → Authorized`).** This API encodes its request lifecycle in the type system so that a handler *cannot* be written that reads a principal before that principal has been proven present. The pipeline is a phantom-typed state machine over `HttpRequestInPipeline<PipelineStage>`:

1. **`RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated`** — created by `HttpRequestInPipeline::originate(correlation_identifier)`. It carries the correlation id and a `None` principal. Nothing may be trusted yet.
2. **`RequestHasBeenValidated`** — produced by `.validate()`, which fails with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if the correlation identifier is empty after trimming. (In practice the extractor's default fills this, so this guard is a belt-and-suspenders check.)
3. **`RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`** — produced by `.authenticate(email)`, which attaches the parsed `Email` principal (`Some(...)`).
4. **`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`** — produced by `.authorize()`, which pattern-matches on the stored principal: `Some(_)` advances the state, `None` yields `AuthorizationWasDenied`. Only in this final state does `authorized_principal()` exist as a method — and it is documented to `expect(...)` a principal, which is safe precisely because the type-state guarantees one was set.

Because the handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, axum runs the entire `FromRequestParts` extractor (which walks all four stages) before the handler body executes. If any stage fails, the corresponding `HttpError` is returned and the handler body never runs.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The endpoint takes no path segments beyond the literal `/api/create-subfolder` and reads no query-string parameters. All caller input arrives in the request body.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then explicitly plucks three required string fields via `extract_required_string_field`. Each must be present and must be a JSON string; a missing field or a non-string value (number, boolean, object, array, null) yields `400 request_body_was_malformed`.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parent_project_identifier` | string | **Yes** | Must be a JSON string; must be present. No length/format validation is applied by the handler — it is stored verbatim into the document body. | — | Opaque identifier of the project that owns the parent folder. Persisted unchanged into the subfolder document's `parent_project_identifier`. |
| `parent_folder_name` | string | **Yes** | Must be a JSON string; must be present. Trimmed of whitespace and of surrounding `/` when composing the path. May be blank/whitespace-only (a blank parent yields a top-level path equal to the subfolder name). | — | Path of the parent folder under which the new subfolder is created. Used only to compose `qualified_subfolder_path`; not stored as a standalone field. |
| `subfolder_name` | string | **Yes** | Must be a JSON string; must be present. Trimmed, then parsed as `NonEmptyText` (rejects blank). Rejected if — case-insensitively — it equals a reserved name (`.`, `..`, `root`, `trash`, `system`). Rejected if it contains `/`, `\`, or the substring `..`. | — | The proposed name of the new subfolder. Stored (trimmed) as `subfolder_name` and used as the last path segment. |

Any field beyond these three is silently ignored — the handler reads only these keys.

**(b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)**

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma-http/schemas/create-subfolder-request.json",
  "title": "CreateSubfolderRequest",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "required": ["parent_project_identifier", "parent_folder_name", "subfolder_name"],
  "properties": {
    "parent_project_identifier": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Opaque identifier of the owning project."
    },
    "parent_folder_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Parent folder path; may be blank for a top-level subfolder."
    },
    "subfolder_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Proposed subfolder name; trimmed, non-empty, non-reserved, no path separators or `..`.",
      "not": {
        "anyOf": [
          { "pattern": "[/\\\\]" },
          { "pattern": "\\.\\." }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**(c) TypeScript interface**

```typescript
interface CreateSubfolderRequest {
  /** Opaque identifier of the owning project. Stored verbatim. */
  parent_project_identifier: string;
  /** Parent folder path; trimmed and slash-stripped when composing the path.
   *  A blank/whitespace-only value produces a top-level subfolder. */
  parent_folder_name: string;
  /** Proposed subfolder name. Must be non-empty after trimming, must not be a
   *  reserved name (".", "..", "root", "trash", "system", case-insensitive),
   *  and must not contain "/", "\\", or "..". */
  subfolder_name: string;
}
```

**(d) Rust struct mirror**

The handler itself does not define a typed struct (it reads a `serde_json::Value`). The following struct is an accurate mirror of the fields it reads, for callers who prefer strong typing:

```rust
    parent_folder_name: String,
    /// Proposed subfolder name; validated to be non-empty, non-reserved,
    /// and free of path separators or `..`.
    subfolder_name: String,
}
```

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns `200 OK` (axum's default status for `Json<Value>`) with a compact acknowledgement built by `build_subfolder_creation_acknowledgement`. Note carefully: the response contains only three fields and does **not** echo the full persisted document — `parent_project_identifier`, `subfolder_name`, `resource_kind`, `created_at`, and `owning_account` are stored but not returned.

**Response field table**

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string (UUID v4) | Yes | The server-generated identifier of the newly created subfolder document. |
| `qualified_subfolder_path` | string | Yes | The composed, slash-delimited path locating the subfolder (parent path + `/` + name, or just the name when the parent is blank). |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Yes | Fixed literal `"subfolder created"`. |

#### Error Responses

Every failure path returns a `SerializedErrorBody` — a JSON object with exactly two fields, `error_category` (a stable machine-readable label) and `error_explanation` (a human-readable string). The table below enumerates every `HttpError` variant and describes precisely when each can arise *for this specific endpoint*.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `request_body_was_malformed` | Any of `parent_project_identifier`, `parent_folder_name`, `subfolder_name` is missing or is not a JSON string; the subfolder name is blank after trimming (`NonEmptyText::parse` fails); the name is reserved (`.`, `..`, `root`, `trash`, `system`); the name contains `/`, `\`, or `..`; or the persistence layer surfaces a `DomainInvariantViolated`. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"field \`subfolder_name\` is required"}` |
| `401` | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | The `x-account-email` header is entirely absent. Raised in the extractor before the handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"the 'x-account-email' header was absent"}` |
| `401` | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` is present but not valid text, or does not parse into a valid email address via the prism. Raised in the extractor. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the account header did not parse into a valid email address"}` |
| `403` | `authorization_was_denied` | Raised if the authorization stage finds no principal (defensively unreachable here since a missing/invalid email already errors earlier), or if the persistence layer returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied`. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| `404` | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | The `insert_document` call returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` (mapped by `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`). | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| `500` | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from persistence (e.g. a `DocumentCollectionFailure`) — the catch-all branch of the error mapper. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the document collection failed"}` |

**Full serialized error body example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "the subfolder name `root` is reserved and cannot be used"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request(&authorized_request)` — reads the authorized principal's `Email`, converts it to a `String`, to be used as the document's `owning_account`.
2. `extract_parent_project_identifier_field(&submitted_body)` — plucks `parent_project_identifier` (via `extract_required_string_field`).
3. `extract_parent_folder_name_field(&submitted_body)` — plucks `parent_folder_name` (via `extract_required_string_field`).
4. `extract_proposed_subfolder_name_field(&submitted_body)` — plucks `subfolder_name` (via `extract_required_string_field`).
5. `extract_required_string_field(body, field_name)` — the shared reader: returns the string, or a `RequestBodyWasMalformed` error distinguishing "not a string" from "required/missing".
6. `validate_proposed_subfolder_name(raw)` — trims the name and parses it into `NonEmptyText`, mapping domain parse failure to `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
7. `reject_reserved_subfolder_name(name)` — case-insensitively rejects `.`, `..`, `root`, `trash`, `system`.
8. `reject_path_traversal_in_subfolder_name(name)` — rejects any name containing `/`, `\`, or `..`.
9. `compose_qualified_subfolder_path(parent, name)` — trims/slash-strips the parent and joins `parent/name`, or returns just `name` when the parent is blank.
10. `generate_subfolder_identifier()` — returns a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` string as the document identifier.
11. `assemble_subfolder_document_body(project_id, path, name)` — builds the JSON body with `parent_project_identifier`, `subfolder_name`, `qualified_subfolder_path`, `resource_kind: "subfolder"`, and `created_at`.
12. `stamp_subfolder_created_timestamp()` — produces an opaque `created-<uuid>` token used as `created_at` (deliberately *not* a real clock timestamp).
13. `build_subfolder_stored_document(id, owner, body)` — wraps the parts into a `StoredDocument { document_identifier, owning_account: Some(owner), document_body }`.
14. `insert_subfolder_document(&application_state, doc)` — inserts into the `PROJECT_FOLDERS_COLLECTION_NAME` (`"project_folders"`) collection via the `document_collection` port, mapping failures through `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`.
15. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error(err)` — translates `ApplicationError` into the appropriate `HttpError` (404 / 403 / 400 / 500).
16. `build_subfolder_creation_acknowledgement(id, path)` — builds the final success JSON returned to the caller.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **The `created_at` value is not a timestamp.** `stamp_subfolder_created_timestamp()` returns `created-<uuid>` — an opaque token derived from a fresh UUID, deliberately avoiding a clock dependency. Do not attempt to parse it as a date; it carries no chronological information and is not even monotonic.
- **A blank `parent_folder_name` is legal.** If the parent is empty or whitespace-only, `compose_qualified_subfolder_path` returns just the subfolder name, silently creating what is effectively a top-level folder. There is no error; callers relying on a nested path must supply a non-blank parent.
- **The endpoint is non-idempotent by design.** Each call generates a new UUID and inserts a new document. Replaying the identical body creates duplicate subfolders sharing the same `qualified_subfolder_path` but with different `document_identifier`s. There is no uniqueness check on the path.
- **Reserved-name and traversal checks are on the name only, not the parent.** `reject_reserved_subfolder_name` and `reject_path_traversal_in_subfolder_name` are applied exclusively to `subfolder_name`. A `parent_folder_name` of `../../etc` is *not* rejected by these guards (it is merely trimmed of surrounding slashes and embedded into the path), so the traversal protection is partial.
- **`..` matching is substring-based, not segment-based.** `reject_path_traversal_in_subfolder_name` rejects any name *containing* the substring `..`, so an innocuous-looking name like `report..final` or `..secret` is rejected even though it is not a real parent-directory reference. Conversely, a single `.` is caught only by the reserved-name list, not the traversal check.
- **No persisted field validates project existence up front.** The handler never verifies that `parent_project_identifier` refers to a real project before inserting; a 404 only surfaces if the underlying `insert_document` itself reports `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated`/`RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`.
- **The success response hides most of the stored document.** Only `document_identifier`, `qualified_subfolder_path`, and the literal `acknowledgement` are returned. Clients wanting `resource_kind`, `owning_account`, or the stored `created_at` token must fetch the document separately.
- **Extra body fields are ignored, not rejected.** Because the body is read as an untyped `Value` and only three keys are plucked, any additional properties are silently discarded rather than causing a validation error.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I supply my own `document_identifier`?**
A: No. Identity is server-assigned via `Uuid::new_v4()`. Any identifier you place in the body is ignored — only `parent_project_identifier`, `parent_folder_name`, and `subfolder_name` are read.

**Q: Why did creating a subfolder named `System` fail?**
A: The reserved-name check is case-insensitive. `system`, `System`, and `SYSTEM` all normalize to `system` and are rejected, along with `.`, `..`, `root`, and `trash`.

**Q: I omitted `x-request-id` and nothing broke. Is that a bug?**
A: No. The extractor substitutes the literal `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"` when the header is absent, so the correlation-identifier validation (which only rejects an empty string) never trips on a merely-missing header. The header is soft-required for tracing, not hard-required for success.

**Q: Will two identical requests be deduplicated?**
A: No. Each request creates a distinct document with a distinct UUID. If deduplication matters to you, enforce it on your side; the handler performs no uniqueness check against existing paths.

### `GET /api/debug-shared-projects` — Diagnostic Inspection of Saved-Project Ownership and Sharing

#### Synopsis

`GET /api/debug-shared-projects` is a strictly read-only diagnostic endpoint that inspects the entire `saved_projects` document collection and reports ownership and sharing statistics computed relative to the currently authenticated principal. It never mutates a single document; it exists so operators can answer "why does this account not see the shared project it expects?" style questions by dumping counts, per-document diagnostics, and data-hygiene flags. The response is a free-form JSON object (an `axum::Json<serde_json::Value>`) assembled entirely on the server from the collection contents.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the parlance of REST, this endpoint is the platonic ideal of a *safe* and *idempotent* resource read: it is a `GET`, it takes no request body, it acquires no locks, it writes nothing, and invoking it one time or one thousand times in succession leaves server state byte-for-byte unchanged. Because it is safe, it is cache-eligible in principle, proxy-repeatable without remorse, and prefetch-safe; because it is idempotent, a client that times out mid-flight may retry with a clear conscience. The endpoint's dossier is diagnostic rather than transactional — it computes a *projection* over the aggregate root's persistence layer rather than issuing a command against it — and so it deliberately sidesteps the write-side invariants that govern the create/save/delete siblings living beside it in `projects_files/routes.rs`.

From a Domain-Driven Design vantage point, `debug_shared_projects_handler` sits squarely in the `projects_files` bounded context, adjacent to the genuine project lifecycle handlers, yet it is an *anti-corruption read model* rather than a domain command. It leans directly on the `document_collection` port (`count_documents`, `list_documents`) exposed by the application state, bypassing any richer aggregate reconstitution because its purpose is forensic: it wants to see the raw, possibly-malformed, possibly-orphaned persisted shapes exactly as they lie on disk, including documents that violate ownership invariants (missing `owning_account`) or sharing invariants (a `is_shared` flag with zero collaborators). This is intentional impurity in service of observability — the endpoint's entire reason to exist is to surface the very inconsistencies that a well-behaved domain command would refuse to produce.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 5f2c1a9e-7b3d-4c8a-9f10-2e6b4d8a1c33` | Correlation identifier threaded through the type-state pipeline; used for tracing this single request end-to-end. Consumed at the `Validated` stage. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: operator@example.com` | Identifies the authenticated principal. Becomes the `authorized_principal()` and is used verbatim (after trim + lowercase) as the `owning_account` for every ownership and collaborator comparison in this handler. |

This endpoint is guarded by the compile-time type-state pipeline. The handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is a *witness type*: the request cannot even be constructed as an argument to this function unless it has already traversed the full progression `Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`. Concretely:

- **Validated** — the raw inbound request is checked for structural well-formedness: required headers such as `x-request-id` are present and parseable, and the body (if any) is syntactically acceptable. A failure here surfaces as `RequestBodyWasMalformed` (HTTP 400).
- **Authenticated** — the principal's identity is established from `x-account-email`. Absent credentials yield `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` (HTTP 401); malformed or unverifiable credentials yield `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` (HTTP 401).
- **Authorized** — the authenticated principal is checked against the policy governing this route. A denial yields `AuthorizationWasDenied` (HTTP 403).

Only after all three transitions succeed does the runtime hand the handler an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, from which `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request` pulls `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str().to_string()`. The type system, not a runtime `if`, is what guarantees the principal exists by the time the handler body runs.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This handler reads no path segments and no query string. The path `/api/debug-shared-projects` is fully static, and the account it operates on is derived exclusively from the authenticated principal (the `x-account-email` header), never from the URL.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

#### Request Body

This endpoint reads **no request body**. It is a `GET` handler whose only extractors are `State(application_state)` and the authorized-request witness; there is no `Json<T>` or `Bytes` extractor, so any body sent by the client is ignored entirely. There are therefore no request-body fields to document.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | No request body is read. |

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) — the empty request body:

```json

  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "DebugSharedProjectsRequestBody",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {},
  "description": "This endpoint reads no request body; any payload is ignored."
}
```

TypeScript interface:

```typescript
export interface DebugSharedProjectsRequestBody {}
```

Rust struct mirror:

```rust
/// This endpoint reads no request body. The handler takes only
/// `State(application_state)` and `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`.

```

#### Request Examples

curl:

```bash
curl -sS -X GET 'https://api.alma.example.com/api/debug-shared-projects' \
  -H 'x-request-id: 5f2c1a9e-7b3d-4c8a-9f10-2e6b4d8a1c33' \
  -H 'x-account-email: operator@example.com'
```

HTTPie:

```bash
http GET 'https://api.alma.example.com/api/debug-shared-projects' \
  x-request-id:5f2c1a9e-7b3d-4c8a-9f10-2e6b4d8a1c33 \

```

JavaScript fetch:

```javascript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.alma.example.com/api/debug-shared-projects",
  {
    method: "GET",
    headers: {
      "x-request-id": "5f2c1a9e-7b3d-4c8a-9f10-2e6b4d8a1c33",
      "x-account-email": "operator@example.com",
    },
  }
);

if (!response.ok) {
  throw new Error(`debug-shared-projects failed: ${response.status}`);
}

const diagnostics = await response.json();
console.log(diagnostics.shared_project_ratio);
```

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object assembled by `assemble_debug_shared_projects_payload`. The exact top-level fields are:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `shared_project_count` | integer (usize) | Count of documents shared *with* the authenticated account (account is a collaborator but not the owner). Numerically identical to `shared_with_account_count`; duplicated for consumer convenience. |
| `total_saved_project_count` | integer (usize) | Total number of documents in the `saved_projects` collection, from `count_documents`. |
| `owned_by_account_count` | integer (usize) | Number of documents whose `owning_account` matches the authenticated account (case-insensitive, trimmed). |
| `shared_with_account_count` | integer (usize) | Same value as `shared_project_count`; count of documents where the account is a collaborator but not the owner. |
| `shared_project_ratio` | number (f64) | `shared_with_account_count / total_saved_project_count`, or `0.0` when the collection is empty (division-by-zero guard). |
| `diagnostic_entries` | array of objects | Per-document diagnostics, restricted to documents that are owned by OR shared-with the account. See sub-fields below. |
| `documents_missing_owning_account` | array of strings | `document_identifier`s of documents whose `owning_account` is `null` or blank/whitespace. |
| `orphaned_share_references` | array of strings | `document_identifier`s of documents that declare an explicit `is_shared`/`shared` boolean of `true` but list zero collaborators. |

Each element of `diagnostic_entries` (from `summarize_document_ownership_diagnostics`):

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string | The stored document's identifier. |
| `owning_account` | string \| null | The document's raw `owning_account`, exactly as persisted (may be null). |
| `is_owned_by_account` | boolean | Whether `owning_account` matches the authenticated account (case-insensitive, trimmed). |
| `declares_shared_flag` | boolean | Whether the document declares itself shared via an explicit `is_shared`/`shared` flag or a non-empty collaborators list. |
| `account_is_collaborator` | boolean | Whether the authenticated account appears among the document's flattened collaborator emails. |
| `collaborator_count` | integer | Number of distinct (deduped, lowercased) collaborator emails found on the document. |

#### Error Responses

Every `HttpError` variant produces a `SerializedErrorBody` of the shape `{ "error_category": string, "error_explanation": string }`. Not every variant below is reachable from this handler's own body (some are enforced by the type-state pipeline before the handler runs), but all are documented for completeness.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Raised by the `Validated` pipeline stage if the inbound request is structurally malformed (e.g. missing/garbled `x-request-id`). The handler body itself reads no body, so it never raises this directly. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the request could not be validated"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Raised by the `Authenticated` pipeline stage when `x-account-email` is absent. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Raised by the `Authenticated` pipeline stage when the supplied credentials are present but unverifiable. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Raised by the `Authorized` pipeline stage, OR mapped from an `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` returned by `count_documents`/`list_documents` via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Mapped from `ApplicationError::RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` if the document-collection port reports the `saved_projects` collection/resource as absent. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The catch-all in `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`: any other `ApplicationError` (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure`) from `count_documents` or `list_documents` becomes this. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"document collection failure: boom"}` |

Full example error body:

```json
{
  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "document collection failure: connection to persistence layer timed out"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. **`extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request`** — pulls the authenticated principal's email out of the authorized-request witness as an owned `String`; this becomes the `owning_account` used for every comparison.
2. **`count_all_saved_project_documents`** — awaits `document_collection.count_documents(SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME)` to get the total; errors mapped via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`.
3. **`list_all_saved_project_documents`** — awaits `document_collection.list_documents(SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME)` to fetch every `StoredDocument`; errors mapped the same way.
4. **`partition_documents_by_ownership`** — splits the (cloned) document list into `(owned_by_account, everything_else)` using case-insensitive, trimmed matching of `owning_account`; only `owned_documents.len()` is retained.
5. **`count_documents_shared_with_account`** — counts documents where the account is a collaborator but NOT the owner.
6. **`build_shared_projects_diagnostic_entries`** — filters to documents that are owned-by OR shared-with the account, then maps each through `summarize_document_ownership_diagnostics`.
7. **`summarize_document_ownership_diagnostics`** (invoked per entry) — emits the per-document JSON object (identifier, owning_account, is_owner, declares_shared_flag, account_is_collaborator, collaborator_count).
8. **`document_declares_shared_flag`** (helper) — true if an explicit `is_shared`/`shared` boolean is set, else true if the collaborator list is non-empty.
9. **`extract_collaborator_emails_from_document`** (helper) — flattens `collaborators` / `shared_with` / `shared_with_emails` (strings or `{email}` objects) into a deduped, lowercased list.
10. **`account_appears_as_collaborator`** (helper) — checks whether the (non-empty, normalized) account is in that flattened collaborator list.
11. **`collect_documents_missing_owning_account`** — collects identifiers of documents whose `owning_account` is `null` or blank.
12. **`detect_orphaned_share_references`** — collects identifiers of documents with an explicit shared flag but zero collaborators.
13. **`compute_shared_project_ratio`** (invoked inside assembly) — `shared / total`, guarded to `0.0` when `total == 0`.
14. **`assemble_debug_shared_projects_payload`** — folds all of the above into the final `serde_json::Value` returned as `Json(payload)`.
15. **`map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`** — the error-translation helper used by steps 2 and 3.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Empty collection returns 200, not 404.** If `saved_projects` contains zero documents, `count_documents` returns `0`, `list_documents` returns `[]`, and `compute_shared_project_ratio` guards the division so `shared_project_ratio` is `0.0`. You get a fully-populated payload with all-zero counts and empty arrays.
- **`shared_project_count` and `shared_with_account_count` are always equal.** They are computed from the same `shared_with_account_count` value and stuffed into two keys. Do not treat them as two independent metrics — they are the same number by construction.
- **Ownership matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed.** `Owner@Example.com` and ` owner@example.com ` are treated as the same account. If you are debugging a "shows as not owned" issue, remember the comparison already normalizes case and surrounding whitespace, so casing is never the culprit.
- **An empty/whitespace account is never a collaborator.** `account_appears_as_collaborator` short-circuits to `false` for a blank account, so if the authenticated principal somehow resolves to an empty string, `shared_with_account_count` will be `0` regardless of collaborator lists.
- **A document owned by the account that also lists the account as a collaborator is NOT counted as shared-with.** `count_documents_shared_with_account` explicitly excludes documents the account owns, so self-collaboration never inflates the shared count (but it can still appear in `diagnostic_entries` with both `is_owned_by_account: true` and `account_is_collaborator: true`).
- **`diagnostic_entries` deliberately omits unrelated documents.** Only documents owned-by or shared-with the account appear. A document owned by someone else with no relation to you will contribute to `total_saved_project_count` but will be invisible in `diagnostic_entries`.
- **Orphaned-share detection only honors the EXPLICIT boolean flag.** `detect_orphaned_share_references` requires an explicit `is_shared`/`shared` == `true`; a document that is "shared" merely by having collaborators is not orphaned by definition, and one with the flag true but zero collaborators is flagged even if it is otherwise valid.
- **The document list is cloned once** (`all_documents.clone()`) to feed `partition_documents_by_ownership`; on very large collections this is an extra full-collection allocation. Acceptable for a diagnostic endpoint, noteworthy under load.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I pass an email in the query string to inspect a different account?**
A: No. There are no query or path parameters. The account is always the authenticated principal from `x-account-email`. To inspect another account, authenticate as that account (subject to authorization policy).

**Q: Why do `shared_project_count` and `shared_with_account_count` both exist if they're identical?**
A: Because the payload assembler writes the same value to both keys. Redundancy is a feature of diagnostic dumps, not a bug. Pick whichever key you prefer; they will never disagree.

**Q: Does calling this endpoint fix the orphaned shares or missing owners it reports?**
A: No. It is strictly read-only and mutates nothing. It reports data-hygiene problems so an operator can go fix them through the appropriate write endpoints; it will report the same orphans on every call until someone repairs the underlying documents.

### `DELETE /api/list-saved-projects` — Delete a Saved Project (with Optional Child-File Cascade)

#### Synopsis

This endpoint removes exactly one saved-project document from the `saved_projects` document collection, keyed by an `identifier` supplied as a query-string parameter, after first confirming both that the document exists and that the authenticated principal is its recorded owner. If — and only if — the caller opts in via the `cascade` query flag, the handler additionally sweeps the `project_files` collection and deletes every child file document whose body references the same project identifier. On success it returns a JSON acknowledgement receipt describing what was deleted, including a best-effort human-readable display name and a coarse deletion timestamp.

#### Theory & Rationale

In strict REST semantics, `DELETE` is the canonical verb for requesting the removal of the resource identified by the effective request URI. It is, per the specification, *idempotent* — issuing the same `DELETE` twice should leave the server in the same observable end-state — but it is decidedly *not* safe, since its entire raison d'être is to mutate server state. This handler honors the idempotency contract only weakly and honestly: the first successful call returns a `200 OK` acknowledgement, while a second identical call (the resource now being gone) yields a `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`. Both leave the collection in the same terminal state ("the project does not exist"), which satisfies the *spirit* of idempotency even though the status codes differ. Idempotency constrains server state, not response bytes, so a differing status code on the second call remains conformant.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, the saved project is the aggregate root and the project files are subordinate entities living within — or at least referentially bound to — that aggregate's consistency boundary. The cascade option is therefore a deliberate, opt-in expression of aggregate-lifecycle policy: deleting the root *may* orphan its children, and the caller must consciously request that the children be reaped alongside the root rather than having that destructive transitive behavior imposed silently. Placing this deletion in the HTTP category layer — thin, orchestrational, and delegating all persistence to the injected `document_collection` port — keeps the transport concern (parsing query params, mapping errors to status codes, emitting a receipt) cleanly separated from the storage concern, in keeping with hexagonal architecture's ports-and-adapters discipline.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

All requests traverse a compile-time type-state pipeline before this handler ever runs. The handler's signature accepts `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is a phantom-typed wrapper whose type parameter can only be `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` once the request has already transited every earlier stage. The stages are modeled as uninhabited marker enums (`RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated`, `RequestHasBeenValidated`, `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`, `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`) and the pipeline advances the request through them in strict order:

- **Validated** — the raw inbound request is structurally checked (required transport headers present, well-formed) and promoted from `RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated` to `RequestHasBeenValidated`.
- **Authenticated** — the caller's identity is established from credential headers and the request is promoted to `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`; the authenticated principal (an account email) is now attached.
- **Authorized** — a policy check confirms the authenticated principal is permitted to invoke this route, promoting the request to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. Only a value of this type can be passed to the handler, so the compiler itself guarantees the handler cannot run on an unauthenticated or unauthorized request.

Inside the handler, `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` yields the owning-account string that is subsequently compared against the stored document's `owning_account` field.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended (validation stage) | `x-request-id: 7f3c1e6a-9b2d-4c8e-a1f0-2b6d4e8a0c11` | Correlation identifier consumed during the Validated stage for tracing; echoed through logs. Absence is tolerated in most builds but supplying it makes the request diagnosable end-to-end. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes (authentication stage) | `x-account-email: owner@example.com` | Identifies the calling principal. Establishes the `authorized_principal()` value used for the ownership check. Missing or unparseable values cause the request to be rejected before the handler runs (Authentication stage). |

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | query | string | Yes | Must be present; trimmed of surrounding whitespace; must be non-empty after trimming | — (required) | Document identifier of the saved project to delete. Used as the lookup key against `saved_projects` and as the key for the delete call. |
| `cascade` | query | string (boolean-ish) | No | Interpreted truthy only for the exact lowercased values `true`, `1`, `yes`, `on` (after trimming). Any other value — including `false`, `0`, `no`, `off`, garbage, or absence — is treated as `false`. | `false` | When truthy, also deletes every document in `project_files` whose body's `project_identifier` equals `identifier`. |

There are **no path parameters**: the path `/api/list-saved-projects` is static, and the target resource is selected entirely via the `identifier` query parameter.

This endpoint reads **no request body whatsoever**. The handler's only extractors are `State<ApplicationState>`, the authorized-request pipeline wrapper, and `Query<HashMap<String, String>>`. No `Json<...>` body extractor is present, so any body sent by the client is ignored and never deserialized. Callers should send no payload (or an empty one).

Status: `200 OK`. Content-Type: `application/json`. The body is an object assembled from `build_deletion_acknowledgement_payload(...)` and then enriched with three additional fields inserted by the handler.

| `document_identifier` | string | The (trimmed) `identifier` that was deleted. |
| `cascaded_file_count` | integer | Number of child files actually removed from `project_files`. `0` when `cascade` was not requested, or when no matching child files existed. |
| `project_display_name` | string | Best-effort human name: first non-blank of body `project_name`, `display_name`, `title`; otherwise falls back to the document identifier. |
| `deleted_at` | string | Coarse deletion timestamp: Unix epoch seconds followed by a literal `Z` (e.g. `"1751856000Z"`). Not RFC-3339. |
| `cascade_requested` | boolean | Whether the caller requested a cascade delete (the parsed value of the `cascade` flag). |

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` as a JSON object `{ "error_category", "error_explanation" }`, where `error_category` is the snake_case label of the variant.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | The `identifier` query parameter is missing, or is present but empty/whitespace after trimming. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the 'identifier' query parameter is required"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | Raised upstream in the pipeline (Authentication stage) when `x-account-email` is absent; the handler is never reached. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | Raised upstream when the supplied credential is present but unparseable/invalid; the handler is never reached. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | The located saved project's `owning_account` does not match the caller, OR the document has no recorded owner, OR the document collection itself denies the operation. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"the authenticated principal does not own this saved project"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | No saved project exists under `identifier`; or the delete returned `false` (it vanished between lookup and delete); or the collection reported the resource/project could not be located. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"no saved project exists under the supplied identifier"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from the document collection during fetch, list, or delete (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure`). | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"document collection failure: boom"}` |

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request(&authorized_request)` — derives the owning-account string from the authorized principal's email.
2. `extract_requested_identifier_from_query(&query_parameters)` — pulls and trims the required `identifier` query param; errors `400` if absent.
3. `validate_requested_identifier_is_non_empty(&requested_identifier)` — rejects blank identifiers with `400` before touching storage.
4. `fetch_saved_project_before_deletion(&application_state, &requested_identifier)` — fetches the saved-project document (if any) from `saved_projects`.
5. `require_located_saved_project(optionally_located)` — converts a `None` lookup into a hard `404`.
6. `assert_account_owns_saved_project(&located_document, &owning_account)` — enforces ownership; `403` on mismatch or missing owner.
7. `extract_project_display_name_for_receipt(&located_document)` — computes the receipt display name from body fields with fallback to the identifier.
8. `stamp_project_deletion_timestamp()` — produces the epoch-seconds-plus-`Z` timestamp for the receipt.
9. `extract_cascade_deletion_flag(&query_parameters)` — parses the optional `cascade` flag into a boolean.
10. `delete_project_files_owned_under_project(&application_state, &requested_identifier)` — (only when cascade is truthy) lists `project_files`, collects children via `collect_child_file_identifiers_for_project` / `document_belongs_to_project`, deletes each, and returns the count.
11. `delete_saved_project_document(&application_state, &requested_identifier)` — deletes the saved-project document, returning a boolean.
12. `interpret_deletion_outcome(deletion_succeeded, &requested_identifier)` — maps `false` to `404`, `true` to success.
13. `build_deletion_acknowledgement_payload(&requested_identifier, cascaded_file_count)` — builds the base receipt JSON, which the handler then augments with `project_display_name`, `deleted_at`, and `cascade_requested`.
14. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error(...)` — used throughout to translate `ApplicationError` values into the appropriate `HttpError`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Cascade deletes children before deleting the root.** If the saved-project delete subsequently fails/returns `false` (yielding `404`), any child files already removed during the cascade are *not* restored — the operation is not transactional across the two collections.
- **The cascade sub-delete uses a bare `?`, bypassing the error mapper.** Inside the per-child loop, `delete_document(...).await?` propagates the raw `ApplicationError` directly (not via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`), relying on the `From<ApplicationError> for HttpError` impl. The mapping is broadly equivalent, but a `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` mid-cascade would surface as `404` rather than being tolerated.
- **`cascade` parsing is exact and unforgiving.** Only `true`, `1`, `yes`, `on` (trimmed, lowercased) are truthy. `cascade=True` works (lowercased), but `cascade=y`, `cascade=enabled`, or `cascade` with no value are all treated as `false`.
- **The `deleted_at` timestamp is not RFC-3339.** It is Unix epoch *seconds* with a literal `Z` suffix (e.g. `1751856000Z`). Do not attempt to parse it as ISO-8601; if the system clock predates the epoch the code falls back to `0Z`.
- **Ownership requires a recorded owner.** A document whose `owning_account` is `None` cannot be deleted by anyone through this endpoint — it returns `403`, not `404` and not success. Legacy documents without owners are effectively undeletable here.
- **`document_identifier` in the response echoes the trimmed input, not necessarily the stored key.** Since `identifier` is trimmed on extraction, the receipt reflects the trimmed value used for the lookup and delete.
- **No request body is read.** Sending a JSON body has no effect; the `identifier` must be in the query string.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I called DELETE twice and got a 404 the second time. Is that a bug?**
A: No. The first call deleted the project; the second correctly reports that it no longer exists. The end-state is identical both times, which is what idempotency actually guarantees. It does not promise you the same status code.

**Q: Why did my cascade only delete some of the files?**
A: A cascade deletes exactly those `project_files` documents whose body field `project_identifier` string-equals the deleted project's identifier. Files that reference the project under any other field, or via a non-string value, or not at all, are invisible to `document_belongs_to_project` and are left untouched.

**Q: I set `cascade=false` but expected the project to survive — instead it was deleted. Why?**
A: `cascade` only governs whether *child files* are also removed. The saved project itself is always deleted regardless of the cascade flag; `cascade=false` merely leaves the child files in place with a `cascaded_file_count` of `0`.

### `GET /api/projects/:project_identifier/folders/:folder_name/files/:file_identifier/download` — Download a Folder File as a Base64-Encoded JSON Envelope

#### Synopsis

This endpoint retrieves a single file that lives inside a named folder of a given project, locates the underlying blob in object storage, and returns the entire file body inline as a standard (padded) base64 string wrapped in a JSON envelope. It does not stream octets, set binary `Content-Type`, or return a `302` redirect to a signed URL; instead it hands you a JSON object containing the decoded display name, MIME type, base64 payload, byte length, a ready-made `Content-Disposition` header value, and a cosmetic `temporary_url`. The handler is read-only: nothing is created, mutated, or deleted as a side effect of calling it.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a strict REST standpoint this is a textbook safe, idempotent resource retrieval: `GET` on a fully-qualified, hierarchical resource path (`project → folder → file → download`) that carries no request body, mutates no server state, and may be replayed an unbounded number of times with identical observable results (modulo the blob itself changing underneath it). The `download` suffix is a sub-resource — a *representation selector* — rather than an RPC verb: it says "give me the byte-materialized representation of this file resource," as opposed to the sibling `GET .../:file_identifier` route which returns the file's metadata document. Because the operation is nullipotent with respect to server state, it is fully cacheable in principle, and a well-behaved intermediary would be within its rights to cache the JSON envelope.

In Domain-Driven Design terms this handler is a thin application-layer orchestration seam that sits squarely in the HTTP adapter ring and delegates every meaningful capability to ports: the `document_collection` port to resolve the file's metadata document, and the `storage_adapter` port to materialize the opaque blob. The handler itself owns no domain logic beyond boundary validation (folder name and file identifier must be `NonEmptyText`) and a deliberate decomposition into fifteen single-purpose helper functions. The base64 encoding, the `Content-Disposition` sanitization, and the `temporary_url` composition are presentation concerns, correctly kept out of the domain and out of the application core, living only here at the edge where bytes meet the wire.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This route is guarded by the type-state request pipeline and is only invoked once the request has reached the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` stage (see the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor in the handler signature). Concretely, that means the following headers are consumed and enforced by upstream pipeline stages before your handler code ever runs.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 3f9a2c7e-1b44-4d2e-9c0a-77b6f2e1c5aa` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces. If omitted, the pipeline typically synthesizes one; supplying your own makes cross-service debugging tractable. Opaque string; not otherwise interpreted by this handler. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@example.com` | Identifies the calling principal. Consumed during the Authenticated and Authorized stages to establish who you are and whether you may reach this resource. Missing or blank values fail the pipeline before the handler runs. |

Type-state pipeline (Validated → Authenticated → Authorized): the request is modeled as a state machine encoded in the Rust type system, so that an unproven request literally cannot be passed to a handler that demands a proven one. A raw request is first driven through **Validated**, where structural well-formedness of the request (headers present, shapes parseable) is checked; only then is it promoted to **Authenticated**, where the identity asserted by `x-account-email` is resolved to a real principal; and only then to **Authorized**, where that principal is checked against the policy governing this specific resource. Each promotion is a distinct type (`RequestHasBeenValidated`, `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`, `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`), and because this handler's extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the compiler guarantees that no code path can reach the download logic without having first traversed all three stages in order. Skipping a stage is not a runtime bug you can hit — it is a program that does not compile.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Any URL path segment | — | The owning project. **Note:** captured and destructured but then bound to `_project_identifier` and *not* used by the handler logic — it participates in routing only. |
| `folder_name` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText` (non-empty after trimming) | — | The folder the file lives in. Validated for non-emptiness, then bound to `_validated_folder_name` and *not* otherwise used for lookup. A blank/whitespace value yields `400`. |
| `file_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText` (non-empty after trimming) | — | The identifier of the file document. This is the value actually used to fetch the document from the `project_files` collection. A blank/whitespace value yields `400`. |

There are **no query parameters** for this endpoint.

This is a `GET` endpoint and the handler reads **no request body whatsoever**. It takes only path parameters and application state. Sending a body is harmless but ignored.

#### Successful Response

**Status:** `200 OK` with `Content-Type: application/json`. The response body is a single JSON object assembled by `build_folder_file_download_payload` and then augmented in-place with two additional fields.

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display_name` | string | Yes | Human-facing file name from the document's `display_name`, or the fallback `"downloaded-file"` if absent/blank. |
| `mime_type` | string | Yes | MIME type from the document's `mime_type`, or the fallback `"application/octet-stream"` if absent/blank. |
| `encoding` | string | Yes | Always the literal `"base64"`. Describes the encoding of `encoded_body`. |
| `encoded_body` | string | Yes | The entire file blob, standard (RFC-4648, padded) base64. Empty string for a zero-byte file. |
| `byte_length` | number (integer) | Yes | The size of the **decoded** blob in bytes (i.e. the pre-encoding length). |
| `content_disposition` | string | Yes | A ready-to-use header value, e.g. `attachment; filename="report.pdf"`, with `"`, `\`, `\r`, `\n` in the name replaced by `_`. |
| `temporary_url` | string | Yes | A cosmetic path of the form `/downloads/<file_identifier>`. See gotchas — this is *not* a functional signed URL. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError` into a `SerializedErrorBody` of the shape `{ "error_category", "error_explanation" }`. The table below lists every variant of `HttpError` and describes precisely when — if ever — this specific handler produces it.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `folder_name` or `file_identifier` fails `NonEmptyText::parse` (blank/whitespace-only). Despite the name, this is triggered by malformed *path* segments here. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"file identifier is invalid: ..."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` absent when the pipeline runs the Authenticated stage. Produced upstream, before the handler body. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Supplied credentials cannot be resolved to a valid principal during the Authenticated stage. Produced upstream. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal is not permitted to reach this resource during the Authorized stage. Produced upstream. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | (a) no document exists in `project_files` for `file_identifier`; **or** (b) the document exists but has no non-blank `storage_object_reference` field. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested folder file does not exist"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The storage adapter fails to fetch the blob (mapped via `map_storage_failure_to_http_error`), or the document-collection lookup itself errors (propagated via `?`). | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"failed to retrieve the file blob: ..."}` |

A full example `SerializedErrorBody`:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "the requested folder file does not exist"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler is deliberately decomposed into fifteen named helpers, invoked in roughly this order:

1. `destructure_folder_file_path_parameters` — splits the `(String, String, String)` tuple into `(project_identifier, folder_name, file_identifier)`.
2. `validate_download_folder_name` — parses the folder name into `NonEmptyText`, mapping failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
3. `validate_download_file_identifier` — parses the file identifier into `NonEmptyText`, mapping failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
4. `fetch_folder_file_document_for_download` — calls `document_collection.fetch_document(PROJECT_FILES_COLLECTION_NAME, file_identifier)`, returning `Option<StoredDocument>`.
5. `require_located_folder_file_for_download` — turns a `None` lookup into `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`.
6. `extract_storage_object_reference_from_document` — reads the non-blank `storage_object_reference` string from the document body; missing/blank → `404`.
7. `fetch_blob_bytes_from_storage` — calls `storage_adapter.fetch_blob(...)`, mapping any failure to `500` via `map_storage_failure_to_http_error`.
8. `extract_download_display_name_from_document` — reads `display_name` or falls back to `"downloaded-file"`.
9. `extract_download_mime_type_from_document` — reads `mime_type` or falls back to `"application/octet-stream"`.
10. `encode_blob_bytes_as_base64` — hand-rolled standard (padded) base64 encoder over the raw blob bytes.
11. `compose_content_disposition_header_value` — builds `attachment; filename="..."`, sanitizing `"`, `\`, `\r`, `\n` to `_`.
12. `compose_temporary_download_url` — formats `/downloads/<file_identifier>` (cosmetic only).
13. `compute_downloaded_blob_byte_length` — returns `raw_bytes.len()`.
14. `build_folder_file_download_payload` — assembles the base JSON envelope (`display_name`, `mime_type`, `encoding`, `encoded_body`, `byte_length`).
15. `map_storage_failure_to_http_error` — helper that converts an `ApplicationError` into `HttpError::UpstreamApplicationFailure` (used by step 7).

After step 14 the handler mutates the payload object in place to insert `content_disposition` and `temporary_url`, then returns `Json(payload)`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`project_identifier` and `folder_name` are essentially decorative for lookup.** The document is fetched by `file_identifier` alone against the flat `project_files` collection. A valid `file_identifier` returns its file regardless of whether the `project_identifier`/`folder_name` in the URL actually correspond to it. Do not rely on the path hierarchy for scoping.
- **Blank folder/file segments raise `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`, not `404`** — even though they arrive via the path, not a body. The error category name is a misnomer in this context.
- **Two distinct causes collapse into one `404`.** "File document not found" and "file document exists but has no `storage_object_reference`" both surface as `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` (with different explanations). If you get a 404 for a file you believe exists, check the stored document actually carries a non-blank `storage_object_reference`.
- **The whole file is materialized in memory and base64-inflated (~33% larger) inside a JSON string.** For large blobs this is expensive on both server memory and response size, and there is no streaming, chunking, or range support. `byte_length` reports the *decoded* size, not the size of `encoded_body`.
- **`temporary_url` (`/downloads/<file_identifier>`) is cosmetic.** It is a formatted string, not a signed, expiring, or even necessarily routable URL. Do not treat it as a working alternative download link.
- **`content_disposition` is returned in the JSON body, not as an actual HTTP header.** If you want the browser to honor it, you must set the header yourself from this value; the endpoint does not emit it on the response.
- **Base64 is standard/padded, not URL-safe.** The alphabet is `A–Za–z0–9+/` with `=` padding; if you feed `encoded_body` to a URL-safe decoder it will reject the `+` and `/`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Why does it return JSON with base64 instead of just streaming the file bytes?**
A: Because it was written to return a JSON envelope with base64. The bytes are encoded via `encode_blob_bytes_as_base64` and packed into `encoded_body`. If you want raw octets, this is the wrong endpoint; there isn't a raw-stream variant here.

**Q: Can I download a file from a specific folder by putting the right folder name in the path?**
A: You can put any non-empty folder name in the path and it will be validated for non-emptiness, then ignored. Resolution is by `file_identifier` only. The folder segment buys you nothing but a `400` if you leave it blank.

**Q: The response has a `temporary_url`. Can I hand that to a client to download the file later?**
A: No. It is the literal string `"/downloads/" + file_identifier`. It is not signed, not expiring, and corresponds to no implemented route in this handler. It exists to look like a download URL.
