#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request` — resolves the authorized caller's `Email` into a plain `String` for audit/ownership context (bound to `_owning_account`, currently unused downstream).
2. `extract_search_query_from_query_parameters` — pulls the mandatory `query` parameter out of the query-string map, or returns `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
3. `validate_query_string_search_expression` — trims and parses the raw query into a `NonEmptyText`, mapping any domain error to `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
4. `extract_folder_path_filter_from_query_parameters` — extracts and trims the optional `folderPath`, discarding blank values (yields `Option<String>`).
5. `extract_pagination_offset_from_query_parameters` — parses `offset` as `usize`, defaulting to `0` on absence or unparseable input.
6. `extract_pagination_limit_from_query_parameters` — parses `limit`, defaulting to `25`, treating `0` as default, and clamping to a maximum of `200`.
7. `list_all_project_file_documents` — awaits `document_collection.list_documents(PROJECT_FILES_COLLECTION_NAME)`, mapping failures via the error translator below.
8. `normalize_query_term_for_case_insensitive_match` — trims and lower-cases the validated query for case-insensitive comparison.
9. `filter_documents_by_query_expression` — filters all documents by substring match (`document_body_contains_normalized_query`) and folder predicate (`document_matches_folder_path_filter`).
10. `count_total_matches_before_pagination` — records the length of the matched set prior to windowing (feeds `totalMatches`).
11. `apply_pagination_window_to_matches` — applies `skip(offset).take(limit)` to slice the requested page.
12. `render_matched_document_as_file_entry` — maps each surviving document into the client-facing file-entry JSON object (invoked per element).
13. `build_query_search_result_payload` — assembles the final `{files, count, totalMatches, query, cached}` envelope.
14. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` — translates `ApplicationError` values from the collection listing into the appropriate `HttpError` variant (404 / 403 / 500).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Full-collection scan in memory.** The handler calls `list_documents` to load *every* document in `project_files` and filters in application memory. This does not scale: search latency and memory use grow linearly with the total number of project files, irrespective of how few match.
- **Matches the raw serialized body AND the identifier.** `document_body_contains_normalized_query` lower-cases the *entire* serialized JSON body (`document_body.to_string()`) and checks for the substring, plus the document identifier. This means a query can match on internal field names, JSON punctuation, MIME strings, or any embedded value — not just the human-facing `name`. A search for `pdf` will match `application/pdf`, `folderPath`, `report.pdf`, etc.
- **`totalMatches` counts pre-pagination; `count` counts the returned page.** These two numbers differ whenever the match set exceeds the page window. Clients must page using `offset`/`limit` and rely on `totalMatches` for the true total.
- **Silent coercion of bad pagination input.** A non-numeric `offset` or `limit` does not error — it silently falls back (`offset` → `0`, `limit` → `25`). A `limit` of `0` also silently becomes `25`, and any `limit` above `200` is silently clamped to `200`. The client receives no signal that its request was reinterpreted.
- **`cached` is always `false`.** The field is hard-coded; there is no caching layer behind this handler despite the field's presence. Do not build client logic that assumes it can ever be `true`.
- **`folderPath` filter is exact (case-insensitive), not prefix/hierarchical.** `document_matches_folder_path_filter` uses `eq_ignore_ascii_case` against the document's `folderPath` body field. A request for `folderPath=PDFs` will NOT match a file in `PDFs/Archive`; only an exact folder-name equality succeeds. Documents lacking a `folderPath` field are excluded whenever the filter is supplied.
- **`owningAccount` may be `null`.** The rendered entry passes through `StoredDocument.owning_account`, which is `Option<String>`; documents with no owner serialize as `"owningAccount": null`. There is no per-caller ownership filtering — the authorized principal is extracted but never used to scope results.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I search with an empty `query` to list all files?**
A: No. An absent `query` yields `400 request_body_was_malformed`, and a blank/whitespace-only `query` fails `NonEmptyText::parse` for the same 400. The term must be non-empty after trimming.

**Q: Does `folderPath` do a recursive/prefix match on subfolders?**
A: No. It is an exact, case-insensitive equality on the document's `folderPath` field. `PDFs` does not match `PDFs/2026`. If you need subtrees, issue separate requests per folder.

**Q: Why does my search for `File` return everything?**
A: Because the matcher scans the full serialized JSON body of each document as lower-cased text, and the search is a naive substring check. Common tokens that appear in field names, MIME types, or JSON structure (`file`, `path`, `name`, `pdf`) will match broadly. Choose distinctive query terms.

**Q: The `count` and `totalMatches` in my response disagree — is that a bug?**
A: No. `count` is the size of the returned page; `totalMatches` is the number of matches before pagination. They coincide only when the entire match set fits in one page.

---

### `GET /api/projects/:project_identifier/folders/folder_id/:folder_identifier/contents` — List the Contents of a Project Folder

#### Synopsis

This endpoint enumerates the contents of a single, folder-identifier-addressed folder that lives inside a given project. It returns a merged directory listing composed of the canonical, always-present top-level folder set concatenated with every stored file document whose body claims membership in the requested folder, sorted so that folders precede files and each group is ordered alphabetically by name. The response is a synthetic directory-listing payload with `files`, `folderCount`, `fileCount`, and `totalCount`.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of REST, this is the canonical safe, idempotent verb: a `GET` against a collection-shaped sub-resource (`.../folders/folder_id/:folder_identifier/contents`). It is, by contract and by conscience, both **safe** (it mutates nothing observable on the server) and **idempotent** (issuing it a thousand times leaves the world precisely as it found it, modulo whatever other principals are concurrently writing documents). No request body is read, no state transition is provoked, no side effect is committed — the handler is a pure projection of the `project_files` document collection through a folder-membership filter and a presentation-layer renderer. That the path segment literal `folder_id` is baked into the route is a deliberate disambiguator: it declares that the trailing dynamic segment is a *folder identifier* rather than a *folder name*, distinguishing this endpoint from its name-addressed siblings elsewhere in the router.

From a Domain-Driven Design vantage, this handler sits squarely in the `projects_files` bounded context and functions as a thin **application/interface adapter**: it validates its two path parameters into `NonEmptyText` value objects at the boundary, delegates all persistence concerns to the `document_collection` port via `list_documents`, and reserves for itself only the humble mechanical labor of filtering, rendering, merging, sorting, and counting. The canonical top-level folder set is a presentation invariant — a fixed skeleton every project pretends to have — while the file entries are the genuine, dynamically discovered domain data. The endpoint thereby preserves the sacred separation between what the domain *knows* (stored documents) and what the interface *promises* (a tidy, Drive-shaped directory listing).

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the type-state request pipeline before this handler's body is ever entered. The handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is the compiler-enforced proof that the request has already been validated, authenticated, and authorized. The following headers drive that pipeline.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 6f3a1c9e-2b74-4a0f-9d21-c0ffee123456` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces for this single request. Absent one, the platform may synthesize one; supplying your own makes cross-service debugging tractable. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: scientist@alma.test` | The caller's account identity. This is the credential the authentication stage consumes to establish *who* the principal is, and the authorization stage consumes to decide *whether* that principal may read this project's folders. Missing → `401 authentication_credentials_were_missing`; malformed/unknown → `401 authentication_credentials_were_invalid`; recognized-but-forbidden → `403 authorization_was_denied`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The request is modeled as a value carrying a phantom stage marker that can only advance in one direction, with each transition gated by a real check. It begins as `RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated`. Structural/shape validation promotes it to `RequestHasBeenValidated`. Consuming and verifying the identity headers (chiefly `x-account-email`) promotes it to `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`. A successful authorization decision — the principal is permitted the requested operation — promotes it to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. Because this handler accepts *only* `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, it is *statically impossible* to invoke the body of `list_folder_contents_handler` with a request that has skipped any earlier stage: the type system, not a runtime `if`, is the guardrail. The `_authorized_request` binding is deliberately underscore-prefixed — the proof of authorization is required to *exist*, but its contents are not further inspected inside this particular handler.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_identifier` | path | string (`NonEmptyText`) | Yes | Must be non-empty and not all-whitespace after parsing | — | The project whose folder is being listed. Validated into `NonEmptyText`; on failure yields `400`. Note: after validation it is bound to `_validated_project_identifier` and is **not** used to scope the document query — see Edge Cases. |
| `folder_identifier` | path | string (`NonEmptyText`) | Yes | Must be non-empty and not all-whitespace after parsing | — | The folder identifier whose contents are requested. Validated into `NonEmptyText`; its `.as_str()` is matched against each document's `folderId`, `folder`, or `folderName` body fields. |

No query parameters are read by this handler.

This endpoint reads **no request body**. It is a `GET`; any body sent is ignored entirely and is never deserialized.

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` into a body of exactly two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | Identity present but unrecognized/unverifiable at the authentication stage. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Pipeline denial, or `list_documents` maps `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` → "the principal is not authorized to view this folder". | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"the principal is not authorized to view this folder"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | `list_documents` returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` → "the requested folder could not be located". | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested folder could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from the document collection (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure`) → "the document collection could not be read: ...". | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the document collection could not be read: ..."}` |

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. `destructure_folder_contents_path_parameters` — splits the `(String, String)` path tuple into the raw project and folder identifiers.
2. `validate_folder_contents_project_identifier` — parses the raw project identifier into `NonEmptyText`, mapping failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` (result bound but not used to scope the query).
3. `validate_folder_contents_folder_identifier` — parses the raw folder identifier into `NonEmptyText`, mapping failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
4. `build_canonical_top_level_folder_names` — returns the fixed vector of 31 canonical top-level folder names.
5. `build_canonical_folder_directory_entries` — maps each canonical name (with its index) into a folder-shaped JSON entry via `render_canonical_folder_name_as_directory_entry`.
6. `list_project_file_documents_for_folder` — calls `document_collection.list_documents(PROJECT_FILES_COLLECTION_NAME)` (`"project_files"`), mapping any failure through `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`.
7. `filter_documents_to_requested_folder` — retains only documents for which `document_belongs_to_requested_folder` is true (body `folderId` / `folder` / `folderName` equals the folder identifier).
8. `render_stored_document_as_file_directory_entry` — renders each surviving document into a file-shaped JSON entry, applying `name`/`fileName`/identifier, `mimeType`, time, `size`, and optional `owner`/`webViewLink` defaults.
9. `merge_folder_entries_and_file_entries` — concatenates canonical folder entries followed by file entries.
10. `sort_directory_entries_folders_before_files` — stable-sorts so folders precede files, each group ordered by `name`.
11. `build_folder_contents_payload` — counts kinds via `count_directory_entries_by_kind` and wraps the entries into the final `{files, folderCount, fileCount, totalCount}` object.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`project_identifier` is validated but never used to scope the query.** It is bound to `_validated_project_identifier` and discarded. `list_documents` reads the *entire* `project_files` collection regardless of project, then filters only by folder identifier — so a document from a different project that happens to match the folder identifier will appear.
- **Folder matching is a loose OR across three string fields.** A document is "in" the folder if its body's `folderId`, `folder`, **or** `folderName` string-equals the requested identifier. A caller passing a *folder name* as the `folder_identifier` can therefore accidentally match documents via `folderName`, despite the route's `folder_id` literal implying identifier-only addressing.
- **`folderCount` is always the canonical count (31), never zero.** The canonical top-level folders are unconditionally injected, so even a totally empty or nonexistent folder yields `folderCount: 31`. Callers must not treat `folderCount` as "folders inside this folder".
- **Timestamps on folder entries are hard-coded literals** (`createdTime` 2026-01-12, `modifiedTime` 2026-06-30) and are identical for every folder in every project — they are not real metadata.
- **A missing folder does not 404 by itself.** `404` only arises from the document-collection port reporting resource/project-not-located. A syntactically valid but nonexistent folder identifier simply returns the canonical folders plus zero files (`fileCount: 0`).
- **`size` is `u64` via `Value::as_u64`.** A body `size` that is negative, fractional, a string, or exceeds u64 falls back to `0` rather than erroring.
- **`modifiedTime` falls back to `createdTime`, which itself falls back to a default literal** (`2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`) for file entries lacking those body fields.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I passed the wrong project but still got files back. Is that a bug?**
A: It is the documented behavior. The project identifier is validated for non-emptiness and then thrown away; folder membership is the only filter applied to a whole-collection read. File a ticket with whoever wrote `let _validated_project_identifier`.

**Q: Why does an empty folder still report 31 folders?**
A: Because the 31 canonical top-level folders are conjured unconditionally before any real data is consulted. `folderCount` describes the fixture, not your folder.

**Q: Can I send a request body to filter results?**
A: You can send one. It will be ignored with the serene indifference of a `GET` handler that never deserializes a body. Use the `folder_identifier` path segment instead.

### `GET /api/projects/:project_identifier/folders/:folder_name/files` — List Files Within a Canonical Project Folder

This endpoint enumerates every stored file document that belongs to a given project and one of its canonical folders, projecting each surviving document into a stable, client-friendly file-listing entry and returning them ordered so that the most recently modified file is listed first. It is a pure read: it accepts no request body, mutates no state, and touches exactly one backing collection (`project_files`). The response is a JSON envelope containing a `files` array and a convenience `count` integer.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of REST, this endpoint is the archetypal collection-`GET`: it is both **safe** (it produces no observable change on the server) and **idempotent** (issuing it once or one thousand times leaves the resource universe exactly as it found it, and any two consecutive calls with no intervening writes will return byte-identical payloads modulo upstream mutation). Because it is safe, it is a legitimate target for caching intermediaries, prefetching, and speculative revalidation; because it is idempotent, a client that suffers a dropped connection may retry with impunity and without the ceremony of an idempotency key. The resource being addressed is a *sub-collection* — the files contained within one folder of one project — and the URI hierarchy `/projects/{id}/folders/{name}/files` is deliberately constructed to read as a containment tree, honoring the principle that the path should describe *what* is being addressed rather than *how* it is to be retrieved.

Within a Domain-Driven Design layering, the handler occupies the outermost ring: it is an HTTP adapter, a translator that speaks the ubiquitous language of the transport (paths, headers, status codes, JSON envelopes) and delegates the actual persistence concern to an application port, `document_collection.list_documents`. Crucially, the handler contains only *presentation* and *filtering* logic — it decides which documents are visible to this project/folder pair and how each document should be shaped for the wire — but it does not itself understand storage. The folder namespace is guarded by a closed vocabulary (`CANONICAL_PROJECT_FOLDER_NAMES`) so that the URL surface cannot be weaponized to probe arbitrary path segments against the backing collection; unrecognized folder names are answered with `404`, not `400`, so that the endpoint reveals nothing about the shape of the store.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request first passes through the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor before the handler body ever runs. Extraction reads two headers:

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | No (recommended) | `x-request-id: 6f9c2a10-4b7e-4d0a-9d2f-8a1c3e5b7d90` | Correlation identifier for tracing. If absent, the pipeline substitutes the literal `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"` rather than rejecting the request. The validation stage rejects only an *empty/whitespace* value; the substituted default is non-empty, so a missing header never fails validation. |
| `x-account-email` | **Yes** | `x-account-email: researcher@alma.example` | Identifies the calling principal. Absence yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`. A value that is not valid UTF-8 text, or that does not parse as an email via the `email_string_prism`, yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The handler's second argument, `_authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, is a compile-time proof object. Axum can only construct it via the `FromRequestParts` implementation, which walks the request through an irreversible ladder of phantom-typed states:

1. **Originate → Validate.** The correlation identifier is read (defaulting when the header is missing). `validate()` rejects an empty/whitespace correlation identifier with `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` and produces a `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>`.
2. **Authenticate.** The `x-account-email` header is required; if missing → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; if non-text or non-email → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. On success the parsed `Email` principal is attached, yielding `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`.
3. **Authorize.** `authorize()` asserts an authenticated principal is present; if somehow absent it returns `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. Success yields `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`.

Because the handler's signature demands the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` marker specifically, it is *statically impossible* to invoke the handler body on a request that skipped any rung of this ladder — the missing-auth and denied-auth branches are handled before the first line of the handler executes. The parameter is prefixed with `_` because the handler needs the *proof* of authorization, not the principal's identity, for its logic.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText` (non-empty after trimming). Failure → `400`. | None | The project whose folder is being listed. Matched case-sensitively against each document's `projectId` / `project_identifier` field. |
| `folder_name` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText`; then, normalized (trimmed + lowercased), must be one of `documents`, `reports`, `agents`, `literature`, `uploads`. Non-canonical → `404`. | None | The canonical folder to list. Matched case-insensitively against each document's `folderName` / `folder_name` / `folder` field. |

No query parameters are read by this handler. **None** beyond the two path parameters above.

#### Request Body

This endpoint reads **no request body**. It is a `GET`; any body sent by the client is ignored entirely and never deserialized. There are no fields.

(a) Field table — not applicable; the handler reads zero body fields.

```json
  "description": "This GET endpoint accepts no request body.",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {},
  "maxProperties": 0
}
```


#### Successful Response

`200 OK`. Body is an envelope object with a `files` array and a `count` integer. Each file entry has the following fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `files` | array of objects | Rendered file entries, sorted by `modifiedTime` descending (lexicographic on the ISO-8601 string). |
| `files[].id` | string | The stored document's identifier (`document_identifier`). |
| `files[].name` | string | Display name from `name`/`fileName`/`displayName`; falls back to `id` when absent or blank. |
| `files[].mimeType` | string | Inferred from the display name's extension; `application/octet-stream` for unknown/absent extensions. |
| `files[].type` | string | Constant literal `"File"`. |
| `files[].createdTime` | string | From `createdTime`/`created_at`; empty string if absent. |
| `files[].modifiedTime` | string | From `modifiedTime`/`modified_at`/`updatedTime`; falls back to `createdTime` if absent. |
| `files[].webViewLink` | string | From `webViewLink`/`viewLink`/`url`; falls back to `https://drive.example.com/file/{id}`. |
| `files[].size` | integer | Byte size from `size`/`sizeBytes`/`byteSize` (numeric or numeric-string); `0` if missing/unparseable. |
| `count` | integer | The number of entries in `files`. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` into a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields, `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `project_identifier` or `folder_name` fails to parse as `NonEmptyText` (empty/whitespace). Also emitted by the pipeline if the correlation identifier is empty. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the folder name was not valid: text was empty"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | The `x-account-email` header is absent. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"the 'x-account-email' header was absent"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` is non-UTF-8 text, or does not parse as an email. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the account header did not parse into a valid email address"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Authorization stage found no principal, or the document collection returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` from `list_documents`. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | `folder_name` is not one of the five canonical folders; or the collection returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` / `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated`. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the folder 'secret' is not a recognized project folder"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from `list_documents` (e.g. a `DocumentCollectionFailure`). | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the document collection failed: boom"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "requested_resource_was_not_found",
  "error_explanation": "the folder 'secret' is not a recognized project folder"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The following are the real helper functions invoked, in order:

1. `destructure_folder_files_path_parameters` — splits the axum `(String, String)` tuple into the raw project identifier and raw folder name.
2. `validate_folder_files_project_identifier` — parses the raw project identifier into `NonEmptyText`; a domain failure maps to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
3. `validate_folder_files_folder_name` — parses the raw folder name into `NonEmptyText`; a domain failure maps to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
4. `assert_folder_name_is_within_canonical_folder_set` — trims + lowercases the folder name and rejects anything outside the five canonical folders with `404`.
5. `list_all_project_file_documents` — calls `document_collection.list_documents(PROJECT_FILES_COLLECTION_NAME)`, mapping failures via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`.
6. `filter_documents_to_folder_files` → `document_is_file_within_folder` — retains only documents whose `projectId`/`project_identifier` matches (case-sensitive), whose `folderName`/`folder_name`/`folder` matches (case-insensitive), and whose declared `type`/`kind` is `"file"` (or is absent).
7. `read_first_string_field` — shared helper used throughout to read the first present string field from a JSON body given a list of candidate field names (including legacy aliases).
8. `render_stored_document_as_file_listing_entry` — projects each surviving document into the wire shape; internally calls:
   - `extract_file_display_name_from_document` — resolves the display name with fallback to the document id.
   - `infer_file_mime_type_from_display_name` — maps the filename extension to a MIME type.
   - `extract_file_size_bytes_from_document` — reads the byte size (numeric or numeric-string), defaulting to `0`.
9. `sort_file_entries_by_modified_time_descending` — sorts entries in place by `modifiedTime` string, most recent first.
10. `count_folder_files` — counts the rendered entries.
11. `build_folder_files_listing_payload` — wraps the entries and their count in the `{ "files", "count" }` envelope.
12. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` — translates an `ApplicationError` into the fitting `HttpError` variant (404 / 403 / 500).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`GET` that can return `400`.** Despite carrying no body, the endpoint emits `request_body_was_malformed` when a *path* parameter fails `NonEmptyText` parsing. The category name is a misnomer here — the offending input is the URL, not a body.
- **Non-canonical folder is `404`, not `400`.** A syntactically valid but unrecognized folder (e.g. `secret`) is deliberately reported as not found to avoid revealing collection structure — even though the string itself parsed fine.
- **Project match is case-sensitive; folder match is case-insensitive.** `document_is_file_within_folder` compares `projectId` with `==` but compares the folder with `eq_ignore_ascii_case`. `Proj-42` and `proj-42` are different projects, but `Documents` and `documents` are the same folder.
- **Typeless documents are optimistically treated as files.** A document with no `type`/`kind` field passes the `is_file_kind` check. Only an explicit non-`"file"` value (e.g. `"Folder"`) is excluded. Malformed or missing type metadata therefore leans toward inclusion.
- **Full-collection scan, then in-memory filter.** The handler calls `list_documents` on the *entire* `project_files` collection and filters in Rust. There is no server-side query by project/folder, so cost scales with total collection size, not with the result count — a latent performance cliff on large tenants.
- **Sort is lexicographic on a string, not chronological on a parsed date.** `modifiedTime` is compared as raw text. This is correct only for zero-padded, same-zone ISO-8601 timestamps. Mixed offsets, missing padding, or non-ISO strings will sort in surprising orders, and an absent `modifiedTime` falls back to `createdTime`, and if that too is absent it becomes `""` which sorts last.
- **`webViewLink` may be fabricated.** When no link field is present, a synthetic `https://drive.example.com/file/{id}` URL is returned. Clients must not assume this resolves to anything real.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

- **Q: Can I filter or paginate with query parameters like `?limit=` or `?type=`?**
  A: No. The handler reads exactly two path parameters and nothing from the query string. Everything after `?` is ignored. The result set is whatever the folder contains, sorted newest-first.

- **Q: The `type` field on every entry is always `"File"` — can I get folders here too?**
  A: No. This endpoint lists files only, and `document_is_file_within_folder` explicitly excludes documents whose declared type is not `"file"`. The `"File"` literal in each entry is a hardcoded constant, not derived from the document. Folders are a different endpoint.

- **Q: I sent a JSON body describing a new file and got back a listing instead of a created file. Why?**
  A: Because this is `GET`, which reads and never writes. The body was discarded unparsed. You want the sibling route `POST /api/projects/:project_identifier/folders/:folder_name/files` (`create_folder_file_handler`).

### `GET /api/list-projects` — List the Saved Projects Owned By or Shared With the Caller

This endpoint enumerates every saved project the authenticated, authorized principal can see: the projects they own outright, plus the projects on which some other owner has added them as a collaborator. It fetches two disjoint document sets from the `saved_projects` document collection, renders each into a stable listing entry, merges and deduplicates the two sets, sorts them newest-modified-first, and returns them wrapped in a small summary envelope. It is a pure read: nothing is created, mutated, or deleted as a side effect of calling it.

#### Theory & Rationale

`GET /api/list-projects` is the textbook embodiment of an HTTP read: it is both **safe** (it induces no observable state change on the server; a client may issue it freely, and intermediaries may reasonably treat it as side-effect-free) and **idempotent** (issuing it once, twice, or two thousand times in succession yields the same server state — namely, none changed). Because it is a collection-listing GET rather than a single-resource GET, it deliberately returns a *representation of a query result set* rather than a canonical resource; the ephemeral, caller-scoped nature of that result set (it is filtered by *who is asking*) is precisely why it must never be cached across principals and why every entry is stamped with `isOwnedByCurrentUser` relative to the authenticated caller. The listing is a projection, not an entity.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler sits squarely in the HTTP adapter layer of a hexagonal architecture: it is an inbound port implementation that translates a transport-level request into calls against the `document_collection` outbound port, and translates the port's `ApplicationError` failures back into transport-level `HttpError` responses. The handler performs no business rules of its own beyond presentation-layer shaping (display-name fallback, ownership/collaborator classification, dedup, sort); all persistence and retrieval concerns live behind the `UnitOfWork` and `DocumentCollection` abstractions. This keeps the aggregate boundary — the "saved project" — cleanly on the far side of the port, and keeps the handler a thin, testable, orchestration-only seam.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 7f3c2b1a-9d4e-4f6a-8b21-c0ffee123456` | Correlation identifier. Consumed at the very start of the pipeline (`HttpRequestInPipeline::originate`) via the extractor constant `CORRELATION_IDENTIFIER_HEADER_NAME = "x-request-id"`. Threaded through the request as `correlation_identifier()` for tracing/log correlation. A missing or malformed value fails the **Validated** stage. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@university.edu` | The authenticated account email. Consumed by the extractor constant `AUTHENTICATED_ACCOUNT_HEADER_NAME = "x-account-email"` during the `authenticate` stage. Becomes the `authorized_principal()` (`Email`) after authorization and is the `owning_account` string this handler filters every document against. |

**The type-state pipeline (Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized).** This handler does not accept a raw axum request; it accepts `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That generic parameter is a zero-sized type-state marker (`RequestHasBeenAuthorized` is an uninhabited enum), and it is the compiler-enforced proof that the request has already traversed the full admission pipeline before a single line of handler code runs:

1. **`RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated` → `RequestHasBeenValidated`.** `originate(correlation_identifier)` seeds the pipeline from the `x-request-id` header; `validate()` checks the structural preconditions of the request. On failure it emits `HttpError::RequestBodyWasMalformed`. You cannot skip this: there is no way to construct the next state without calling `validate()`.
2. **`RequestHasBeenValidated` → `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`.** `authenticate(...)` reads `x-account-email` and establishes *who* the caller claims to be. Missing credentials yield `HttpError::AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; invalid ones yield `HttpError::AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`.
3. **`RequestHasBeenAuthenticated` → `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`.** `authorize()` decides whether that authenticated principal is permitted to proceed. Denial yields `HttpError::AuthorizationWasDenied`. Only after this transition does the `authorized_principal()` accessor (returning `&Email`) become available.

Because the handler's signature demands the final `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` marker, it is *statically impossible* to route an unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request into this function — the type system rejects it at compile time. The handler therefore treats the presence of an authorized principal as a given and never re-checks credentials itself.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint reads no path segments and no query-string parameters whatsoever. Any query string a client appends (e.g. `?foo=bar`) is silently ignored by the handler.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. This endpoint takes no path or query parameters. |

#### Request Body

**This endpoint reads no request body.** It is a `GET` request; the handler's only inputs are the pipeline-supplied authorized principal (from `x-account-email`) and the correlation identifier (from `x-request-id`). No JSON, form, or binary body is deserialized, inspected, or required. Sending a body is harmless but pointless — it is never read.

| — | — | — | — | — | None. This endpoint reads no request-body fields. |

JavaScript `fetch`:

```javascript
const response = await fetch("https://api.alma.example/api/list-projects", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    "x-request-id": "7f3c2b1a-9d4e-4f6a-8b21-c0ffee123456",
    "x-account-email": "researcher@university.edu",
    "accept": "application/json",
  },
});
if (!response.ok) {
  const err = await response.json(); // { error_category, error_explanation }
  throw new Error(`${err.error_category}: ${err.error_explanation}`);
}
const { projects, summary } = await response.json();
```

#### Successful Response

`200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is a `serde_json::Value` object with a `projects` array and a `summary` object. Each element of `projects` is a listing entry with the exact fields produced by `render_project_document_as_listing_entry`.

Top-level envelope fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `projects` | array of object | Merged, deduplicated (by `id`), and modified-time-descending list of listing entries. |
| `summary` | object | Aggregate counts over `projects`. |
| `summary.totalCount` | integer | Total number of entries in `projects`. |
| `summary.ownedCount` | integer | Count of entries with `isOwnedByCurrentUser == true`. |
| `summary.sharedCount` | integer | Count of entries with `isOwnedByCurrentUser != true` (i.e. everything else, including entries missing the flag). |

Per-entry fields (each object in `projects`):

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The `document_identifier` of the stored document. Used as the dedup key. |
| `name` | string | Display name (see `displayName`); duplicated here for compatibility. |
| `displayName` | string | `body.displayName` if non-blank, else `body.name` if non-blank, else `document_identifier` if non-blank, else `"Untitled Project"`. |
| `createdTime` | string | `body.createdTime` as a string, or `""` if absent. |
| `modifiedTime` | string | `body.modifiedTime` as a string, or `""` if absent. Also the sort key (descending string comparison). |
| `collaborators` | array of string | Collaborator emails, extracted from either bare strings or objects carrying `emailAddress`, trimmed, blanks dropped. |
| `almaRootName` | string | `body.almaRootName` as a string, or `""` if absent. |
| `almaRootOwner` | string | `body.almaRootOwner` as a string, or `""` if absent. |
| `isOwnedByCurrentUser` | boolean | True when the caller owns the document (matched via `owning_account` or `owners[].emailAddress`, case-insensitively). |
| `hasUserAccess` | boolean | Always `true` (every returned entry is, by construction, accessible to the caller). |
| `shared` | boolean | For owned entries: `true` if the document has any collaborators. For shared entries: always `true` (`force_shared`). |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` as `SerializedErrorBody { error_category, error_explanation }`. The `error_category` is the snake_case label of the variant. For this endpoint the *reachable* failures come from the pipeline (auth stages) and from `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` mapping `ApplicationError` values raised by the `document_collection` port.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | Not raised by the handler body itself (there is no body to parse), but the pipeline's `validate()` stage can emit it if the request fails structural validation before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"request failed validation"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | The `x-account-email` header is absent at the `authenticate` stage, so no principal can be established. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` is present but not a valid/parsable account identity at the `authenticate` stage. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | The `authorize` stage rejects the authenticated principal, OR the document collection returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` (mapped by `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`). | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | The collection returns `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` while listing (e.g. the `saved_projects` collection or an owner scope cannot be located). | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from `list_documents_owned_by` or `list_documents` (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure`) — the datastore/upstream failed. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"document collection failure: boom"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example (a 500 from the collection):

```json
{
  "error_category": "upstream_application_failure",
  "error_explanation": "document collection failure: boom"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates these real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request(&authorized_request)` — pulls the caller's email out of `authorized_principal()` as an owned `String`; this is the `owning_account` used for all subsequent filtering.
2. `list_saved_project_documents_owned_by_account(&application_state, &owning_account)` — awaits `document_collection.list_documents_owned_by(SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME, owning_account)`, mapping any failure through `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`.
3. `list_saved_project_documents_shared_with_account(&application_state, &owning_account)` — awaits `document_collection.list_documents(SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME)` (the *entire* collection), then keeps only documents where the caller is **not** the owner **and** is listed as a collaborator.
4. `determine_project_ownership_flag(candidate_document, owning_account)` — used inside step 3 (and later during rendering) to test ownership via `owning_account` or `owners[].emailAddress`, case-insensitively.
5. `document_lists_account_as_collaborator(candidate_document, owning_account)` — used inside step 3 to test collaborator membership case-insensitively.
6. `extract_project_collaborator_emails(stored_document)` — collects collaborator emails from bare strings or `{emailAddress}` objects, trimming and dropping blanks.
7. `render_owned_project_document_as_listing_entry(stored_document, &owning_account)` — maps each owned document into a listing entry (calls the shared renderer with `force_shared = false`).
8. `render_shared_project_document_as_listing_entry(stored_document, &owning_account)` — maps each shared document into a listing entry (calls the shared renderer with `force_shared = true`).
9. `render_project_document_as_listing_entry(...)` — the shared building block that assembles the per-entry JSON object (also invokes `extract_project_display_name_from_document`).
10. `merge_owned_and_shared_project_entries(owned_entries, shared_entries)` — concatenates owned-first then shared, then dedupes.
11. `deduplicate_project_entries_by_identifier(...)` — drops later entries sharing an existing `id` (entries with an empty/missing `id` are always kept).
12. `sort_project_entries_by_modified_time_descending(&mut merged_entries)` — sorts by the `modifiedTime` **string** in descending order.
13. `build_projects_listing_payload(merged_entries)` — wraps the entries in the `projects` + `summary` envelope, calling `count_owned_versus_shared_projects` for the summary counts.
14. `count_owned_versus_shared_projects(&project_entries, "")` — tallies owned vs. shared by reading each entry's `isOwnedByCurrentUser` flag (the account argument is unused: it is passed as `""`).
15. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error(err)` — the shared error translator used by steps 2 and 3.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Full-collection scan for shared projects.** `list_saved_project_documents_shared_with_account` calls `list_documents` on the *entire* `saved_projects` collection and filters in memory. This is O(all saved projects across all users) per request — a genuine scaling hazard as the collection grows, not a paginated query.
- **`modifiedTime` is sorted as a raw string, not a parsed timestamp.** Ordering is correct only because the values are lexicographically sortable ISO-8601 (e.g. `2026-06-30T...Z`). A non-ISO or differently-zoned timestamp will sort wrong, and a missing `modifiedTime` (rendered as `""`) sorts to the very end.
- **`sharedCount` is "everything not owned," not "genuinely shared."** `count_owned_versus_shared_projects` increments `shared_count` for any entry whose `isOwnedByCurrentUser` is not exactly `true` — including entries where the flag is missing. Do not treat `sharedCount` as a precise collaborator metric.
- **The `owning_account` argument to the counter is deliberately `""`.** `build_projects_listing_payload` passes an empty string, and `count_owned_versus_shared_projects` ignores its `_owning_account` parameter entirely — the tally is driven purely by the per-entry `isOwnedByCurrentUser` boolean set earlier during rendering.
- **Case-insensitive email matching, but exact-string dedup.** Ownership and collaborator checks use `eq_ignore_ascii_case`, whereas deduplication compares `id` values with exact equality. Two documents with the same logical project but differently-cased identifiers would *not* be deduped.
- **Empty `id` entries are never deduplicated.** In `deduplicate_project_entries_by_identifier`, an entry whose `id` is empty/missing is always pushed through, so multiple id-less entries can coexist. In practice `id` comes from `document_identifier`, so this is mostly a defensive edge.
- **`hasUserAccess` is hardcoded `true`.** It is not computed per document; every returned entry carries `true` because, by construction, only accessible documents reach the response.
- **Blank display names fall through a four-level ladder.** `displayName` → `name` → `document_identifier` → literal `"Untitled Project"`, with whitespace-only values treated as blank at each step.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I pass a query parameter like `?owner=someone@else.com` to list another user's projects?**
A: No. There are no query parameters. The listing is scoped entirely to the `authorized_principal()` derived from `x-account-email`; the handler never reads the query string. To see another user's projects you would need to be that user (or be a collaborator on their projects).

**Q: If I POST to this route with a JSON body, will it be validated?**
A: This route is registered only for `GET`. Sending `POST` reaches a different handler (or a 405, depending on routing). Even on the correct `GET`, no request body is read, so any body you attach is inert.

**Q: The same project shows up once but I own it *and* collaborate on it — is that a bug?**
A: No, that is the dedup working as designed. Owned documents are gathered first; the shared-projects scan explicitly excludes documents you own (`!determine_project_ownership_flag(...)`), and `merge_owned_and_shared_project_entries` dedupes by `id` keeping the first (owned) occurrence. You will see exactly one entry, flagged `isOwnedByCurrentUser: true`.

---

### `GET /api/list-saved-projects` — List the caller's saved AI-3D projects

This endpoint returns the collection of saved projects owned by the authenticated caller, filtered down to documents that declare the `ai3d-project` kind, normalized into a compact listing shape, and sorted so the most-recently-modified project appears first. It reads nothing from the request body and accepts no path or query parameters — the only inputs it consults are the authentication headers that identify the owning account. The response is a JSON object containing a `projects` array and a `totalCount` integer that always equals the length of that array.

#### Theory & Rationale

This is a textbook `GET` collection resource. Under REST semantics `GET` is defined to be both **safe** (it MUST NOT mutate server state) and **idempotent** (issuing it once or one thousand times yields the same server-observable effect — none). The handler honors this contract to the letter: it opens no write transaction, persists nothing, and merely projects existing stored documents into a read model. Because it is safe, intermediaries and clients are entitled to cache and prefetch it; because it is idempotent, a nervous client may retry it after a timeout without fear of duplicating anything. The response is deliberately a *representation* of a filtered, sorted view rather than the raw persisted documents, which is exactly the read-side flattening one expects from a query handler that must not leak the storage schema to the network boundary.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler lives squarely in the thin HTTP adapter layer of a hexagonal architecture: it translates a wire request into a call against the `document_collection` port, then translates the returned `StoredDocument` aggregates back into a transport DTO. The domain concept it surfaces — a saved AI-3D project owned by an account — is expressed through the `SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME` collection (`"saved_projects"`) and the `ai3d-project` kind marker. All business-relevant decisions (which documents belong to the account, which are AI-3D projects, how to order them) are made here as read-model shaping; nothing here belongs to the write model, and nothing here mutates an aggregate. It is, precisely stated, a pure query in the CQRS sense: a function from account identity to a materialized view.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: scientist@example.org` | The authenticated principal's email. Consumed by the pipeline to build the `Authenticated`/`Authorized` states; the handler reads it back via `authorized_principal()` and uses it verbatim as the `owning_account` scope for the document query. Its absence or invalidity is rejected before the handler body ever runs. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7` | Correlation identifier (`CORRELATION_IDENTIFIER_HEADER_NAME`) threaded through the pipeline for tracing/log correlation. Not used to make authorization decisions and does not affect the response payload, but strongly recommended so a single request can be followed across logs and upstream calls. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` -> `Authenticated` -> `Authorized`).** This handler does not receive a raw axum request; it receives `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That generic marker is not decoration — it is a compile-time proof. The request first exists as `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated>`; it is promoted to `RequestHasBeenValidated` only after structural validation succeeds, then to `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated` only after the `x-account-email` credential is resolved into a real principal, then finally to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` only after the authorization stage confirms that principal may perform this operation. Because the handler signature demands the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` marker, it is *statically impossible* to invoke this handler on a request that has not already traversed Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized. Any failure along that chain is converted to an `HttpError` (missing/invalid credentials, denied authorization) before control reaches line one of the handler. Consequently the handler body itself contains no authentication or authorization code beyond calling `authorized_principal()` to read the already-proven identity.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

This endpoint declares no path parameters and mounts no query extractor. The handler contains an internal `kind`-filter code path (`extract_optional_kind_filter_from_query` / `apply_kind_filter_to_saved_entries`), but it is fed a freshly constructed **empty** `HashMap` — see the inline comment in the handler — so no query string a client sends is read. A `?kind=...` in the URL is silently ignored: it is neither an error nor an effective filter.

#### Request Body

This endpoint reads **no request body**. It is a `GET`; the handler signature has no `Json<...>` or body extractor, and no field of any inbound body is consulted anywhere in the handler. Send an empty body.

```json
}
```

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK`. Content-Type `application/json`. The top-level object has two fields; each element of `projects` is a normalized listing entry produced by `render_saved_document_as_listing_entry`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `projects` | array of object | The filtered, sorted list of saved AI-3D project listing entries. May be empty. |
| `projects[].id` | string | The stored document identifier (`StoredDocument.document_identifier`). |
| `projects[].owningAccount` | string \| null | The document's `owning_account` (`Option`, so may be `null` if the stored document had none). |
| `projects[].displayName` | string | Human-readable name. Prefers body `displayName`, then `name`, then `title`; falls back to `"Untitled Project"`. |
| `projects[].modifiedTime` | string | ISO-8601 timestamp. Prefers body `modifiedTime`, then `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`; falls back to `"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`. |
| `projects[].size` | integer | Serialized byte size. Uses a recorded numeric `size` field if present, otherwise the byte length of the serialized document body. |
| `projects[].version` | string | Version label. Uses string `version`, or numeric `version` rendered as `v<n>`, or nested `metadata.version`; falls back to `"v1"`. |
| `projects[].kind` | string | Always the constant `"ai3d-project"` (entries are already filtered to this kind). |
| `totalCount` | integer | Count of entries in `projects`. Always equals `projects.length`. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` into a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` (a stable snake_case label) and `error_explanation` (human-readable detail). The prompt's canonical variant names map to the following categories.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | Not reachable from parsing (no body). Only if the document collection surfaces `ApplicationError::DomainInvariantViolated`, which `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` maps here. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"domain invariant violated"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | `x-account-email` absent — rejected in the Authenticated stage before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"account email header was missing"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` present but not a resolvable/valid principal — rejected before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"account email header was invalid"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Principal not permitted; also emitted if the document collection returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied`. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Document collection returns `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`. (Uncommon for a list call — an empty account yields `200` with `[]`, not `404`.) | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from `list_documents_owned_by` (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure`) — the catch-all arm of `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"document collection failure: boom"}` |

One full serialized error body example:

```json
  "error_category": "upstream_application_failure",
  "error_explanation": "document collection failure: boom"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request` — reads `authorized_principal()` off the type-state request and returns the account email as a plain `String`.
2. `list_saved_project_documents_for_account` — calls `document_collection.list_documents_owned_by(SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME, owning_account)`, mapping any failure via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`.
3. `filter_saved_documents_to_ai3d_projects` — retains only documents for which `document_declares_ai3d_project_kind` is true.
4. `document_declares_ai3d_project_kind` — checks the top-level `kind` field, then nested `metadata.kind`, against the `"ai3d-project"` marker.
5. `render_saved_document_as_listing_entry` — maps each surviving document into the listing shape, calling the four extractors below.
6. `extract_saved_project_display_name` — resolves `displayName` -> `name` -> `title` -> `"Untitled Project"`.
7. `extract_saved_project_modified_timestamp` — resolves `modifiedTime` -> `updatedAt` -> `createdAt` -> epoch fallback.
8. `compute_saved_project_serialized_size_bytes` — uses recorded numeric `size` or the serialized JSON byte length.
9. `extract_saved_project_version_label` — resolves string `version`, numeric `version` as `v<n>`, or nested `metadata.version`, else `"v1"`.
10. `sort_saved_project_entries_by_modified_time_descending` — lexicographically sorts entries by `modifiedTime` newest-first.
11. `extract_optional_kind_filter_from_query` — reads a `kind` filter from a (here empty) parameter map, trimming and dropping blanks.
12. `apply_kind_filter_to_saved_entries` — case-insensitively filters by `kind` when a filter is present; here a no-op because the filter is always `None`.
13. `count_saved_projects` — returns the entry count.
14. `build_saved_projects_listing_payload` — wraps entries as `{ "projects": [...], "totalCount": n }`.
15. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` — translates an `ApplicationError` into the correct `HttpError` variant.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Query parameters are inert.** The handler builds an empty `HashMap` and derives the `kind` filter from it, so `?kind=anything` in the URL has zero effect. The filter machinery exists purely as a forward-compatibility hook.
- **The `kind` field in every entry is a constant.** Because entries are pre-filtered to AI-3D projects, `render_saved_document_as_listing_entry` hardcodes `"ai3d-project"` for `kind` regardless of what the stored document actually said.
- **Empty account is a `200`, not a `404`.** An account with no saved projects yields `{"projects":[],"totalCount":0}`. `404` arises only if the document collection port itself reports a not-located error.
- **`size` can be self-reported and untrusted.** If the stored body contains a numeric `size`, it is returned verbatim without recomputation; it may not match the real serialized byte length. Only when absent is the size actually measured.
- **Sorting relies on lexicographic ISO-8601 comparison.** Non-ISO or differently-formatted timestamps will sort incorrectly, and any missing timestamp is treated as the epoch (`"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`), sinking such entries to the bottom.
- **`owningAccount` may be `null`.** It is taken from `StoredDocument.owning_account`, an `Option`; the response passes through `null` when the stored document lacked an owner, even though the query was scoped by the caller's email.
- **Kind detection is dual-path.** A document matches if either the top-level `kind` OR nested `metadata.kind` equals the marker, so older records using the nested layout still appear.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I filter the results by passing `?kind=ai3d-project`?**
A: No. You can pass it. It will be ignored. The query map the handler consults is constructed empty by design. Everything returned is already `ai3d-project` anyway.

**Q: I sent a JSON body describing a filter. Why did nothing change?**
A: This is a `GET` handler with no body extractor. Your body was never read. It has been returned to the void from whence it came.

**Q: My account has zero saved projects and I got a `200`. Is that a bug?**
A: No. Absence of projects is a perfectly valid list — an empty one. `{"projects":[],"totalCount":0}` is the correct, safe, idempotent answer. `404` is reserved for the storage layer failing to locate a resource, not for you owning nothing.

### `GET /api/load-ai3d-project` — Load a Persisted AI 3D-Generation Project

#### Synopsis

This endpoint retrieves a single, previously persisted AI 3D-generation project from the `saved_projects` document collection, keyed by a caller-supplied `identifier` query parameter. It reads the stored document body — an inherently free-form JSON blob written by the browser canvas — and defensively normalizes every field the frontend depends upon (project name, semantic version, creation timestamp, canvas settings, and the ordered list of generation entries) so the returned shape is stable regardless of how sloppy or partial the persisted document happens to be. The response is a `{ success: true, projectData: { ... } }` envelope containing the fully normalized, self-consistent project representation.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of REST as originally sermonized by Fielding and subsequently over-litigated in every design review since, this endpoint is a textbook **safe, idempotent, cacheable read**. It uses the `GET` method precisely because it is a pure retrieval operation with no observable side effects on server state: invoking it once, twice, or ten thousand times in succession yields the identical resource representation and mutates nothing. Safety here is not merely a courtesy to intermediaries and prefetchers; it is a contractual guarantee that the request carries no semantic payload and that the URL — including the `identifier` query parameter — constitutes the complete, self-describing specification of the resource being addressed. That the handler accepts a query parameter rather than a path segment is a deliberate, if debatable, ergonomic concession to the browser canvas's persistence layer; the identifier remains, ontologically, the primary key of the resource.

Within the Domain-Driven Design stratification of this service, the handler sits squarely in the HTTP presentation layer — the outermost ring — and studiously refuses to encode business logic. Its sole responsibilities are the parsing and validation of the inbound request at the boundary, the delegation of the actual document retrieval to the `document_collection` port exposed on `ApplicationState`, and the anti-corruption translation of an untrusted, denormalized persisted document into a canonical outbound view model. The normalization helpers (name, version, timestamp, settings, entries) collectively function as a lightweight anti-corruption layer: they enforce the invariant that the frontend never observes a missing key, a null where a string is expected, or a scalar where an object is expected. This is a conscious inversion of trust — the persistence tier is treated as an unreliable external system whose output must be sanitized, rather than as a co-equal partner whose shapes can be assumed correct.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

The handler's signature threads an `_authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor. Even though the underscore prefix signals the handler body never reads it, its mere presence in the signature is load-bearing: axum will run the full extraction machinery for the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` type-state before the handler body executes, meaning authentication and authorization are enforced as a precondition of entry. The identity headers below feed that machinery.

| Header            | Required | Example                                | Notes |
|-------------------|----------|----------------------------------------|-------|
| `x-request-id`    | Yes      | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a2e-1b44-4c8e-a9d1-2e6f0b5c8a71` | Correlation identifier for the request. Threaded through the pipeline and echoed into logs/traces so a single request can be reconstructed end-to-end. Supply a UUID per request; do not reuse across logically distinct calls. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes      | `x-account-email: engineer@example.com` | The acting account's email. This is the authenticated principal against which authorization is evaluated. A missing value produces `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; a malformed or unrecognized value produces `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** This service models request trust as a sequence of compile-time-distinct marker states carried by `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`. A request begins its life as `Validated` once the raw HTTP envelope has been parsed and its basic structural invariants (well-formed headers, decodable body if any) hold. It is promoted to `Authenticated` only after the identity headers — principally `x-account-email` — have been resolved to a known principal; failure at this gate is surfaced as one of the two `401` variants. It is finally promoted to `Authorized` after the service confirms that the authenticated principal is permitted to perform this particular operation; failure at this final gate is surfaced as `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. Because these stages are encoded as distinct Rust types rather than runtime booleans, it is *structurally impossible* for this handler — which demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — to be invoked with a request that has not traversed all three gates in order. The type system, not a code review, is the enforcement mechanism.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name         | In    | Type   | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|--------------|-------|--------|----------|-------------|---------|-------------|
| `identifier` | query | string | Yes      | Non-empty after trimming; length ≤ 256 characters; must not contain control characters, `/`, or `\`. | None | The primary key of the saved project to load. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before use. A missing or blank value is a `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`; a value violating the length or forbidden-character rules is likewise `400`. |

There are no path parameters — the route `/api/load-ai3d-project` is static. Any additional, unrecognized query parameters are ignored: the handler extracts the query into a `HashMap<String, String>` and reads only the `identifier` key.

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` endpoint and the handler reads **no request body whatsoever**. No `Json<...>` or other body extractor appears in the handler signature; the sole input is the `identifier` query parameter documented above. A body, if sent, is neither parsed nor consulted. For completeness, the "expected body" is the empty object:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "LoadAi3dProjectRequestBody",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "This endpoint accepts no request body. Send none."
}
```

```typescript
// No request body is read by this endpoint.
export type LoadAi3dProjectRequestBody = Record<string, never>;
```

```rust
// No request-body struct exists for this handler; the only input is the
// `identifier` query parameter extracted via `Query(HashMap<String, String>)`.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct LoadAi3dProjectRequestBody; // deliberately empty; unused
```

```bash
  -H 'x-account-email: engineer@example.com'
```

```javascript
const response = await fetch(

const body = await response.json();
console.log(body.projectData.projectName);
```

#### Successful Response

Returns `200 OK` with a JSON envelope. The `projectData` object is fully normalized: every field below is guaranteed present with the stated type, even when the underlying stored document omitted or malformed it.

| Field                              | Type    | Description |
|------------------------------------|---------|-------------|
| `success`                          | boolean | Always `true` on a successful load. |
| `projectData`                      | object  | The normalized project view model. |
| `projectData.projectName`          | string  | Human-readable project name. Defaults to `"Untitled 3D Project"` when absent/non-string. |
| `projectData.currentVersion`       | string  | Semantic version string. Defaults to `"1.0.0.0"` when absent/non-string. |
| `projectData.createdAt`            | string  | ISO-8601 creation timestamp. Defaults to `"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` when absent/non-string. |
| `projectData.settings`             | object  | Normalized canvas settings (see below). Always present with all keys. |
| `projectData.settings.width`       | integer | Canvas width. Default `512`. |
| `projectData.settings.height`      | integer | Canvas height. Default `512`. |
| `projectData.settings.zoom`        | integer | Zoom factor. Default `1`. |
| `projectData.settings.color`       | string  | Background color. Default `"#ffffff"`. |
| `projectData.settings.includeSettings` | boolean | Whether settings are included. Default `false`. |
| `projectData.entries`              | array   | Ordered normalized generation entries (see below). Empty array when absent/non-array. |
| `projectData.entries[].prompt`     | string  | The generation prompt. Default `""`. |
| `projectData.entries[].chatResponse` | string | The chat response. Default `""`. |
| `projectData.entries[].settings`   | object  | Per-entry normalized canvas settings, same shape as `projectData.settings`. |
| `projectData.entryCount`           | integer | Count of entries in `entries`; kept consistent with the array length. |

#### Error Responses

All errors serialize to the standard `SerializedErrorBody` shape: `{ "error_category": <string>, "error_explanation": <string> }`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|--------|----------------|--------------------------|--------------|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `identifier` query param is missing, blank after trimming, exceeds 256 characters, or contains a control character / `/` / `\`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'identifier' query parameter is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The identity headers required to authenticate (e.g. `x-account-email`) are absent; the request never reaches `Authenticated`. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Identity headers are present but do not resolve to a known principal. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal is not permitted to load this resource; also emitted when the document-collection port returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` during fetch. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No document exists under the given `identifier` in `saved_projects` (lookup returns `None`), or the port returns `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` / `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested AI 3D project could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other document-collection failure (e.g. `ApplicationError::DocumentCollectionFailure`) during the fetch is mapped to an upstream failure. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"boom"}` |

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "the requested AI 3D project could not be located"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. `extract_requested_identifier_from_query(&query_parameters)` — pulls the mandatory `identifier` key, trims surrounding whitespace, and rejects a missing or blank value as `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. `validate_ai3d_project_identifier(&requested_identifier)` — guards length (≤ 256) and forbids control characters and path separators (`/`, `\`).
3. `fetch_ai3d_project_document(&application_state, &requested_identifier)` — asynchronously fetches the raw `StoredDocument` from the `SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME` (`"saved_projects"`) collection via the `document_collection` port.
4. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error(originating_error)` — invoked inside step 3's `map_err`; translates `ApplicationError` variants into `404`, `403`, or `500` HTTP errors.
5. `require_located_ai3d_project(optionally_located_document)` — converts an absent (`None`) lookup result into `RequestedResourceWasNotFound`.
6. `extract_ai3d_project_name(&located_document)` — reads `projectName`, defaulting to `"Untitled 3D Project"`.
7. `extract_ai3d_current_version(&located_document)` — reads `currentVersion`, defaulting to `"1.0.0.0"`.
8. `extract_ai3d_created_timestamp(&located_document)` — reads `createdAt`, defaulting to `"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`.
9. `extract_ai3d_canvas_settings_object(&located_document)` — reads `settings` and normalizes it via `normalize_ai3d_canvas_settings`.
10. `extract_ai3d_generation_entries_array(&located_document)` — reads `entries`; maps each element through `normalize_ai3d_generation_entry`, yielding `[]` when the field is absent or not an array.
11. `normalize_ai3d_generation_entry(raw_entry)` — coerces each entry into `{ prompt, chatResponse, settings }` with string/settings normalization.
12. `normalize_ai3d_canvas_settings(raw_settings)` — normalizes a settings blob against the default shape (per-key type-checked fallback).
13. `build_default_ai3d_canvas_settings()` — the canonical default settings object used whenever a raw settings value is missing/malformed.
14. `read_string_field_or(source, field, default)` / `read_number_field_or(raw, default)` — shared pure utilities backing the extractors; the latter tolerates both integer and float JSON numbers.
15. `assemble_ai3d_project_data_object(...)` — assembles the outward `projectData` object, embedding `entryCount` via `count_ai3d_generation_entries`.
16. `build_ai3d_load_success_payload(project_data)` — wraps `projectData` in the `{ success: true, ... }` envelope, which is returned as `Json(Value)`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Whitespace-only identifiers are 400, not 404.** The value `"   "` is trimmed to empty by `extract_requested_identifier_from_query` and rejected as malformed *before* any lookup — you never reach the not-found branch.
- **Type coercion is silent, not error-producing.** A `projectName` stored as the number `42`, or a `chatResponse` stored as `true`, does not error; the reader simply falls back to the default (`"Untitled 3D Project"` / `""`). Callers relying on the persisted value must ensure they wrote a JSON string.
- **`entryCount` is derived, never trusted.** Even if the stored document carried its own `entryCount`, it is ignored; the returned count is computed from the normalized `entries` array length by `count_ai3d_generation_entries`, so it is always internally consistent with `entries`.
- **Float dimensions are truncated toward zero.** `read_number_field_or` converts `zoom: 2.9` to the integer `2` via `as f64 -> as i64`, not rounded. Fractional canvas settings silently lose their fractional part.
- **A non-array `entries` field vanishes.** If `entries` is a string, object, or number rather than an array, the handler returns an empty list rather than erroring — `entryCount` will be `0` even though the raw document had "something" under `entries`.
- **Extra query parameters are ignored, not rejected.** Only `identifier` is read from the `HashMap`; junk params like `?identifier=x&foo=bar` pass through cleanly.
- **The 403 has two distinct origins.** `AuthorizationWasDenied` can be produced by the pipeline's authorization gate (before the handler body runs) *or* by the document-collection port returning `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` mid-fetch. The response body is identical but the failure point differs.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I send the identifier in the request body instead of the query string?**
A: No. This is a `GET` handler with no body extractor. The only input read is the `identifier` query parameter. A body is silently ignored.

**Q: Why did I get `"Untitled 3D Project"` back when I clearly saved a name?**
A: You saved it as a non-string JSON value (a number, boolean, object, or null). `read_string_field_or` only accepts JSON strings; anything else falls back to the default. Persist the name as a string.

**Q: The document exists in the database — why a 404?**
A: Either the lookup returned `None` for that exact `identifier` in the `saved_projects` collection (identifiers are exact-match, trimmed, and case-sensitive), or the port returned `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` / `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`. Check that you are querying the correct collection and the identifier matches byte-for-byte after trimming.
