### `GET /api/load-project` — Load a Single Saved Project by Opaque Identifier

#### Synopsis

The `GET /api/load-project` endpoint retrieves exactly one previously saved project document from the `saved_projects` document collection, keyed by an opaque `identifier` supplied as a query parameter. It enforces per-account access control (owner or collaborator), transparently migrates legacy (schema v1) project bodies to the current schema (v2), and returns the project body wrapped in a response envelope annotated with the loading account, an ownership flag, a load timestamp, and the current schema version. This is a read-only, retrieval-shaped operation: it never mutates the stored document, only the representation it hands back to the caller.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of HTTP semantics, this endpoint is the archetypal `GET`: a *safe* method (it induces no server-side state change that the client is accountable for) and an *idempotent* one (issuing the identical request N times yields the same observable outcome as issuing it once). No project is created, no last-opened cursor is persisted, no side-effecting write is committed — the `loaded_at` timestamp is computed in-memory and returned in the response envelope rather than stamped back into the collection, which preserves both safety and idempotency in the strictest RFC-9110 reading. Because retrieval is keyed by a single opaque identifier passed on the query string rather than in a request body, the operation is fully cacheable in principle and trivially replayable, and it participates cleanly in the ambient read-transaction discipline of the surrounding `UnitOfWork`.

Within the project's Domain-Driven Design layering, `load_project_handler` is deliberately a thin *interface-adapter*: it translates an authenticated, authorized HTTP request into a document-collection port call (`fetch_document(SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME, ...)`), applies presentation-tier concerns (access annotation, schema migration, envelope construction), and maps application-layer errors (`ApplicationError`) onto transport-layer errors (`HttpError`). The saved-projects *collection name* is an infrastructure constant, `SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME = "saved_projects"`, imported from `collections.rs`; ownership and collaboration are treated as read-model concerns computed from the stored document rather than re-derived from any external identity service. The handler is generic over `TransactionalUnitOfWork`, so the same code path composes over any concrete persistence backend that satisfies the `UnitOfWork` port — the hallmark of hexagonal, ports-and-adapters architecture.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request must arrive already carrying the ambient authentication headers consumed by the request pipeline before this handler ever runs. The handler itself does not parse headers directly; it receives an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, a type-state proof that the earlier middleware stages have already succeeded.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended (echoed/traced) | `x-request-id: 8f14e45f-ea3c-4d2b-9a7e-1c0f5b2d3e4a` | Correlation identifier threaded through the pipeline for tracing/observability; propagate it on every call so upstream failures can be traced back to a single request. |
| `x-account-email` | **Yes** | `x-account-email: francesca@example.com` | The authenticated principal's email. This becomes the canonical *account key* (`owning_account`) used throughout the `projects_files` category and is compared against the project's `owning_account`/`owner`/`collaborators` for authorization. A missing or unverifiable value causes the pipeline to reject the request with a 401 before the handler executes. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** This handler's `authorized_request` argument has the concrete type `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That generic parameter is not decoration — it is a compile-time *proof token*. The request pipeline advances a request through a sequence of type-states, each of which can only be produced by successfully completing the prior stage:

1. **Validated** — the raw inbound request has been structurally validated (well-formed, headers present in the expected shape). A malformed request is rejected here as `RequestBodyWasMalformed` (400) and never advances.
2. **Authenticated** — the credentials carried by the validated request (chiefly `x-account-email`) have been checked and resolved to a concrete principal. Missing credentials yield `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` (401); present-but-invalid credentials yield `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` (401). Only an authenticated request produces the next token.
3. **Authorized** — the authenticated principal has been granted access to the route. The handler receives `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, and calls `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` to obtain the account email. Because the type system forbids constructing this token except via the authenticated stage, **it is statically impossible for this handler body to run against an unauthenticated or unauthorized request.** Endpoint-specific *resource-level* authorization (does this account own or collaborate on *this* project?) is still enforced inside the handler via `assert_account_may_access_project`, which can emit `AuthorizationWasDenied` (403).

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | query | string | **Yes** | Trimmed of surrounding whitespace; must be non-blank; length ≤ 128 characters (`MAXIMUM_PROJECT_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH`); each character must be ASCII alphanumeric, `-`, or `_` | — | The opaque handle (typically a UUID) of the saved project to load. Passed as `?identifier=...`. An absent, blank, over-long, or ill-formed identifier is treated as a malformed request (400), *not* as "not found". |

There are no path parameters for this route (`/api/load-project` is a fixed path).

#### Request Body

**This endpoint reads no request body.** It is a `GET` handler whose only input is the `identifier` query parameter and the ambient authentication headers. The handler signature accepts `Query(query_parameters): Query<HashMap<String, String>>` and never deserializes a body. Any body sent by a client is ignored.

For completeness, the effective request-body schema is the empty object:

| — | — | — | — | — | No request body fields are read by this handler. |

```json
  "description": "This GET endpoint reads no request body; the only input is the 'identifier' query parameter.",
```

```typescript
}

export interface LoadProjectQueryParameters {
  /** Opaque project handle (typically a UUID). <=128 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_-] only. */
  identifier: string;
}

export interface LoadProjectRequestHeaders {
  "x-account-email": string;   // required: authenticated principal / account key
  "x-request-id"?: string;     // recommended: correlation id
}
```

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns `200 OK` with `Json(Value)` — a JSON envelope produced by `build_loaded_project_payload`.

Response field table (top-level envelope):

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | object | Yes | The migrated, access-annotated project body. When the stored body is a JSON object, its original fields are preserved and augmented; when it is a non-object, it is wrapped (see below). |
| `project.loaded_by_account` | string | Yes (object bodies) | The account email under which the project was loaded (the authorized principal). Injected by `augment_project_body_with_access_flags`. |
| `project.viewer_is_owner` | boolean | Yes (object bodies) | `true` if the loading account owns the project (per `owning_account` field or body `owner`), else `false`. |
| `project.schema_version` | string | Yes (object bodies) | Stamped/normalized to the current schema version `"2"` by the migration step. |
| `project.canvas_nodes` | any | Only for migrated legacy bodies | For legacy (v1) documents, the historical `nodes` field is renamed to `canvas_nodes` during migration (only inserted if `canvas_nodes` was absent). |
| `project.project` | any | Only when the stored body is NOT a JSON object | If the stored body is a scalar/array, it is nested here inside the wrapper object alongside the access flags. |
| `loaded_at` | string | Yes | Coarse Unix-epoch-seconds timestamp (as a decimal string) computed at response time by `stamp_project_last_opened_timestamp`. |
| `schema_version` | string | Yes | The current project schema version constant, `"2"` (`CURRENT_PROJECT_SCHEMA_VERSION`). |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` of the form `{ "error_category": ..., "error_explanation": ... }`. The variants below are the complete `HttpError` set; the "When (for THIS endpoint)" column states which are actually reachable on `GET /api/load-project`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Missing `identifier` query param; blank identifier after trim; identifier > 128 chars; identifier containing anything other than `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. Emitted by `extract_requested_identifier_from_query` / `validate_load_project_identifier`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'identifier' query parameter is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | No authentication (`x-account-email`) supplied. Rejected by the pipeline's Authenticated stage *before* the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Credentials supplied but not valid/verifiable. Rejected by the pipeline's Authenticated stage before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated account is neither owner nor collaborator on the located project (`assert_account_may_access_project`); or the document-collection port itself returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` (mapped by `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`). | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"the authenticated account is not permitted to load this project"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No document exists under the supplied identifier (`require_located_project_document` maps `None`); or the port returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` / `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no saved project exists under the supplied identifier"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other document-collection/application failure (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure`) surfaced by `fetch_saved_project_document` via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"the document collection failed: boom"}` |

Full serialized error body example (403):

```json
{
  "error_category": "AuthorizationWasDenied",
  "error_explanation": "the authenticated account is not permitted to load this project"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler body invokes these real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request(&authorized_request)` — reads `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` and returns it as the owning/loading account `String`.
2. `extract_requested_identifier_from_query(&query_parameters)` — pulls the mandatory `identifier` query param, trims whitespace, and errors (400) if absent or blank.
3. `validate_load_project_identifier(&requested_identifier)` — rejects (400) empty, over-128-char, or non-`[A-Za-z0-9_-]` identifiers before any collection lookup.
4. `fetch_saved_project_document(&application_state, &requested_identifier).await` — calls `document_collection.fetch_document(SAVED_PROJECTS_COLLECTION_NAME, identifier)`, mapping port failures via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`.
5. `require_located_project_document(optionally_located_document)` — converts `None` into a 404 `RequestedResourceWasNotFound`; otherwise yields the concrete `StoredDocument`.
6. `assert_account_may_access_project(&located_document, &owning_account)` — allows only owners or collaborators; otherwise 403 `AuthorizationWasDenied`. Internally calls `account_is_owner_of_project` and `account_is_collaborator_on_project`.
7. `account_is_owner_of_project(&located_document, &owning_account)` — computes the ownership flag (checks `owning_account` field, falling back to body `owner`).
8. `extract_project_schema_version(&located_document)` — reads body `schema_version` (string or number), defaulting to `"1"` (`LEGACY_PROJECT_SCHEMA_VERSION`) when missing/blank/non-scalar.
9. `extract_project_body_for_response(located_document)` — consumes the document and returns its `document_body`.
10. `migrate_project_body_to_current_schema(project_body, &detected_schema_version)` — if already at v2, stamps the version (via `stamp_schema_version`); if legacy, renames `nodes` → `canvas_nodes` (only if absent) and stamps `schema_version` = `"2"`.
11. `augment_project_body_with_access_flags(migrated_project_body, &owning_account, requester_is_owner)` — injects `loaded_by_account` and `viewer_is_owner`; wraps non-object bodies under `project`.
12. `build_loaded_project_payload(annotated_project_body)` — assembles the final envelope `{ project, loaded_at, schema_version }`, calling `stamp_project_last_opened_timestamp` for `loaded_at`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`loaded_at` is not persisted.** Despite the name of `stamp_project_last_opened_timestamp`, the timestamp is only computed in-memory and returned in the response envelope. Loading a project does not write anything back to the collection, preserving `GET` safety/idempotency.
- **`loaded_at` is coarse and clock-dependent.** It is Unix-epoch *seconds* as a decimal string, and if the system clock is behind the epoch (`duration_since` fails) it falls back to `"0"`. Do not treat it as a high-resolution or monotonic timestamp.
- **Two distinct ownership sources.** Ownership is `true` if either the document's top-level `owning_account` field matches OR the body's `owner` string matches. Legacy documents may carry the owner only in the body; both are honored, which can surprise callers expecting a single source of truth.
- **Non-object bodies are wrapped, not augmented.** If a stored `document_body` is a scalar/array (not a JSON object), the response nests it under `project.project` and adds `loaded_by_account`/`viewer_is_owner` to the wrapper — the shape of `project` therefore differs from the object case.
- **Migration only renames `nodes` when `canvas_nodes` is absent.** `migrate_project_body_to_current_schema` uses `.entry("canvas_nodes").or_insert(...)`, so a legacy document that somehow already has a `canvas_nodes` key keeps it and discards the removed `nodes`. Legacy migration on a *non-object* body is a no-op except that no version is stamped.
- **Identifier validation vs. not-found are different failures.** An identifier with a `/`, a space, or over 128 chars is a **400**, never a 404 — the code deliberately treats malformed handles as malformed requests rather than missing resources.
- **Schema version is normalized to a string.** A numeric `schema_version` in the body (e.g. `3`) is read via `to_string()`; any value other than exactly `"2"` is treated as needing migration, and the response always re-stamps `schema_version` to `"2"`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I send the project identifier in the request body instead of the query string?**
A: No. The handler reads only `Query<HashMap<String, String>>` and looks up the `identifier` key. A body is ignored, and an absent query `identifier` is a 400.

**Q: Does loading a project update its "last opened" time in the database?**
A: No. The `loaded_at` value is computed at response time and returned only in the payload. Nothing is written back. This is a safe, idempotent `GET`.

**Q: I'm a collaborator, not the owner — why is `viewer_is_owner` false but I can still load the project?**
A: Working as intended. Access is granted to owners *or* collaborators (`assert_account_may_access_project`), while `viewer_is_owner` (`account_is_owner_of_project`) reports strictly whether *you* own it. Collaborators load successfully with `viewer_is_owner: false`.

---

### `PUT /api/projects/:project_identifier/folders/:folder_name/files/:file_identifier` — Replace a Single File Inside a Named Project Folder

#### Synopsis

This endpoint wholesale-replaces the persisted body of a single file that lives inside a named folder of a project, addressed by its file identifier. The prior document is located first — so that ownership can be enforced and immutable metadata (its creation marker and original file name, if any) preserved — and only then is the caller-supplied replacement content swapped in under the `content` key. The operation returns a small JSON acknowledgement echoing the file identifier and folder name it re-bound.

#### Theory & Rationale

`PUT` is the canonical HTTP verb for *replacement at a known URI*: the client already possesses the full address of the resource (`project_identifier`, `folder_name`, `file_identifier`) and submits the representation that should henceforth live there. `PUT` is, by the letter of RFC 9110, idempotent but not safe — issuing the identical request twice leaves the resource in the same terminal state as issuing it once, which is precisely the contract this handler honours: each call overwrites the `content` field and re-asserts the `folder_name` binding, so a retry after a dropped connection converges rather than compounds. It is emphatically not safe, because it mutates stored state; it must never be triggered by a prefetch, a link crawler, or a speculative cache warm. Note that idempotency here is *content-level*, not *existence-level* — the handler requires the target to already exist and returns `404` when it does not, so `PUT` is used strictly in its replace-the-existing sense and never as an upsert.

Within the Domain-Driven Design layering of the alma-http crate, this handler is a thin *interface-adapter*: it performs syntactic validation of the addressing segments, marshals the acting principal, and delegates all persistence to the application layer's `document_collection` port against the `project_files` collection. The handler deliberately owns the ownership check and the metadata-preservation merge — these are HTTP-surface policies about *who may replace* and *what survives a replace* — while the raw fetch/replace primitives live behind the `UnitOfWork`-parameterised port so that storage technology remains a swappable detail. The result is a handler that reads as a numbered pipeline of pure, individually-testable helper functions, each translating a single application concern into a single HTTP outcome.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 3f9c1e2a-7b40-4c9d-9f21-88ad0e6b1c7e` | Correlation identifier propagated through the pipeline and echoed into logs/traces; strongly advised for debugging idempotent retries of this `PUT`. |
| `x-account-email` | **Yes** | `x-account-email: owner@example.com` | Identifies the authenticated principal. Its value becomes the `owning_account` used both to authorize the replacement and to stamp the rewritten `StoredDocument`. Absent → `401`; malformed/invalid → `401`; present-but-not-the-owner → `403`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** This handler does not accept a raw `Request`; it accepts an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That generic parameter is a compile-time *type-state* witness. A request enters the crate's pipeline as `HttpRequestInPipeline<Validated>` (structural well-formedness of headers and framing has been checked), is then transitioned to `HttpRequestInPipeline<Authenticated>` once the `x-account-email` principal has been established, and finally to `HttpRequestInPipeline<Authorized>` (aliased through `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`) once the coarse-grained authorization gate has passed. Because the handler's signature demands the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` stage specifically, it is *impossible* to route an unvalidated or unauthenticated request into this function — the code would not compile. The handler therefore trusts that `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` yields a genuine, authenticated identity, and layers its own *resource-level* ownership check (does this principal own *this specific document*?) on top of that pipeline-level authorization.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Captured but **not** used by the handler (bound to `_project_identifier` and discarded); any non-empty path segment routes | — | The owning project's identifier. Present for URI addressing and routing symmetry only; lookup is by `file_identifier` against the `project_files` collection, not scoped by project. |
| `folder_name` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText` — non-empty and not all-whitespace; else `400` | — | The folder the file is (re)bound to. Written verbatim into the merged body as `folder_name`, re-asserting/overwriting any prior binding. |
| `file_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText` — non-empty and not all-whitespace; else `400` | — | The document identifier used to fetch and then replace the existing record in the `project_files` collection. |

No query parameters are read.

#### Request Body

The body is deserialized as an arbitrary `serde_json::Value` (not a fixed struct), then interpreted by helper logic. The handler reads at most two logical fields; everything else the client sends is treated as opaque replacement content.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | any JSON value | Conditional | If present, must **not** be JSON `null` (else `400`). If present, its value becomes the stored `content` verbatim. | — | Preferred, explicit wrapper for the replacement payload. When present it is used and the rest of the top-level body is ignored for content purposes. |
| `mime_type` | string | No | Advisory only. A non-string value or a blank/whitespace-only string is treated as absent, not an error. | `None` | Declared MIME type of the payload. Read, trimmed, and then **discarded** (bound to `_declared_mime_type`); it does not influence storage or the response. |
| *(whole body)* | JSON object / value | Conditional | If no `content` key is present: the body must not be JSON `null` and, if it is an object, must not be `{}` (either → `400`). | — | Fallback path. When `content` is absent, the entire submitted body is used as the replacement content. |

In short: send `{"content": <anything non-null>}`, or send any non-empty, non-null body directly. An empty object `{}` with no `content` key is rejected.

**(b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)**

```json
  "anyOf": [
    {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["content"],
      "properties": {

          "description": "Replacement content; anything except JSON null.",

        },

          "type": "string",

        }
      },

    },
    {
      "description": "Fallback: whole body used as content; must be non-null and, if an object, non-empty.",
      "not": { "type": "null" },
      "anyOf": [
        { "type": "object", "minProperties": 1 },

        { "type": "string" },

      ]
    }
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with an `error_category` and a human-readable `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `folder_name` or `file_identifier` fails `NonEmptyText::parse`; `content` is present but `null`; no `content` key and the body is `null` or an empty `{}`; or an application-layer domain-invariant violation is mapped down. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the folder name is not valid: value was empty"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The `x-account-email` credential is absent — request never reaches the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` type-state (rejected upstream in the pipeline). | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | The supplied credential is present but not a valid/recognised principal — rejected upstream before this handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| `403` | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal does not own the located document (owner mismatch, or the document has no recorded owner); also emitted if the port maps `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied`. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"the authenticated principal does not own this folder file"}` |
| `404` | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No document exists for `file_identifier` at fetch time; or `replace_document` returns `false` (the record vanished between fetch and write); or the port maps a not-found application error. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no folder file exists under the supplied identifier"}` |
| `500` | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from the `document_collection` port (e.g. a `DocumentCollectionFailure` from the underlying store) during fetch or replace. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"document collection failure: boom"}` |

**Full `SerializedErrorBody` example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "AuthorizationWasDenied",
  "error_explanation": "the authenticated principal does not own this folder file"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler executes these real helper functions, in order:

1. `destructure_replace_folder_file_path_parameters` — unpacks the axum three-tuple `(project, folder, file)` into named components (order asserted by test; project is discarded).
2. `validate_replace_folder_name` — parses the raw folder segment into `NonEmptyText`, mapping failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
3. `validate_replace_file_identifier` — parses the raw file segment into `NonEmptyText`, mapping failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
4. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request` — reads the authorized principal's email as the owning-account string.
5. `extract_replacement_file_content_field` — pulls `content` (rejecting `null`) or falls back to the whole non-empty, non-null body; rejects an empty `{}`.
6. `extract_replacement_declared_mime_type` — optionally reads/trims `mime_type`; non-string or blank → `None`; value is then discarded.
7. `fetch_existing_folder_file_document` — fetches the document by identifier from the `project_files` collection via the `document_collection` port.
8. `require_existing_folder_file` — converts a missing document (`None`) into `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`.
9. `assert_account_owns_existing_folder_file` — enforces that the principal equals the document's recorded owner; else `403 AuthorizationWasDenied` (unowned documents are non-replaceable).
10. `merge_replacement_body_preserving_metadata` — builds a new body preserving `created_at` and `original_file_name` (if non-null), re-asserting `folder_name`, and writing the replacement under `content`.
11. `build_replacement_stored_document` — assembles the `StoredDocument` (identifier, `Some(owning_account)`, merged body) to overwrite the record.
12. `replace_folder_file_document` — persists the replacement via the port, returning a boolean success flag.
13. `interpret_replacement_outcome` — turns a `false` result into `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound` (record disappeared between fetch and write).
14. `build_folder_file_replacement_acknowledgement` — constructs the success JSON returned to the caller.
15. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` — named mapping from `ApplicationError` to `HttpError` (not-found → `404`, authorization → `403`, domain-invariant → `400`, everything else → `500`), used at both port calls.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`project_identifier` is decorative.** It is captured for URI addressing but immediately bound to `_project_identifier` and discarded. Lookup is by `file_identifier` alone against the shared `project_files` collection — the file is *not* scoped by project or folder during fetch. A correct-file / wrong-project URL still succeeds.
- **The folder in the URL is not verified — it is imposed.** The handler never checks that the existing document already lives in `folder_name`; it simply overwrites the stored `folder_name` with whatever segment you sent. A `PUT` to `.../folders/archive/files/file-42` will silently re-bind a file previously in `drafts` to `archive`.
- **`mime_type` is read and then thrown away.** It is trimmed and validated only to be bound to `_declared_mime_type`. Sending it changes nothing about storage or the response; do not rely on it being persisted.
- **Empty-object body is rejected, but empty *content* is not.** `{}` with no `content` key → `400`. But `{"content": {}}` is accepted (an empty object is not `null`), and `{"content": ""}` or `{"content": false}` are likewise accepted — only JSON `null` under `content` is forbidden.
- **Unowned documents are un-replaceable by anyone.** If the stored document's `owning_account` is `None`, the ownership check falls through to `403` for every caller — there is no principal that "matches" a missing owner. Such records can never be replaced through this endpoint.
- **Two distinct paths yield `404`.** Both a genuine miss at fetch time and a `replace_document` returning `false` (a TOCTOU race where the record was deleted between fetch and write) surface as `404`, with different explanation strings.
- **Content is stored verbatim under `content`, even if you sent the fallback whole-body form.** In the fallback path your entire top-level body (including any stray `mime_type` you added) becomes the value of `content`, nested one level deeper than the explicit-wrapper form would produce.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Does `PUT` create the file if it doesn't exist yet?**
A: No. Despite `PUT`'s upsert reputation, this handler requires the target to already exist and returns `404` otherwise. It is a replace, not an upsert. Use the folder-file creation endpoint (`POST .../folders/:folder_name/files`) to create.

**Q: Will my `created_at`, `original_file_name`, or the old `content` survive the replacement?**
A: `created_at` and `original_file_name` survive if they were present and non-null on the prior document. The old `content` does not — it is entirely replaced. Any other fields on the prior body (e.g. a custom key) are dropped, because the merge rebuilds the body from a fresh map containing only the preserved metadata, the re-asserted `folder_name`, and your new `content`.

**Q: Why did I get `403` when I'm clearly authenticated?**
A: Pipeline-level authentication (`x-account-email` valid) is necessary but not sufficient. This endpoint additionally enforces *resource-level* ownership: your principal must equal the located document's recorded `owning_account`. A valid identity that isn't the file's owner — or a file with no owner at all — yields `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`.

---

### `POST /api/save-project` — Persist (Create or Replace) a Saved Project Document

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts an arbitrary JSON payload describing a "project", stamps it with server-side save metadata, and persists it into the `saved_projects` document collection under the authenticated principal's ownership. If the submitted body carries a non-blank `identifier` field the endpoint performs an ownership-guarded *replacement* of the existing document; if the `identifier` field is absent, blank, whitespace-only, or non-string, the endpoint *inserts* a brand-new document under a freshly minted UUID identifier. In both branches it returns a small JSON acknowledgement echoing the identifier, the operation performed, and the serialized byte size of what was stored.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a strict REST perspective this endpoint is a pragmatic design rather than a strict one. The canonical REST vocabulary would have us split "create" onto `POST` (unsafe, non-idempotent, server-assigns-identity) and "replace" onto `PUT /api/save-project/{identifier}` (unsafe, idempotent, client-asserts-identity). This handler instead overloads a single `POST /api/save-project` route to do both, discriminating at runtime on the presence of an `identifier` field inside the request *body* rather than in the URL. The consequence is that the endpoint is neither safe (it mutates persistent state) nor idempotent in the general case (repeated calls without an `identifier` will each mint a new UUID and produce a new document). The replacement branch, taken in isolation, *is* effectively idempotent — replacing the same document with the same body twice converges to the same stored state — but because the caller cannot statically know which branch will execute without inspecting their own body, the endpoint as a whole must be treated by clients and intermediaries as unsafe and non-idempotent. Do not place this behind a naive retry-on-timeout policy without an `identifier`, or you will accumulate duplicate projects.

In Domain-Driven Design terms this handler lives squarely in the HTTP transport layer (the `alma-http` crate) and is deliberately thin: it validates the one field the domain actually cares about (`name`, via the `ProjectName` value object and its invariants), delegates persistence to the `document_collection` port on `ApplicationState`, and translates application-layer failures back into transport-level `HttpError` variants. The saved-project body itself is treated as an opaque, schemaless `serde_json::Value` blob — the domain does not model its interior structure, which is a conscious anti-corruption boundary: the "project" is a client-owned document, and the server asserts authority only over the `name` field, the injected `saved_metadata`, and the `owning_account` attached to the stored document. Ownership is the load-bearing invariant here, enforced by `assert_account_owns_existing_saved_project` before any replacement is allowed to proceed.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request is funneled through the type-state pipeline via the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor, which reads exactly two headers off the raw request parts.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | No (optional) | `x-request-id: 3f9a1c2e-7b6d-4a10-9e5f-2c8d1a0b7654` | Correlation / tracing identifier. If absent or non-UTF-8, the extractor silently substitutes the literal string `unassigned-correlation-identifier`. A present-but-empty/whitespace value would fail the `.validate()` stage with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` ("the correlation identifier was empty"), but note the fallback only applies when the header is *missing*, so an explicit empty header can still trip validation. |
| `x-account-email` | **Yes** | `x-account-email: researcher@university.edu` | Identifies the authenticated principal. Must be present, valid UTF-8 text, and parse as a valid email via the `email_string_prism`. This value becomes the `owning_account` written onto the stored document and is the sole basis for the ownership check on replacement. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** Authentication and authorization are not performed with `if` statements inside the handler; they are encoded in Rust's type system as a compile-time state machine, so that a handler *cannot* be written that runs before authorization has occurred. The `FromRequestParts` implementation for `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` drives the full progression on every request to this endpoint:

1. **Originate** — `HttpRequestInPipeline::originate(correlation_identifier)` constructs a request in the `RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated` state, carrying the resolved `x-request-id` (or the fallback) and no principal.
2. **Validated** — `.validate()` checks that the correlation identifier is non-empty and transitions to `RequestHasBeenValidated`, else returns `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
3. **Authenticated** — the `x-account-email` header is read (missing → `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`), converted to text (non-UTF-8 → `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`), and parsed into an `Email` value object via the prism (unparseable → `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`); `.authenticate(email)` transitions to `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`.
4. **Authorized** — `.authorize()` asserts a principal is present and transitions to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` (a missing principal here yields `AuthorizationWasDenied`, though in practice authentication would already have failed). Only a value of this final type can be injected into the handler signature.

Because the handler's parameter is typed `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the compiler guarantees that by the time the handler body executes, validation, authentication, and authorization have all provably succeeded. The handler then calls `authorized_principal()` — which is safe to `.expect()` a principal precisely because the type proves one exists.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint reads nothing from the URL path or query string; the operation is entirely driven by headers and the JSON request body.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the entire body as an untyped `serde_json::Value`, then reads specific fields out of it. The body should be a JSON object. All fields *other* than those listed below are preserved verbatim and stored inside the document (the whole body is what gets persisted, minus the server-injected `name` normalization and `saved_metadata`). If the top-level body is a non-object JSON value (string, number, array, etc.), it is wrapped under an `original_payload` key before metadata is injected — but note that a non-object body will *fail earlier* at `name` extraction, so in practice the body must be an object.

##### (a) Fields the handler reads

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **Yes** | Non-empty after trimming; at most 200 characters (Unicode scalar count) per `ProjectName::parse`. Missing or non-string → `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. | — | Human-readable project name. Trimmed and canonicalized by the `ProjectName` value object, then written back into the stored body under `name` and mirrored into `saved_metadata.canonical_name`. |
| `identifier` | string | No | Discriminator. A non-string, absent, or blank/whitespace-only value routes to the *insert* branch; a non-blank string routes to the *replace* branch and must correspond to an existing document owned by the caller. Trimmed before use. | (absent → new document) | If present and non-blank, selects the existing document to replace. Ownership is verified before replacement. |
| *(any other fields)* | any JSON | No | None; treated as opaque. | — | Arbitrary project payload. Stored verbatim inside the persisted document body. |

Server-injected fields (not supplied by the client, written into the stored document): `name` (normalized/canonical), and `saved_metadata` = `{ "canonical_name": <normalized name>, "saved_at_epoch_seconds": "<unix seconds as string>" }`. Any client-supplied `saved_metadata` will be overwritten.

##### (b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma.example/schemas/save-project-request.json",
  "title": "SaveProjectRequest",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["name"],
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "maxLength": 200,
      "description": "Human-readable project name; trimmed and validated by ProjectName::parse."
    },
    "identifier": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Optional. Non-blank value selects an existing document to replace; blank/absent triggers insert."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

##### (c) TypeScript interface

```typescript
interface SaveProjectRequest {
  /** Required. Trimmed, non-empty, <= 200 chars. */
  name: string;
  /** Optional. Non-blank => replace existing; blank/absent => create new. */
  identifier?: string;
  /** Arbitrary additional project payload; stored verbatim. */
  [key: string]: unknown;
}
```

##### (d) Rust struct mirror

The handler itself uses `serde_json::Value`, but a mirror of the fields it reads would be:

```rust
use serde_json::Value;

/// Mirror of the fields `save_project_handler` reads from the body.
/// The real handler deserializes into `serde_json::Value` and reads
/// `name` and `identifier` ad hoc; everything else is opaque payload.
struct SaveProjectRequest {
    /// Required. Validated via `ProjectName::parse` (non-empty, <= 200 chars).
    name: String,
    /// Optional discriminator. `Some(non_blank)` => replace; else insert.
    identifier: Option<String>,
    /// Any additional fields, stored verbatim.
    additional_payload: Value,
}
```

#### Request Examples

##### curl (create a new project)

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.alma.example/api/save-project \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-id: 3f9a1c2e-7b6d-4a10-9e5f-2c8d1a0b7654" \
  -H "x-account-email: researcher@university.edu" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Doctoral Thesis Draft",
    "canvas": { "nodes": [], "edges": [] },
    "notes": "first save"
  }'
```

##### HTTPie (replace an existing project)

```bash
http POST https://api.alma.example/api/save-project \
  x-request-id:3f9a1c2e-7b6d-4a10-9e5f-2c8d1a0b7654 \
  x-account-email:researcher@university.edu \
  name="Doctoral Thesis Draft" \
  identifier="c0ffee00-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678" \
  notes="second save, replacing"
```

##### JavaScript (fetch)

```javascript
const response = await fetch("https://api.alma.example/api/save-project", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "x-request-id": "3f9a1c2e-7b6d-4a10-9e5f-2c8d1a0b7654",
    "x-account-email": "researcher@university.edu",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    name: "Doctoral Thesis Draft",
    // omit `identifier` to create; include it to replace
    canvas: { nodes: [], edges: [] },
  }),
});

if (!response.ok) {
  const err = await response.json(); // { error_category, error_explanation }
  throw new Error(`${err.error_category}: ${err.error_explanation}`);
}

const ack = await response.json();
console.log(ack.document_identifier, ack.operation, ack.serialized_size_bytes);
```

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is a small acknowledgement object built by `build_save_acknowledgement_for_insertion` (new) or `build_save_acknowledgement_for_replacement` (replace).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string | The identifier of the stored document. For a create this is a freshly generated UUID v4; for a replace this is the caller-supplied (trimmed) `identifier`. |
| `operation` | string | `"created"` for an insertion, `"replaced"` for a replacement. |
| `serialized_size_bytes` | integer | Byte length of the enriched, stored document body when serialized to JSON (0 only if serialization somehow fails). |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Constant human string, always `"project saved"`. |

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "SaveProjectResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["document_identifier", "operation", "serialized_size_bytes", "acknowledgement"],
  "properties": {
    "document_identifier": { "type": "string" },
    "operation": { "type": "string", "enum": ["created", "replaced"] },
    "serialized_size_bytes": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
    "acknowledgement": { "type": "string", "const": "project saved" }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

Realistic 200 example (new document created):

```json
{
  "document_identifier": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-abcd-0123456789ef",
  "operation": "created",
  "serialized_size_bytes": 184,
  "acknowledgement": "project saved"
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` as a `SerializedErrorBody` — a JSON object with exactly two fields, `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `name` field missing or non-string; `name` empty after trimming or longer than 200 chars (from `ProjectName::parse`); an upstream `DomainInvariantViolated` mapped by `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`; an empty `x-request-id` at the validate stage. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the request body must contain a string 'name' field"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | The `x-account-email` header is entirely absent from the request. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"the 'x-account-email' header was absent"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` present but not valid UTF-8 text, or present but not parseable as a valid email address. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the account header did not parse into a valid email address"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Replace branch: the referenced `identifier` exists but is owned by a different account (or has no recorded owner); or an application-layer `AuthorizationWasDenied` bubbles up from the collection. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"the authenticated principal does not own this saved project"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Replace branch: the referenced `identifier` cannot be located during the ownership check, or `replace_document` reports no matching document was overwritten; or an application `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`/`RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated`. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the saved project 'c0ffee00-...' could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from `insert_document`, `replace_document`, or `fetch_document` (e.g. a `DocumentCollectionFailure` / storage backend error) mapped via `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error`. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the document collection backend failed: connection refused"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "authorization_was_denied",
  "error_explanation": "the authenticated principal does not own this saved project"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates these real helper functions, in roughly this order:

1. `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request` — pulls the authenticated principal's email out of the authorized pipeline request and materializes it as an owned `String`.
2. `extract_project_name_field_for_save` — reads the mandatory string `name` field from the body; missing/non-string yields `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
3. `validate_project_name_for_save` — runs `ProjectName::parse` over the raw name, surfacing empty/too-long violations as `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
4. `stamp_project_saved_timestamp` — produces a Unix-epoch-seconds string (falls back to `0` if the clock predates the epoch).
5. `inject_saved_metadata_into_body` — clones the body, normalizes `name`, and folds in a `saved_metadata` object (wrapping non-object bodies under `original_payload`).
6. `compute_saved_project_serialized_size_bytes` — serializes the enriched body and reports its byte length (0 on serialization failure).
7. `extract_optional_provided_identifier_field` — reads the optional `identifier`, trimming it and treating blank values as absent to choose the branch.
8. `assert_account_owns_existing_saved_project` *(replace branch only)* — `fetch_document`s the target and errors with not-found (missing) or denied (foreign owner) before allowing replacement.
9. `build_saved_project_stored_document` — assembles the `StoredDocument` (identifier + `owning_account` + enriched body).
10. `replace_existing_saved_project_document` *(replace branch)* — calls `replace_document` on the `saved_projects` collection, returning whether a match was overwritten.
11. `generate_project_identifier_for_new_save` *(insert branch)* — mints a fresh UUID v4 string.
12. `insert_new_saved_project_document` *(insert branch)* — calls `insert_document` on the `saved_projects` collection.
13. `build_save_acknowledgement_for_replacement` / `build_save_acknowledgement_for_insertion` — shape the 200 acknowledgement JSON.
14. `map_document_collection_failure_to_http_error` — translates any `ApplicationError` from the collection port into the appropriate `HttpError` variant.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Blank identifier silently becomes a create.** An `identifier` of `""`, `"   "`, `42`, or `null` is treated as absent by `extract_optional_provided_identifier_field`, so the request quietly inserts a brand-new document under a new UUID instead of replacing anything. Clients expecting a replace and passing a malformed identifier will silently duplicate.
- **No `identifier` means non-idempotent retries.** Because a create mints a fresh UUID every time, retrying a create (e.g. after a network timeout) produces multiple documents. There is no client-supplied idempotency key.
- **The replacement check is not transactional with the replace.** `assert_account_owns_existing_saved_project` fetches and checks ownership, then `replace_existing_saved_project_document` runs separately. Between the two, `replace_document` may still report `false` (no match), yielding a 404 even though the earlier fetch succeeded — a TOCTOU window if a concurrent delete lands in between.
- **`name` is validated but the rest of the body is not.** Only `name` passes through the domain (`ProjectName`). Everything else is stored verbatim as opaque JSON; there is no size cap, schema, or sanitization applied to the arbitrary payload here (only `serialized_size_bytes` is reported, not enforced).
- **Server overwrites `name` and `saved_metadata`.** The stored `name` is the *trimmed/canonical* form, not necessarily what the client sent (leading/trailing whitespace is stripped). Any client-provided `saved_metadata` field is clobbered by the injected one.
- **A missing `x-request-id` never fails, but an explicitly empty one can.** Absent header → fallback string. But if the header is present and empty/whitespace, the `.validate()` stage returns a 400 `request_body_was_malformed` with "the correlation identifier was empty".
- **`serialized_size_bytes` measures the enriched body, not the raw request.** It counts the stored document body *after* metadata injection, so it will be slightly larger than the bytes the client sent.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Why is a "save/replace" operation a `POST` and not a `PUT`?**
A: Because the endpoint decides create-vs-replace from a body field (`identifier`), not from the URL. A single `POST` route (`/api/save-project`) multiplexes both. If you want PUT-like idempotent replacement semantics, always send a valid `identifier` and understand you're still hitting a POST route.

**Q: I sent `identifier` but got a 200 with `"operation":"created"`. Why?**
A: Your `identifier` was blank, whitespace-only, or not a JSON string. Blank/non-string identifiers are treated as absent, so you fell into the insert branch and a new UUID was minted. Check that you sent a non-empty string.

**Q: Do I need the `x-request-id` header?**
A: No. It is optional; if you omit it the server uses `unassigned-correlation-identifier` for correlation. You *do*, however, need a valid `x-account-email` — without it you get a 401, and it is the identity used to own and later re-own your saved projects.

### `POST /api/projects/:project_identifier/files/:file_identifier` — Store (Upsert) a Project File

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts an arbitrary JSON payload and persists it as a single, self-describing project-file document keyed by `file_identifier` and scoped to `project_identifier`, folding server-computed metadata (owning account, resolved MIME type, byte size, and a stored-at timestamp) around the caller's original body. It behaves as an idempotent-by-key **upsert**: if a document already exists under the same identifier it is replaced wholesale; otherwise a fresh document is inserted. The response is a small acknowledgement envelope that reports the document identifier and whether the write was a replacement or a fresh insert.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a REST-semantics standpoint this endpoint occupies a slightly heterodox position: it is exposed as `POST`, yet its runtime behavior is that of an upsert against a fully client-named resource path (`/files/:file_identifier`). One could argue that a caller-chosen identifier combined with last-writer-wins replacement semantics is the textbook definition of `PUT` — and they would not be wrong. The handler nonetheless remains `POST`, and consequently it is neither *safe* (it mutates durable state) nor formally *idempotent* under the HTTP spec's contract, even though the underlying storage operation is, in practice, key-idempotent: submitting the same body twice yields the same terminal document state, differing only in the `was_replacement` flag and the recomputed `stored_at` timestamp. This distinction — practical idempotency of state versus the protocol-level idempotency guarantee — is important and worth stating explicitly.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler is a thin *application-layer* orchestrator living in the `projects_files` bounded context of the `http` crate. It performs no domain logic of its own beyond boundary validation (parsing identifiers into `NonEmptyText` value objects); the actual persistence is delegated across the hexagonal boundary to the `document_collection` port on `ApplicationState`, which the handler treats as an opaque outbound adapter. The document written is a generic `StoredDocument` addressed into the `project_files` collection constant, meaning the HTTP layer deliberately owns the *shape* of the enriched envelope (content, metadata) while remaining ignorant of the *mechanism* of storage. This is the ports-and-adapters ideal: the transport concern (HTTP request shape, header extraction, error taxonomy) is quarantined here, and the infrastructure concern (how bytes hit disk) is quarantined behind the port.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the crate's type-state request pipeline before the handler body executes. The handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is a compile-time proof that the request has already been carried through the full three-stage pipeline. If any stage fails, the handler is never entered and the corresponding error is returned by the pipeline machinery itself.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@alma.example` | Identifies the authenticating principal. Consumed during the pipeline's authentication stage; the resulting authorized principal is later read back inside the handler via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` and recorded as the document's `owning_account`. Absent or empty → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; present but not accepted → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 8f2b6c1e-2a4d-4f9a-9b0c-1d2e3f4a5b6c` | Correlation identifier echoed through logging/tracing for this request. Not read by this handler's business logic but honored by the surrounding pipeline/observability layer for request correlation. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | Required for axum's `Json<Value>` extractor to deserialize the body. A non-JSON or unparseable body is rejected by the extractor before the handler runs, surfacing as `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated → Authenticated → Authorized`).** The `http` crate models request admission as a sequence of *type-states*, where each successful stage transforms the request marker type into the next, and only the final marker type is accepted by protected handlers. Conceptually:

1. **Validated** — the raw inbound request is parsed and structurally validated (required transport-level shape, header presence). A request that cannot be validated never advances.
2. **Authenticated** — the validated request's credential headers (notably `x-account-email`) are checked; on success the request carries an authenticated principal. Missing credentials yield `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; malformed/unaccepted credentials yield `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`.
3. **Authorized** — the authenticated principal is checked against the policy governing the requested action; on success the request becomes `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the exact type this handler requires. Denial yields `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`.

Because `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` is the handler's declared input type, it is *impossible* to invoke this handler on a request that has not walked all three stages — the guarantee is enforced by the compiler, not by a runtime `if`. Inside the body, `extract_owning_account_from_authorized_request` reads `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` to recover the vetted e-mail for ownership stamping.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText` (at least one non-whitespace character after parsing). Empty/blank → `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. | None | The identifier of the owning project. Validated, then folded into the stored document body as `project_identifier`. |
| `file_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must parse as `NonEmptyText` (at least one non-whitespace character). Empty/blank → `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. | None | The identifier under which the file document is stored; becomes the `document_identifier` of the persisted `StoredDocument` and is echoed in the acknowledgement. |

No query parameters are read by this handler.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the entire body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` (`Json<Value>`) and preserves it verbatim under `content` in the stored document. It therefore accepts **any** valid JSON. Two optional top-level keys are given special meaning if — and only if — the body is a JSON object containing them; all other keys are passed through untouched inside `content`.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mime_type` | string | No | Read only if it is a JSON string; trimmed; ignored if empty/blank after trimming; ignored if non-string. | `"application/octet-stream"` | The MIME type recorded on the stored document. Resolved by `extract_stored_file_mime_type`; falls back to the default constant `DEFAULT_PROJECT_FILE_MIME_TYPE` when absent or blank. |
| `display_name` | string | No | Read only if it is a JSON string; trimmed; omitted entirely if empty/blank after trimming; omitted if non-string. | (field omitted from stored doc) | A human-friendly display name. Resolved by `extract_stored_file_display_name`; when present, inserted as `display_name` on the assembled stored body. When absent/blank/non-string, no `display_name` key is written. |
| *(any other keys)* | any JSON | No | None — passed through as-is. | — | The complete submitted body (including `mime_type`/`display_name` themselves) is preserved verbatim under the `content` key of the stored document. |

The body need not be an object; a JSON array, string, number, boolean, or `null` is also accepted and stored under `content`, in which case `mime_type`/`display_name` extraction simply yields the default/omitted behavior because `.get(...)` on a non-object returns `None`.

```json
  "title": "StoreProjectFileRequest",
  "description": "Arbitrary JSON payload. If it is an object, `mime_type` and `display_name` are read as metadata; all keys are preserved verbatim under `content`.",
  "type": ["object", "array", "string", "number", "boolean", "null"],
  "properties": {
    "mime_type": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "MIME type recorded on the stored document; blank values are ignored and default to application/octet-stream."
    },
    "display_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Optional human-friendly display name; blank values are ignored and the field is omitted."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

**TypeScript interface:**

```typescript

// these two optional fields carry special meaning; every other key is
// preserved verbatim under `content` in the stored document.
interface StoreProjectFileRequest {
  /** MIME type; blank/absent -> "application/octet-stream". */
  mime_type?: string;
  /** Human-friendly display name; blank/absent -> omitted from stored doc. */
  display_name?: string;
  /** Any other JSON keys are preserved as-is under `content`. */
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

// In truth the body type is simply:
type StoreProjectFileBody = unknown; // any valid JSON value
```

**Rust struct mirror:**

```rust
// This struct mirrors the two keys it interprets when the body is an object.

    /// Read only if a non-blank string; else omitted from the stored body.

    #[serde(flatten)]
    passthrough: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
```

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns `200 OK` with a JSON acknowledgement envelope built by `build_store_project_file_acknowledgement`. Note: the endpoint returns `200` for both fresh inserts and replacements (it does not distinguish via `201 Created`); the distinction is carried in the `was_replacement` field.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string | The `file_identifier` under which the document was stored (echoed from the validated path segment). |
| `was_replacement` | boolean | `true` if an existing document was replaced, `false` if this was a fresh insert. |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Human-readable status: `"project file replaced"` when `was_replacement` is `true`, otherwise `"project file stored"`. |

```json
{

  "title": "StoreProjectFileAcknowledgement",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["document_identifier", "was_replacement", "acknowledgement"],
  "properties": {
    "document_identifier": { "type": "string" },
    "was_replacement": { "type": "boolean" },
    "acknowledgement": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["project file stored", "project file replaced"]
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```
