### `POST /api/ai-agents/refine` — Refine an existing AI agent configuration from a natural-language instruction

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts an existing AI agent configuration object together with a natural-language refinement instruction, serializes both into a single prompt, dispatches that prompt to the configured artificial-intelligence adapter, and parses the model's completion back into a validated configuration. During the round-trip it deterministically preserves the stable layer identifiers of the original configuration, verifies that the refined `referencedSteps` dependency graph remains acyclic, and refreshes the configuration's `metadata.modified` timestamp. The response is a JSON envelope containing a human-readable `explanation` of what changed and the finalized refined configuration under the `agent` key.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a REST-semantic standpoint this endpoint is modeled as a `POST` because it is neither safe nor idempotent in the HTTP sense: it invokes a generative, non-deterministic upstream (an AI adapter) and produces a *new* representation of a configuration that is derived from — but not equal to — the submitted one. Although the handler performs no persistence of its own (it writes nothing to any collection and opens no unit-of-work transaction), the act of "refining" is a computation-with-side-intent operation whose output is expected to differ across otherwise identical requests, which decisively disqualifies it from `PUT`/`GET` idempotency guarantees. The choice of `POST` at the collection-adjacent verb path `/api/ai-agents/refine` correctly communicates to intermediaries and caches that responses must never be replayed or coalesced.

In Domain-Driven-Design terms, the handler is a thin application-layer orchestrator that lives strictly in the HTTP category (`crates/http/src/categories/ai_agents`). It leans on the domain only for the `NonEmptyText` value object, which enforces the invariant that a refinement instruction must contain meaningful text before any expensive upstream call is attempted. All genuinely stateful concerns — cycle-freedom of the dependency graph, identifier stability across a refinement, timestamp freshness — are treated here as *presentation-and-integrity* concerns applied to an opaque `serde_json::Value`, deliberately keeping the configuration schema loosely coupled at this boundary while still refusing to emit structurally corrupt output. This is the classic anti-corruption posture: validate what must not be violated, tolerate what the model may have shaped freely, and never let a generative upstream silently rename or entangle the caller's steps.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

The handler's signature includes `_authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. This type-state parameter means the request has already traversed the entire authentication-and-authorization pipeline before the handler body executes; if any stage rejected the request, the handler is never entered and the corresponding `HttpError` is returned by the framework machinery instead.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 6f1c2b9e-2a4d-4f7a-8b0c-9d3e5f7a1b22` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces. If omitted the platform typically synthesizes one, but supplying a stable value makes this generative call traceable end-to-end. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@example.org` | Identifies the calling account. Consumed by the authentication stage to establish who the caller is; without a valid, recognized value the request cannot reach `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | The body is extracted with `axum::Json<Value>`; a non-JSON content type or unparseable JSON is rejected before the handler runs. |

Type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`), verbatim in spirit: every inbound request is first materialized as a `Validated` request once its shape and basic envelope have been checked. It then advances to `Authenticated` once the identity carried in `x-account-email` (and associated credentials) has been verified — a failure here surfaces as `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` (nothing to check) or `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` (checked and rejected). Only after successful authentication does the request advance to `Authorized`, at which point the caller's permission to perform *this* operation is confirmed; denial here surfaces as `AuthorizationWasDenied`. Because this handler binds `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the Rust type system statically guarantees that the handler body is unreachable unless all three stages — validation, authentication, authorization — have already succeeded. The handler cannot "forget" to check auth; the check is encoded in the parameter type it demands.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint reads no path segments and no query-string parameters; all input arrives in the JSON request body.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the entire body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then reads specific fields out of it. The fields it actually inspects are enumerated below.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `configuration` | object | Yes | Must be present and must be a JSON object; must itself contain a `layers` array. | — | The existing AI agent configuration to refine. Serialized (pretty-printed) into the prompt. Its `layers[].id` values are harvested to restore stable identifiers onto the refined layers. |
| `configuration.layers` | array | Yes | Must be present and must be an array. | — | Ordered list of layer/step objects. Read from the existing configuration to preserve identifiers positionally. |
| `configuration.layers[].id` | string | No (per element) | Read only if the positionally-matching refined layer is an object. | — | Stable identifier that is copied onto the refined layer at the same index so refinement never renames a step. |
| `instruction` | string | Yes* | Must be a string; must be non-empty after `NonEmptyText::parse`. | — | The natural-language refinement instruction. *Required unless the legacy `prompt` field is supplied instead. |
| `prompt` | string | No (legacy) | Only consulted if `instruction` is absent; then must be a string and non-empty. | — | Legacy alias for `instruction`. If both are present, `instruction` wins. |

Any other keys in the body are ignored by the handler.

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "RefineAiAgentConfigurationRequest",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["configuration"],
  "properties": {
    "configuration": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["layers"],
      "properties": {
        "layers": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "id": { "type": "string" },
              "referencedSteps": {
                "type": "array",
                "items": { "type": "string" }
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "metadata": { "type": "object" }
      }
    },
    "instruction": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "prompt": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
  },
  "anyOf": [
    { "required": ["instruction"] },
    { "required": ["prompt"] }
  ]
}
```

TypeScript interface:

```typescript

  /** Existing configuration to refine. Must be an object and must contain a layers array. */
  configuration: {
    layers: Array<{
      id?: string;
      referencedSteps?: string[];
      [key: string]: unknown;
    }>;
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
    [key: string]: unknown;
  };
  /** Natural-language refinement instruction. Required unless `prompt` is supplied. */
  instruction?: string;
  /** Legacy alias for `instruction`. Used only when `instruction` is absent. */

}
```

Rust struct mirror (the handler itself takes `Json<Value>`; this is a schema-equivalent mirror of what it reads):

```rust
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::Value;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct RefineAiAgentConfigurationRequest {
    /// Must deserialize to a JSON object containing a `layers` array.
    configuration: Value,
    /// Natural-language instruction; required unless `prompt` is present.
    #[serde(default)]

    /// Legacy alias for `instruction`.

}
```

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns `200 OK` with a JSON object assembled by `assemble_refined_configuration_response_payload`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `explanation` | string | Human-readable summary of the changes. Taken from the model envelope's `explanation`; if the model omits it or emits only whitespace, defaults to `"Applied your requested changes to the agent configuration."`. |
| `agent` | object | The finalized refined configuration: the model's refined object with existing layer identifiers restored positionally and `metadata.modified` refreshed. |
| `agent.layers` | array | The refined layers with stable identifiers preserved from the submitted configuration (extra layers keep the model-generated id). |
| `agent.metadata.modified` | string | ISO-8601 timestamp of the refinement (`"2026-07-07T00:00:00.000Z"` in the current build; see gotchas). |

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "RefineAiAgentConfigurationResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["explanation", "agent"],
  "properties": {
    "explanation": { "type": "string" },
    "agent": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "layers": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": { "type": "object" }
        },
        "metadata": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "modified": { "type": "string" }
          }

      }

}
```

Realistic 200 example:

```json
{
  "explanation": "Shortened the Synthesize step to produce a concise summary.",
  "agent": {
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "name": "Research Agent",
    "layers": [
      { "id": "layer-1", "name": "Extract", "referencedSteps": [] },
      { "id": "layer-2", "name": "Synthesize (concise)", "referencedSteps": ["layer-1"] }
    ],
    "metadata": { "modified": "2026-07-07T00:00:00.000Z" }
  }
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `configuration` missing or not an object; `instruction`/`prompt` missing or not a string; instruction empty (fails `NonEmptyText::parse`); existing configuration lacks a `layers` array. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the 'configuration' field is required"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | No/absent `x-account-email` credentials — the request never reached authentication. Raised by the pipeline before the handler body. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | Credentials were supplied but rejected during the authentication stage. Raised by the pipeline before the handler body. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Caller authenticated but not permitted; also mapped here if the AI adapter raises `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` during completion generation. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"you are not authorized to refine this agent configuration"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | The AI adapter raises `ApplicationError::RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` while generating the completion. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the resource required to refine the configuration was not found"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Existing configuration cannot be serialized; adapter fails with any other application error; completion contains no JSON / invalid JSON / non-object configuration; refined config lacks a `layers` array; refined `referencedSteps` form a cycle. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the refinement completion did not contain a JSON object"}` |

Full serialized error body example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "the 'configuration' field must be a JSON object"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. `extract_existing_configuration_object` — pulls `configuration` from the body, rejecting an absent field or a non-object value (400).
2. `extract_refinement_instruction_field` — reads `instruction`, falling back to the legacy `prompt`; requires a string (400).
3. `parse_refinement_instruction_into_non_empty_text` — validates the instruction as a `NonEmptyText` value object (400 on empty).
4. `serialize_existing_configuration_for_prompt` — pretty-prints the existing configuration into a JSON string for embedding (500 on serialization failure).
5. `build_configuration_refinement_prompt` — assembles the full instructional prompt (existing config + instruction + strict JSON-envelope directive) as a `NonEmptyText`.
6. `application_state.artificial_intelligence_adapter.generate_completion` — dispatches the prompt to the AI adapter and awaits the completion.
7. `map_refinement_completion_failure_to_http_error` — maps adapter/application errors to 403 / 404 / 500 as appropriate.
8. `extract_produced_refinement_text_from_completion` — takes ownership of the model's produced text.
9. `parse_refined_configuration_from_completion_text` — locates and parses the JSON envelope, returning the embedded `configuration` (or the whole object as a fallback); requires an object (500).
10. `locate_embedded_json_object` — finds the outermost balanced `{ ... }` region in arbitrary prose, tolerating surrounding text.
11. `extract_refinement_explanation_from_completion_text` — reads `explanation` from the envelope or returns the default message.
12. `extract_existing_layer_array` — reads the existing `layers` array (400 if absent/not an array).
13. `extract_refined_layer_array` — reads the refined `layers` array (500 if absent/not an array).
14. `read_layer_array_from_configuration` — shared helper backing the two layer-array readers.
15. `preserve_existing_layer_identifiers_onto_refined_layers` — restores each existing layer `id` onto the positionally-matching refined layer.
16. `ensure_refined_referenced_steps_remain_acyclic` — builds the dependency edge list and rejects cycles (500).
17. `detect_dependency_cycle` / `dependency_visit_detects_cycle` — DFS cycle detection over the `referencedSteps` edges.
18. `touch_refined_configuration_modified_timestamp` — inserts/overwrites `metadata.modified` with the current timestamp, creating `metadata` if absent.
19. `current_iso8601_timestamp` — supplies the timestamp string used above.
20. `assemble_refined_configuration_response_payload` — builds the final `{ explanation, agent }` response object.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Legacy `prompt` fallback**: if `instruction` is missing, the handler silently accepts `prompt` instead. If both are present, `instruction` takes precedence and `prompt` is ignored.
- **Model-error masking becomes 500**: any failure to locate JSON, parse JSON, or obtain a JSON-object configuration from the model surfaces as `500 upstream_application_failure`, not `400`. A malformed *model* response is treated as an upstream fault, not a client fault.
- **Identifier preservation is positional, not by name**: `id` values are copied index-by-index. If the model reorders layers, the wrong identifiers may be reattached. Refined layers *beyond* the existing count keep the model-generated `id`.
- **Cycle detection uses the preserved ids**: `ensure_refined_referenced_steps_remain_acyclic` runs *after* identifier restoration, so `referencedSteps` targets are matched against the restored `id`s. A self-reference (a layer listing its own id in `referencedSteps`) is treated as a cycle and rejected.
- **The timestamp is a hard-coded constant**: `current_iso8601_timestamp` returns the fixed string `"2026-07-07T00:00:00.000Z"` to keep the handler deterministic and free of wall-clock dependencies. Do not treat `metadata.modified` as a real clock reading in this build.
- **`metadata` is force-created / coerced**: if the refined configuration has no `metadata`, one is created; if `metadata` exists but is not an object, it is *replaced* wholesale with `{ "modified": ... }`, discarding any non-object value the model emitted there.
- **No persistence**: this endpoint does not write to any collection and opens no unit-of-work transaction. It is a pure request/response transform over the AI adapter; nothing is saved server-side.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Why did I get a 500 when my request body was clearly fine?**
A: Because the 500 is almost certainly about the *model's* output, not yours. If the AI adapter returned prose with no JSON, invalid JSON, or a non-object configuration, or if the refined layers contain a `referencedSteps` cycle, the handler emits `upstream_application_failure`. Your body passed validation; the completion did not.

**Q: Can I rename a layer's `id` through a refinement?**
A: No, not for any layer within the original count. The handler deliberately restores the existing `id` positionally after the model responds, precisely so refinement never silently renames a step. Only layers added beyond the existing count keep a fresh id.

**Q: Is this endpoint idempotent — can I safely retry it?**
A: It is safe to retry in that it persists nothing, but it is not idempotent: it calls a generative AI adapter, so two identical requests may yield different `agent` payloads and different `explanation` text. Do not assume replay produces the same configuration.

### `POST /api/ai-agents/share` — Share an AI Agent Configuration with a Recipient

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts an AI agent configuration payload together with a recipient email address, persists an immutable share record into the `ai_agent_exports` document collection, and enqueues a rendered plain-text notification email (written as a storage blob for an out-of-band mailer to deliver later). It mints an opaque, hard-to-guess access token, wraps that token into a public access link of the form `https://alma.app/shared-agents/<token>`, and returns the link plus the persisted share record identifier to the caller. In short: it is the "invite someone to view my agent" action, and it succeeds by creating exactly one durable share record and one queued email artifact per call.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a REST semantics standpoint, `POST /api/ai-agents/share` is a resource-creation operation and is therefore, quite deliberately, **neither safe nor idempotent**. Every successful invocation calls `generate_share_record_identifier()` and `generate_share_access_token()`, both of which are backed by freshly-minted `Uuid::new_v4()` values, so replaying the exact same request body will not converge on the same server state — it will instead materialize a second, entirely distinct share record with a second, entirely distinct access link. This is the intended contract: sharing is an append-only act of creation, not a declarative "make the world look like this" PUT. Clients that require at-most-once semantics must implement their own de-duplication (typically via an `x-request-id` correlation key) because the handler itself performs no such collapsing.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler is a thin **application/interface-layer orchestrator** that sits above the domain. The only genuine domain object it touches is the `Email` value object (`alma_domain::value_objects::Email`), whose `parse` constructor enforces the invariant that an email address is well-formed before it is ever allowed to travel deeper into the system. Everything else — the share record body, the notification email, the storage blob — is assembled from anonymous `serde_json::Value` structures at the HTTP boundary and pushed through the `document_collection` and `storage_adapter` ports. The handler never opens a transactional unit of work despite being generic over `UnitOfWork`; persistence is expressed purely through those two port calls, keeping the endpoint firmly in the "coordinate infrastructure" role rather than the "enforce business rules" role.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This endpoint is mounted behind the standard authorization pipeline: the handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, meaning the request must have already traversed the full type-state pipeline before this handler body ever executes.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 3f6c1e2a-8b4d-4c9a-9f10-2a7c5d1e0b33` | Client-supplied correlation identifier used for tracing/log stitching. Because this endpoint is non-idempotent, this header is the client's only lever for correlating retries; the handler does not de-duplicate on it. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: owner@example.com` | Identifies the authenticated principal. It becomes the `authorized_principal()`, which is normalized (trimmed + lowercased) into the `sharing_owner_account` and stamped on both the persisted share record body and the `StoredDocument.owning_account`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The request handle carried into this function is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That generic marker is the terminal stage of a compile-time-enforced progression:

1. **Validated** — the raw inbound request has been structurally validated (headers present and well-formed, body decodable). Only after this stage can the request advance.
2. **Authenticated** — the caller's identity has been established from the credential headers (the `x-account-email` principal). A request cannot become `Authenticated` unless it was first `Validated`.
3. **Authorized** — the authenticated principal has been checked against the policy governing this route, yielding `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. Only a value of this exact type can be handed to this handler.

Because the stage is encoded in the type system rather than checked with a runtime `if`, it is structurally impossible for this handler body to run against a request that has not passed all three stages — the code would not compile otherwise. Inside the body, `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` is the only piece of authentication state the handler reads, and it does so through the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`-typed handle.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint reads no path segments and no query-string parameters; all input arrives in the JSON request body.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as a free-form `serde_json::Value` and then reads specific fields by hand. The fields it actually inspects are:

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recipient_email` | string | Yes | Non-empty after trim; must parse as a valid `Email` value object | — | Destination address for the share. Trimmed, then validated via `Email::parse`. |
| `shared_configuration` | object | Yes | Must be a JSON object (not a string/array/scalar) | — | The AI agent configuration payload being shared. Stored verbatim (cloned) into the persisted share record. |
| `shared_configuration.display_name` | string | Yes | Non-empty after trim | — | Human-readable name of the shared agent, interpolated into the notification email subject line. |
| `note` | string | No | Read as string; non-string/absent yields empty | `""` (empty string) | Optional free-text personal note appended to the notification email when non-empty. |

Any additional keys inside `shared_configuration` (or the top-level body) are ignored by the handler's own logic, but the *entire* `shared_configuration` object is cloned verbatim into the persisted record, so extra nested keys are retained there.

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `recipient_email` missing/blank; `recipient_email` fails `Email::parse`; `shared_configuration` missing or not an object; `shared_configuration.display_name` missing/blank. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'recipient_email' field is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Pipeline stage before this handler: no authentication credentials (e.g. missing `x-account-email`) were supplied. Not raised inside this handler body. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Pipeline stage before this handler: supplied credentials could not be authenticated. Not raised inside this handler body. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Pipeline stage before this handler: the authenticated principal is not authorized for this route. Not raised inside this handler body. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not produced by this handler; documented for completeness of the shared `HttpError` enum. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested resource was not found"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | `document_collection.insert_document(...)` fails, OR `storage_adapter.persist_blob(...)` fails; both map through `map_share_persistence_failure_to_http_error`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"failed to persist the agent share notification: <cause>"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "the shared configuration requires a non-empty 'display_name'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates these real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_recipient_email_field(&submitted_body)` — reads, trims, and requires a non-empty `recipient_email` string; else 400.
2. `parse_recipient_email_into_email_value_object(raw)` — validates the string into an `Email` value object via `Email::parse`; else 400.
3. `extract_shared_configuration_object(&submitted_body)` — requires `shared_configuration` to be present and a JSON object; else 400.
4. `extract_shared_agent_display_name(config)` — reads, trims, and requires a non-empty `display_name` inside the configuration; else 400.
5. `extract_optional_share_note_message(&submitted_body)` — reads the optional `note`, trims it, defaults to empty string.
6. `resolve_sharing_owner_account_from_authorized_principal(principal)` — trims + lowercases the authorized principal; falls back to `"unknown-principal"` if blank.
7. `generate_share_record_identifier()` — mints `agent-share-<uuid-v4>`.
8. `generate_share_access_token()` — mints an opaque token from `Uuid::new_v4().simple()`.
9. `build_share_access_link_from_token(&token)` — formats `https://alma.app/shared-agents/<token>`.
10. `assemble_share_persistence_body(...)` — builds the JSON record: recipient, owner, token, cloned configuration, `share_status: "pending"`.
11. `assemble_stored_share_document(...)` — wraps that body into a `StoredDocument` with identifier + owning account.
12. `document_collection.insert_document(AI_AGENT_EXPORTS_COLLECTION_NAME, doc)` — persists into collection `"ai_agent_exports"`; failure → `map_share_persistence_failure_to_http_error` (500).
13. `build_share_notification_email_body(...)` — renders the plain-text email, appending the personal note only if non-empty.
14. `assemble_share_notification_storage_blob(...)` — builds a `StorageBlob` in folder `ai_agent_share_notifications`, filename `<sanitized-email>.eml`, using `sanitize_email_for_file_name`.
15. `storage_adapter.persist_blob(blob)` — persists the email blob; failure → `map_share_persistence_failure_to_http_error` (500).
16. `assemble_share_success_response_payload(...)` — builds the 200 JSON response with the link and record identifier.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Non-idempotent by construction.** Each call generates a brand-new UUID record identifier and access token; retrying the same body produces a second independent share record and a second email blob. There is no de-duplication on `x-request-id` or on `recipient_email`.
- **The email is not actually sent here.** The handler only writes a rendered `.eml` blob into the `ai_agent_share_notifications` storage folder. Delivery is delegated to an out-of-band mailer; a `200` means "queued", not "delivered". The response `message` says exactly `"Share notification queued"`.
- **Filename collisions in the blob store.** The blob name is `<sanitized-email>.eml` with no uniqueness suffix. Sharing to the same recipient twice writes to the same declared name — depending on the storage adapter's semantics this may overwrite the previous notification blob even though a distinct share *record* was created.
- **Email sanitization is lossy and can collide.** `sanitize_email_for_file_name` replaces every non-alphanumeric character except `.`, `-`, `_` with `_`. So `a+b@x.com` and `a-b@x.com` do not collide, but `a+b@x.com` becomes `a_b_x.com` — different raw addresses can sanitize to identical filenames.
- **The whole `shared_configuration` object is cloned and stored.** Only `display_name` is validated, but every other key (including potentially large or sensitive nested data) is persisted verbatim into the `ai_agent_exports` collection. There is no size cap or field allow-list.
- **`note` is silently coerced.** If `note` is present but not a string (e.g. a number or object), `and_then(as_str)` yields `None` and it defaults to empty — no error is raised, the note is simply dropped.
- **Blank authorized principal is tolerated.** If the authorized principal is empty/whitespace, the record's `sharing_owner_account` becomes the literal `"unknown-principal"` rather than failing — a `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` handle with an empty principal will still persist a record.
- **No transaction despite `UnitOfWork` generics.** The two persistence steps (document insert, then blob persist) are independent awaited calls. If the document insert succeeds but the blob persist fails, you get a `500` with a share record already committed and no corresponding email blob — a partial-write window.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I call this twice with the same body to make sure the share "goes through"?**
A: You can, but you will create two separate share records with two separate access links, and (per the filename gotcha) the second email blob may clobber the first. If you need retry safety, dedupe on your side.

**Q: Does the recipient need an account, and is their address checked against anything?**
A: The address is only checked for syntactic validity via `Email::parse`. There is no lookup of whether the recipient exists as a user; any well-formed email is accepted.

**Q: The response returned `200` and `"Share notification queued"` — why did my recipient never get an email?**
A: This endpoint's job ends at writing the `.eml` blob to storage. Actual delivery is an out-of-band mailer's responsibility. A `200` guarantees the record was persisted and the blob was written, nothing about SMTP.

### `POST /api/ai-agents/verify-bibliography` — Verify AI Agent Bibliography Entries

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts a batch of client-declared bibliography entries and, for each one, attempts to prove that the referenced material can actually be located — either as a stored blob living behind the storage adapter (google-drive / storage / blob / s3 scheme), or as a real publication discoverable through the literature adapter. Every entry is independently classified by the shape of its declared path, checked against the appropriate backend, and folded into a per-entry verification result. The handler then summarises the whole batch, reporting how many entries were located, how many went missing, and whether the bibliography as a whole passed verification.

#### Theory & Rationale

At first glance one might reflexively file a "verify" operation under `GET`, because it is conceptually read-only: it mutates no server-side state, persists nothing, and creates no resource. The endpoint is, in the strict HTTP taxonomy, *safe* in effect. It is nonetheless modelled as a `POST`, and deliberately so. The verification input is an unbounded, structurally rich array of entry objects whose cardinality and nesting make it wholly unsuitable for a query string; a request body is the only honest transport. Moreover, the operation is emphatically **not idempotent in the guarantees it offers**: because verification consults live external backends (a storage adapter and a literature-search adapter whose corpus drifts over time), two identical requests submitted minutes apart may legitimately return different `found` verdicts as blobs are deleted or publications are indexed. `POST` is the correct verb precisely because it promises neither safety-as-contract nor idempotency-as-contract to the caller, even though the server itself writes nothing.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler sits squarely at the *application boundary* — the thin, orchestration-only layer of the hexagon. It owns no domain invariants of its own beyond the modest one that a name must be `NonEmptyText`; instead it composes two outbound ports (the `storage` port via `application_state.storage_adapter` and the `literature` port via `application_state.literature_adapter`) into a single coordinated read. The handler is intentionally a *coordinator, not a decision-maker*: the domain contributes value-object validation (`NonEmptyText::parse`), the ports contribute existence facts, and the handler merely reconciles those facts into a batch verdict. This keeps the transport layer ignorant of *how* a blob is fetched or *how* publications are searched, which is exactly the separation the type-state pipeline (below) is designed to preserve.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 3f2a9c14-7b8e-4d2a-9f1c-2e6b0d5a71cc` | Correlation identifier consumed during the **Validated** stage of the pipeline; echoed through logs and error surfaces so a single request can be traced across the storage and literature adapters. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@university.edu` | Identifies the calling account; consumed during the **Authenticated** stage to establish *who* is asking, and subsequently during the **Authorized** stage to establish *whether they may*. |

The handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. This is not decoration — it is a compile-time proof obligation enforced by Rust's type system, and it encodes a three-stage type-state pipeline that every request must traverse before this function body can even begin to execute:

- **Validated** — The raw inbound request has been structurally validated: mandatory headers such as `x-request-id` are present and well-formed. A request that fails here never reaches the handler; it is rejected upstream as a malformed request.
- **Authenticated** — Building on the `Validated` proof, the pipeline resolves `x-account-email` into a known, authenticated principal. Absence or invalidity of credentials terminates the request here with a `401` (`AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` / `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`); the handler is never invoked.
- **Authorized** — Building on the `Authenticated` proof, the pipeline confirms the authenticated principal is *permitted* to perform this operation. Only once this final proof is minted does the type `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` exist, and only a value of that exact type can be supplied as the `_authorized_request` argument. Because Rust will not construct that type by any other route, it is *structurally impossible* for this handler body to run against a request that has not been Validated → Authenticated → Authorized, in that order. The underscore prefix on `_authorized_request` signals that the handler consumes the *proof* but reads no further data from it.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The endpoint takes no path segments beyond the fixed route and reads no query-string parameters whatsoever. Every piece of caller-supplied data arrives in the request body.

#### Request Body

The body is deserialized as an untyped `serde_json::Value`, so the handler is deliberately permissive at the envelope level and strict at the field level. The top-level payload may be **either** a bare JSON array of entry objects, **or** a JSON object carrying the array under one of the keys `bibliography`, `entries`, or `references` (checked in that order). Each element of the array is an entry object. The handler reads exactly two logical fields per entry, each under several accepted key spellings.

**Top-level envelope fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (root as array) | `array<object>` | Conditional | Must contain ≥1 entry | — | If the body is a bare array, it is used directly as the entry array. |
| `bibliography` | `array<object>` | Conditional | Must be an array if present; ≥1 entry | — | First-choice named holder of the entry array. |
| `entries` | `array<object>` | Conditional | Must be an array if present; ≥1 entry | — | Second-choice alias for the entry array. |
| `references` | `array<object>` | Conditional | Must be an array if present; ≥1 entry | — | Third-choice alias for the entry array. |

At least one of {bare array, `bibliography`, `entries`, `references`} must resolve to an array, and that array must be non-empty.

**Per-entry object fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` / `filePath` / `file_path` / `url` / `reference` | `string` | Yes | Non-empty after trimming; first matching key wins (in listed order) | — | The declared location of the reference. Classified into `gdrive`, `storage`, `external`, `doi`, or `citation` by its scheme/shape. |
| `name` / `title` / `fileName` / `file_name` / `label` | `string` | Yes | Non-empty after trimming; first matching key wins (in listed order) | — | The human-readable title of the reference. Used verbatim as the literature-search query for non-storage entries and echoed into every result. |

**Rust struct mirror**

The handler itself reads a raw `serde_json::Value`; the following is a *documentation-only* mirror of the shape it expects, not the actual deserialization target.

```rust
/// Documentation mirror only — the handler deserializes `serde_json::Value`.
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
enum VerifyBibliographyRequest {
    Bare(Vec<BibliographyEntry>),
    Wrapped(BibliographyEntryEnvelope),
}

#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct BibliographyEntryEnvelope {
    bibliography: Option<Vec<BibliographyEntry>>,
    entries: Option<Vec<BibliographyEntry>>,
    references: Option<Vec<BibliographyEntry>>,
}

#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct BibliographyEntry {
    // path candidates, tried in order: path, filePath, file_path, url, reference
    path: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "filePath")]
    file_path_camel: Option<String>,
    file_path: Option<String>,
    url: Option<String>,
    reference: Option<String>,
    // name candidates, tried in order: name, title, fileName, file_name, label
    name: Option<String>,
    title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "fileName")]
    file_name_camel: Option<String>,
    file_name: Option<String>,
    label: Option<String>,
}
```

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK`, body `application/json`. The top-level object carries the batch verdict plus a `results` array of per-entry verification objects.

**Response field table**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `found` | `boolean` | Overall batch verdict — `true` iff `missingEntries == 0`. Note: this key is reused, confusingly, as the batch-level all-located flag. |
| `totalEntries` | `integer` | Total entries verified (`locatedEntries + missingEntries`). |
| `locatedEntries` | `integer` | Count of entries whose `found` was `true`. |
| `missingEntries` | `integer` | Count of entries whose `found` was `false`. |
| `message` | `string` | `"all bibliography entries were verified"` or `"some bibliography entries could not be verified"`. |
| `results` | `array<object>` | One object per input entry, in input order. |
| `results[].name` | `string` | The declared name of the entry, echoed back. |
| `results[].pathType` | `string` | One of `gdrive`, `storage`, `external`, `doi`, `citation`. |
| `results[].found` | `boolean` | Whether *this* entry was located. |
| `results[].webViewLink` | `string \| null` | A viewable link when located (google-drive `view` URL, DOI URL, or the echoed path); `null` when not located. |
| `results[].message` | `string` | `"entry was successfully located"` or `"entry could not be located"`. |

```json
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The table below enumerates every `HttpError` variant and precisely when *this* endpoint emits it.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Body is neither a bare array nor an object with an array under `bibliography`/`entries`/`references`; a named field is present but not an array; the entry array is empty; an entry lacks a non-empty path key; an entry lacks a non-empty name key; a name fails `NonEmptyText::parse`; or the literature lookup surfaces `DomainInvariantViolated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the bibliography must contain at least one entry"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Raised upstream in the pipeline before the handler runs when `x-account-email` credentials are absent. The handler body never executes. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Raised upstream when supplied credentials cannot be authenticated. The handler body never executes. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| `403` | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Raised upstream when the authenticated principal is not authorized for this route; also mapped from the literature adapter's `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` during a per-entry lookup. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| `404` | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Mapped from `ApplicationError::RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` / `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` when a literature lookup (not a storage fetch — see gotchas) fails with a not-found. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| `500` | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from the storage fetch or literature search — e.g. `StorageAdapterFailure`, `LiteratureAdapterFailure` — is mapped here. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"the storage adapter failed: connection reset"}` |

**Full SerializedErrorBody example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "each bibliography entry must declare a non-empty 'path'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_bibliography_entry_array` — Pulls the entry array out of the body, accepting a bare array or the `bibliography`/`entries`/`references` keys; errors `400` on mismatch.
2. `ensure_bibliography_entry_array_is_not_empty` — Rejects an empty batch with a `400`.
3. `extract_entry_declared_path` (per entry) — Reads the first non-empty path among `path`/`filePath`/`file_path`/`url`/`reference`.
4. `extract_entry_declared_name` (per entry) — Reads the first non-empty name among `name`/`title`/`fileName`/`file_name`/`label`.
5. `classify_bibliography_entry_path_type` (per entry) — Classifies the path into `gdrive`, `storage`, `external`, `doi`, or `citation` by scheme/shape.
6. `build_storage_object_identifier_from_entry_path` (storage/gdrive entries) — Strips a recognised scheme prefix into an opaque `StorageObjectIdentifier`.
7. `application_state.storage_adapter.fetch_blob` (storage/gdrive entries) — Attempts to fetch the blob via the storage port.
8. `interpret_storage_fetch_result_as_existence` — Maps `Ok`→located, not-found→missing, any other error→`500`.
9. `build_web_view_link_for_located_entry` (located storage/gdrive entries) — Produces a canonical google-drive `view` URL or echoes the path.
10. `parse_entry_declared_name_into_non_empty_text` (non-storage entries) — Validates the name into `NonEmptyText`; `400` on failure.
11. `build_literature_lookup_expression_from_entry_name` — Reuses the validated name verbatim as the search expression.
12. `application_state.literature_adapter.search_publications` — Searches publications via the literature port.
13. `map_verification_lookup_failure_to_http_error` — Maps literature/storage `ApplicationError`s onto `404`/`403`/`400`/`500`.
14. `select_best_matching_publication_summary` — Chooses exact title match, else substring overlap, else none; builds a `https://doi.org/...` link when a DOI exists.
15. `assemble_single_entry_verification_result` — Builds the per-entry `{name, pathType, found, webViewLink, message}` object.
16. `summarize_bibliography_verification_outcomes` — Counts located vs. missing across the batch.
17. `assemble_bibliography_verification_response_payload` — Assembles the final `{found, totalEntries, locatedEntries, missingEntries, results, message}` payload.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`found` is overloaded.** The batch-level `found` means "were *all* entries located" (`missingEntries == 0`), while each `results[].found` means "was *this one* located." Do not conflate them; a batch `found: false` is entirely normal and non-fatal.
- **Storage not-found is a soft miss; literature not-found is a hard error.** A storage/gdrive blob that returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` yields `found: false` for that entry (via `interpret_storage_fetch_result_as_existence`). But the *same* `ApplicationError` arising from the literature search path is mapped by `map_verification_lookup_failure_to_http_error` into a `404` that aborts the entire request. The asymmetry is intentional but surprising.
- **One bad entry can sink the whole batch.** Verification is sequential and fail-fast: a `400` (missing path/name, invalid `NonEmptyText`) or a `500` (adapter failure) on entry N aborts the loop and discards the successful results of entries 0..N. There is no partial-success response.
- **Path type, not path validity, drives routing.** `classify_bibliography_entry_path_type` only inspects prefixes/substrings. A `doi:`- or `10.`-prefixed path and a plain `citation` string both fall into the `_ =>` (literature-search) branch — the `doi`/`citation`/`external` classifications are all treated identically for lookup purposes; only `storage`/`gdrive` hit the storage adapter.
- **Matching is lenient and order-sensitive.** `select_best_matching_publication_summary` returns the first exact case-insensitive title match; failing that, the *first* candidate whose title contains the needle *or* whose title is contained by the needle. A short declared name (e.g. "AI") can spuriously substring-match an unrelated publication, and a located literature entry with no DOI yields `webViewLink: null` even though `found` is `true`.
- **webViewLink for non-gdrive storage just echoes the input.** `build_web_view_link_for_located_entry` only rewrites `gdrive:`-prefixed (or drive/docs URL) paths; a located `storage:blob-9` entry returns the literal `"storage:blob-9"` as its link, which is not a browser-clickable URL.
- **Unknown keys are silently ignored.** The body is parsed as `serde_json::Value`, so misspelled keys (e.g. `"paths"`, `"names"`) do not error at deserialization — they simply fail the per-entry non-empty checks and surface as a `400` about a missing `path`/`name`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I send a bare JSON array as the body instead of wrapping it in `{ "bibliography": [...] }`?**
A: Yes. `extract_bibliography_entry_array` checks for a bare array first, then `bibliography`, `entries`, `references` in that order. Pick whichever offends you least.

**Q: If one entry is unverifiable, do I still get the results for the others?**
A: No. A malformed entry or an adapter failure aborts the batch mid-loop with an error status; you get an error body, not a partial `results` array. Verification is all-or-nothing at the transport level even though each entry's `found` verdict is individual.

**Q: My entry came back `found: true` but `webViewLink` is `null`. Is that a bug?**
A: No. A publication located via the literature adapter that carries no DOI has no link to offer, so the field is `null` by design. Likewise a non-gdrive storage path echoes a non-clickable reference. "Located" and "linkable" are independent properties here.

### `GET /api/medium-articles` — List Medium Articles (Literature Feed Projection)

This endpoint retrieves a collection of Medium article entries synthesized from the application's literature adapter, projecting each underlying `PublicationSummary` into a compact, RSS-flavored JSON object suitable for direct consumption by a front-end feed widget. It accepts two optional query parameters (`source` and `limit`), falls back to a hard-coded default publication handle when no source is supplied, and returns a top-level JSON array sorted by publication date in descending order (most recent first). The endpoint is read-only, side-effect-free, and always returns a JSON array — never a wrapping object — including the empty array `[]` when the upstream feed yields no publications.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a REST-semantic standpoint this endpoint is a textbook *collection resource read*. It is bound to the `GET` verb precisely because it is both **safe** (invoking it does not mutate any server-side state; no domain aggregate is created, updated, or deleted) and **idempotent** (invoking it N times in succession produces the same observable server state as invoking it once — modulo the fact that the *upstream* Medium feed is itself a living, changing resource, which is a property of the world and not of this handler). Because the operation is safe, its inputs are legitimately expressed as query-string parameters rather than a request body: `GET` requests conventionally carry no semantically significant body, and this handler honors that convention by reading exclusively from the query string. The response is a *representation* of a filtered, sorted, truncated projection of the literature port's output, and the client is free to cache it subject to the usual freshness caveats of an aggregated third-party feed.

In Domain-Driven Design terms this handler sits squarely in the **application/interface layer** of the `literature` bounded context. It performs no domain reasoning of its own: the actual act of "searching publications" is delegated across a port (`LiteraturePort::search_publications`) to whatever adapter is wired into `ApplicationState::literature_adapter`, keeping the domain ignorant of Medium, RSS, HTTP, and JSON entirely. The handler's job is strictly *presentation and orchestration* — parse and validate transport-level inputs, invoke the port, and map the returned `PublicationSummary` value objects into a transport-shaped DTO array. This is a deliberate anti-corruption seam: the JSON shape emitted here (`title`/`link`/`pubDate`/`description`/`guid`) is an interface-layer concern that mimics the well-known RSS-item vocabulary, and it is intentionally decoupled from the internal `PublicationSummary` field names (`publication_title`/`digital_object_identifier`/`originating_source`), so that the internal model may evolve without breaking the wire contract.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This endpoint is guarded by the standard alma-http type-state request pipeline. The handler's signature accepts an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which means the framework will only ever construct and dispatch to this handler *after* the request has been driven all the way through validation, authentication, and authorization. If any of those stages fail, the handler body never executes and the corresponding `HttpError` is returned before your code is reached.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7f3c1e2a-9b44-4d21-9f0e-1a2b3c4d5e6f` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces for this request. If omitted, the pipeline may synthesize one; supplying your own makes end-to-end tracing across the client/server boundary tractable. |
| `x-account-email` | Required | `x-account-email: francesco@example.com` | Identifies the calling principal. This is the credential the authentication stage consumes to establish identity; without it the request cannot advance past `RequestHasBeenValidated` into `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`, and authentication fails. |

**The type-state pipeline (Validated → Authenticated → Authorized).** alma-http encodes each request-processing milestone as a distinct *type* using the type-state pattern, so that an entire class of ordering bugs is made unrepresentable at compile time:

1. **`RequestHasBeenValidated`** — The inbound request's transport-level shape has been checked (well-formed headers, parseable query string, a body that parses if one is expected). A request that fails validation yields `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` and never becomes a validated value.
2. **`RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`** — Starting from a *validated* request, the pipeline consumes the identity headers (notably `x-account-email`) and establishes *who* the caller is. A missing credential yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; a present-but-bogus credential yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Authentication is only reachable from a validated request — you cannot authenticate an unvalidated one because the type does not exist yet.
3. **`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`** — Starting from an *authenticated* request, the pipeline decides whether that established identity is permitted to perform *this* operation. Denial yields `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. This is the exact type the `list_medium_articles_handler` demands as an extractor, so by the time the handler runs, all three guarantees hold simultaneously and irrevocably.

Because each stage consumes the previous stage's *type* and produces the next, it is impossible to write a handler that runs on an unauthenticated or unauthorized request — the code simply would not compile.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | query | string | No | Trimmed; must be non-empty *after trimming* to be used, and must parse as a `NonEmptyText`. Blank/whitespace-only values are ignored (default applied). | `@francesco.cozzolino` | The Medium feed source / publication handle passed to the literature adapter's `search_publications`. If absent, whitespace-only, or empty after trimming, the default publication handle is substituted. A value that fails `NonEmptyText::parse` yields `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. |
| `limit` | query | integer (`usize`) | No | Must parse as a non-negative integer if present and non-blank. Value `0` is coerced to the default. Values above `50` are clamped to `50`. | `10` | The maximum number of article entries to return. Absent or blank → `10`. Zero → `10`. Anything above the supported ceiling of `50` → `50`. A non-integer/negative value yields `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. |

There are **no path parameters** for this endpoint.

#### Request Body

**This endpoint reads no request body.** It is a `GET` handler and consumes its inputs exclusively from the query string (`HashMap<String, String>` via `Query`). Any body supplied by the client is ignored by this handler. The (empty) body contract is therefore:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "ListMediumArticlesRequestBody",
  "description": "This endpoint accepts no request body; any body is ignored.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

```typescript
// No request body is read by this endpoint. Inputs are query parameters only.
export interface ListMediumArticlesRequestBody {
  // intentionally empty — GET carries no meaningful body here
}
```

```rust

//   Query(query_parameters): Query<std::collections::HashMap<String, String>>
// Represented for completeness as an empty struct:
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct ListMediumArticlesRequestBody;
```

#### Successful Response

**Status:** `200 OK`. **Body:** a top-level JSON **array** of article entry objects (never a wrapping object). The array is sorted by `pubDate` descending and truncated to the effective limit. When the upstream feed is empty, the body is the empty array `[]`.

Each array element has the following fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | The publication title, copied verbatim from `PublicationSummary.publication_title`. |
| `link` | string | Permalink. If a DOI is present and already an `http(s)` URL, it is used directly; a bare DOI becomes `https://doi.org/<doi>`; otherwise a canonical Medium URL is synthesized as `https://medium.com/<default-handle>/<title-slug>`. |
| `pubDate` | string | ISO-8601 timestamp. If the originating source already looks ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DDT...`) it is passed through trimmed; otherwise the placeholder `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` is emitted. |
| `description` | string | The originating source text, trimmed and truncated to at most 240 characters (character-counted, not byte-counted), with a trailing `…` when truncated. |
| `guid` | string | Stable identifier. `medium-<doi>` when a non-empty DOI exists; otherwise `medium-<title-slug>-<ordinal>`, or `medium-<ordinal>` when the title slug is empty. |

```json
    "properties": {
      "title": { "type": "string" },
      "link": { "type": "string" },
      "pubDate": { "type": "string" },
      "description": { "type": "string" },
      "guid": { "type": "string" }
    },
    "required": ["title", "link", "pubDate", "description", "guid"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` object with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | The `source` value fails `NonEmptyText::parse`, **or** the `limit` value is present, non-blank, and not a parseable non-negative integer. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'limit' query parameter must be a non-negative integer: invalid digit found in string"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Raised by the pipeline before the handler runs when no identity credential (e.g. `x-account-email`) is supplied. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Raised by the pipeline before the handler runs when the supplied credential cannot be authenticated. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| `403` | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal is not permitted to call this endpoint (pipeline stage), **or** the literature port returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` (mapped to "access to the requested Medium feed was denied"). | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"access to the requested Medium feed was denied"}` |
| `404` | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | The literature port returns `ApplicationError::RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`, i.e. the requested Medium feed could not be located. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested Medium feed could not be located"}` |
| `500` | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other `ApplicationError` returned by the literature adapter (e.g. `LiteratureAdapterFailure`) is mapped to this catch-all upstream failure. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"the literature adapter failed: boom"}` |

A full example `SerializedErrorBody`:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "the requested Medium feed could not be located"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

Once the type-state pipeline has produced a `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, the handler body executes the following real helper functions in order:

1. **`parse_medium_feed_source_url_from_query_parameters`** — Reads `source`, trims it, drops it if empty, otherwise falls back to the default handle, then validates via `NonEmptyText::parse` (400 on failure).
2. **`resolve_default_medium_publication_handle`** — Returns the constant default handle `@francesco.cozzolino` used when no source is supplied.
3. **`parse_maximum_medium_article_count_from_query_parameters`** — Reads `limit`; absent/blank → default `10`; otherwise parses as `usize` (400 on malformed input).
4. **`clamp_requested_medium_article_count_to_supported_ceiling`** — Coerces `0` to the default `10` and caps any value at the ceiling of `50`, producing the effective count.
5. **`application_state.literature_adapter.search_publications(&feed_source)`** — Awaited port call that fetches the raw `Vec<PublicationSummary>` from the literature adapter.
6. **`map_literature_port_failure_into_medium_http_error`** — On adapter error, maps `ApplicationError` variants into the appropriate `HttpError` (404 / 403 / 500).
7. **`render_empty_medium_article_response_array`** — Short-circuits and returns `[]` when the port yields no publications.
8. **`map_publication_summaries_into_medium_article_entries`** — Maps each summary (with its ordinal index) into a JSON entry, internally invoking the GUID, permalink, description, and date helpers.
9. **`derive_medium_article_guid_from_publication_summary`** — Computes the stable `guid` (DOI-preferred, else title-slug-plus-ordinal, else ordinal).
10. **`slugify_title_for_guid`** — Produces a lowercase dash-separated ASCII slug from a title, used by both GUID and permalink synthesis.
11. **`build_medium_article_permalink_from_publication_summary`** — Computes the `link` (direct http(s) DOI, `doi.org`-wrapped bare DOI, or synthesized Medium URL).
12. **`truncate_medium_article_description_to_preview_length`** — Trims and character-truncates the description to 240 chars, appending `…` on truncation.
13. **`format_medium_publication_date_as_iso_8601`** / **`looks_like_iso_8601_timestamp`** — Normalizes the source instant into ISO-8601 or the epoch placeholder, using the heuristic timestamp check.
14. **`assemble_medium_article_entry_object`** — Builds the per-entry `{title, link, pubDate, description, guid}` JSON object.
15. **`sort_medium_article_entries_by_publication_date_descending`** — Sorts entries in place by `pubDate` descending (missing/empty dates sort last).
16. **`take_first_n_medium_article_entries`** — Retains only the first `effective_count` entries.
17. **`wrap_medium_article_entries_into_response_array`** — Wraps the retained entries into the top-level JSON array returned to the client.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **The `limit` value `0` is NOT "return nothing" — it is silently rewritten to the default `10`.** `clamp_requested_medium_article_count_to_supported_ceiling` explicitly maps `0` to the default. If you want an empty list, you cannot get it via `limit=0`.
- **The hard ceiling of `50` is applied AFTER parsing and is silent.** `limit=1000000` does not error; it returns at most `50` entries. Clients must not assume they received exactly what they asked for.
- **`pubDate` sorting is a lexicographic string comparison, not a chronological one.** This works only because ISO-8601 timestamps sort lexically the same as chronologically. Non-ISO source values are replaced with the `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` epoch placeholder, so all such entries collapse to the same key and sink to the bottom of the list.
- **`limit` is validated but `source` misuse is largely tolerated.** A blank or whitespace-only `source` is not an error — it silently falls back to the default handle. Only a value that survives trimming yet fails `NonEmptyText::parse` produces a 400. In practice most non-empty strings parse fine.
- **A malformed query parameter returns `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` even though there is no request body.** This is a reused error variant; the `error_explanation` clarifies it refers to the `limit` (or `source`) query parameter, not an actual body.
- **Truncation counts characters, not bytes.** The 240-char limit uses `chars().count()` / `chars().take(240)`, so multibyte (non-ASCII) descriptions are truncated safely on character boundaries and will never split a UTF-8 sequence.
- **An empty upstream feed returns `200` with `[]`, never `404`.** Absence of articles is a successful empty result; `404` is reserved for the port explicitly reporting the *feed itself* could not be located.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I POST to this endpoint with a JSON body of options instead of using query params?**
A: No. The route is registered as `get(...)` and the handler reads only the query string. A `POST` will not match the route, and a body on the `GET` is ignored. Use `?source=...&limit=...`.

**Q: Why did I ask for `limit=200` and only get 50 articles back? Is this a bug?**
A: It is working exactly as designed. Any requested count above `50` is silently clamped to the ceiling of `50`. There is no error, no header, and no field telling you clamping occurred. Ask for `50` or fewer if you want predictability.

**Q: Some of my articles have a `pubDate` of `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` — did I break time?**
A: No. That is the deterministic epoch placeholder emitted whenever the originating source string does not resemble an ISO-8601 timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDT...`). Those entries sort to the very end of the descending-by-date list, which is intentional.

### `GET /api/rss-updates` — List Syndication (RSS) Publication Updates

#### Synopsis

This endpoint retrieves a collection of publication "updates" from a configured RSS feed source, normalizes each located publication summary into a frontend-consumable RSS-update entry, optionally filters those entries by category, sorts them by publication date in descending (most-recent-first) order, and returns them wrapped in a standardized success envelope. It is a read-only, side-effect-free query handler mounted on the literature router. Despite exposing conceptual `source` and `category` knobs in its internal helper functions, the currently mounted route registers **no** query-string extractor, so at present every invocation operates against the default feed source with no category filter applied.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the grammar of Hypertext Transfer Protocol semantics, `GET` is the archetypal *safe* and *idempotent* verb: it is a pure interrogation of server state that promises to induce no observable mutation and to yield the same conceptual result no matter how many times the client, in its anxious repetition, elects to ask. This handler honors that covenant faithfully — it opens no unit of work, commits no transaction, writes to no store, and mutates nothing beyond an in-memory `Vec<Value>` that lives and dies entirely within the span of a single request. Because it is safe, intermediaries are free to cache it, prefetchers are free to speculatively fetch it, and clients are free to retry it after a timeout without the dread of double-submission that haunts the `POST`-shaped corners of this same literature category.

Within the Domain-Driven Design stratification of the `alma-http` crate, this handler is a thin member of the interface-adapter ring. Its sole responsibilities are transport-layer concerns: extracting (nominal) query parameters, delegating the genuine work of publication retrieval to `application_state.literature_adapter` (a *port* into the application layer), and translating the two vocabularies — the application's `ApplicationError` enumeration and the transport's `HttpError` enumeration — across the boundary between them. It contains no business rules that belong to the domain; the shaping of publication summaries into RSS entries is presentation logic, deliberately isolated in a battery of small, pure, individually testable helper functions so the impure I/O edge stays vanishingly thin. This is DDD placement by discipline: the handler knows *how to speak HTTP*, the adapter knows *how to fetch literature*, and neither is permitted to learn the other's job.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

The handler's signature accepts `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. The presence of the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` type-state parameter is load-bearing: it is a compile-time proof, threaded through Rust's type system, that by the time the handler body executes the incoming request has already traversed the full authentication and authorization pipeline. If any earlier stage failed, the handler body is never entered.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 3f1c9a2e-8b7d-4e5f-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b` | Correlation identifier used to trace this request across the pipeline stages and downstream logs. Consumed while constructing/validating the `HttpRequestInPipeline`. Echoed in structured logs for observability. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: francesco@example.com` | Identifies the calling principal. This is the identity that the pipeline authenticates and against which authorization for reading RSS updates is decided. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** This handler participates in a compile-time-enforced request lifecycle expressed as a progression of marker type-states on `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`:

1. **Validated** — The raw inbound request is first parsed and structurally validated. Required transport headers (notably `x-request-id` and `x-account-email`) are checked for presence and well-formedness. A request that survives this stage carries proof that its envelope is coherent. A failure here surfaces as `RequestBodyWasMalformed` (or a missing-credential error, depending on what was absent).
2. **Authenticated** — The validated request's `x-account-email` principal is resolved and verified. Success advances the type-state to the authenticated marker; failure yields `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` (no credentials supplied) or `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` (credentials supplied but rejected).
3. **Authorized** — The authenticated principal is checked against the policy governing this resource. Only upon success is the type-state promoted to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, which is exactly the type this handler demands in its signature. Failure yields `AuthorizationWasDenied`.

Because the handler requires `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` by type, the Rust compiler makes it *impossible* to route an un-authorized request into this function body. The parameter is bound as `_authorized_request` — the proof is required to exist, but the handler needs none of its fields to do its work.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

> Explanatory note (grounded in source): The handler contains helper functions — `parse_rss_feed_source_url_from_query_parameters` and `parse_requested_rss_category_filter_from_query_parameters` — that *would* read `source` and `category` query parameters. However, the mounted route in `routes.rs` registers `get(list_rss_updates_handler::<…>)` with **no** `Query` extractor, and the handler body explicitly constructs `let query_parameters: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();`. Consequently, no query parameters are ever populated at runtime; `source` always resolves to its default and `category` is always absent. The (currently inert) parameters that the helpers understand are documented below for completeness only.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | (query, not wired) | string | No | Trimmed; blank/whitespace-only treated as absent; must parse as `NonEmptyText` | `https://frankcozzolino.github.io/rss.xml` | RSS feed source URL passed to the literature port. **Not readable at runtime** — no `Query` extractor is registered. |
| `category` | (query, not wired) | string | No | Trimmed and lowercased; blank/whitespace-only treated as no filter | none (no filter) | Case-insensitive category filter applied to entry `categories` arrays. **Not readable at runtime**. |

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` endpoint and reads **no request body**. The handler function takes only `State(...)` and the authorized pipeline request; it declares no `Json<...>` or other body extractor. Any body sent by a client is ignored.

```json
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "This GET endpoint accepts no request body."
}
```

#### Successful Response

**HTTP status:** `200 OK`. The body is always a JSON object — the success envelope. It has one of two shapes: the populated envelope (`wrap_rss_update_entries_into_success_envelope`) or the empty envelope (`render_empty_rss_updates_success_envelope`). Both share the same top-level keys.

Top-level envelope fields:

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `success` | boolean | Yes | Always `true` for a `200`. Literal `true`. |
| `count` | integer | Yes | Number of entries in `articles` (`articles.len()`). `0` for the empty envelope. |
| `articles` | array of RSS-update entry objects | Yes | The list of normalized RSS entries. Empty array when no publications matched. |

Per-entry object fields (from `assemble_rss_update_entry_object`):

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Yes | Stable identifier. `rss-<sanitized-doi>` when a DOI exists (non-alphanumeric chars → `-`, lowercased); otherwise `rss-<ordinal>` (1-based positional index). |
| `title` | string | Yes | The publication title (`publication_summary.publication_title`). |
| `description` | string | Yes | Currently identical to `title` — the handler passes the title as both title and description. |
| `link` | string | Yes | `https://doi.org/<doi>` when a DOI is present, else the default feed source URL `https://frankcozzolino.github.io/rss.xml`. |
| `pubDate` | string | Yes | ISO-8601 timestamp. Preserved from `originating_source` if it structurally resembles ISO-8601; otherwise the sentinel `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`. |
| `author` | string | Yes | Constant `"Francesco Cozzolino"` (`resolve_default_rss_update_author_name`). |
| `categories` | array of strings | Yes | Lowercased, trimmed, non-empty labels split from `originating_source` on `,`, `;`, or `\|`. |
| `imageUrl` | string | **Conditional** | Present only when a non-empty DOI exists: `https://frankcozzolino.github.io/images/<doi>.png`. Key is entirely omitted otherwise. |
