### `GET /api/pubmed/doi` — Search PubMed Literature by Digital Object Identifier

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts a single Digital Object Identifier (DOI) as a query-string parameter, normalizes and syntactically validates it, delegates a search to the configured literature adapter, and then rigorously filters the returned publication summaries down to only those whose DOI *exactly* matches the requested identifier (after normalization). The surviving summaries are rendered into a PubMed-shaped envelope of match entries, each carrying a title, a synthesized abstract descriptor, a synthesized body descriptor, a derived permalink, a (best-effort) author list, and the DOI itself. If nothing matches, a canonical empty-results envelope is returned with `totalCount: 0` — the request is still considered a success.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of REST, this is the canonical safe, idempotent form of resource interaction: a `GET` against a collection-shaped resource (`/api/pubmed/doi`), parameterized by a query string, returning a representation of the subset of literature identified by the supplied DOI. Because it is a `GET`, it is by contract both **safe** (it MUST NOT mutate observable server state) and **idempotent** (issuing the identical request N times yields the identical observable outcome as issuing it once). No transaction is committed, no row is written, no side effect is emitted; the handler merely reads from the literature adapter and folds the result into a presentation envelope. The DOI, notably, is carried in the query string rather than the path, which is a deliberate concession to the fact that DOIs contain forward slashes (`10.1038/s41586-...`) that would otherwise fracture path routing — a query parameter sidesteps the segment-splitting semantics of a URL path entirely.

From a Domain-Driven Design perspective, this handler is a thin *interface-layer* orchestrator that owns none of the domain logic it appears to wield. It sits squarely in the HTTP category (`literature`) and its job is translation: it lifts a raw, untrusted `String` from the wire into a domain-validated `NonEmptyText` value object, hands that to an application *port* (`literature_adapter.search_publications`), and demotes any `ApplicationError` back down into the transport-appropriate `HttpError` taxonomy. The "PubMed-shaped" envelope is a *presentation* concern invented entirely at this boundary — the underlying `PublicationSummary` port type carries no publication date, no abstract, no body, and no author list, so those fields are synthesized deterministically from the metadata that *does* exist. This is a textbook anti-corruption seam: the outside world's expectations (a PubMed-like JSON shape) are honored without contaminating the domain with them.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the type-state request pipeline before the handler body executes. The handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is a compile-time proof that the request has already passed validation, authentication, and authorization. The identity is asserted through the following headers.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@alma.example` | Identifies the calling account. Absence or emptiness fails the pipeline at the authentication stage, yielding `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`. A malformed or unrecognized value yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 5f3c1e0a-2b7d-4a11-9c6e-1f2a3b4c5d6e` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces for this request. Not a credential; used for observability and support triage. If omitted, one is typically generated upstream. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The alma-http request pipeline encodes each processing guarantee as a distinct *type-state*, so the compiler — not a runtime `if` — enforces that stages run in order. A raw request first becomes `RequestHasBeenValidated` once its transport envelope (headers, shape) is well-formed. It then advances to `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated` once the `x-account-email` credential has been resolved to a known identity. Finally it becomes `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` once that identity has been granted access to this operation. Because this handler accepts precisely `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, it is *statically impossible* to invoke the handler body with an unauthenticated or unauthorized request — the value simply cannot be constructed. The `_authorized_request` binding is deliberately unused (prefixed with `_`); its mere presence in the argument list is the proof obligation, and consuming it discharges that obligation. There is no imperative auth check inside the handler because there does not need to be one.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `doi` | query | string | Yes | Must be present; must be non-empty after trimming; after normalization must begin with `10.`, contain a `/`, have an all-ASCII-digit registrant body after `10.`, and a non-empty suffix. | None | The Digital Object Identifier to search for. Accepts bare DOIs (`10.1038/s41586-023-05881-4`) as well as resolver-prefixed forms (`https://doi.org/...`, `http://doi.org/...`, `doi:...`), which are stripped during normalization. |

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` endpoint and reads **no request body**. All input arrives via the `doi` query-string parameter (see above). The handler extracts query parameters as an untyped `HashMap<String, String>`; there is no deserialized body struct.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |

```javascript
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    "x-account-email": "researcher@alma.example",
    "x-request-id": "5f3c1e0a-2b7d-4a11-9c6e-1f2a3b4c5d6e",
  },

if (!response.ok) {
  const problem = await response.json();
  throw new Error(`${response.status}: ${problem.error_explanation}`);
}

console.log(`${envelope.totalCount} match(es)`, envelope.results);
```

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK` with a JSON envelope. The envelope always contains a `results` array and an integer `totalCount`. Each entry in `results` has the following fields (all synthesized or derived at the presentation boundary).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `results` | array of objects | The matching PubMed-shaped entries. Empty when nothing matched. |
| `totalCount` | integer (u64) | The number of entries in `results`. |
| `results[].title` | string | Trimmed publication title from the summary. |
| `results[].pubdate` | string | Always the literal `"unknown"` — the port summary carries no publication date. |
| `results[].doi` | string | The trimmed DOI of the summary; empty string if the summary had none (in practice always populated, since matching requires a DOI). |
| `results[].abstract` | string | Synthesized descriptor, e.g. `Abstract for '<title>' (indexed via <source>) is not available.` |
| `results[].bodyText` | string | Synthesized descriptor, e.g. `Full text for '<title>' is not available through this endpoint.` |
| `results[].pubMedLink` | string | Derived permalink: `https://doi.org/<doi>` when a DOI is present, else a PubMed title search URL. |
| `results[].authors` | array of strings | Best-effort author list split from `originating_source` on `,`/`;`; empty when source is blank. |

**JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the success response:**

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "SearchPubmedByDoiResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["results", "totalCount"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "results": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["title", "pubdate", "doi", "abstract", "bodyText", "pubMedLink", "authors"],
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "title": { "type": "string" },
          "pubdate": { "type": "string" },
          "doi": { "type": "string" },
          "abstract": { "type": "string" },
          "bodyText": { "type": "string" },
          "pubMedLink": { "type": "string", "format": "uri" },
          "authors": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }
        }
      }
    },
    "totalCount": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
  }
}
```

**Realistic `200 OK` example body:**

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "A high-resolution map of the human genome",
      "pubdate": "unknown",
      "doi": "10.1038/s41586-023-05881-4",
      "abstract": "Abstract for 'A high-resolution map of the human genome' (indexed via Nature, Science) is not available.",
      "bodyText": "Full text for 'A high-resolution map of the human genome' is not available through this endpoint.",
      "pubMedLink": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-05881-4",
      "authors": ["Nature", "Science"]
    }
  ],
  "totalCount": 1
}
```

An empty-match request returns `200 OK` with the canonical empty envelope:

```json
{
  "results": [],
  "totalCount": 0
}
```

#### Error Responses

Errors are serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` object carrying `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The table below enumerates every `HttpError` variant and the specific circumstances under which THIS endpoint emits it.

| Status | error_category | When (for this endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `doi` param missing; `doi` blank after trim; DOI empty after normalization; missing `10.` prefix; missing `/` separator; non-digit/empty registrant body; empty suffix; `NonEmptyText::parse` failure; or the adapter reported `DomainInvariantViolated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"a digital object identifier must begin with the '10.' registrant prefix"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` header absent — rejected by the pipeline before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` present but not resolvable to a valid identity — rejected in the pipeline. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Pipeline authorization stage denies the account, OR the literature adapter returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied`. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"the literature adapter denied access for the supplied identifier"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | The adapter returns `ApplicationError::RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`. Note: an empty match set does NOT produce a 404 — it produces `200` with an empty envelope. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no literature record could be located for the supplied identifier"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from the adapter (e.g. `LiteratureAdapterFailure`) — network, upstream service, or unexpected port failure. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"boom"}` |

**Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:**

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "the 'doi' query parameter is required"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler body invokes the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_digital_object_identifier_parameter_from_map` — pulls the required `doi` key from the query map; errors `400` if absent or blank-after-trim; returns the trimmed value.
2. `normalize_pubmed_digital_object_identifier_lowercasing_and_trimming` — trims, lowercases, and strips any `https://doi.org/`, `http://doi.org/`, or `doi:` resolver prefix, producing a canonical comparison key.
3. `validate_pubmed_digital_object_identifier_syntactic_shape` — enforces non-empty, `10.` prefix, presence of `/`, all-digit non-empty registrant body, and non-empty suffix; errors `400` otherwise.
4. `parse_digital_object_identifier_parameter_into_non_empty_text` — parses the normalized identifier into the domain `NonEmptyText` value object; maps parse failure to `400`.
5. `application_state.literature_adapter.search_publications(&search_expression)` — the actual port call that queries the literature backend for candidate publications (awaited).
6. `map_literature_port_failure_into_pubmed_doi_http_error` — translates any `ApplicationError` from the adapter into the correct `HttpError` (404 / 403 / 400 / 500).
7. `filter_publication_summaries_by_matching_digital_object_identifier` — retains only summaries whose normalized DOI equals the requested identifier; drops DOI-less summaries.
8. `render_empty_pubmed_doi_match_results_envelope` — short-circuits with `{"results":[],"totalCount":0}` when nothing survived filtering.
9. `map_publication_summaries_into_pubmed_doi_match_entries` — maps each surviving summary into a PubMed-shaped entry, internally invoking `extract_pubmed_abstract_text_from_publication_summary`, `extract_pubmed_body_text_from_publication_summary`, `derive_pubmed_article_permalink_from_publication_summary`, `split_pubmed_author_names_from_publication_summary`, and `assemble_pubmed_doi_match_entry_object`.
10. `count_pubmed_doi_match_entries` — returns the entry count as a `u64`.
11. `wrap_pubmed_doi_match_entries_into_results_with_total` — assembles the final `{"results":[...],"totalCount":N}` envelope.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Empty match set is a success, not a 404.** If the adapter returns publications but none of them carry a DOI matching the request, you get `200 OK` with `{"results":[],"totalCount":0}`. A `404` only occurs when the *adapter itself* reports `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`.
- **`pubdate` is always the literal string `"unknown"`.** The `PublicationSummary` port type carries no publication date, so every entry's `pubdate` is hardcoded to `"unknown"`. Do not parse it as a date.
- **`abstract` and `bodyText` are synthesized placeholders, not real content.** They are deterministic strings assembled from the title (and, for the abstract, the originating source). They will never contain actual abstract or full-text prose from this endpoint.
- **`authors` is derived from `originating_source`, not a real author list.** The port has no author field, so the originating source is split on `,` and `;`. A source like `"Nature"` becomes `["Nature"]`; a blank source becomes `[]`. These are not necessarily human author names.
- **Resolver-prefix stripping is order-sensitive and case-insensitive.** Normalization lowercases first, so a pasted `HTTPS://DOI.ORG/10.1038/S41586` is correctly stripped and lowercased to `10.1038/s41586`. Only the three known prefixes are stripped; other resolver forms (e.g. `dx.doi.org`) are NOT stripped and will fail syntactic validation.
- **Registrant body must be purely ASCII digits.** `10.abc/xyz` and `10./xyz` both fail validation with `400`; only `10.<digits>/<non-empty-suffix>` passes. The suffix, by contrast, is only checked for non-emptiness.
- **The `doi` must contain a `/`.** A bare registrant like `10.1000` (no slash) is rejected at step 3, before any upstream call is made.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Why does the response tell me the abstract "is not available" for every single record?**
A: Because it genuinely is not available. The underlying `PublicationSummary` port carries only a title, an optional DOI, and an originating source. The `abstract` field is a synthesized courtesy string so clients receive a stable shape rather than an empty value. If you need real abstracts, you need a different upstream.

**Q: I searched for a DOI I know exists and got `totalCount: 0`. Is that an error?**
A: No. It means the literature adapter returned zero summaries whose normalized DOI matched yours (or returned summaries without DOIs). It is a fully successful `200`. Check for typos, stray resolver forms the normalizer doesn't strip, or that the record is actually indexed by the adapter.

**Q: Can I send the DOI in the request body to avoid URL-encoding the slash?**
A: No. This is a `GET` and reads no body whatsoever. The `doi` must be a query-string parameter, and yes, you must URL-encode the `/` as `%2F`. This is the price of DOIs containing slashes.

### `GET /api/pubmed/fullsearch` — PubMed Full-Text Publication Search

#### Synopsis

This endpoint performs a full-text search against the configured PubMed literature adapter, accepting a free-text search expression via the mandatory `query` query-string parameter and an optional `limit` page-size control. It returns a JSON envelope containing an array of richly-shaped full-text publication entries (title, DOI, abstract, body text, permalink, and author list) alongside a `totalCount` of the entries actually emitted. The result count is clamped to a hard ceiling so that no single caller can coerce the service into materialising an unbounded payload.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the grand cathedral of Representational State Transfer, this endpoint occupies the humble but sacred position of a *safe, idempotent read*. It is a `GET`, and it means it: invoking `GET /api/pubmed/fullsearch?query=oncology` a thousand times in succession produces no observable mutation of server-side state, no side effect beyond the ephemeral warming of an upstream cache, and no violation of the safety guarantee that HTTP intermediaries — proxies, CDNs, the browser's own speculative prefetcher — rely upon when they cache, retry, or prefetch the representation. Because search parameters are carried in the query string rather than a request body, the resource is addressable, bookmarkable, and cache-keyable, exactly as the founding scriptures of REST demand. The response is a *representation of a search result set*, not the resource itself; it is a projection, a lens, a momentary photograph of the literature corpus as filtered through the caller's expression.

Viewed through the lens of Domain-Driven Design, the handler is a thin adapter in the *interface layer* whose sole legitimate ambitions are to parse the untrusted transport-shaped input into validated domain value objects (notably `NonEmptyText`), to delegate the actual searching to the `literature_adapter` port that lives in the application layer, and to translate the port's failure taxonomy back into the HTTP error dialect. The handler itself holds no business logic — the search semantics belong to the port and its implementation — and this deliberate anaemia is a feature, not an accident. The full-text *entries* it emits are a presentation-layer confection: because the `PublicationSummary` port shape carries no structured abstract, body, or authors, the handler *synthesises* deterministic, human-legible placeholders from the fields it does have, keeping the wire contract stable even as the underlying corpus remains sparse.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the type-state authentication pipeline before the handler body executes. The handler's signature demands an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is a compile-time proof that the request has already passed through validation, authentication, and authorization stages; the handler cannot even be constructed for a request that has not.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff` | Opaque correlation identifier echoed through logs and tracing. If omitted, one is typically synthesised upstream. Used to stitch a single logical request across service boundaries. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@example.org` | The caller's account identity. Consumed by the authentication stage to resolve the principal, then by the authorization stage to decide whether a PubMed full-text search is permitted. Absent or empty → `401`. Present but unresolvable/invalid → `401`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The request is threaded through a sequence of marker-typed stages, each represented by a distinct phantom type parameter on `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`. First, the request is *Validated*: its transport-level shape (headers present, well-formed) is checked, yielding `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>`. Only a validated request can be advanced to *Authenticated*, wherein the `x-account-email` identity is resolved into a known principal, yielding `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthenticated>`. Only an authenticated request can be advanced to *Authorized*, wherein the principal's permission to perform *this* operation is adjudicated, yielding `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — the exact type this handler requires as its `_authorized_request` extractor. Because each stage is a different Rust type and each transition consumes the prior state, it is *structurally impossible* to invoke this handler with a request that has skipped a stage: the illegal states do not compile. The handler binds the authorized request to `_authorized_request` (underscore-prefixed: the proof is required to exist, but its contents are not otherwise read by this particular handler).

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | query | string | Yes | Trimmed; must not be blank after trimming; must parse as a non-empty `NonEmptyText` domain value | — | The free-text search expression handed to the literature port. Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped before validation. |
| `limit` | query | integer (usize) | No | Must be a non-negative integer; must be strictly greater than zero; effectively capped at `100` | `20` | The maximum number of full-text entries to return. Absent or empty string → default of `20`. Values above `100` are silently clamped to `100`. A value of `0` is rejected. |

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` endpoint and reads **no request body**. All input arrives via the query string (see above). Any body sent is ignored by the handler.

For completeness, the accepted request-body JSON Schema is the empty object:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma-http.example/schemas/search_pubmed_full_text.request.json",
  "title": "SearchPubmedFullTextRequestBody",
  "description": "This endpoint reads no request body; the empty object is the only valid payload.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

TypeScript interface for the (non-existent) body:

```typescript
/** GET /api/pubmed/fullsearch reads no request body. */
export interface SearchPubmedFullTextRequestBody {}
```

Rust struct mirror (there is no deserialized body struct; input is `Query<HashMap<String, String>>`):

```rust
/// GET /api/pubmed/fullsearch reads no request body.
/// Input is extracted from the query string only.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct SearchPubmedFullTextRequestBody;

/// The actual extractor used by the handler:
/// axum::extract::Query<std::collections::HashMap<String, String>>
```

#### Request Examples

curl:

```bash
curl -sS -G 'https://api.example.org/api/pubmed/fullsearch' \
  --data-urlencode 'query=cancer genomics' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=10' \
  -H 'x-request-id: 6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff' \
  -H 'x-account-email: researcher@example.org'
```

```bash
http GET 'https://api.example.org/api/pubmed/fullsearch' \
  query=='cancer genomics' \
  limit==10 \
  x-request-id:6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff \

```

JavaScript fetch:

```javascript
const url = new URL("https://api.example.org/api/pubmed/fullsearch");
url.searchParams.set("query", "cancer genomics");
url.searchParams.set("limit", "10");

const response = await fetch(url, {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    "x-request-id": "6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff",
    "x-account-email": "researcher@example.org",
  },
});

if (!response.ok) {
  const problem = await response.json();
  throw new Error(`${problem.error_category}: ${problem.error_explanation}`);
}

const body = await response.json();
console.log(body.totalCount, body.results);
```

#### Successful Response

`200 OK` with a JSON envelope. The envelope has two top-level fields; each entry inside `results` has seven fields.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `results` | array of object | The full-text entries, already truncated to the effective limit. |
| `results[].title` | string | The publication title, copied from `PublicationSummary.publication_title`. |
| `results[].pubdate` | string | Publication date. Always emitted as the empty string `""` (the port carries no date). |
| `results[].doi` | string | The DOI, trimmed, or `""` when absent. |
| `results[].abstract` | string | A synthesised deterministic placeholder abstract derived from title and source. May be `""` when both are empty. |
| `results[].bodyText` | string | A synthesised deterministic placeholder body-text string. |
| `results[].pubMedLink` | string | A permalink: `https://doi.org/<doi>` when a DOI exists, otherwise `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=<url-encoded-title>`. |
| `results[].authors` | array of string | Author names split from `originating_source` on `,` and `;`. Empty array when the source is blank. |
| `totalCount` | integer (u64) | The count of entries actually present in `results` (post-truncation), not the corpus-wide match count. |

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma-http.example/schemas/search_pubmed_full_text.response.json",
  "title": "SearchPubmedFullTextResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["results", "totalCount"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "results": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["title", "pubdate", "doi", "abstract", "bodyText", "pubMedLink", "authors"],
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "title": { "type": "string" },
          "pubdate": { "type": "string" },
          "doi": { "type": "string" },
          "abstract": { "type": "string" },
          "bodyText": { "type": "string" },
          "pubMedLink": { "type": "string", "format": "uri" },
          "authors": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }
        }
      }
    },
    "totalCount": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
  }
}
```

Realistic `200` example:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "Somatic mutation landscapes in pediatric cancer genomics",
      "pubdate": "",
      "doi": "10.1000/j.cancer.2023.001",
      "abstract": "Abstract for \"Somatic mutation landscapes in pediatric cancer genomics\", indexed from Nature Genetics, is not available in the indexed record.",
      "bodyText": "Full text for \"Somatic mutation landscapes in pediatric cancer genomics\" is not available through the current PubMed indexing tier.",
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `query` missing; `query` blank after trimming; `NonEmptyText::parse` rejects the value; `limit` not a non-negative integer; `limit` equal to `0`; or the port returns `DomainInvariantViolated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'query' query parameter is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` absent — rejected by the authentication stage before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` present but cannot be resolved to a valid principal — rejected by the authentication stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Principal is authenticated but not permitted to run a PubMed full-text search — from the authorization stage, or from the port returning `AuthorizationWasDenied` (explanation: "not authorized to perform a PubMed full-text search"). | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"not authorized to perform a PubMed full-text search"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | The port returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested PubMed resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The port fails with any other `ApplicationError` variant (e.g. `LiteratureAdapterFailure`) — upstream/adapter breakage. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"literature adapter failure: connection reset"}` |

Full example error body:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "the 'limit' query parameter must be greater than zero"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_full_text_search_query_from_query_parameters` — pulls the mandatory `query` param, trims it, and errors `400` when missing or blank.
2. `parse_full_text_search_query_into_non_empty_text` — validates the trimmed query into a `NonEmptyText` domain value, mapping parse failure to `400`.
3. `parse_pubmed_maximum_result_count_from_query_parameters` — parses the optional `limit` into a `usize`, defaulting to `20` when absent/empty and rejecting `0` or non-numeric values with `400`.
4. `clamp_requested_pubmed_result_count_to_supported_ceiling` — clamps the requested count down to the `100`-entry ceiling.
5. `application_state.literature_adapter.search_publications(&search_expression)` — the actual port call that performs the search (awaited).
6. `map_literature_port_failure_into_pubmed_full_text_http_error` — translates an `ApplicationError` from the port into the correct `HttpError` variant.
7. `map_publication_summaries_into_pubmed_full_text_entries` — shapes each `PublicationSummary` into a full-text entry `Value`, internally calling helpers 8–13.
8. `split_pubmed_author_names_from_publication_summary` — splits `originating_source` on `,`/`;` into an author list.
9. `derive_pubmed_article_permalink_from_publication_summary` — builds a DOI link or a title-search permalink.
10. `encode_query_term_for_url` — minimal percent-encoding for the title-search permalink (spaces → `+`).
11. `extract_pubmed_abstract_text_from_publication_summary` — synthesises a placeholder abstract from title/source.
12. `extract_pubmed_body_text_from_publication_summary` — synthesises a placeholder body-text string from title.
13. `resolve_pubmed_digital_object_identifier_or_empty` — trims and returns the DOI, or `""` when absent.
14. `assemble_pubmed_full_text_entry_object` — assembles the seven-field entry JSON object.
15. `take_first_n_pubmed_full_text_entries` — truncates the entry list down to the effective limit.
16. `count_total_pubmed_full_text_matches` — counts the (post-truncation) entries as a `u64`.
17. `wrap_pubmed_full_text_entries_into_results_with_total` — wraps entries and count into the `{results, totalCount}` envelope.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`totalCount` is not the corpus match count.** It is computed *after* truncation by `count_total_pubmed_full_text_matches`, so it always equals `results.length` and never reveals how many matches actually existed upstream. Do not use it for pagination math.
- **`limit` above 100 is silently clamped, not rejected.** Asking for `limit=5000` returns at most `100` entries with no warning; the clamp is invisible in the response.
- **`limit=0` *is* an error (`400`), but `limit=` (empty) is *not*** — an empty or whitespace-only `limit` falls back to the default of `20`, whereas an explicit zero is rejected.
- **`abstract` and `bodyText` are always synthetic placeholders**, never real article text — the `PublicationSummary` port carries no abstract or body. They are deterministic strings derived from title/source, so treating them as genuine content will mislead downstream consumers.
- **`authors` is a heuristic reinterpretation of `originating_source`**, split on commas and semicolons. A source like `"Nature, Science"` becomes two "authors"; a single-source string becomes a single "author". These are not necessarily real author names.
- **`pubdate` is always the empty string.** The handler hardcodes `""` for the date argument to `assemble_pubmed_full_text_entry_object`; there is no date in the port shape.
- **Permalink fallback percent-encoding is minimal.** `encode_query_term_for_url` only preserves `A–Z a–z 0–9 - _ . ~`, maps space to `+`, and percent-encodes everything else byte-wise; it is not a full RFC 3986 encoder.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I POST my search parameters in a JSON body instead of the query string?**
A: No. The route is registered as `get(...)` and the handler extracts `Query<HashMap<String, String>>`. A body is ignored. Put `query` and `limit` in the query string.

**Q: Why does `totalCount` say 10 when I know there are thousands of matching papers?**
A: Because `totalCount` counts the entries in the response after truncation, not the upstream match total. If you asked for `limit=10`, you get `totalCount: 10` (or fewer). This is working as coded.

**Q: The `abstract` field just says the abstract "is not available in the indexed record." Is that a bug?**
A: No, that is the deterministic placeholder the handler synthesises because the underlying `PublicationSummary` port carries no abstract. Every abstract and `bodyText` value from this endpoint is a placeholder of this shape.

### `POST /api/pubmed/batchsearch` — Batch PubMed Reference Resolver

#### Synopsis

Accepts a JSON body containing an array of free-text search terms under the `queries` field, concatenates those terms into a single space-separated search expression, and dispatches that expression through the configured literature adapter's `search_publications` port. The resulting publication summaries are normalized into front-end-friendly reference entries — each carrying a rendered citation string, a canonical permalink, a heuristic match-confidence score, an originating-source label, and (conditionally) a direct PDF URL — deduplicated by DOI, and returned inside a `{ "results": [...], "resultCount": N }` envelope. This endpoint exists specifically to feed the front-end batch citation resolver, which submits many loosely-worded bibliographic fragments at once and expects a single flattened, deduplicated result set in return.

#### Theory & Rationale

Although this operation is fundamentally a *read* — it retrieves publications and mutates no server-side state — it is deliberately modeled as `POST` rather than `GET`. The justification is threefold. First, the request payload is an unbounded, structured collection (`queries` is an array), and cramming a variable-length list of arbitrary human search terms into a query string is both impractical and fragile against URL length limits and over-eager intermediary caching. Second, `POST` is neither safe nor idempotent per RFC 9110, and while this handler happens to be side-effect-free, refusing to promise idempotence is *honest*: an upstream literature provider may legitimately return different, freshly-ranked results for identical inputs on successive calls, so pretending the call is idempotent would be a lie encoded into the HTTP method. Third, submitting a search *expression* as an entity in the request body correctly frames the operation as "process this document and return a derived representation," which is the semantically defensible reading when the input is a query specification rather than a resource identifier.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler is a thin *application-layer* orchestrator that lives squarely in the HTTP adapter ring and studiously avoids leaking transport concerns into the domain. It borrows exactly one domain value object — `NonEmptyText` — to enforce the single genuine domain invariant it cares about (a search expression must not be empty), and otherwise delegates all publication retrieval across the `literature_adapter` port, keeping the domain core ignorant of PubMed, DOIs, and HTTP entirely. Every projection concern — confidence heuristics, permalink derivation, PDF-URL speculation, DOI deduplication — is *presentation* logic that belongs to the adapter, not the domain, and is implemented here as a chain of small pure helper functions precisely so the domain remains uncontaminated by front-end serialization trivia.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

The handler's signature requires `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, meaning the request must have already traversed the full type-state authentication pipeline before this handler body is ever invoked. The authentication and authorization outcome is therefore carried in the type system, not re-checked inside the handler.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 8f3c1e2a-9b44-4d7e-a1f0-2c6b9e0d5a71` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces; used to stitch this request to upstream literature calls. If absent, the pipeline typically generates one. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@lab.example.edu` | Identifies the calling account. Consumed during the `Validated -> Authenticated` transition; a missing value yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, an unrecognized/rejected value yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | Axum's `Json<Value>` extractor requires a JSON content type; a mismatch results in a `400`-class malformed-body rejection. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The alma-http request pipeline models each phase of admission as a distinct *type-state* wrapped in `HttpRequestInPipeline<S>`, so that reaching a later stage is impossible unless the earlier stages provably succeeded:

1. **Validated** — the raw inbound request is parsed and its structural/transport-level invariants are checked (well-formed headers, decodable body envelope). Only a request that clears this stage is admitted as validated.
2. **Authenticated** — the validated request's credentials, principally `x-account-email`, are resolved against the identity subsystem. Missing credentials collapse the pipeline into `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing (401)`; present-but-rejected credentials into `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid (401)`.
3. **Authorized** — the now-authenticated principal is checked against the policy governing this route. A denial produces `AuthorizationWasDenied (403)`. Only upon success is the request re-typed to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`.

Because `search_pubmed_in_batch_handler` accepts exactly `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` (bound to `_authorized_request` and intentionally unused thereafter), the Rust compiler statically guarantees the handler body cannot run for any request that has not been validated, authenticated, *and* authorized. There is no imperative `if not authorized { reject }` inside the handler because such a check would be redundant: the state is a precondition encoded in the parameter type.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint reads no path segments beyond the fixed literal `/api/pubmed/batchsearch` and inspects no query-string parameters whatsoever. All input arrives in the request body.

#### Request Body

The handler extracts the raw body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then reads exactly one field from it: `queries`. No other top-level field is read; unknown fields are silently ignored.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `queries` | array | Yes | Must be present and must be a JSON array (`extract_batch_queries_array_from_request_body`). Non-array or absent → `400 request_body_was_malformed`. | None | The list of raw search terms to combine. |
| `queries[]` | string | — | Only string elements are read; non-string elements (numbers, booleans, objects, nulls) are silently discarded. Each string is trimmed; empty-after-trim strings are dropped. After filtering, at least one non-empty term must remain, otherwise `400 request_body_was_malformed`. | — | An individual free-text search term. |

Note: the terms are joined with a single space into one expression, which must itself parse as a `NonEmptyText`; in practice this can only fail if every term filtered away, which is already caught earlier.

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is the results envelope produced by `wrap_batch_reference_entries_into_results_envelope`.

**Response field table**

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `results` | array | Yes | Deduplicated reference entries, ordered by the adapter's original ranking. |
| `resultCount` | integer | Yes | The length of `results` (`results.len()`). |
| `results[].reference` | string | Yes | Human-readable citation; `"<title>. doi:<doi>"` when a DOI exists, otherwise just the title (or `"Untitled publication"` if the title is blank). |
| `results[].doi` | string | Yes | The DOI, or `""` (empty string) when the summary lacked one. |
| `results[].pubMedLink` | string | Yes | `https://doi.org/<doi>` when a DOI exists, otherwise a PubMed title search URL. |
| `results[].confidence` | number | Yes | Heuristic score in `[0.05, 0.99]`, rounded to two decimals; decays with rank, +0.03 bonus if a DOI is present. |
| `results[].source` | string | Yes | Lowercased originating source, defaulting to `"pubmed"` when blank. |
| `results[].pdfUrl` | string | No | `https://doi.org/<doi>.pdf` — **present only when a non-empty DOI exists**; omitted entirely otherwise. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError`'s `IntoResponse` as `{ "error_category": <label>, "error_explanation": <text> }` with the corresponding status.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `queries` missing or not an array; every term filtered away leaving none; combined expression fails `NonEmptyText::parse`; or a `DomainInvariantViolated` from the port. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the 'queries' field is required and must be an array"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | `x-account-email` absent; request never reaches `Authenticated`. Raised by the pipeline before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` present but rejected by the identity subsystem. Raised by the pipeline before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Authenticated principal not permitted for this route, or the literature port returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied`. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Port returns `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` (mapped by `map_literature_port_failure_into_pubmed_batch_http_error`). | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other port failure (e.g. `LiteratureAdapterFailure` / network/provider errors) falls through to the catch-all upstream mapping. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"literature adapter failure: connection reset"}` |

**Full SerializedErrorBody example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "the 'queries' array must contain at least one non-empty search term"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler is a linear composition of the following real helper functions (numbered as annotated in the source):

1. `extract_batch_queries_array_from_request_body` — pulls the required `queries` field, requiring it be a JSON array; otherwise `400`.
2. `collect_batch_query_terms_from_json_array` — keeps only string entries, trims them, drops blanks.
3. `reject_empty_batch_query_term_collection` — errors `400` if no usable terms survived collection.
4. `combine_batch_query_terms_into_single_expression` — joins surviving terms with single spaces.
5. `parse_combined_batch_expression_into_non_empty_text` — validates the expression into a domain `NonEmptyText`.
6. `application_state.literature_adapter.search_publications(&combined_query_text)` — the actual async port call returning `Vec<PublicationSummary>`.
7. `map_literature_port_failure_into_pubmed_batch_http_error` — maps a port `ApplicationError` onto the correct `HttpError` (404 / 403 / 400 / 500).
8. `map_publication_summaries_into_batch_reference_entries` — projects each summary into a normalized entry (calls helpers 9–14 below per item).
9. `format_publication_summary_into_batch_reference_string` — renders the human-readable `reference` string.
10. `derive_batch_article_permalink_from_publication_summary` — builds `pubMedLink` (DOI URL or title-search fallback).
11. `compute_batch_match_confidence_for_publication_summary` — computes the rank-decayed, DOI-bonused, clamped `confidence`.
12. `resolve_batch_originating_source_label_from_publication_summary` — normalizes/lowercases `source`, defaulting to `pubmed`.
13. `build_optional_batch_pdf_url_from_publication_summary` — conditionally builds `pdfUrl` (only when a DOI exists).
14. `assemble_batch_reference_entry_object` — assembles the per-entry JSON object, inserting `pdfUrl` only when present.
15. `deduplicate_batch_reference_entries_by_digital_object_identifier` — removes duplicate non-empty DOIs (first wins; empty-DOI entries always kept).
16. `wrap_batch_reference_entries_into_results_envelope` — wraps the entries into `{ results, resultCount }`.
17. Auxiliary: `round_confidence_to_two_decimal_places` and `encode_query_component_for_permalink` support helpers 11 and 10 respectively.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Non-string `queries` elements are silently dropped, not rejected.** `[42, true, {"x":1}, "gene"]` is accepted and treated as `["gene"]`. Only if *all* elements are non-string/blank do you get a `400` — via the empty-collection check, not a type error.
- **`doi` is always a string, never `null`.** Summaries without a DOI serialize `"doi": ""` (via `unwrap_or_default()`). Consumers testing "has DOI" must check for empty string, not `null` or absence.
- **`pdfUrl` presence is the DOI signal.** The field is *omitted entirely* (not `null`) when no DOI exists, so downstream code can gate PDF behavior purely on key presence — but must not assume the key always exists.
- **Deduplication is DOI-only and case-insensitive.** Two entries with DOIs `10.1/X` and `10.1/x` collapse to one (first wins). Entries with empty DOIs are *never* deduplicated, so title-only duplicates from the adapter will all pass through.
- **Confidence is a cosmetic heuristic, not a relevance metric.** It is computed purely from ordinal rank plus a DOI bonus, clamped to `[0.05, 0.99]` and rounded to two decimals. It says nothing about semantic match quality and is identical across queries for a given rank/DOI shape.
- **All terms are merged into one query, not searched independently.** `queries: ["cancer", "therapy"]` becomes the single expression `"cancer therapy"` — this is one combined search, not two batched searches. Distinct per-term result sets are not available from this endpoint.
- **The permalink encoder is deliberately minimal.** `encode_query_component_for_permalink` only escapes space, `&`, `#`, `?`, `=`, `+`. Titles containing other reserved characters (e.g. `%`) are left raw in the fallback PubMed URL.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: It's just a search — why is it a `POST` and not a `GET`?**
A: Because the input is an arbitrarily long array of arbitrary human text, and because we decline to promise idempotence for a call whose upstream provider may re-rank on every invocation. Encoding a JSON array into a query string is a URL-length grenade with the pin pulled. See *Theory & Rationale*.

**Q: I sent `queries: ["", "  ", 99]` and got a 400. Is that a bug?**
A: No. Non-string entries are discarded, blank strings are trimmed away, and once nothing usable remains, `reject_empty_batch_query_term_collection` correctly returns `request_body_was_malformed`. Send at least one non-blank string.

**Q: Why does one of my results have `"doi": ""` and no `pdfUrl`, while my code expected `null`?**
A: Because the handler never emits `null` for `doi` — it defaults to an empty string — and it omits `pdfUrl` entirely rather than nulling it. Check for empty-string DOIs and key presence for `pdfUrl`. This is intentional, exhaustively so.

---

### `GET /api/scholar` — Search Scholar Publications

Performs a free-text scholarly literature search against the configured literature adapter and returns a de-duplicated, ceiling-limited envelope of publication result entries. The mandatory search expression is supplied via the `query` query-string parameter, and the optional result ceiling via `limit`. Each returned entry is a synthesised object carrying a title, a stable Scholar cluster-style permalink, a truncated snippet, an optional DOI, and a source label.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is a textbook example of a **safe, idempotent, cacheable read** expressed as an HTTP `GET`. It mutates nothing: repeated invocations with the same query string are semantically equivalent to a single invocation, and the handler carries no side effects beyond a fan-out call to the downstream literature adapter. Because all of the salient input — the search expression and the result ceiling — is carried in the query string rather than a request body, the resource is a pure function of its URL, which is precisely what REST's uniform-interface constraint would have you do for a search collection. The choice of `GET` over `POST` here is not incidental: search is a retrieval, not a submission, and modelling it as a submission would be an abuse of verbs that breaks intermediary caching, safe-retry semantics, and the mental model of every client author who has ever read the HTTP specification.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, the handler lives squarely in the **HTTP adapter / interface layer** and does almost nothing of consequence itself. It validates and coerces primitive query-string strings into a domain value object (`NonEmptyText`), delegates the actual search to an **application port** (`literature_adapter.search_publications`) behind a hexagonal boundary, and then performs presentation-only shaping — permalink synthesis, snippet truncation, title de-duplication, and ceiling application — that is intentionally kept out of the domain because it concerns transport-level formatting rather than business invariants. This separation is why the handler reads as a long series of narrowly-named helper functions: the endpoint's job is orchestration and translation, and the domain's job is to remain blissfully ignorant that HTTP, Google Scholar permalinks, or 220-character snippets ever existed.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the type-state request pipeline and must arrive already carrying the identity headers the pipeline expects. The handler binds `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which means the compiler itself refuses to let this handler run against a request that has not been driven all the way to the authorized state.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 6f2c9b1a-2d4e-4f7a-9a1b-8c3d5e6f7a8b` | Correlation identifier threaded through the pipeline for tracing and log correlation. Echoed into structured logs; supply a fresh UUID per logical request. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@institution.edu` | Identifies the calling principal. Consumed during the `Authenticated` stage to resolve identity; a missing value yields `401 authentication credentials were missing`, an unresolvable value yields `401 authentication credentials were invalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>` wrapper encodes the request's progress through the middleware pipeline in its *type parameter*, so that each stage is a distinct compile-time state rather than a runtime flag. A request first enters the **`RequestHasBeenValidated`** state, in which structural preconditions (required headers present and well-formed, such as `x-request-id` and `x-account-email`) have been checked; only from a validated request can the pipeline attempt the transition to **`RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`**, in which the `x-account-email` principal has been resolved to a known identity; and only an authenticated request can be promoted to **`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`**, in which that identity has been confirmed to hold the permissions required to reach the handler. This handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, so it is *statically impossible* to invoke the handler body with a request that skipped validation, authentication, or authorization — the type system, not a runtime guard, enforces the ordering. Note that the extracted `_authorized_request` value is deliberately unused (prefixed with `_`): its sole purpose is to prove, at the type level, that the pipeline reached the authorized state before the handler ran.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | query | string | Yes | Must be present and non-blank after trimming; must parse as a domain `NonEmptyText`. | None | The free-text search expression sent to the literature adapter. Absent or whitespace-only values are rejected with `400`. |
| `limit` | query | integer | No | Must parse as `usize`; must be strictly greater than `0`. Values above `50` are silently clamped to `50`. | `10` | Maximum number of result entries to return after de-duplication. Blank or absent values fall back to the default of `10`. |

Unrecognised query parameters are ignored: the handler extracts only `query` and `limit` from the `HashMap<String, String>` and does not reject extras.

#### Request Body

This endpoint is a `GET` and **reads no request body**. All input is carried in the query string (`query`, `limit`). Any body sent is ignored by the handler.

#### Successful Response

`200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is an envelope object with a single `results` array; each element is a scholar result entry object assembled by the handler.

Response fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `results` | array | Ordered, de-duplicated, ceiling-limited list of scholar result entries. May be empty. |
| `results[].title` | string | The publication title, taken verbatim from the summary's `publication_title`. |
| `results[].link` | string | Synthesised Scholar permalink. `…/scholar?q=<encoded-doi>` when a DOI is present; otherwise `…/scholar?cluster=<1000000000 + ordinal_index>`. |
| `results[].snippet` | string | `"<title> (via <source>)"`, word-boundary-truncated to 220 characters with a trailing `…` when clipped. |
| `results[].doi` | string | The trimmed DOI, or an empty string `""` when the summary carries none. |
| `results[].source` | string | The trimmed originating source label, or `"scholar"` when the summary carries no source. |

```json
          "link":    { "type": "string", "format": "uri" },
          "snippet": { "type": "string" },
          "doi":     { "type": "string" },
          "source":  { "type": "string" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Realistic `200` example:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "A Programmable Dual-RNA-Guided DNA Endonuclease",
      "link": "https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=10.1126%2Fscience.1225829",
      "snippet": "A Programmable Dual-RNA-Guided DNA Endonuclease (via crossref)",
      "doi": "10.1126/science.1225829",
      "source": "crossref"
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiplex Genome Engineering Using CRISPR/Cas Systems",
      "link": "https://scholar.google.com/scholar?cluster=1000000001",
      "snippet": "Multiplex Genome Engineering Using CRISPR/Cas Systems (via scholar)",
      "doi": "",
      "source": "scholar"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialised as `HttpError` into a `SerializedErrorBody` of the shape `{ "error_category", "error_explanation" }`. The table below lists every variant and the specific circumstances that trigger it for *this* endpoint.

| Status | error_category | When (for this endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `query` missing; `query` blank; `query` fails `NonEmptyText::parse`; `limit` non-numeric; `limit` equals `0`; adapter returns `DomainInvariantViolated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'query' query parameter is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Pipeline could not reach the authenticated stage because `x-account-email` was absent. Raised in the pipeline before the handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` was present but could not be resolved to a valid principal. Raised in the pipeline before the handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Adapter returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` (principal may not perform scholar searches), or the pipeline denies authorization before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"the authenticated principal may not perform scholar searches"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Adapter returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested scholar resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Adapter returns `LiteratureAdapterFailure`, or any other unmapped `ApplicationError` variant. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"the upstream literature service is unavailable"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "the 'limit' query parameter must be greater than zero"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler body orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_scholar_search_query_from_query_parameters` — pulls the mandatory `query` value out of the parameter map, rejecting absent or blank values with `400`.
2. `parse_scholar_search_query_into_non_empty_text` — parses the raw string into a domain `NonEmptyText`, mapping validation failures to `400`.
3. `parse_maximum_scholar_result_count_from_query_parameters` — resolves `limit`, defaulting to `10` when absent/blank and rejecting non-numeric or zero values with `400`.
4. `clamp_requested_scholar_result_count_to_supported_ceiling` — clamps the requested count down to the `50`-entry ceiling.
5. `application_state.literature_adapter.search_publications` — the actual port call that performs the search and returns `Vec<PublicationSummary>`.
6. `map_literature_port_failure_into_scholar_http_error` — translates any `ApplicationError` from the adapter into the appropriate `HttpError`.
7. `map_publication_summaries_into_scholar_result_entries` — shapes each summary into a result entry object, delegating to permalink, snippet, DOI, source, and assembly helpers.
8. `build_scholar_cluster_permalink_from_publication_summary` — synthesises the DOI-based or ordinal-cluster permalink for each entry.
9. `build_scholar_result_snippet_from_publication_summary` — builds and word-boundary-truncates the `"<title> (via <source>)"` snippet.
10. `resolve_scholar_digital_object_identifier_or_empty` — extracts the trimmed DOI or an empty string.
11. `resolve_scholar_originating_source_label_from_publication_summary` — extracts the trimmed source or the `"scholar"` default.
12. `assemble_scholar_result_entry_object` — composes the final per-entry JSON object.
13. `deduplicate_scholar_result_entries_by_publication_title` — removes case-insensitive, trimmed title duplicates, preserving first-appearance order.
14. `take_first_n_scholar_result_entries` — trims the list to the effective (clamped) result count.
15. `wrap_scholar_result_entries_into_results_envelope` — wraps the final list into `{ "results": [...] }`.

Supporting utilities used along the way: `encode_query_component` (conservative percent-encoding of space, `&`, `?`, `=`, `#`), `truncate_text_on_word_boundary` (word-boundary truncation with ellipsis), and `scholar_default_source_label` (returns the constant `"scholar"`).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Clamping is silent.** `limit=1000` does not error; it is quietly reduced to `50`. Clients cannot distinguish "I asked for 50" from "I asked for 5000" by response shape alone.
- **De-duplication happens before the limit is applied.** The order is: dedupe by title, *then* take the first N. Duplicate-heavy result sets can therefore return fewer entries than `limit` even when the adapter returned many summaries.
- **Title de-duplication is case-insensitive and trim-normalised.** `"Same Paper"` and `"same paper "` collapse to one entry (first wins). Entries with an empty or missing title are *never* de-duplicated and are always kept.
- **The permalink is synthesised, not authoritative.** Without a DOI, `link` is `…?cluster=<1000000000 + ordinal_index>` — a deterministic pseudo-cluster id seeded from list position, not a real Google Scholar cluster. It is stable per position, not per publication.
- **`doi` is always a string, never null.** A missing or whitespace-only DOI serialises as `""`, not JSON `null`. Consumers must treat empty string as "no DOI".
- **The percent-encoder is deliberately partial.** `encode_query_component` only escapes space, `&`, `?`, `=`, and `#`. Other reserved characters in a DOI pass through unescaped, so the permalink is "valid enough" rather than RFC 3986-strict.
- **Snippet truncation reserves a character for the ellipsis** and only cuts on a word boundary if that boundary keeps at least half the budget; otherwise it hard-cuts. The result may be shorter than the 220-character limit.
- **`limit=0` is an error, not "return nothing".** Zero is explicitly rejected with `400`, unlike a blank/absent `limit` which defaults to `10`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I sent a JSON body with my search terms. Why did nothing happen?**
A: Because this is a `GET`, and the handler reads only the query string. Your body was carried across the network, ignored on arrival, and is now a monument to unrealised effort. Put the terms in `?query=`.

**Q: I asked for `limit=200` and got 50 results. Is the endpoint broken?**
A: No, the endpoint is working exactly as designed. Fifty is the ceiling, and the ceiling is applied silently. The endpoint is not broken; your expectations were merely optimistic.

**Q: Two of my results have identical `cluster=` links. Bug?**
A: Only if two results share the same ordinal position, which is impossible, so no. Cluster ids are seeded from list index (`1000000000 + index`), meaning identical searches yield stable links across calls but say nothing about whether two publications are actually the same. The `link` is decorative infrastructure, not a citation key.

### `GET /api/rag/drive/folder/:folder_identifier` — Browse a Google Drive Folder for RAG Ingestion

#### Synopsis

This endpoint enumerates the contents of a single Google Drive folder so that a caller can decide which files to feed into the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) knowledge base. It resolves the folder listing through the configured Artificial Intelligence adapter (which is asked to emit a strict JSON array), normalizes and classifies each returned entry by MIME type, and cross-references every entry against the `rag_knowledge` document collection so that files already ingested from this folder are flagged. The response is a paginated envelope describing the folder, its (normalized) files, a running count of previously ingested documents, and an opaque cursor for fetching the next page.

#### Theory & Rationale

`GET` is the correct and only defensible verb here: browsing a folder is a *safe* and *idempotent* read operation in the strict HTTP sense — repeatedly issuing the same request produces no observable server-side state mutation and leaves the RAG knowledge corpus untouched. No document is ingested, deleted, or reordered as a side effect of a browse; the endpoint merely projects a read-model over an external Drive folder and an internal document collection. Because the operation is safe, intermediaries are within their rights to treat it as cacheable in principle, although the AI-mediated listing makes the response non-deterministic enough that aggressive caching is inadvisable; consumers should treat each response as a fresh snapshot rather than a stable resource representation. The folder identifier is expressed as a path segment (`:folder_identifier`) rather than a query parameter precisely because it *identifies the resource being browsed* — it is the noun of the URL, not an adverbial refinement of it, which is the textbook REST distinction between a path parameter and a query parameter.

In Domain-Driven Design terms this handler sits squarely in the *application/interface* layer and orchestrates two distinct ports without leaking either into the other: the `ArtificialIntelligencePort` (an anti-corruption boundary around whatever completion model backs the deployment) and the `DocumentCollectionPort` (the persistence-facing view of the ingested knowledge aggregate). The handler itself owns no domain invariants; it composes small, individually-testable helper functions into a read pipeline. The one genuine domain value object it constructs is `NonEmptyText`, used to guarantee that a folder identifier is never the empty string before it is ever interpolated into a model prompt or a collection query — a small but principled refusal to let an invalid value cross a boundary.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request must traverse the full type-state pipeline before this handler body ever executes. The handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, and the compiler will not allow the handler to run unless the request has already been carried through `Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended (validation stage) | `x-request-id: 3f2a9c1e-8b44-4c7e-bf1a-9d2e6c0a1122` | Correlation identifier attached at the `Validated` stage. Echoed through logs and error traces so a single browse can be followed end-to-end. If omitted, an identifier is typically synthesized upstream; supplying your own is strongly preferred for traceability. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@example.org` | The caller's account identity, consumed at the `Authenticated`/`Authorized` stages. Absence or an unparseable value causes the pipeline to reject the request with `401` before the handler runs. It is the principal against which folder-browse authorization is decided. |

The **type-state pipeline** is the enforcement mechanism behind the table above, and it is enforced by the Rust type system rather than by defensive runtime checks inside the handler:

1. **Validated** — The inbound request is first parsed into `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>`. This stage confirms the structural well-formedness of the request: headers such as `x-request-id` are read here, and any malformed envelope is rejected as `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` before authentication is even attempted. A request that fails validation can never advance to the next state; the type parameter literally forbids it.
2. **Authenticated** — A validated request is promoted to `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthenticated>` only after the caller's identity (`x-account-email`) is established. Missing credentials yield `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; present-but-unusable credentials yield `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. There is no code path that produces an `Authenticated` value without a proven identity.
3. **Authorized** — Finally, an authenticated request is promoted to `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — the exact type this handler demands — only after the authenticated principal is confirmed to be permitted to perform this operation. A denied principal produces `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. Because the handler's signature names `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, it is *statically impossible* to invoke this handler with a request that has not been validated, authenticated, and authorized in that order. The `_authorized_request` binding is deliberately unused inside the body: its sole purpose is to encode, at the type level, that all three gates were passed.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `folder_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Trimmed of surrounding whitespace; must be non-empty after trimming (parsed into `NonEmptyText`). A blank or whitespace-only value is rejected. | None | The Google Drive folder identifier whose contents are to be listed. Used both to build the AI listing prompt and to match previously ingested documents via their `sourceFolderIdentifier`. |

**Query parameters:** None are consumed by the route as currently wired. The handler constructs an *empty* `HashMap` internally and passes it to the pagination helpers, so `cursor` and `pageSize` in the URL query string are **silently ignored today**. The helper functions (`parse_optional_pagination_cursor_from_query`, `parse_requested_page_size_or_default`) are written to read a `cursor` key and a `pageSize` key and to degrade gracefully to defaults, but no wiring exists to populate the map from the request's query string. In practice this means the effective page size is always the default (see below) and the effective cursor is always absent.

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` endpoint and the handler reads **no request body whatsoever**. There is no `Json<...>` body extractor in the handler signature; the only extractors are `State`, the type-state `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, and the `Path` segment. Any body sent with the request is ignored.

For completeness, the accepted request body is the empty object:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "BrowseRagDriveFolderRequestBody",
  "description": "This GET endpoint reads no request body. The only valid body is none; an empty object is shown for completeness.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

```typescript
// This endpoint reads no request body. An empty interface documents that fact.
export interface BrowseRagDriveFolderRequestBody {}
```

```rust
// The handler declares no body extractor; this mirror is intentionally empty.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct BrowseRagDriveFolderRequestBody {}
```

```javascript
const folderIdentifier = "1AbCDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRsTuVwXyZ012345";
const response = await fetch(
  `https://api.example.org/api/rag/drive/folder/${encodeURIComponent(folderIdentifier)}`,
  {
    method: "GET",
    headers: {
      "x-request-id": "3f2a9c1e-8b44-4c7e-bf1a-9d2e6c0a1122",

);

if (!response.ok) {

const payload = await response.json();
console.log(payload.files, payload.nextCursor, payload.previouslyIngestedCount);
```

#### Successful Response

The handler returns `Json<Value>` with HTTP `200 OK`. The envelope contains a `folder` object, a `files` array (each element normalized and classified), a `returnedCount`, a nullable `nextCursor`, a boolean `hasMore`, and a `previouslyIngestedCount` inserted after the base envelope is assembled.

**Top-level response fields**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `folder` | object | Describes the browsed folder. Contains a single `id` string equal to the trimmed folder identifier. |
| `folder.id` | string | The folder identifier that was browsed (post-trim). |
| `files` | array of objects | The normalized, page-limited, ingestion-annotated entries in the folder. |
| `returnedCount` | integer | Number of elements in `files` (i.e. `files.length`). |
| `nextCursor` | string \| null | Opaque cursor for the next page — the `id` of the last returned entry — or `null` when the page was not full (fewer than `pageSize` entries), signalling no further pages. |
| `hasMore` | boolean | `true` iff `nextCursor` is non-null. |
| `previouslyIngestedCount` | integer | Count of documents in the `rag_knowledge` collection whose `sourceFolderIdentifier` matches this folder. Independent of the returned page. |

**Per-file fields (`files[]`)**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Entry identifier from the model's `id` key (trimmed, non-empty; rows lacking it are dropped). |
| `name` | string | Display name — whitespace-collapsed; `"Untitled"` when the source name was empty/blank. |
| `mimeType` | string | Declared MIME type, trimmed; defaults to `application/octet-stream` when absent. |
| `kind` | string | Classification tag: one of `folder`, `pdf`, `json_corpus`, `plain_text`, `spreadsheet`, `unknown`. |
| `size` | integer | Byte size; parsed from a number or a numeric string; `0` when missing/unparseable. |
| `alreadyIngested` | boolean | `true` when this entry's normalized display name matches a previously-ingested document name for this folder. |
