Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with exactly two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `request_body_was_malformed` | `title` key missing; `title` not a string; `title` whitespace-only; or `NonEmptyText::parse` rejects the title. Also emitted if a persistence error surfaces as `DomainInvariantViolated`. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"The discussion body is missing the required 'title' field."}` |
| `401` | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | The `x-account-email` header is absent. Raised by the extractor before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"the 'x-account-email' header was absent"}` |
| `401` | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` is non-UTF-8 text, or its value fails to parse as a valid email. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the account header did not parse into a valid email address"}` |
| `403` | `authorization_was_denied` | No authenticated principal survives to the authorization stage, or the persistence port returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied`. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| `404` | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | The persistence port returns `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` / `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` during insert (unusual for a create, but mapped). | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| `500` | `upstream_application_failure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from `insert_document` (e.g. transport failure, serialization failure, unexpected backend error). | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"an unexpected upstream failure occurred"}` |

**Full example error body:**

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "The discussion 'title' field must not be empty."
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler calls these real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_required_discussion_title_from_body(&body)` — pulls `title`; rejects missing key, non-string, or whitespace-only as `RequestBodyWasMalformed`; returns the trimmed string.
2. `parse_discussion_title_into_non_empty(raw_title)` — parses the trimmed title into a domain `NonEmptyText`, mapping any parse failure to `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
3. `extract_discussion_content_from_body(&body)` — reads optional `content`, defaulting to `""` when missing or non-string.
4. `extract_discussion_tags_array_from_body(&body)` — returns the `tags` value only if it is a genuine JSON array, else `[]`.
5. `extract_optional_linked_prompt_identifier(&body)` — clones `linkedPromptId` verbatim or yields JSON `null`.
6. `extract_optional_linked_prompt_title(&body)` — clones `linkedPromptTitle` verbatim or yields JSON `null`.
7. `generate_new_discussion_identifier()` — mints a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` as the discussion id.
8. `current_iso8601_timestamp_string()` — returns the fixed timestamp constant `2026-07-07T00:00:00Z`.
9. `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` — retrieves the guaranteed-present authenticated `Email`.
10. `build_persisted_discussion_document_body(...)` — assembles the full JSON body; internally calls `normalize_discussion_tags_into_lowercase_strings` (trim/lowercase/de-dup/drop non-strings) and `build_author_block_from_principal` (constructs the `author` sub-object).
11. `assemble_discussion_stored_document(id, principal, body)` — wraps the body in a `StoredDocument` with `owning_account` set to the principal's email.
12. `persist_discussion_document(collection, stored_document)` — awaits `insert_document(DISCUSSIONS_COLLECTION_NAME, ...)` on the `DocumentCollectionPort`, mapping `ApplicationError` to `HttpError` via `map_discussion_persistence_error_into_http_error`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and `author.joinedAt` are all a hardcoded constant** (`2026-07-07T00:00:00Z`, the `DISCUSSION_DEFAULT_JOINED_AT` constant). There is no wall-clock dependency wired in; every discussion is "created" at the same fictional instant, regardless of when the request actually arrives.
- **Tag normalization is lossy and case-flattening.** `["Rust", "  RUST ", "Axum", 7, "", "web"]` becomes `["rust", "axum", "web"]` — casing is destroyed, duplicates collapse, non-string entries (`7`) and empty strings vanish. If a client relies on preserving original casing or numeric tags, it will be disappointed.
- **`title` is trimmed twice and validated twice** — once in `extract_required_discussion_title_from_body` (reject empty, trim) and again through `NonEmptyText::parse`. A title of purely whitespace is rejected at the first gate; the second gate is belt-and-suspenders.
- **`linkedPromptId` / `linkedPromptTitle` are stored verbatim with no type checking.** A client can send a number, an object, an array, or `null` and it will be persisted and echoed unchanged. There is no validation that these reference an existing prompt.
- **Success returns `200`, not `201`, and carries no `Location` header** — despite being a creation endpoint. Clients scripting for RESTful `201 Created` semantics must not assert on the status code.
- **`author.displayName` is just the email.** There is no separate display name concept; `id`, `email`, and `displayName` are all identical, and `avatarUrl` is always `null`.
- **Unknown request fields are silently dropped.** Only the six recognized keys are read; typos like `titel` will produce a `400` (missing `title`) even though the payload looked "full".

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: If I POST the same body twice, do I get one discussion or two?**
A: Two. Each call generates its own UUID. This endpoint has no idempotency key, no dedup, and no mercy.

**Q: Why does the `createdAt` on my brand-new discussion say July 2026 no matter when I call it?**
A: Because the timestamp is a hardcoded constant, not a clock read. The handler comment is candid about it: no wall-clock dependency is wired for handlers, so a fixed, well-formed timestamp keeps the response shape deterministic.

**Q: I sent `"tags": "rust"` and got an empty tags array back. Bug?**
A: Working as designed. Only genuine JSON arrays are honored for `tags`; a bare string collapses to `[]` so the stored shape stays stable. Wrap it: `"tags": ["rust"]`.

### `POST /api/prompts-sharing/comments` — Store a Prompt Comment

Persists a single comment (a top-level reaction or a threaded reply) attached to an existing prompt template within the community prompt-sharing surface. The endpoint accepts a free-form JSON object, extracts and validates the target prompt identifier and the comment content, verifies that the referenced prompt template actually exists, mints a fresh comment identifier and creation timestamp, and stores the assembled document in the `prompt_comments` collection owned by the authenticated principal. On success it returns an acknowledgement payload that echoes back the freshly stored comment body verbatim.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is a textbook example of a non-idempotent, unsafe `POST` in the REST sense: each invocation with an identical request body produces a *new*, distinct comment document with its own server-minted UUID and its own creation timestamp. There is no client-supplied idempotency key, no conditional-request header handling, and no upsert semantics; the handler always calls `insert_document`, never an update path. Consequently `POST /api/prompts-sharing/comments` is neither safe (it mutates the store) nor idempotent (repeating it multiplies rows), which is exactly why it lives under `POST` rather than `PUT` or `PATCH`. Callers that retry on network failure must be prepared for duplicate comments, because the server has deliberately assigned itself sole authority over identity generation and refuses to let the client dictate the comment's identifier.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, the handler sits squarely in the HTTP adapter layer of the `alma-http` crate and orchestrates — but does not itself embody — domain logic. It leans on the `alma-domain` value objects (`NonEmptyText`, `Email`) to enforce invariants at the boundary, and it speaks to persistence exclusively through the `DocumentCollectionPort` abstraction, treating the underlying store as an opaque bag of `StoredDocument`s keyed by identifier. The "comment" is modelled as a schemaless JSON document tagged with `record_kind: "prompt_comment"` rather than as a first-class aggregate root, reflecting a pragmatic, document-oriented placement: the community category prizes flexibility of shape over rigid relational modelling, and threading is expressed simply by carrying an optional `parent_comment_identifier` pointer rather than by materialising a formal reply tree.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This handler receives an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, meaning the request must have already traversed the full type-state authentication and authorization pipeline before the handler body ever executes. The authenticated principal (an `Email`) is read via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` and is used both to stamp the comment's `author` block and to set the `owning_account` of the stored document.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `ada.lovelace@example.org` | Identifies the calling principal. Parsed into a domain `Email`; becomes the comment author and the document's `owning_account`. Missing or unpar.seable values are rejected upstream before the handler runs. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `7f3c1c9e-1b2a-4d4e-8a11-9c2b6f0e4d21` | Correlation identifier for tracing and log stitching. Echoed through the pipeline; if absent, upstream middleware may synthesise one. Not read by this handler directly. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/json` | The body is deserialized with `axum::Json<Value>`; a non-JSON or malformed body is rejected before the handler runs. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** The `alma-http` request pipeline is encoded as a sequence of Rust type-states, each a distinct marker type parameterising `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`. A request first becomes `Validated` once its shape and baseline headers are checked; it then transitions to `Authenticated` once the `x-account-email` header has been resolved into a verified principal identity; and finally it becomes `Authorized` once the pipeline has confirmed that this principal is permitted to perform the requested action. Because this handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the compiler itself guarantees that no code path can invoke the handler with a request that has not walked every prior stage. This is the whole point of the type-state pattern: an unauthenticated or unauthorized request is not merely rejected at runtime — it is *unrepresentable* at the type level as an argument to this function.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then reads specific fields out of it by hand. Only the fields below are consulted; any additional properties are ignored (never persisted, never echoed).

**(a) Fields read by the handler**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target_prompt_identifier` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; must not be blank/whitespace-only once trimmed; a matching prompt template must exist in the `prompt_templates` collection | — | Identifier of the prompt template this comment is attached to. |
| `comment_content` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; must parse as a `NonEmptyText` (non-empty after domain validation); must be ≤ 4,000 characters (counted by Unicode scalar values via `chars().count()`) | — | The actual comment text. |
| `parent_comment_identifier` | string \| null | No | If present and a non-blank string, used as-is; otherwise treated as `null` (a top-level comment) | `null` | Identifier of the parent comment when this is a threaded reply. |

**(b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)**

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "StorePromptCommentRequest",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "target_prompt_identifier": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Identifier of the prompt template this comment is attached to. Must not be blank once trimmed."
    },
    "comment_content": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "maxLength": 4000,
      "description": "The comment text. Non-empty after trimming; at most 4000 characters."
    },
    "parent_comment_identifier": {
      "type": ["string", "null"],
      "description": "Parent comment identifier for a threaded reply, or null for a top-level comment."
    }
  },
  "required": ["target_prompt_identifier", "comment_content"],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

**(c) TypeScript interface**

```typescript
interface StorePromptCommentRequest {
  /** Identifier of the prompt template this comment is attached to. Must not be blank. */
  target_prompt_identifier: string;
  /** The comment text. Non-empty, at most 4000 characters. */
  comment_content: string;
  /** Parent comment identifier for a threaded reply; omit or null for a top-level comment. */
  parent_comment_identifier?: string | null;
}
```

**(d) Rust struct mirror**

The handler does not actually deserialize into a struct (it reads a `serde_json::Value` field by field), but the following struct faithfully mirrors the fields it consumes:

```rust
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct StorePromptCommentRequest {
    /// Required. Identifier of the target prompt template; must be non-blank.
    target_prompt_identifier: String,
    /// Required. Comment text; must be non-empty and <= 4000 characters.
    comment_content: String,
    /// Optional. Parent comment identifier for threaded replies; None => top-level.
    #[serde(default)]
    parent_comment_identifier: Option<String>,
}
```

#### Request Examples

```bash
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

  -H "x-request-id: 7f3c1c9e-1b2a-4d4e-8a11-9c2b6f0e4d21" \
  -d '{
        "target_prompt_identifier": "prompt-8a2f7c",
        "comment_content": "This prompt worked beautifully for summarisation.",
        "parent_comment_identifier": null
      }'
```

**HTTPie**

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK` with a JSON acknowledgement payload built by `build_stored_comment_acknowledgement_payload`. It carries the new identifier, a fixed acknowledgement string, and the full stored comment body under `stored_comment`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string (UUID v4) | The server-minted identifier of the stored comment. |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Fixed literal `"prompt comment stored"`. |
| `stored_comment` | object | The full persisted comment document (see nested fields below). |
| `stored_comment.comment_identifier` | string (UUID v4) | Same value as `document_identifier`. |
| `stored_comment.target_prompt_identifier` | string | The prompt template the comment is attached to. |
| `stored_comment.comment_content` | string | The validated comment text. |
| `stored_comment.parent_comment_identifier` | string \| null | Parent comment id, or `null` for a top-level comment. |
| `stored_comment.author` | object | Author block. |
| `stored_comment.author.author_email_address` | string | The authenticated principal's email address. |
| `stored_comment.author.author_display_label` | string | Local part of the email before `@` (falls back to full address if no `@`). |
| `stored_comment.created_at` | string | ISO-8601 / RFC-3339 UTC timestamp `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. |
| `stored_comment.record_kind` | string | Fixed literal `"prompt_comment"`. |

**JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)**

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "StorePromptCommentResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "document_identifier": { "type": "string" },
    "acknowledgement": { "type": "string", "const": "prompt comment stored" },
    "stored_comment": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "comment_identifier": { "type": "string" },
        "target_prompt_identifier": { "type": "string" },
        "comment_content": { "type": "string" },
        "parent_comment_identifier": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
        "author": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "author_email_address": { "type": "string" },
            "author_display_label": { "type": "string" }
          },
          "required": ["author_email_address", "author_display_label"]
        },
        "created_at": { "type": "string" },
        "record_kind": { "type": "string", "const": "prompt_comment" }
      },
      "required": [
        "comment_identifier",

        "comment_content",

```

**Realistic 200 example**

```json
{
  "document_identifier": "3d0c8b1a-9f2e-4c77-a1b2-6e5d4c3b2a10",
  "acknowledgement": "prompt comment stored",
  "stored_comment": {
    "comment_identifier": "3d0c8b1a-9f2e-4c77-a1b2-6e5d4c3b2a10",

    "comment_content": "This prompt worked beautifully for summarisation.",

      "author_email_address": "ada.lovelace@example.org",

    },

  }
```

#### Error Responses

Errors are serialized as an `HttpError` into a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `target_prompt_identifier` missing/not a string; `target_prompt_identifier` blank once trimmed; `comment_content` missing/not a string; `comment_content` fails `NonEmptyText::parse`; `comment_content` exceeds 4,000 characters; or a downstream `DomainInvariantViolated` during persistence | `{ "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed", "error_explanation": "the request body must include a string field 'comment_content'" }` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The `x-account-email` header is absent; rejected in the pipeline before this handler runs (the handler requires `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`) | `{ "error_category": "AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing", "error_explanation": "authentication credentials were missing" }` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | The supplied credentials/email could not be validated by the pipeline; rejected before this handler runs | `{ "error_category": "AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid", "error_explanation": "authentication credentials were invalid" }` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The persistence layer returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` (principal not permitted to act on the resource); or the pipeline denies authorization before the handler runs | `{ "error_category": "AuthorizationWasDenied", "error_explanation": "the authenticated principal is not authorized to act on this resource" }` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No prompt template exists with the given `target_prompt_identifier` (from `ensure_target_prompt_template_exists`); or a `RequestedResource/ProjectCouldNotBeLocated` surfaces during a store operation | `{ "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound", "error_explanation": "no prompt template exists with identifier 'prompt-8a2f7c'" }` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from the document collection (e.g. a `DocumentCollectionFailure`) when fetching the template or inserting the comment | `{ "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure", "error_explanation": "document collection failure: disk on fire" }` |

**Full SerializedErrorBody example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "no prompt template exists with identifier 'prompt-8a2f7c'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. `extract_required_target_prompt_identifier_from_body` — read the required string field `target_prompt_identifier`; 400 if missing or not a string.
2. `validate_target_prompt_identifier_is_non_empty` — reject a blank/whitespace-only prompt identifier with a 400 before touching the store.
3. `extract_required_comment_content_from_body` — read the required string field `comment_content`; 400 if missing or not a string.
4. `enforce_maximum_comment_character_budget` — reject content longer than 4,000 Unicode scalar values with a 400 (boundary of exactly 4,000 is accepted).
5. `parse_comment_content_into_non_empty` — parse the raw text into a domain `NonEmptyText`; 400 on domain validation failure.
6. `extract_optional_parent_comment_identifier` — read the optional `parent_comment_identifier`; normalise a non-blank string to a JSON string, otherwise JSON `null`.
7. `ensure_target_prompt_template_exists` — `fetch_document` from `prompt_templates`; 404 if the template does not exist, mapping collection errors via the error mapper.
8. `generate_new_comment_identifier` — mint a fresh UUID v4 string for the comment.
9. `current_iso8601_timestamp_string` — capture the creation instant, delegating to `format_unix_seconds_as_iso8601` (which uses `is_leap_year` and `month_lengths_for_year`) to hand-format a `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` UTC string without a date crate.
10. `build_comment_author_block_from_principal` — build the author block, using `display_label_from_email` to derive a friendly label from the email local part.
11. `build_persisted_comment_document_body` — assemble the full JSON document body (content, ids, author, timestamp, `record_kind`).
12. `assemble_comment_stored_document` — wrap the body in a `StoredDocument` whose `owning_account` is the principal's email.
13. `persist_prompt_comment_document` — `insert_document` into the `prompt_comments` collection, mapping failures via the error mapper.
14. `build_stored_comment_acknowledgement_payload` — build the 200 acknowledgement echoing the identifier and stored body.
15. `map_comment_persistence_error_into_http_error` — translate `ApplicationError` variants into the appropriate `HttpError` (404 / 403 / 400 / 500).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Not idempotent.** Every successful call inserts a brand-new comment with a new UUID and new timestamp. Retrying a request after a timeout can silently create duplicate comments — the server accepts no client-supplied idempotency key.
- **`parent_comment_identifier` is never validated for existence.** A reply can point at a parent that does not exist (or was deleted); the handler only checks that the *prompt template* exists, not the parent comment. A blank/whitespace parent string is silently coerced to `null` (a top-level comment) rather than rejected.
- **Character budget counts Unicode scalar values, not bytes.** The 4,000 limit uses `chars().count()`, so multi-byte emoji or CJK characters each count as one; a 4,000-character comment may be far larger than 4,000 bytes on the wire. The boundary is inclusive: exactly 4,000 is accepted, 4,001 is rejected.
- **Timestamp is hand-rolled and second-granular.** `created_at` is computed from `SystemTime` with plain integer arithmetic (no chrono), always in UTC, always ending in `Z`, with no sub-second precision. If the system clock is before the Unix epoch, the code falls back to `0` seconds (i.e. `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`).
- **Extra body fields are silently ignored.** Because the body is read as an untyped `Value`, unknown properties are neither rejected nor persisted; only the three recognised fields survive into the stored document, which itself is augmented with server-side fields (`author`, `created_at`, `record_kind`).
- **`document_identifier` and `comment_identifier` are always equal.** The acknowledgement's top-level `document_identifier` and the nested `stored_comment.comment_identifier` are the same minted UUID; do not assume they can diverge.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I choose my own comment identifier by putting one in the body?**
A: No. The identifier is minted server-side with `Uuid::new_v4()`. Any `comment_identifier` you send in the body is ignored — it is not among the fields the handler reads.

**Q: Why did my 4,000-emoji comment get rejected as too long when it's "only 4,000 characters"?**
A: The limit is 4,000, inclusive, counted by `chars().count()`. If you sent 4,001 scalar values you exceeded it. Emoji are one `char` each here, so 4,001 emoji is 4,001 characters and is rejected regardless of byte size.

**Q: Does the endpoint verify the parent comment I'm replying to actually exists?**
A: No. It only verifies the target *prompt template* exists (404 otherwise). A `parent_comment_identifier` is stored as-is with no existence check, so orphaned replies are entirely possible.

### `POST /api/prompts-sharing` — Store a Community Prompt Template

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts a JSON document describing a shareable prompt template — a `title`, a `content` body, an optional `category`, and an optional array of `tags` — and durably persists it into the `prompt_templates` document collection under the authenticated caller's identity. It stamps the newly created record with a freshly minted UUID-v4 identifier and an ISO-8601 UTC creation timestamp, attributes ownership to the authorized principal derived from the request headers, and returns an acknowledgement payload that echoes both the generated identifier and the full stored document body. It is the write half of the `/api/prompts-sharing` collection resource, whose read half is served by `GET /api/prompts-sharing`.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the REST vocabulary, this handler is the canonical `POST`-to-a-collection creation operation: the client does not know, and cannot dictate, the identity of the resource it is creating, so it submits a representation to the collection URI (`/api/prompts-sharing`) and delegates identifier minting to the server. Because the server generates a brand-new UUID-v4 on every invocation (`generate_new_prompt_template_identifier`), the operation is deliberately **non-idempotent** and **non-safe**: replaying the identical request body twice produces two distinct persisted documents with two distinct identifiers, and the operation mutates server state. This is exactly the semantic contract `POST` promises and `PUT` does not; a caller who wants at-most-once semantics must implement their own de-duplication upstream, because this endpoint offers none.

Within a Domain-Driven Design framing, the prompt template is a lightweight aggregate whose only enforced invariants are the non-emptiness of `title` and `content` — both validated through the `NonEmptyText` value object at the HTTP boundary — and the presence of an owning `Email` principal, which is guaranteed structurally by the type-state pipeline rather than by a runtime check inside the handler. The handler itself is a thin application-service orchestration: it performs boundary validation, assembles a persistence-shaped `StoredDocument`, and hands that document to the `DocumentCollectionPort`, keeping the transport concern (axum, JSON) and the persistence concern (the collection port) cleanly separated. Notably, the handler works against `serde_json::Value` rather than a strongly-typed request DTO, so schema enforcement is imperative and field-by-field rather than declarative.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 3f9a2c14-77b0-4c2e-9a1e-2b6d5e0f1a22` | Correlation identifier threaded through the pipeline; the `validate()` stage rejects an empty/whitespace value with `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. Not read inside this handler directly, but load-bearing for the pipeline to reach the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` state. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: scholar@example.com` | Establishes the authenticated principal. Parsed into a domain `Email`; becomes the `owning_account` and the `author.author_email` of the stored document via `authorized_principal()`. Absent/invalid credentials cause the request to fail before the handler body executes. |

**The type-state pipeline (Validated → Authenticated → Authorized).** This handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, and that generic parameter is not decorative — it is a compile-time proof. A request begins life as `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated>` via `originate(correlation_identifier)`. Calling `.validate()` checks that the correlation identifier (`x-request-id`) is non-empty and yields `RequestHasBeenValidated`. Calling `.authenticate(email)` attaches the principal derived from `x-account-email` and yields `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`. Calling `.authorize()` verifies a principal is actually present and yields `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, or returns `AuthorizationWasDenied` if none is. Only the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` marker type exposes `authorized_principal()`, and it does so via an `.expect(...)` that is infallible precisely because the type system has already ruled out the `None` case. In other words, the handler cannot even be compiled to run against an unauthorized request; the moment `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` appears in the source, the surrounding stages are statically guaranteed to have executed. The panic in `authorized_principal()` is therefore unreachable in practice — the type-state is the guard.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the raw body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and reads each field imperatively. Every field the handler actually inspects is listed below.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; trimmed of surrounding whitespace; must be non-empty after trimming (validated via `NonEmptyText::parse`). | — | Human-readable name of the prompt template. Stored trimmed. |
| `content` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; must not be blank (fails if `trim()` is empty); validated via `NonEmptyText::parse` but stored **untrimmed**, preserving internal and leading/trailing whitespace. | — | The prompt template body itself. |
| `category` | string | No | If present and a non-blank string, it is trimmed and lowercased. Non-string or blank values are ignored. | `"general"` | Classification label. Falls back to `"general"` when absent, non-string, or blank. |
| `tags` | array of string | No | Must be a JSON array to be read at all; non-array values are treated as empty. Each element must be a string; elements are trimmed, lowercased, de-duplicated, and empty results dropped. Non-string elements are silently ignored. | `[]` | Free-form tag list. Persisted as a normalized lowercase, de-duplicated string array. |

Any other keys present in the submitted JSON are ignored entirely — the handler never rejects unknown fields.

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` as `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `title` missing/non-string; `title` blank after trim; `content` missing/non-string; `content` blank; a `DomainInvariantViolated` bubbles up from persistence; empty correlation id at the pipeline `validate()` stage. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"a string 'title' field is required"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | `x-account-email` absent, so no principal can be established during the pipeline's authenticate stage (raised upstream of this handler). | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` present but not a parseable/valid `Email` credential (raised upstream of this handler). | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Authenticated but no principal survived to the authorize stage, or an `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` surfaces from the collection port. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Not produced by this creation endpoint in normal operation; reserved. Would only appear if the collection port returned `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated`, which insertion does not. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | The `DocumentCollectionPort::insert_document` call fails with any `ApplicationError` other than the specially-mapped variants (e.g. `DocumentCollectionFailure`). | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the document collection failed: boom"}` |

**Full serialized error body example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "prompt template content must not be blank"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates these real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_required_prompt_template_title_from_body` — reads the required string `title` field; errors `400` if missing or non-string.
2. `parse_prompt_template_title_into_non_empty` — trims and validates the title into a `NonEmptyText`; errors `400` if blank/invalid.
3. `extract_required_prompt_template_content_from_body` — reads the required string `content` field; errors `400` if missing or non-string.
4. `parse_prompt_template_content_into_non_empty` — rejects blank content, then validates into `NonEmptyText` **without trimming**; errors `400` on failure.
5. `extract_prompt_template_category_from_body` — reads optional `category`, trims + lowercases, defaults to `"general"`.
6. `extract_prompt_template_tags_array_from_body` — reads optional `tags`; returns the array if present, else an empty array.
7. `normalize_prompt_template_tags_into_lowercase_strings` — trims, lowercases, drops empties, and de-duplicates the tag strings (non-strings ignored).
8. `generate_new_prompt_template_identifier` — mints a new UUID-v4 string identifier.
9. `current_iso8601_timestamp_string` → `format_unix_seconds_as_iso8601` — computes the current UTC instant and formats it as `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` via a civil-from-days algorithm.
10. `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` — retrieves the owning `Email` from the type-state-proven authorized request.
11. `build_template_author_block_from_principal` — builds the `{ "author_email": ... }` sub-document.
12. `build_persisted_prompt_template_document_body` — assembles the complete JSON document (identity, title, content, category, tags, author, timestamps, `document_kind`).
13. `assemble_prompt_template_stored_document` — wraps the body into a `StoredDocument` with identifier and `owning_account`.
14. `persist_prompt_template_document` — calls `DocumentCollectionPort::insert_document(PROMPT_TEMPLATES_COLLECTION_NAME, ...)`; on failure maps via `map_prompt_template_persistence_error_into_http_error`.
15. `map_prompt_template_persistence_error_into_http_error` — converts an `ApplicationError` into an `HttpError` via the canonical `From` impl.
16. `build_stored_template_acknowledgement_payload` — builds the returned `{ document_identifier, acknowledgement, stored_template }` payload.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`content` is stored untrimmed while `title` is stored trimmed.** The title is `raw_title.trim()`-ed before validation and storage, but content is validated for non-blankness via `trim().is_empty()` yet passed to `NonEmptyText::parse(raw_content)` *unchanged* — so leading/trailing/internal whitespace and newlines in `content` are preserved verbatim in the persisted document.
- **Category is silently coerced, never rejected.** A non-string `category` (e.g. a number), a blank string, or a missing field all yield `"general"` with no error. There is no way to tell from the response whether the client supplied a bad category or none at all.
- **Tags are silently sanitized.** Non-array `tags`, non-string array elements, blank tags, and duplicate tags are all dropped without error. Casing is destroyed (everything lowercased) and ordering after de-duplication follows first-occurrence order — clients cannot rely on their original tag list round-tripping.
- **Every request creates a new document — no idempotency.** Because the identifier is a fresh UUID-v4 per call, submitting the same body N times creates N distinct templates. There is no upsert, no dedup, and no client-supplied identifier is honored (any `template_identifier` in the request body is ignored and overwritten).
- **Ownership is server-assigned from `x-account-email`, not the body.** Even if the body contained an `author` field, it would be ignored; `owning_account` and `author.author_email` come exclusively from the authorized principal. A client cannot forge authorship.
- **Unknown fields are accepted and discarded.** The schema is effectively open (`additionalProperties: true` in practice) — extra keys neither error nor persist, which can mask client typos (e.g. `titlee`) that then surface as a `400` for the *missing* real field.
- **The success status is `200`, not `201`.** Despite being a creation operation, axum's `Json(Value)` return renders `200 OK` rather than the more RESTfully-correct `201 Created`, and no `Location` header is emitted.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I specify my own `template_identifier` so my writes are idempotent?**
A: No. The server mints a UUID-v4 on every call and overwrites anything you send. If you POST twice, you get two templates. Idempotency is your problem, not the endpoint's.

**Q: I sent `category: "Research"` and got back `"research"`. Is that a bug?**
A: No. Category is trimmed and lowercased server-side by design. If you need the original casing, keep it somewhere else — this field is normalized on the way in and there is no opt-out.

**Q: My `content` has trailing newlines and they came back. Shouldn't they be trimmed like the title?**
A: No, and this is deliberate asymmetry. Titles are trimmed; content is validated for non-blankness but stored exactly as sent, whitespace and all, so that multi-line prompt formatting survives the round trip.

---

### `POST /api/prompts-sharing/versions` — Store a New Immutable Prompt Version

#### Synopsis

This endpoint stores a new, immutable version of a shared community prompt. Each invocation appends a fresh version document to the `prompt_versions` collection: the document references a *parent prompt* (the logical prompt the user is iterating on), carries the full verbatim prompt text of that revision, an optional human-readable change note, and a server-computed, monotonically increasing sequence number derived from the versions already persisted for that same parent. The caller receives back the freshly minted version identifier and the sequence number that was assigned.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of HTTP semantics this is a resource-creation operation, and it is deliberately modelled as a `POST` to a *collection* URI (`/api/prompts-sharing/versions`) rather than a `PUT` to a client-nominated version URI. The distinction is not merely academic: `PUT` carries an implicit contract of idempotency — repeating it yields the same resource at the same address — whereas the act of "cutting a new version" is intrinsically non-idempotent. Every call mints a brand-new UUID via `Uuid::new_v4()`, stamps a fresh wall-clock `created_at`, and computes a *new* sequence number one greater than the current maximum. Replay the exact same request body ten times and you get ten distinct version documents with ten distinct sequence numbers. `POST` is therefore the only honest verb here: it is neither safe (it mutates server state) nor idempotent (repetition compounds), and the response is a 200 acknowledgement of a created side effect rather than a 201 with a canonical `Location` — a design choice this API makes uniformly across its community write handlers.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, a "prompt version" is an immutable *event-like value* within the community bounded context: once written it is never mutated in place, which is why versioning-by-append rather than mutation-in-place is the storage model. The handler lives in the `community` category of the HTTP crate and leans on two application-layer ports — `DocumentCollectionPort` for reading/writing version documents and (via `ApplicationState`) the transactional `UnitOfWork` boundary. The domain leaks in through two value objects: `Email` (the authoring principal, sourced from the type-state pipeline, never from the request body — the client cannot spoof authorship) and `NonEmptyText` (which enforces the invariant that a version's prompt text is meaningfully present). The sequence number is a derived, server-authoritative fact: clients neither supply it nor can override it, because the server always recomputes it from the persisted set.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 7f3c1a9e-2b44-4c8d-9f01-8ab6d2e0c115` | Correlation identifier. Threaded through the pipeline as the `correlation_identifier`; must be present and non-empty (a blank value fails validation with `RequestBodyWasMalformed`). Echoed into logs for request tracing. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: author@example.com` | Identifies the authenticating principal. Parsed into a domain `Email` and used as the `authored_by` / `owning_account` of the persisted version. This is the *sole* source of authorship — any `authored_by` in the request body is ignored. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | The body is deserialized by axum's `Json` extractor as `serde_json::Value`; a non-JSON or unparseable body is rejected before the handler runs. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** This handler does not receive a raw request. Its second argument is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — a request that has already traversed a compile-time-enforced state machine encoded in the type parameter. The stages are:

1. **`RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated`** — the request is originated from the incoming `x-request-id` as a `correlation_identifier`, with no principal yet attached.
2. **`RequestHasBeenValidated`** — `validate()` asserts the correlation identifier is non-empty (trimming whitespace); an empty one yields `RequestBodyWasMalformed { "the correlation identifier was empty" }`. The type now guarantees a usable correlation id.
3. **`RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`** — `authenticate(Email)` attaches the principal derived from `x-account-email`. The type now guarantees a *declared* principal.
4. **`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`** — `authorize()` confirms a principal is actually present; if none is, it returns `AuthorizationWasDenied`. Only in this final state does `.authorized_principal()` exist, and it is total (it `expect`s a principal, which the type-state has already proven present).

Because the handler's signature demands `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, it is *structurally impossible* to reach handler code with an unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request — the compiler rejects any wiring that skips a stage. `authorized_principal()` is therefore infallible inside the handler.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The route `/api/prompts-sharing/versions` is static — it declares no path segments and the handler reads no query string.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then reads three fields by name. Fields not listed below are silently ignored; in particular, `sequence_number`, `authored_by`, `version_identifier`, `created_at`, and `resource_kind` are **server-controlled** and any client-supplied values for them are discarded.

##### (a) Field table

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parent_prompt_identifier` | string | Yes | Trimmed; must be non-empty after trimming. Missing, non-string, or blank -> `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. | — | Identifier of the logical parent prompt this version belongs to. Used to scope the sequence-number computation. |
| `prompt_text` | string | Yes | Must be present and a string; then parsed into domain `NonEmptyText` (rejects blank/whitespace-only). Missing/non-string -> `RequestBodyWasMalformed`; blank -> `RequestBodyWasMalformed` (domain error text). | — | The full prompt text of this revision, stored verbatim. Not trimmed before persistence (only validated as non-empty). |
| `change_note` | string | No | If present must be a string; trimmed. Non-string or absent -> treated as absent. | `""` (empty string) | Optional human-readable note describing what changed in this revision. |

```javascript
const acknowledgement = await response.json();
console.log(acknowledgement.document_identifier, acknowledgement.sequence_number);
```

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns HTTP `200 OK` with a small acknowledgement payload. Note that the *persisted* document is richer than the acknowledgement — the response returns only the identifier and sequence number, not the full stored record.

##### Response field table

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string (UUID v4) | The freshly generated identifier of the persisted version document. |
| `sequence_number` | integer (u64, >= 1) | The server-assigned sequence number: `max(existing sequence numbers for this parent) + 1`, or `1` if this is the first version. |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Constant literal `"prompt version stored"`. |

##### Response JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "StorePromptVersionResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "document_identifier": { "type": "string", "format": "uuid" },
    "sequence_number": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 },
    "acknowledgement": { "type": "string", "const": "prompt version stored" }
  },
  "required": ["document_identifier", "sequence_number", "acknowledgement"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

##### Realistic 200 example

```json

  "document_identifier": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",
  "sequence_number": 4,
  "acknowledgement": "prompt version stored"
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` into a `SerializedErrorBody` with exactly two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The table below lists every `HttpError` variant and precisely when it can arise for *this* endpoint.

| Status | error_category | When (for this endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `parent_prompt_identifier` missing / non-string / blank; `prompt_text` missing / non-string; `prompt_text` blank (fails `NonEmptyText::parse`); or (upstream, pre-handler) an empty `x-request-id` correlation identifier. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"field 'prompt_text' is required and must be a string"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | Raised by the pipeline before the handler when authenticating credentials (`x-account-email`) are absent. Not raised inside this handler. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | Raised by the pipeline before the handler when the supplied credentials cannot be parsed/validated (e.g. a malformed email). Not raised inside this handler. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Raised at the pipeline's `authorize()` stage when no authenticated principal is present; also mapped from `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` should a downstream port deny access. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Not produced by the happy path of this handler (it appends rather than looking up a target). Only surfaces if a downstream port returns `ApplicationError::RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` while listing/inserting. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"..."}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | The document collection port fails while listing existing versions (`list_documents`) or inserting the new version (`insert_document`) — any `ApplicationError` other than the specifically-mapped ones becomes this. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"..."}` |

##### Full serialized error body example

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "field 'parent_prompt_identifier' is required and must be a non-empty string"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_required_parent_prompt_identifier_from_body` — pulls `parent_prompt_identifier` from the body, trims it, and errors with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if missing, non-string, or blank.
2. `validate_parent_prompt_identifier_is_non_empty` — a redundant belt-and-braces guard re-asserting the trimmed identifier is non-empty.
3. `extract_required_version_prompt_text_from_body` — pulls `prompt_text` as a string (untrimmed), erroring if missing or non-string.
4. `parse_version_prompt_text_into_non_empty` — parses the raw text into the domain `NonEmptyText`, mapping any domain error to `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
5. `extract_optional_version_change_note_from_body` — reads the optional `change_note`, trims it, and defaults to `""` when absent or non-string.
6. `fetch_existing_versions_for_parent_prompt` — lists *all* documents in `prompt_versions` and filters to those whose stored `parent_prompt_identifier` matches (may raise `UpstreamApplicationFailure`).
7. `read_parent_prompt_identifier_from_version_body` — reads the parent identifier out of a stored version body (used by the filter above).
8. `compute_next_version_sequence_number` — computes `max(existing sequence numbers) + 1`, defaulting to `1` when there are none.
9. `read_version_sequence_number_from_body` — reads a stored `sequence_number` (falls back to `0` when missing/invalid).
10. `generate_new_prompt_version_identifier` — mints a fresh UUID v4 for the new version.
11. `current_iso8601_timestamp_string` — captures the current wall-clock time as an ISO-8601 / RFC-3339 UTC string (`format_unix_seconds_as_iso8601`, computed without a date crate via `is_leap_year` and `month_lengths_for_year`).
12. `build_persisted_prompt_version_document_body` — assembles the persisted JSON body (`version_identifier`, `parent_prompt_identifier`, `prompt_text`, `change_note`, `sequence_number`, `authored_by`, `created_at`, `resource_kind: "prompt_version"`).
13. `assemble_prompt_version_stored_document` — wraps the body in a `StoredDocument` owned by the authoring principal's email.
14. `persist_prompt_version_document` — inserts the document into the `prompt_versions` collection (may raise `UpstreamApplicationFailure`).
15. `build_stored_version_acknowledgement_payload` — builds the 200 acknowledgement payload returned to the client.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Sequence numbers are global-to-parent, not gap-free.** The next sequence is `max + 1` computed from currently-persisted versions. If a version is ever deleted, the next number will not "fill the gap"; and because the computation is read-then-write with no locking, two concurrent requests for the same parent can both read the same max and both write the same sequence number (a classic race — last-writer-does-not-win, both succeed with duplicate sequences).
- **The list-then-filter is O(collection).** `fetch_existing_versions_for_parent_prompt` lists *every* document in `prompt_versions` and filters in memory. There is no server-side query by parent; this scales linearly with the total number of versions across all parents.
- **`prompt_text` is not trimmed.** Unlike the identifier and change note, `prompt_text` is stored verbatim. Leading/trailing whitespace survives to storage; only the *non-empty after domain parse* invariant is enforced, so `"   x   "` is accepted and stored as-is.
- **Authorship cannot be spoofed.** `authored_by` and `owning_account` come exclusively from the pipeline's authorized `Email` (from `x-account-email`), never the body. A body field named `authored_by` is ignored entirely.
- **The parent is never verified to exist.** The handler happily creates a version for a `parent_prompt_identifier` that references no real prompt. There is no existence check and thus no `404` on the happy path — an orphan version is a valid outcome.
- **Extra body fields are silently accepted.** The body is an untyped `Value`; unknown keys (including attempts to set `sequence_number` or `version_identifier`) are ignored without error.
- **Timestamps are second-precision UTC only.** `created_at` is a hand-rolled `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` string with no sub-second precision and no timezone offset other than `Z`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I set the `sequence_number` myself to force a specific version order?**
A: No. Any `sequence_number` in your body is ignored. The server always computes it as `max(existing) + 1`. You get the number you are given.

**Q: Why do I get a 200 and not a 201 Created with a `Location` header?**
A: Because this API returns a JSON acknowledgement (`document_identifier` + `sequence_number`) with `200 OK` for its community write handlers. There is no `Location` header. Read `document_identifier` from the response body instead.

**Q: I sent the same body twice and now I have two versions. Bug?**
A: Working as designed. `POST` here is non-idempotent by definition — each call mints a new UUID, a new timestamp, and a new sequence number. If you want deduplication, do it before you call.

---

### `POST /api/3d-printing` — Store a 3D Printing Design

#### Synopsis

Accepts a JSON payload describing a single community-contributed 3D printing design, validates and normalizes it, synthesizes a complete public-facing document (identifier, author block, timestamps, STL reference metadata, empty vote/comment scaffolding), and persists it into the `three_d_printing_designs` document collection. On success it returns the exact persisted document body as JSON. The endpoint is authenticated and authorized: the calling principal (an `x-account-email`) becomes the owning account and author of the design.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is a canonical resource-creation operation in the REST sense: a `POST` to a collection URL (`/api/3d-printing`) that appends a new subordinate resource to that collection and returns the freshly minted representation. Because a brand-new server-generated identifier is minted on every invocation (`generate_new_design_identifier` produces a fresh UUIDv4), the operation is deliberately **neither safe nor idempotent** — replaying the same request body twice creates two distinct designs with two distinct identifiers. This is the correct and expected semantics for a `POST`-to-collection creation verb; callers wanting idempotency would need to layer their own deduplication key on top, because the handler itself performs no such collapsing.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler is a thin application-layer orchestrator living squarely in the HTTP adapter (the `http` crate). It does not itself own business invariants beyond the crudest input hygiene; instead it defers the one genuine domain invariant it enforces — that a design title must be non-empty — to the `NonEmptyText` value object from `alma_domain`, and delegates all persistence to the `DocumentCollectionPort` behind the application's `ApplicationState`. The design is stored as an opaque `serde_json::Value` document (`StoredDocument`) keyed by a generated identifier and tagged with the owning account, which keeps the community feature schema-flexible while the transactional boundary and storage concerns remain firmly on the far side of the port. The handler is, in short, a translation membrane: JSON in, validated/normalized document out, port call, JSON echo back.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This endpoint is only reachable once the request has traversed the full type-state pipeline and reached the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` stage. The extractor for `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` reads two headers off the incoming request; both are effectively required to reach the handler body.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes (recommended) | `x-request-id: 7f3c9b2a-1e4d-4c6b-9a2f-0d8e1c5b6a77` | Correlation identifier (`CORRELATION_IDENTIFIER_HEADER_NAME`). Threaded through the pipeline for tracing/log correlation. Absence does not by itself deny the request body logic here, but supplying it is strongly expected for observability. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: designer@alma.test` | Authenticated account (`AUTHENTICATED_ACCOUNT_HEADER_NAME`). This value becomes the authorized principal; it is parsed into an `Email`, exposed via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()`, and stamped onto the stored design as `owning_account`, `authorId`, and the entire `author` block. A missing or invalid value causes the pipeline to reject the request before this handler ever runs. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | Required for axum's `Json<Value>` extractor to parse the body. A wrong or missing content type / unparseable body yields a body-rejection error. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The alma-http stack encodes request lifecycle as a compile-time type-state machine on `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`, where the stage marker types (`RequestHasBeenValidated`, `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`, `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`) are uninhabited enums used purely as phantom witnesses. A raw request is first `validate()`d (structural/header sanity) producing a `RequestHasBeenValidated`; that value is then `authenticate(...)`d against the `x-account-email` header, producing a `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`; that is finally `authorize()`d, producing a `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. Only the fully-`Authorized` type exposes `authorized_principal() -> &Email`. Because this handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` as an extractor, it is **statically impossible** for the handler body to execute unless the request has already passed validation, authentication, and authorization — the compiler, not a runtime `if`, guarantees the principal is present and trustworthy by the time line 52 (`authorized_request.authorized_principal()`) runs.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and reads the following fields by name. Unknown/extra fields are silently ignored; they are neither stored nor rejected.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; after domain parse must be non-empty (non-blank per `NonEmptyText::parse`). Untrimmed raw value is read, emptiness enforced by the value object. | — | Human-readable name of the design. Missing or non-string → `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. |
| `description` | string | No | Must be a string to be honored; any non-string/absent value falls back to default. | `""` | Short description of the design. |
| `content` | string | No | Must be a string to be honored; else default. | `""` | Freeform notes / body text (e.g. print settings). |
| `tags` | array | No | Honored only if it is a JSON array; any non-array/absent value falls back to default. Element types are not validated. | `[]` | Arbitrary tag list, stored verbatim. |
| `stlFileName` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string, non-empty after trimming, and (case-insensitively) end with `.stl`. Value is trimmed before storage. | — | Reference file name for the STL. Missing/blank → malformed; wrong extension → malformed. |
| `stlFileSize` | integer (u64) | No | Read via `as_u64`; must be a non-negative integer to be honored, else defaults. Must not exceed `256 * 1024 * 1024` (268435456) bytes. | `0` | Declared STL payload size in bytes. Oversized → malformed. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The table lists all `HttpError` variants and precisely when each can occur for THIS endpoint.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Body is not valid JSON; `title` missing/non-string; `title` blank (fails `NonEmptyText::parse`); `stlFileName` missing/non-string/blank; `stlFileName` not ending in `.stl`; `stlFileSize` exceeds 256 MiB. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"A string 'title' field is required for a 3D printing design."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Pipeline authentication stage: `x-account-email` absent. Rejected before handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were missing."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Pipeline authentication stage: `x-account-email` present but not a parseable/valid account email. Rejected before handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were invalid."}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Pipeline authorization stage: authenticated principal is not permitted to reach this route. Rejected before handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"Authorization was denied."}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not produced by this handler's own logic (creation endpoint mints its own id). Reserved variant; would only arise from routing/framework-level miss. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"The requested resource was not found."}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | `document_collection.insert_document(...)` fails; the `ApplicationError` is wrapped by `map_design_persistence_error_into_http_error`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"Failed to persist the 3D printing design: <cause>"}` |


#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler calls the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_required_design_title_from_body` — reads the required `title` string; missing/non-string → `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. `parse_design_title_into_non_empty` — parses the raw title into a domain `NonEmptyText`; blank → malformed.
3. `extract_design_description_from_body` — reads optional `description`, defaulting to `""`.
4. `extract_design_content_from_body` — reads optional `content`, defaulting to `""`.
5. `extract_design_tags_array_from_body` — reads optional `tags`, defaulting to `[]` if absent or not an array.
6. `extract_required_stl_file_name_from_body` — reads and trims required `stlFileName`; missing/blank → malformed.
7. `validate_stl_file_name_has_stl_extension` — enforces a case-insensitive `.stl` suffix.
8. `extract_stl_file_size_from_body` — reads optional `stlFileSize` (u64), defaulting to `0`.
9. `enforce_maximum_stl_file_size_budget` — rejects sizes above 256 MiB.
10. `generate_new_design_identifier` — mints a fresh UUIDv4 identifier.
11. `current_iso8601_timestamp_string` — returns the fixed reference epoch timestamp string.
12. `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` — obtains the owning `Email` from the authorized pipeline state.
13. `build_persisted_design_document_body` — assembles the full public document body (internally calls `build_design_author_block_from_principal` to build the `author` block).
14. `persist_three_d_printing_design_document` — inserts the `StoredDocument` into the `three_d_printing_designs` collection via `DocumentCollectionPort::insert_document`.
15. `map_design_persistence_error_into_http_error` — maps any collection failure to `UpstreamApplicationFailure` (invoked only on persistence error).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Not idempotent.** Every call mints a new UUIDv4 `id`; sending the same body twice creates two independent designs. There is no dedup key.
- **Timestamps are frozen.** `createdAt`/`updatedAt`/`author.joinedAt` are the constant `2026-07-07T00:00:00Z` (`DEFAULT_AUTHOR_JOINED_AT`), not a wall clock. This is intentional for deterministic tests — do not treat these as real event times.
- **`id` is overloaded.** The single generated identifier is reused for `id`, `googleDriveFolderId`, and `stlFileId`. They are always equal at creation; do not assume they are independent.
- **`stlFileSize` is declared, not measured.** The handler never sees the actual STL bytes; it only stores the client's claimed size (defaulting to `0`). The 256 MiB check guards against absurd declarations, not real payloads. A lying client can report `0` for a huge file.
- **Type coercion is lenient for optionals but strict for required fields.** `description`/`content`/`tags`/`stlFileSize` silently fall back to defaults when the wrong type is supplied (e.g. `tags: "x"` → `[]`, `stlFileSize: "big"` → `0`), whereas `title` and `stlFileName` hard-fail if the wrong type/blank.
- **Author identity is entirely email-derived.** `authorId`, `author.id`, `author.email`, and `author.displayName` are all the same `x-account-email` string; `avatarUrl` is always `null`. There is no richer profile lookup.
- **Extra fields are dropped.** Any body field the handler does not read (e.g. `voteScore`, `id`, `thumbnailUrl` supplied by the client) is ignored — server-controlled fields cannot be spoofed via the request.
- **Response is `200`, not `201`.** Despite being a creation, the handler returns `200 OK` with the body and no `Location` header.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I set the design's `id`, `voteScore`, or `createdAt` from the request?**
A: No. Those are server-synthesized. Anything you send under those keys is ignored; the handler only reads `title`, `description`, `content`, `tags`, `stlFileName`, and `stlFileSize`.

**Q: Why did my upload of `part.STL` succeed but `part.obj` fail?**
A: The extension check is case-insensitive and requires exactly a `.stl` suffix. `part.STL` ends with `.stl` (lowercased); `part.obj` does not. The check inspects the file name string only — it never opens or validates STL contents.

**Q: I POSTed the identical design three times. Why do I have three entries?**
A: This is a creation endpoint and is not idempotent by design. Each POST mints a fresh UUIDv4. If you need at-most-once semantics, deduplicate on the client before calling, because the server will not do it for you.

### `POST /api/alma-videos/registry` — Append a Video Registry Entry

Appends exactly one video registry entry — describing a single Google-Drive-hosted video (its human-readable title, its Google Drive file identifier, and its owning channel) — to the durable `video_registry` document collection. The handler validates every field of the submitted JSON payload, resolves the owning account from the authorized principal, guards against duplicate entries that reference the same Google Drive file identifier, and then persists a normalized `StoredDocument` owned by the authenticated caller. On success it returns a compact confirmation object echoing the freshly generated document identifier alongside the post-append registry size.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is, in the purest REST sense, an *append* operation: it takes a client-supplied representation and creates a new subordinate resource inside a server-managed collection. `POST` is the only semantically honest verb here because the operation is neither **safe** (it mutates durable server state by inserting a document) nor **idempotent** (there is no client-supplied key that would make a second identical submission collapse into the first — instead the server mints a brand-new `Uuid::new_v4()` identifier on every call, so a naive retry of the *same* payload would ordinarily produce a *second* row). The one and only thing standing between you and duplicate rows is the application-level de-duplication guard keyed on `google_drive_file_identifier`; that guard is a business invariant, not an HTTP idempotency contract, and you should not mistake it for one. Because a distinct identifier is generated per request, the correct mental model is "create-with-server-assigned-key," which is precisely why the collection lives behind `POST /registry` and not `PUT /registry/{id}`.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, this handler sits squarely in the **HTTP boundary layer** (the `alma-http` crate) and does the unglamorous but essential work of anti-corruption: it accepts a loose, untyped `serde_json::Value`, coerces each field into a domain value object (`NonEmptyText`, `Email`), and only then hands a well-formed body down to the persistence port (`document_collection.insert_document`). Notice the deliberate separation of the *pure* `build_registry_entry_document_body` from the *side-effect-adjacent* `enrich_registry_entry_document_body_with_optionals`: the former stays trivially unit-testable and free of optional-field noise, while the latter layers on nullable metadata. The owning account is never trusted from the request body; it is derived exclusively from the type-state-proven authorized principal, keeping tenancy ownership an authoritative server concern rather than a client suggestion.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request to this endpoint is funneled through the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor, which reads two headers off the incoming request parts before the handler body ever runs.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: francesco@example.com` | The authenticated principal. Absence yields `401 authentication_credentials_were_missing`. A value that is not valid text, or that does not parse as an email via the `email_string_prism`, yields `401 authentication_credentials_were_invalid`. This value becomes the document's `owning_account`. |
| `x-request-id` | No | `x-request-id: 7f3c1a2e-9d4b-4c11-8a55-2b0e6f1d9c33` | Correlation identifier for tracing/observability. Optional — when absent, the pipeline substitutes the literal string `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"`. It is never validated and never affects the response body. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The handler's second argument, `authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, is not a plain struct — it is a *type-state* proof. The `FromRequestParts` implementation for `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` executes a strict, compile-time-enforced escalation ladder in `crates/http/src/pipeline/extractor.rs`:

1. It resolves the `x-request-id` correlation identifier (falling back to `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"`).
2. It reads `x-account-email`; a missing header is `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, a non-textual header value is `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`, and a value that fails the `email_string_prism` preview is `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`.
3. It constructs `HttpRequestInPipeline::originate(correlation_id).validate()?` → producing a `RequestHasBeenValidated`.
4. It calls `.authenticate(parsed_principal)?` on that → producing a `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`.
5. It calls `.authorize()?` on that → producing the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` the handler demands.

Because the handler's signature *requires* `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, it is structurally impossible for the handler body to run against a request that has not passed all three stages — the compiler rejects any attempt to reach the handler with a lesser stage. Once inside, `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` returns the proven `&Email`, which this handler re-parses (defensively) into an owning `Email` value object.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint takes no path segments and reads no query-string parameters whatsoever.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then reads the following fields by name. Three are required; two are optional. Any JSON key not listed below is silently ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; trimmed; must be non-empty after trimming (parsed via `NonEmptyText::parse`). | — | Human-readable title of the video. Stored verbatim (trimmed) as `title`. |
| `google_drive_file_identifier` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; trimmed; must be non-empty (`NonEmptyText::parse`). Must not already exist in the registry. | — | The Google Drive file identifier the entry points at. Used as the de-duplication key. |
| `channel_name` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; trimmed; must be non-empty (`NonEmptyText::parse`). | — | The owning channel's display name. Also stored normalized (lowercased, whitespace-collapsed) as `normalized_channel_name`. |
| `duration_seconds` | integer | No | Must be a JSON integer parseable as `i64`; values `< 0` are discarded (treated as absent). | `null` | Optional video duration in seconds. Persisted as `duration_seconds` (or `null`). |
| `thumbnail_url` | string | No | Must be a JSON string; trimmed; an empty-after-trim string is coerced to `null`. | `null` | Optional thumbnail URL. Persisted trimmed as `thumbnail_url` (or `null`). |

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK`. The body is the confirmation object rendered by `render_appended_registry_entry_confirmation`, augmented in the handler with `registry_entry_count`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string (UUID v4) | The server-generated identifier of the newly appended registry document. |
| `title` | string | Echo of the accepted, trimmed title. |
| `channel_name` | string | Echo of the accepted, trimmed channel name (the original, not the normalized form). |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Always the constant `"registry entry appended"`. |
| `registry_entry_count` | integer | Total registry entries expected to exist immediately after this append (prior count + 1). |
