#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The variants below are the full `HttpError` surface; the "When (for THIS endpoint)" column describes whether and how each can actually arise here.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Registry is **not empty** (double-init guard fires), OR the reconstructed default owner email fails `Email::parse`. Note: reused as the guard/validation error here despite no body being read. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"video registry already contains 3 entries and cannot be re-initialized"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Pipeline stage before the handler: `x-account-email` absent. Handler never runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Pipeline stage before the handler: supplied credentials could not be resolved to a valid caller. Handler never runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Pipeline authorization stage: authenticated caller lacks permission for this route. Handler never runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not produced by this handler's own logic. Would only appear via routing/framework layers, not the seeding code path. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"requested resource was not found"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Underlying `DocumentCollectionPort` failure — from `list_documents` (via `?`) or from any `insert_document` call (mapped by `HttpError::from`). A per-document insert failure is also counted into `videosFailed` rather than aborting. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"document collection unavailable"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "video registry already contains 3 entries and cannot be re-initialized"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEO_REGISTRY_COLLECTION_NAME)` — reads all currently-stored registry documents (collection name `"video_registry"`); errors propagate via `?` as `UpstreamApplicationFailure`.
2. `validate_registry_is_empty_before_initialization(&existing_documents)` — the double-init guard; returns `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if the registry already holds any entries.
3. `parse_default_channel_owner_email(DEFAULT_SEED_CHANNEL_NAME)` — reconstructs and validates the owning `Email` from the slug; itself calls `reconstruct_email_from_channel_slug`.
4. `reconstruct_email_from_channel_slug(channel_slug)` — heuristically turns `roberto_almalearn_at_gmailcom` into an email-like string by splitting on `_at_`, replacing `_` with `.`, and appending `.com` to a dotless domain.
5. `build_seed_registry_entry_bodies(DEFAULT_SEED_CHANNEL_NAME)` — produces the three fixed seed bodies; internally calls `build_single_seed_registry_entry_body` three times.
6. `build_single_seed_registry_entry_body(title, gdrive_id, channel)` — assembles one seed body JSON (`title`, `googleDriveFileId`, `channelName`, `source: "seed"`).
7. `partition_seed_bodies_into_new_and_existing(seed_bodies.clone(), &existing_documents)` — splits seeds into new vs. already-present (existing set is discarded here); relies on `seed_entry_is_new`.
8. `count_seed_entries_added(&seed_bodies, &existing_documents)` — counts seeds that are new (the intent count).
9. `count_seed_entries_skipped(&seed_bodies, &existing_documents)` — counts seeds already present.
10. `seed_entry_is_new(seed_body, existing_documents)` — true when the seed's `googleDriveFileId` is not already registered; missing ids are treated as new.
11. `determine_seed_entry_was_already_registered(existing_documents, id)` — scans existing docs' `googleDriveFileId` for a match; uses the two `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_*` helpers.
12. `generate_registry_entry_identifier()` — mints a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` string per new document.
13. `assemble_seed_registry_document(id, &owning_account, seed_body)` — wraps id + owner + body into a `StoredDocument`.
14. `insert_seed_registry_documents(document_collection, seed_documents)` — inserts each document via `insert_document`, collecting per-doc outcomes; returns the successfully-inserted count.
15. `map_seed_insertion_failure_count(&insertion_outcomes)` — counts failed inserts inside the insertion routine.
16. `render_registry_initialization_summary(effective_added, skipped, failed, channel)` — builds the final JSON summary; internally calls `compute_total_videos_after_initialization(added, skipped)`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Non-empty registry is a hard 400, not a no-op.** If even one document already exists, `validate_registry_is_empty_before_initialization` fails and the whole call returns `RequestBodyWasMalformed` — despite no request body being involved. The error category is semantically misleading here; it is reused as a generic validation error.
- **The request body is completely ignored.** You cannot customize the seed set, channel, or owner via the payload. All three seed entries (`gdrive_seed_0001..0003`) and the channel `roberto_almalearn_at_gmailcom` are compile-time constants.
- **The de-dup partitioning is nearly vestigial in practice.** Because initialization is guarded to only run on an empty registry, `existing_documents` is always empty when the seeding proceeds — so `videosSkipped` is always `0` and the partition's "already existing" bucket (`_already_present_bodies`) is discarded (`_`-prefixed). The skip machinery exists defensively but cannot fire on the happy path.
- **`videosFailed` reflects partial persistence failures, not aborts.** `insert_seed_registry_documents` does not stop on the first failing insert; it records each outcome and returns only the success count. A partial upstream outage can therefore yield `200 OK` with, e.g., `videosAdded: 2, videosFailed: 1`. Whether an insert error surfaces as a hard `500` or as a counted failure depends on the port's behavior — errors are mapped with `HttpError::from` inside the async insert loop.
- **The owning email is synthesized, not real.** `reconstruct_email_from_channel_slug` is explicitly lossy: `roberto_almalearn_at_gmailcom` becomes `roberto.almalearn@gmailcom.com` (dotless domain gets `.com` appended). This is only meant to satisfy `Email::parse`; do not treat the stored `owning_account` as a deliverable address.
- **Fresh UUIDs every run.** Each seeded document gets a new `Uuid::new_v4()` identifier, so document identifiers are non-deterministic across (hypothetical) re-inits — de-duplication keys on `googleDriveFileId`, never on `document_identifier`.
- **`RequestedResourceWasNotFound` cannot originate in this handler's logic** — it is listed for completeness but no code path here emits it.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I re-run this to add more seed videos later?**
A: No. The second call sees a non-empty registry and returns `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. This is a bootstrap primitive, not an upsert. Use `POST /api/alma-videos/registry` (the append endpoint) to add entries afterward.

**Q: Why does a `POST` that reads nothing from the body still return a `400 "RequestBodyWasMalformed"`?**
A: Because that variant is reused as the endpoint's generic validation/guard error. The "malformed body" name is a historical artifact of the shared `HttpError` enum; the actual trigger is a non-empty registry (or an email that fails to parse), not your payload.

**Q: `videosSkipped` is always `0`. Is the skip logic dead code?**
A: Effectively yes on the happy path. Initialization only proceeds when the registry is empty, so no seed can collide with an existing entry. The counting and partitioning helpers are kept for defensive symmetry and are fully unit-tested, but they cannot produce a non-zero skip count during a real init.

**Q: Which collection does this write to, and can I change it?**
A: It writes to the collection named `video_registry` (the `VIDEO_REGISTRY_COLLECTION_NAME` constant). It is not configurable via the request; it is a hard-coded constant shared with the other registry handlers.

### `GET /api/alma-videos/channels` — List All Distinct Video Channels

#### Synopsis

This endpoint enumerates the distinct set of *channels* that are present across the entire `videos` document collection, returning for each channel a compact summary object (identifier, human-friendly display name, raw channel key, video count, most-recent upload timestamp, and a representative thumbnail URL). It performs no filtering, no pagination, and no client-supplied input handling beyond authorization; it simply reads every stored video document, folds them into per-channel aggregates, and returns the fully materialized listing wrapped in an envelope with a `channelCount`. When the collection yields no discoverable channels, the handler deterministically substitutes a default trio of channels so that downstream UI never renders an empty channel picker.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a REST-semantic standpoint this is the archetypal *collection read*: an unconditionally safe, side-effect-free `GET` whose purpose is to project a derived, denormalized view over an underlying document store. Because it is a `GET`, it is both **safe** (invoking it never mutates server state — it only calls `list_documents`) and **idempotent** (calling it once or one thousand times leaves the system in the same observable state, network and clock permitting). Note, however, that safety is not the same as *purity of representation*: the response is time-dependent (upload timestamps drift) and content-dependent (channels appear and disappear as documents are added or removed), so while the verb is idempotent the *body* is emphatically not deterministic across time. Consumers who conflate "idempotent verb" with "cacheable-forever payload" will be disappointed; the resource is a live projection, not a frozen artifact.

Within the broader Domain-Driven Design topology of the alma-http service, this handler sits squarely in the thin **HTTP presentation layer** (`crates/http`), acting as a translator between the transport boundary and the application's `document_collection` port (`alma_application::ports::document_collection`). It deliberately performs its aggregation *in the handler* rather than pushing a bespoke query into the persistence adapter — a pragmatic concession that keeps the port surface narrow (`list_documents`) at the cost of moving the fan-out/fold logic up into the presentation tier. The lone domain touchpoint is the defensive parse of each channel name through `alma_domain::value_objects::NonEmptyText`, a value-object invariant check that guards the boundary even though the names were themselves synthesized from stored data. This is DDD hygiene bordering on ceremony: the code validates data it has, in most paths, already implicitly proven non-empty.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the service's type-state authentication pipeline before this handler's body executes. The handler's signature demands a `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is a compile-time proof token: the handler *cannot even be constructed* by the router unless the request has already passed validation, authentication, and authorization stages. Concretely, the middleware chain drives the request through three successive type-states:

- **`Validated`** — the raw inbound request has been structurally validated (well-formed transport envelope; required identity headers syntactically present). This is the entry state produced after the request survives the first middleware stage.
- **`Authenticated`** — the caller's identity (the account email carried in `x-account-email`) has been verified against the authentication mechanism, upgrading the token from `Validated` to `Authenticated`. A failure here yields `401`.
- **`Authorized`** (`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`) — the authenticated principal has been checked against the authorization policy for this route and granted access, upgrading the token to its final state. A failure here yields `403`.

Because each transition is encoded as a distinct Rust type, the type system makes it impossible to write a handler that reads authorized data without having threaded the request through all three stages first; there is no runtime "did I check auth?" branch to forget — the compiler enforces it.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended (echoed / traced) | `x-request-id: 6f1c2d3e-8a90-4b21-9f0e-1a2b3c4d5e6f` | Correlation identifier for tracing a single request across logs and the pipeline stages. If omitted, the service may synthesize one; supplying your own makes distributed debugging tractable. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: roberto@almalearn.example` | Identifies the calling principal. Consumed during the `Validated → Authenticated` transition. Missing or unparseable → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; present but rejected → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint reads no path segments beyond the literal route `/api/alma-videos/channels`, accepts no query string parameters, and ignores anything appended. There is deliberately no pagination, no `channel` filter, and no sort override — ordering is fixed (see below).

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

Any body sent by the client is silently ignored by the handler. For schema-completeness, the accepted body is the empty object.

#### Successful Response

**Status:** `200 OK` · **Content-Type:** `application/json`

The response is an envelope object with two top-level fields: `channels` (an array of per-channel summary objects) and `channelCount` (the length of that array). Each summary object carries exactly the six fields synthesized by `render_single_channel_summary`.

**Response field table**

| Field | Type | Nullable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | array&lt;object&gt; | no | The list of distinct channel summaries, sorted case-insensitively by raw channel name. |
| `channels[].id` | string | no | Stable folder identifier derived from the channel's ordinal index, formatted `folder_%04d` (1-based). E.g. index 0 → `folder_0001`. |
| `channels[].name` | string | no | Human-friendly display name derived from the raw channel key (email domain suffix `_at_...` stripped, `_`/`.`/`-` split, each word capitalized). E.g. `roberto_almalearn_at_gmailcom` → `Roberto Almalearn`. |
| `channels[].rawChannel` | string | no | The unmodified channel key exactly as stored in the documents' `channel` field. |
| `channels[].videoCount` | integer (i64) | no | Count of stored documents whose `channel` equals this channel. |
| `channels[].lastUpdated` | string | no | Most recent `uploadedAt` timestamp among this channel's documents (lexicographic max, valid for ISO-8601). Falls back to `2026-07-01T09:30:00.000Z` when none carry a timestamp. |
| `channels[].thumbnailUrl` | string \| null | yes | Thumbnail URL of the first document of this channel that carries a non-blank `thumbnailUrl`; JSON `null` if none. |
| `channelCount` | integer | no | Number of entries in `channels`. |

#### Error Responses

All errors are serialized by `HttpError` into a `SerializedErrorBody` of shape `{ "error_category": <string>, "error_explanation": <string> }`. The variants below are the full `HttpError` set; the "When" column describes whether/how each can actually surface for *this* handler.

| Status | error_category | When (for this endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Emitted by `parse_channel_name_into_non_empty_text` if a discovered (or default) channel name fails `NonEmptyText::parse` — i.e. an empty/blank name slipped through the boundary check. In practice extremely rare because blank channel names are filtered upstream. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"value must not be empty"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | Raised in the pipeline before the handler runs when the identity header (`x-account-email`) is absent or unparseable during `Validated → Authenticated`. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"missing account email header"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Raised in the pipeline when the supplied credentials are present but rejected by the authentication mechanism. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"account email failed authentication"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Raised in the pipeline during the `Authenticated → Authorized` transition when the authenticated principal is not permitted to access this route. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"principal not authorized for videos"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not produced by this handler's own logic (it lists a collection rather than fetching a keyed resource); reserved by the shared error type and would only appear if a lower layer surfaced it. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"resource not found"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Propagated via `?` when `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` fails (e.g. the persistence backend is unreachable or errors). | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"failed to list documents"}` |

**Full serialized error body example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "failed to list documents from collection 'videos'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions (numbering follows the annotations in the source), in this order:

1. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — asynchronously loads every `StoredDocument` in the `videos` collection; the sole I/O call, and the sole source of `UpstreamApplicationFailure`.
2. `collect_distinct_channel_names_from_documents(&stored_documents)` — walks every document and gathers the unique set of `channel` values, preserving first-seen order.
3. `extract_channel_name_from_stored_document(...)` — (helper of #2, #4, #6, #8) reads the `channel` string field from a document body, rejecting blank/whitespace values.
4. `fall_back_to_default_channel_names_when_empty(discovered_channels)` — substitutes a deterministic default trio (`roberto_almalearn_at_gmailcom`, `maria_docente_at_gmailcom`, `luca_studente_at_gmailcom`) when nothing was discovered.
5. `sort_channel_names_alphabetically(discovered_channels)` — sorts the channel names case-insensitively for stable, human-friendly ordering.
6. `parse_channel_name_into_non_empty_text(channel_name.clone())` — per-channel defensive boundary validation via `NonEmptyText::parse`; the only in-handler source of `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
7. `render_all_channel_summaries(&discovered_channels, &stored_documents)` — maps each channel (with its ordinal index) into a summary object.
8. `count_videos_belonging_to_channel(...)` — (per channel) counts matching documents into an `i64` `videoCount`.
9. `extract_latest_updated_timestamp_for_channel(...)` — (per channel) computes the lexicographic max of `uploadedAt` values, or `DEFAULT_CHANNEL_TIMESTAMP`.
10. `extract_uploaded_at_timestamp_from_document(...)` — (helper of #9) reads the `uploadedAt` string field, rejecting blanks.
11. `derive_channel_thumbnail_url_or_null(...)` — (per channel) finds the first document with a non-blank `thumbnailUrl`, else JSON `null`.
12. `extract_thumbnail_url_from_document(...)` — (helper of #11) reads the `thumbnailUrl` string field, rejecting blanks.
13. `derive_channel_folder_identifier(index)` — (per channel) formats the `folder_%04d` `id` from the 0-based index (1-based output).
14. `determine_channel_display_name_from_account(channel_name)` — (per channel) derives the friendly `name` by stripping the `_at_<domain>` suffix, splitting on `_`/`.`/`-`, and capitalizing each word via `capitalize_word`.
15. `render_single_channel_summary(...)` — assembles the six-field summary object per channel.
16. `build_channels_listing_envelope(rendered_channels)` — wraps the summaries into `{ "channels": [...], "channelCount": N }`, then returned as `Json(Value)`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Empty collection yields fabricated channels, not an empty list.** If no documents carry a non-blank `channel`, the response is *not* `{"channels":[],"channelCount":0}` — it is the hardcoded default trio with `channelCount: 3`. Clients cannot distinguish "genuinely three default channels" from "database was empty." A `videoCount` of `0` on all three is the only hint.
- **Sorting overrides discovery order.** `collect_distinct_channel_names_from_documents` preserves first-seen order, but `sort_channel_names_alphabetically` then re-sorts case-insensitively, so the final `id` (`folder_NNNN`) is assigned by *alphabetical index*, not insertion order. A channel's `id` can therefore change between calls as new channels are added and the alphabetical position shifts. Do **not** treat `id` as a stable primary key.
- **`lastUpdated` is a string max, not a parsed date.** The "most recent" timestamp is chosen by lexicographic `max()` over the raw `uploadedAt` strings. This is correct only for uniformly formatted, zero-padded, UTC ISO-8601 values. Mixed formats, missing millisecond padding, or non-UTC offsets can produce a wrong "latest" without any error.
- **The default timestamp is a real, plausible date.** When a channel has no dated documents, `lastUpdated` becomes `2026-07-01T09:30:00.000Z` — indistinguishable from a genuine upload at that instant. Consumers relying on `lastUpdated` for freshness/sorting may be misled by this sentinel.
- **`thumbnailUrl` is first-match, not newest.** The thumbnail is taken from the first document (in stored iteration order, filtered to the channel) that has a non-blank `thumbnailUrl` — *not* from the most recently uploaded video. The displayed thumbnail can be from an old video even though `lastUpdated` reflects a newer one.
- **The `NonEmptyText` boundary check is near-dead code that can still 400.** Discovered names are already filtered for non-blank, and the defaults are hardcoded non-empty, so validation almost never fails — yet a failure surfaces as `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`, a category that makes no sense for a bodyless `GET`. Treat a 400 here as an internal invariant violation, not a client error.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I filter to a single channel or paginate the results?**
A: No. There are no path or query parameters. You receive the entire distinct channel set every time. Filter client-side, or use `GET /api/alma-videos/channel/:channel_name` for a specific channel's videos.

**Q: Is `channels[].id` stable enough to store as a foreign key?**
A: No. `id` is `folder_%04d` derived from the *alphabetical index at request time*. Add or remove a channel and the indices — and thus the ids — shift. Use `rawChannel` as the durable key.

**Q: Why did I get three channels when my database is empty?**
A: By design. `fall_back_to_default_channel_names_when_empty` injects a default trio so the UI never renders an empty channel picker. An empty database and a three-default database look identical in the response envelope.

### `GET /api/alma-videos/registry` — List Video Registry Entries

#### Synopsis

Returns the full, denormalized listing of every document stored in the `video_registry` collection, rendered into a stable, consumer-friendly envelope under a top-level `registry` key. Each entry is guaranteed a `videoId`, a normalized `owningAccount`, and a derived `thumbnailUrl`; entries lacking a usable Google Drive file identifier are silently dropped, the survivors are sorted newest-upload-first, and — should the registry turn out empty — a pair of representative placeholder entries is synthesized so first-run and demo UIs never render a blank screen. The response additionally carries a compact `summaryRows` array for list previews that do not need each full body.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is the canonical **read model** of the video registry aggregate. In strict REST terms it is a *collection resource* accessed via the safe, idempotent `GET` verb: it MUST NOT mutate server state, it MAY be cached and prefetched, and any number of repeated invocations MUST be observationally equivalent to a single one (modulo concurrent writes from the sibling `POST /api/alma-videos/registry`). Note carefully that "safe" here is a promise about *externally observable side effects*, not about the shape of the payload — the handler performs a substantial amount of in-memory projection, normalization, filtering, sorting, and placeholder synthesis, all of which are pure functions of the persisted state at read time and therefore preserve the safety guarantee. The reader who conflates "safe" with "returns exactly what is in the database" will be disappointed; this is a *view*, not a *dump*.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, the handler is deliberately thin at the transport edge and delegates all shaping to a battery of small, individually-testable private functions (`render_registry_entry_bodies`, `inject_registry_entry_identifier_into_body`, `filter_registry_entries_by_optional_channel`, and so on), which together constitute an anti-corruption layer between the persistence port's `StoredDocument` representation and the JSON contract expected by downstream video consumers. The `document_collection` port is the aggregate's repository; the envelope builder is the read-side assembler. The endpoint's placement in the `videos` category — sharing the `/api/alma-videos/registry` path with its `POST` counterpart — reflects the CQRS-adjacent separation of the query path (this handler) from the command path (the append handler), even though both currently live behind the same route table.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Authentication and authorization are enforced upstream of the handler body by the request pipeline: the handler's second extractor, `_authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, will fail extraction — and therefore short-circuit the request with an error before a single line of listing logic runs — unless the request has successfully traversed the full pipeline. The leading underscore signals that the handler does not *read* the authorized principal; it merely *requires* that authorization has happened.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7c1a9f2e-3b4d-4e5f-8a91-2c3d4e5f6a7b` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces. Absence does not fail the request but cripples observability; supply a UUID per logical request. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: roberto_almalearn@gmail.com` | The caller's account identity. Consumed by the pipeline's authentication stage to establish the principal. A missing or blank value yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; a value that cannot be resolved to a valid principal yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** The `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>` type encodes the request's progress through the pipeline in its *type parameter*, making illegal states unrepresentable at compile time. A request begins its life in the **Validated** state once its transport-level shape (headers, method, path, body framing) has been checked. It is then promoted to the **Authenticated** state only after the `x-account-email` credential has been resolved to a concrete principal — this transition is where the two `401` variants originate (missing credential vs. invalid credential). Finally it is promoted to the **Authorized** state (`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`) once the authorization stage confirms the authenticated principal is permitted to perform *this* operation on *this* resource; failure here produces `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. Because this handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the Rust type system statically guarantees the handler body can never execute for a request that has not passed all three stages in order — there is no code path by which an unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request reaches the `list_documents` call.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

Note: the handler *contains* logic to parse an optional `channel` query parameter (`parse_optional_channel_filter_query_parameter`) and to filter by it (`filter_registry_entries_by_optional_channel`), but per the inline comment in the source, "the public listing endpoint carries no query string in the current route contract, so we resolve the optional channel filter against an empty map." The filter is wired against a hard-coded empty `HashMap`, so in the current contract there are no accepted query parameters and no channel filtering occurs. The scaffolding exists so a real `Query` extractor can be added later without touching the filtering path.

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` endpoint and reads **no request body**. Any body sent is ignored by the handler. For completeness, the accepted request body schema is the empty object:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "ListVideoRegistryEntriesRequestBody",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {}
}
```

```typescript
// No request body is read by this endpoint.
export type ListVideoRegistryEntriesRequestBody = Record<string, never>;
```

```rust
// No request body deserialization occurs in this handler.
// The handler's only extractors are State<ApplicationState<_>> and
// HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct ListVideoRegistryEntriesRequestBody {}
```

The `200 OK` body is a single JSON object with one top-level key, `registry`, whose value carries the listing.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `registry` | object | Top-level envelope. Always present. |
| `registry.entries` | array of object | Rendered listing bodies, sorted by `uploadDate` descending (undated entries sink to the bottom). Each entry is the persisted body augmented with guaranteed fields. Falls back to placeholder entries when the registry is empty. |
| `registry.entries[].videoId` | string | Stable identifier. Preserved from the body if present; otherwise injected from the stored `document_identifier`. |
| `registry.entries[].owningAccount` | string \| null | Normalized owning account; `null` when the stored document has no (non-blank) owner. Always overwritten by the handler. |
| `registry.entries[].thumbnailUrl` | string | Derived `https://drive.google.com/thumbnail?id=<googleDriveFileId>&sz=w320` when the body lacked a usable thumbnail. Left untouched if the body already carried a non-blank one. |
| `registry.entries[].googleDriveFileId` | string | Backing Drive file id. Entries missing this (after rendering) are dropped and never appear. |
| `registry.entries[].title` | string | Passed through from the stored body (not guaranteed). |
| `registry.entries[].channelName` | string | Passed through from the stored body (not guaranteed). |
| `registry.entries[].uploadDate` | string | ISO-8601 timestamp used for sorting and `lastUpdated` (not guaranteed). |
| `registry.entries[].*` | any | Any other fields present in the persisted body are passed through verbatim. |
| `registry.totalEntries` | integer | Count of documents *after* optional-channel filtering but *before* the file-id/placeholder rendering steps. May differ from `entries.length`. |
| `registry.lastUpdated` | string \| null | Maximum non-empty `uploadDate` across the rendered entries; `null` when no entry carries a date. |
| `registry.summaryRows` | array of object | Compact preview rows built directly from the matched stored documents (one per matched document, independent of the file-id filter applied to `entries`). |
| `registry.summaryRows[].videoId` | string | Stored `document_identifier`. |
| `registry.summaryRows[].title` | string \| null | Non-blank title or `null`. |
| `registry.summaryRows[].channelName` | string \| null | Non-blank channel name or `null`. |
| `registry.summaryRows[].googleDriveFileId` | string \| null | Non-blank Drive file id or `null`. |
| `registry.summaryRows[].owningAccount` | string \| null | Non-blank owning account or `null`. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` object of the form `{ "error_category": <string>, "error_explanation": <string> }`. The variants below enumerate the full `HttpError` surface; the "When" column describes how each can arise for *this specific endpoint*.

| Status | error_category | When (for this endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Not reachable through normal use — this endpoint reads no body. Reserved by the shared error type. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"The request body could not be parsed."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` header absent or blank; the pipeline's authentication stage cannot establish a principal, so `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extraction fails. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were missing."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` present but does not resolve to a valid principal. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were invalid."}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Principal authenticated but not authorized to list the video registry; the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` promotion fails. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"Authorization was denied for this request."}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not produced by the handler body itself — the registry listing returns placeholder entries rather than 404 when empty. May surface from routing/framework layers. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"The requested resource was not found."}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The `document_collection.list_documents(VIDEO_REGISTRY_COLLECTION_NAME)` call fails (persistence/port error); propagated via the `?` operator on line 25. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"An upstream application failure occurred."}` |

```json
{
  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "An upstream application failure occurred."
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler, after the pipeline has authorized the request, executes the following real helper functions in order:

1. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEO_REGISTRY_COLLECTION_NAME)` — asynchronously fetches all `StoredDocument`s from the `video_registry` collection; errors bubble up as `500 UpstreamApplicationFailure` via `?`.
2. `parse_optional_channel_filter_query_parameter(&empty_query_parameters)` — trims and interprets the optional `channel` filter; always resolves to `None` today because it is fed an empty `HashMap`.
3. `filter_registry_entries_by_optional_channel(registered_documents, requested_channel)` — case-insensitively keeps only documents whose `channelName` matches the requested channel; with `None`, passes all documents through unchanged.
4. `count_total_registry_entries(&matching_documents)` — counts the matched documents into `totalEntries` (computed before the file-id/placeholder rendering steps).
5. `render_registry_entry_summary_row` (mapped over `matching_documents`) — builds one compact `summaryRows` entry per matched document via `render_registry_entry_summary_row`, drawing on `extract_title_from_registry_document`, `extract_channel_name_from_registry_document`, `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_from_registry_document`, and `coerce_registry_entry_owning_account_to_value`.
6. `render_registry_entry_bodies(matching_documents)` — maps each stored document through `inject_registry_entry_identifier_into_body`, which guarantees `videoId`, overwrites `owningAccount`, and derives `thumbnailUrl` (via `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_from_registry_document` + `derive_thumbnail_url_for_registry_entry`) when absent.
7. `skip_registry_entries_missing_file_identifier(rendered_bodies)` — drops any rendered body without a non-blank `googleDriveFileId`.
8. `sort_registry_entries_by_uploaded_at_descending(rendered_bodies)` — sorts newest-first by `uploadDate` (via `extract_uploaded_at_from_registry_body`), with undated entries sinking to the bottom.
9. `build_placeholder_registry_entries()` — invoked only when the rendered list is empty; synthesizes two representative entries and re-runs them through the render+sort path.
10. `build_registry_listing_envelope(rendered_bodies, total_entries)` — assembles `{ registry: { entries, totalEntries, lastUpdated } }`, computing `lastUpdated` as the max non-empty `uploadDate`.
11. Post-envelope mutation — `envelope.get_mut("registry")` inserts the `summaryRows` array into the `registry` object before the whole thing is wrapped in `Json(...)` and returned.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`totalEntries` can disagree with `entries.length`.** `totalEntries` is counted from `matching_documents` *before* entries without a `googleDriveFileId` are dropped and before placeholder substitution. A registry of 5 documents where 2 lack a file id yields `totalEntries: 5` but only 3 entries.
- **Empty registry never returns an empty array.** When rendering produces zero entries, the handler swaps in two hard-coded placeholder videos (`v_0001`, `v_0002`). Clients cannot distinguish "genuinely empty" from "populated with these exact demo values" without inspecting the identifiers — and `totalEntries` will read `2` in the empty case because placeholders flow through the counting-independent envelope builder.
- **`owningAccount` is always overwritten.** Even if the persisted body already contains an `owningAccount`, `inject_registry_entry_identifier_into_body` unconditionally replaces it with the value coerced from `StoredDocument.owning_account` (or `null`). A body-level `owningAccount` is ignored.
- **`videoId` is preserved but `thumbnailUrl` is conditionally derived.** A pre-existing non-blank `videoId` in the body wins over the document identifier, but a blank/null/whitespace `thumbnailUrl` is regenerated from the Drive file id. If the body has no `googleDriveFileId`, no thumbnail is derived — yet such an entry is then dropped anyway by step 7.
- **`summaryRows` and `entries` are not row-aligned.** `summaryRows` is built from all matched documents (step 5), while `entries` has the file-id filter and placeholder logic applied. A document with no `googleDriveFileId` will appear in `summaryRows` (as `null`) but be absent from `entries`.
- **The `channel` filter is dead code today.** Despite full parsing/filtering/case-insensitive-matching logic and tests, the handler feeds it an empty `HashMap`, so no query parameter is ever honored. Do not expect `?channel=foo` to filter anything on this route.
- **Non-object persisted bodies are wrapped, not rejected.** If a stored document's body is a scalar/array, `inject_registry_entry_identifier_into_body` wraps it as `{ videoId, owningAccount, rawBody }` — but with no `googleDriveFileId`, that wrapped entry is dropped by step 7 and never surfaces in `entries`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Why does `?channel=roberto` return everything?**
A: Because it returns everything. The route contract exposes no query string; the filter is resolved against an empty map. The matching logic is fully implemented and fully unused. It is patiently waiting for a `Query` extractor that has not been added.

**Q: My registry has documents but the response shows `v_0001` and `v_0002`. Is that a caching bug?**
A: No. Those are the placeholder entries returned when the rendered list is empty — which happens when none of your documents survive the `googleDriveFileId` filter. Check that your persisted bodies actually carry a non-blank `googleDriveFileId`.

**Q: `totalEntries` says 5 but I count 3 entries. Which one lies?**
A: Neither. `totalEntries` counts documents after channel filtering but before the file-id drop and placeholder step; `entries` reflects the fully rendered survivors. They are measuring different points in the pipeline, exactly as designed, unbearably.

### `GET /api/alma-videos/channel/:channel_name` — List Every Video Registered Under a Named Channel

#### Synopsis

This endpoint enumerates every stored video document whose embedded `channel` field exactly matches the channel name supplied in the URL path, returning a JSON envelope that bundles the fully rendered video bodies (sorted alphabetically by title, ascending, case-insensitively), a compact `summary` table for list/table views, and a `videoCount`. When the requested channel yields zero matching videos, the handler deliberately responds with a `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound` rather than an empty list, so that callers can unambiguously distinguish "this channel has no videos" from a successful-but-empty response. The channel name path segment is validated into a `NonEmptyText` before any collection I/O occurs, meaning a blank or whitespace-only segment short-circuits into a `400` long before the persistence layer is touched.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of HTTP, this is the canonical safe, idempotent verb: a `GET`. It is, by the letter of RFC 9110, both **safe** (it induces no observable server-side state mutation — no document is created, amended, or destroyed by its invocation) and **idempotent** (issuing the identical request one time or one thousand times leaves the resource universe in precisely the same condition, network jitter and concurrent uploads notwithstanding). Because it is safe, it is eligible for aggressive intermediary caching, speculative prefetching, and cavalier retry-on-timeout by any well-behaved client, none of which this handler will punish. The channel name is projected into the path hierarchy — `/api/alma-videos/channel/{channel_name}` — rather than into a query string, a deliberate act of REST resource-modeling that asserts "the collection of videos belonging to channel X" is itself a first-class, addressable, bookmarkable resource, not a mere filtered view.

Within the Domain-Driven Design stratification of the `alma-http` crate, this handler is a thin, ceremonious inhabitant of the **interface/adapter layer**. It owns no business rules of its own worth defending; its solemn duties are to (a) parse and validate the inbound path segment into a domain value object (`NonEmptyText`), (b) delegate the retrieval of documents to the `document_collection` port exposed on `ApplicationState`, and (c) shape the domain-shaped `StoredDocument` values into an outward-facing transport envelope decorated with derived stream and thumbnail URLs. The filtering, counting, sorting, and URL-derivation logic is expressed as a constellation of small, single-purpose, individually unit-tested free functions — an aesthetic choice that keeps the orchestrating handler legible and every transformation independently verifiable, exactly as the extensive `#[cfg(test)]` module at the foot of the source file attests.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 3f9a8c21-7b6e-4d0a-9f11-2e5c8ab41d77` | Correlation identifier consumed by the request pipeline's `Validated` stage; echoed through logs and error correlation. Without it the request cannot be shaped into a valid `HttpRequestInPipeline`. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@alma.example` | Identifies the calling account. Consumed by the `Authenticated` stage to establish caller identity and by the `Authorized` stage to confirm the caller may reach this route. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** This handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That generic parameter is not decoration — it is a compile-time proof obligation. The request-processing pipeline is modeled as a type-state machine in which an incoming HTTP request is only ever advanced through a strict, irreversible sequence of marker-typed stages:

1. **`Validated`** — the raw request has been checked for structural well-formedness: required correlation headers such as `x-request-id` are present and parseable. A request that fails validation never acquires this marker and is rejected with `400`.
2. **`Authenticated`** — building atop a `Validated` request, the caller's identity has been established from `x-account-email`. A request lacking credentials cannot be advanced to this stage and is rejected with `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; a request whose credentials are malformed or unrecognized yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`.
3. **`Authorized`** (`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`) — building atop an `Authenticated` request, the caller has been confirmed to hold the permission required to reach this specific route. A caller who is authenticated but not permitted is rejected with `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`.

Because the handler signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the Rust type system makes it *structurally impossible* for the handler body to execute unless the request has already traversed all three stages successfully. The handler binds this proof to `_authorized_request` (the leading underscore signals it is required for its authorization side-effect but its fields are not otherwise read in the body). There is no code path in this handler that can observe an unauthenticated or unauthorized request; the guarantee is discharged before the first line of business logic runs.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channel_name` | path | string | Yes | Must be non-empty and not whitespace-only after parsing into `NonEmptyText`; matched **case-sensitively and exactly** against each document's stored `channel` value. URL-encode reserved/space characters. | None | The name of the channel whose videos are to be listed. Extracted via `Path(channel_name): Path<String>`, then parsed by `parse_channel_name_into_non_empty_text`. |

No query parameters are read by this handler.

Non-object stored bodies are wrapped as `{ videoId, thumbnailUrl, rawBody }`. |

| `summary[].title` | string | Title, defaulting to `"Untitled"` when the field is absent. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` — an object with `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | The `channel_name` path segment is blank/whitespace-only and fails `NonEmptyText::parse` inside `parse_channel_name_into_non_empty_text`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"channel name is invalid: text must not be empty"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The request never reached the `Authenticated` stage — e.g. `x-account-email` (and/or the correlation headers) absent, so `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` cannot be produced. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Credentials were supplied but rejected during authentication (malformed/unrecognized account email). | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| `403` | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Caller is authenticated but lacks permission for this route; the `Authorized` stage refuses to issue `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| `404` | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No stored document has a `channel` equal to the requested name; `map_empty_channel_to_resource_not_found` fires on the empty match set. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no videos were found for channel 'Research Talks'"}` |
| `500` | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | `document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` returns an error (persistence/upstream failure), propagated via `?`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"an upstream application failure occurred"}` |

Full example `SerializedErrorBody` (the 404 that is unusually common for this endpoint):

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "no videos were found for channel 'Research Talks'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. **`parse_channel_name_into_non_empty_text(channel_name)`** — parses the raw path segment into a `NonEmptyText`, mapping a blank/whitespace-only value to `HttpError::RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. **`application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)`** — awaited port call that loads all documents from the `"videos"` collection; `?`-propagated errors become `UpstreamApplicationFailure`.
3. **`filter_videos_matching_channel(&stored_documents, &requested_channel_name)`** — retains only documents whose embedded `channel` equals the requested name (exact, case-sensitive), tolerating missing/non-string `channel` fields.
4. **`extract_channel_name_from_stored_document(stored_document)`** — helper reading the `channel` field as a string, returning `None` when absent or non-string.
5. **`map_empty_channel_to_resource_not_found(&matching_documents, &requested_channel_name)`** — converts an empty match set into `HttpError::RequestedResourceWasNotFound`.
6. **`count_videos_in_channel(&matching_documents)`** — returns the number of matched documents.
7. **`render_channel_video_summary_row(stored_document)`** (mapped over matches) — builds one compact summary object per video (`videoId`, `title` defaulting to `"Untitled"`, `channel` defaulting to `""`, derived `thumbnailUrl`, optional `streamUrl`).
8. **`render_channel_video_bodies(matching_documents)`** — maps each document through `inject_video_identifier_into_body`.
9. **`inject_video_identifier_into_body(stored_document)`** — guarantees a `videoId`; conditionally adds `streamUrl` (when `googleDriveFileId` present); inserts `thumbnailUrl` only if absent; wraps non-object bodies under `rawBody`.
10. **`extract_document_identifier_as_str` / `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_from_document` / `derive_stream_url_for_channel_video` / `derive_thumbnail_url_for_channel_video`** — leaf helpers that read the document id, read `googleDriveFileId`, and format the Drive stream URL and the internal thumbnail URL respectively.
11. **`sort_channel_videos_by_title_ascending(rendered_bodies)`** — sorts the rendered bodies by lowercased `title` (via `extract_title_from_video_body`, which defaults missing titles to `""`).
12. **`build_channel_videos_envelope(&requested_channel_name, rendered_bodies, video_count)`** — assembles `{channel, videoCount, videos}`; the handler then inserts the `summary` array into the envelope object before returning `Json(envelope)`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`videos` is sorted, `summary` is not.** The `videos` array is passed through `sort_channel_videos_by_title_ascending`, but the `summary` rows are collected from `matching_documents` in original filtered order and attached afterward. The two arrays can therefore be in different orders for the same channel — do not assume `videos[i]` corresponds to `summary[i]`.
- **Channel matching is exact and case-sensitive.** `"Research"`, `"research"`, and `"RESEARCH"` are three distinct channels. `filter_videos_matching_channel` compares raw strings; there is no trimming or case-folding of the stored `channel` value.
- **Empty channel = 404, never `videoCount: 0`.** By design, a channel with no matching videos returns `RequestedResourceWasNotFound`, not a successful envelope with an empty `videos` array. A `200` therefore always has `videoCount >= 1`.
- **`thumbnailUrl` is preserved if it already exists; `streamUrl` is not.** `inject_video_identifier_into_body` uses `.entry(...).or_insert_with(...)` for `thumbnailUrl` (existing value wins) but unconditionally `insert`s `streamUrl` whenever a `googleDriveFileId` is present (would overwrite any pre-existing `streamUrl`).
- **Non-object stored bodies survive but change shape.** If a stored document body is not a JSON object (e.g. a bare string), `inject_video_identifier_into_body` returns `{ videoId, thumbnailUrl, rawBody }` instead of enriching in place — so `videos` elements are not guaranteed to carry `title`, `channel`, etc.
- **Sort tie-breaking is unspecified.** Two videos with identical lowercased titles keep whatever relative order `Vec::sort_by` produces (it is a stable sort, so their pre-sort order — the filtered order — is preserved), but callers should not depend on any particular secondary ordering.
- **Missing title sorts first.** `extract_title_from_video_body` defaults an absent `title` to `""`, which lexicographically precedes all non-empty titles.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I know the channel exists because I just uploaded to it, but I got a 404. Why?**
A: The channel string almost certainly does not match exactly. Matching is case-sensitive with no trimming; `"News "` (trailing space) and `"news"` are not `"News"`. Confirm the stored `channel` value byte-for-byte and URL-encode any spaces in the path.

**Q: Can I get an empty list back for a valid, known-but-empty channel?**
A: No. There is no such thing as a `200` with zero videos here. An empty match set is converted to `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`. That is intentional, per the handler doc comment: it lets callers distinguish "no videos" from a genuine empty payload.

**Q: Why do some videos have a `streamUrl` and others don't?**
A: `streamUrl` is derived solely from the document's `googleDriveFileId` field. Documents without that field get no `streamUrl` in `videos`, and `null` for `streamUrl` in `summary`. The presence of a stream URL is a property of the stored document, not of this endpoint.

---

### `PATCH /api/alma-videos/video/:video_identifier/rename` — Rename a Video Registry Document

#### Synopsis

This endpoint mutates the human-readable `name` of exactly one video document that lives inside the `videos` document collection, addressed positionally by the `:video_identifier` path segment. The caller submits a JSON body carrying a single non-empty `new_name` string; the handler locates the matching stored document, verifies that the authorized principal is entitled to rename it (either because they own it, or because the document has no owner and is therefore treated as shared), and then persists the mutated document back into the collection. The response is a JSON confirmation object echoing the previous name, the new name, and a boolean flag indicating whether the rename was in fact a no-op.

#### Theory & Rationale

The `PATCH` verb is deliberate and load-bearing here. This is a *partial* mutation of an existing resource: we are surgically overwriting a single scalar field (`name`) inside a larger stored document, and we are emphatically *not* replacing the entire representation (which would be `PUT`) nor creating a new resource (which would be `POST`). REST semantics classify `PATCH` as neither safe nor idempotent in the general case, and this handler honors that classification honestly — although, as it happens, this particular implementation is *effectively* idempotent for a fixed `new_name`, because re-issuing the same rename against an already-renamed document short-circuits through the "name is identical to previous" branch and returns success without touching storage a second time. Consumers should nonetheless treat the operation as non-idempotent in principle and must not rely on retry-safety for a body whose `new_name` differs between attempts.

From a Domain-Driven Design perspective, this handler sits squarely in the HTTP adapter layer (`crates/http`), acting as a thin translation membrane between the transport concern (path segments, JSON bodies, headers, status codes) and the application's `DocumentCollectionPort`. The handler itself performs no persistence logic beyond orchestration; it delegates reads to `list_documents` and writes to `replace_document`, both exposed through the injected `ApplicationState`. Value-object parsing (`NonEmptyText`, `Email`) is pushed to the domain crate so that invariants — non-emptiness, email well-formedness — are enforced at the boundary and never leak malformed primitives inward. Authorization is expressed as a pure, testable function over the stored document and the requesting principal, keeping the policy declarative and auditable rather than smeared across imperative control flow.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request that reaches this handler has already traversed the type-state pipeline and arrived as an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. The authorized principal's email is extracted inside the handler via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` and re-parsed into a domain `Email`.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00cf4fc964ff` | Populates the pipeline's `correlation_identifier`. Pipeline validation (`validate()`) rejects an empty/whitespace-only correlation identifier with `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. Supply a stable UUID per logical request for traceability. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: owner@example.com` | Identifies the calling principal. Becomes the `declared_principal` carried through `authenticate()` → `authorize()`, and is what the handler re-parses via `parse_requesting_principal_email`. Must be a syntactically valid email or the handler returns `401 authentication_credentials_were_invalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (Validated → Authenticated → Authorized).** Authentication and authorization are encoded in Rust's type system as an unforgeable sequence of state transitions on `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`, where `Stage` is a zero-sized `PhantomData` marker. A request is born as `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated>` via `originate(correlation_identifier)`. Calling `.validate()` checks that the correlation identifier is non-empty and yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>` (or `RequestBodyWasMalformed`). Calling `.authenticate(email)` attaches the authenticated principal and yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthenticated>`. Calling `.authorize()` asserts that a principal is actually present — returning `AuthorizationWasDenied` if somehow it is not — and yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. Only that final type is accepted as an extractor argument by this handler's signature, so it is a *compile-time guarantee* that no unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request can ever invoke the rename logic. The `authorized_principal()` accessor is defined exclusively on the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` type and `.expect()`s a present principal, which is safe precisely because the type-state chain proves one exists.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `video_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must be non-empty after parsing into `NonEmptyText`; an empty/whitespace value yields `404 requested_resource_was_not_found`. Compared verbatim against each stored document's `document_identifier`. | None | The identifier of the video registry document to rename. |

There are no query parameters. **None.**

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and reads exactly one field from it: `new_name`. Any additional fields present in the submitted JSON are ignored.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `new_name` | string | Yes | Must be present and be a JSON string; must be non-empty per `NonEmptyText::parse` (whitespace-only strings such as `"   "` are rejected as empty). Leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed before storage via `sanitize_new_name_for_storage`. Missing field or non-string value → `400 request_body_was_malformed`. | None | The desired new display name for the video. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` (the snake_case category label) and `error_explanation` (a human-readable string). Note the field name in the wire body is `error_explanation`, populated from the variant's `explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `new_name` missing / not a string, or fails `NonEmptyText::parse` (empty/whitespace-only). | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the 'new_name' field is required and must be a string"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | Not raised inside this handler directly; produced upstream by the pipeline when no principal credentials are supplied before reaching the authorized stage. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"no account email header was provided"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | The authorized principal string fails `Email::parse` in `parse_requesting_principal_email`. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the authorized principal is not a valid email: ..."}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | The located document has an `owning_account` that differs from the requesting principal's email (`authorize_owning_account_may_rename_video`). Also raised upstream by `.authorize()` if a principal is absent. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"only the owning account may rename this video"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Path `video_identifier` is empty/unparseable; no document matches the identifier; or the document vanished between read and `replace_document` (replace returned `false`). | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"no video exists under the identifier 'video-123'"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | The stored document body is not a JSON object (`validate_document_body_is_object`), or any `DocumentCollectionPort` error surfaces from `list_documents` / `replace_document` (mapped via `From<ApplicationError>`). | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the stored video document body is malformed and cannot be renamed"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "authorization_was_denied",
  "error_explanation": "only the owning account may rename this video"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in call order:

1. `extract_requested_new_name_from_body` — pulls `new_name` from the body, requires it be a present string, and parses it into a `NonEmptyText` (400 on failure).
2. `parse_video_identifier_into_non_empty_text` — parses the path segment into a `NonEmptyText`, mapping emptiness to a 404.
3. `parse_requesting_principal_email` — re-parses the authorized principal string into a domain `Email` (401 invalid on failure).
4. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — reads all documents from the `"videos"` collection (async port call).
5. `locate_matching_registry_entry_for_rename` — linearly scans the loaded documents for one whose `document_identifier` matches, cloning it if found.
6. `map_missing_video_to_resource_not_found` — converts a `None` lookup into a 404.
7. `validate_document_body_is_object` — ensures the stored body is a JSON object; a non-object body is treated as corruption (500).
8. `authorize_owning_account_may_rename_video` — allows the rename if the owner matches the principal or the document is ownerless; otherwise 403. Internally calls `extract_owning_account_from_stored_document`.
9. `extract_previous_name_before_rename` — reads the current `name` (defaults to empty string).
10. `detect_new_name_is_identical_to_previous` — compares trimmed old vs. new name; if identical, short-circuits and returns the confirmation without writing.
11. `apply_new_name_to_document_body` — clones-in the sanitized (trimmed) new name onto the body, replacing a non-object body with `{ "name": ... }` as a fallback. Uses `sanitize_new_name_for_storage`.
12. `application_state.document_collection.replace_document(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME, renamed_document)` — persists the mutated document; returns a boolean indicating whether a replacement occurred.
13. `map_replace_flag_to_result` — turns a `false` replace outcome into a 404 (the document vanished mid-flight).
14. `render_rename_confirmation` — builds the final JSON confirmation object returned to the caller.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **No-op renames still return 200 without a write.** If the trimmed `new_name` equals the trimmed existing `name`, the handler returns early with `name_was_unchanged: true` and never calls `replace_document`. Do not use this endpoint to force a "touch"/re-save; an identical name is silently skipped.
- **Whitespace is trimmed before both comparison and storage.** `"  Title  "` and `"Title"` are considered identical, and only `"Title"` is ever stored. A body of `"   "` (all whitespace) is rejected as empty (400), not stored as a blank name.
- **Ownerless documents are renameable by anyone authenticated.** If a stored document's `owning_account` is `None`, `authorize_owning_account_may_rename_video` returns `Ok` for any valid principal. This is intentional ("shared/public") but surprising if you assume ownership is always enforced.
- **The whole collection is loaded to find one document.** The handler calls `list_documents` and then linearly scans with `locate_matching_registry_entry_for_rename` rather than a targeted `fetch_document`. On large `videos` collections this is an O(n) read per rename.
- **A non-object stored body is a 500, not a 400.** If the located document's `document_body` is, say, a string or number, `validate_document_body_is_object` classifies it as `UpstreamApplicationFailure` (500) — it's treated as server-side corruption, not client error. (Note: the unreached `apply_new_name_to_document_body` has a fallback for non-object bodies, but the validation gate rejects them first.)
- **TOCTOU window between read and replace.** The document is read, mutated in memory, then written back. If another actor deletes it in between, `replace_document` returns `false` and the caller receives `404 requested_resource_was_not_found` with the "vanished before it could be renamed" explanation.
- **The response `name` is the sanitized (trimmed) value, which may differ from what you sent.** Clients should read the returned `name` rather than assume the exact submitted string was stored.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I rename a video by sending `{ "name": "..." }` instead of `{ "new_name": "..." }`?**
A: No. The handler reads only `new_name`. A body without `new_name` yields `400 request_body_was_malformed`, regardless of any `name` field you include.

**Q: Is this endpoint idempotent, so I can safely retry?**
A: For a fixed `new_name`, effectively yes — a repeated identical rename short-circuits to a no-op 200. For semantic correctness, treat `PATCH` as non-idempotent and do not rely on retry-safety when the `new_name` differs between attempts.

**Q: I renamed a video that isn't mine and it worked. Is authorization broken?**
A: The document you renamed almost certainly has no `owning_account` (it is treated as shared). Ownership is only enforced when `owning_account` is present and differs from your `x-account-email`; that case returns `403 authorization_was_denied`.

**Q: Why did I get a 404 when the video clearly exists?**
A: Either your `:video_identifier` did not match any `document_identifier` verbatim (matching is exact string equality), the identifier parsed as empty, or the document was deleted between the read and the write.

### `GET /api/alma-videos/stream/:google_drive_file_identifier` — Mint a Time-Bounded Video Stream URL

#### Synopsis

This endpoint resolves a Google Drive file identifier to a registered video document, enforces per-document ownership rules, and returns a freshly minted bundle of stream URLs (a direct download URL and an embeddable preview URL) accompanied by a metadata envelope describing the derived MIME content type and a one-hour validity window. It performs a read-only catalogue lookup against the `videos` document collection and never mutates state. The response is a JSON envelope combining top-level URL fields with a nested `stream` object carrying lifetime metadata.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the grand REST tradition, this endpoint is a paragon of the `GET` verb's twin virtues: it is both **safe** (it induces no observable change of server state that the caller could be held responsible for) and **idempotent** (issuing the identical request N times yields the identical class of representation, modulo the wall-clock `expires_at_epoch_seconds` and `issued_at` moment, which drift forward with time but never with side effect). Note that the response is not byte-for-byte identical across calls because it embeds `current_epoch_seconds()` at rendering time; idempotency is a property of *server-side effects*, not of timestamp determinism, and that a clock advancing is not a mutation the endpoint authored. The URLs themselves are deterministic string templates over the validated identifier; only the envelope's temporal metadata varies.

Within the surrounding Domain-Driven Design topology, this handler sits squarely in the HTTP interface-adapter layer of the `videos` bounded context. It orchestrates but does not own business logic: value objects (`NonEmptyText`, `Email`) enforce domain invariants at the boundary, the `document_collection` port abstracts persistence, and the handler's private helper functions form a small, testable pipeline of pure-ish transformations. Ownership authorization is expressed as an explicit domain rule (owner-or-public) rather than smeared across middleware, keeping the resource-level access decision colocated with the resource it protects. The endpoint deliberately returns *URLs to* the media rather than proxying the bytes, cleanly delegating the actual streaming to Google Drive and keeping this service in the role of a catalogue-and-authorization gateway.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Requests traverse a type-state pipeline before the handler body ever runs. The handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, meaning the compiler itself refuses to let this code execute against a request that has not already been validated, authenticated, and authorized upstream.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7f3c9b2e-1a44-4c8e-9f0a-2b6d5e8c1a90` | Correlation identifier for tracing a single request across logs and pipeline stages. Echoed/propagated by infrastructure; not read by the handler body itself. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: owner@example.com` | Identifies the calling principal. Consumed upstream to build the authenticated principal; this handler reads it back via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` and re-parses it into an `Email`. Missing/blank ⇒ `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` upstream; malformed-as-email ⇒ `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` inside this handler. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The request is threaded through a sequence of marker type-states, each of which is a distinct compile-time proof:

1. **Validated** — structural well-formedness of the incoming request has been established (headers parsed, envelope shape confirmed). Only a `Validated` request is eligible to be authenticated.
2. **Authenticated** — the principal named by `x-account-email` has been resolved and attached to the request. The identity is now *known*, though not yet *permitted*.
3. **Authorized** — coarse-grained access to this route has been granted, producing the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` state carried by `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. Because the handler accepts only this concrete type-state, it is statically impossible to invoke the handler with an unauthorized (or merely authenticated, or merely validated) request — the earlier states simply do not satisfy the parameter's type. Any attempt to short-circuit the pipeline is a *compile error*, not a runtime check.

Note that this route-level "Authorized" state is distinct from the *resource-level* ownership check performed inside the handler (`authorize_principal_may_stream_video`): passing the pipeline gets you into the handler; owning (or the document being unowned) gets you the stream.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `google_drive_file_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must be non-empty after trimming; ASCII alphanumeric plus `-` and `_` only; maximum length 256 characters | — | The Google Drive file id whose registered video document should be resolved and for which stream URLs should be minted. |

No query parameters are read by this handler.

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` request and the handler reads **no request body whatsoever**. It extracts only `State`, the authorized pipeline request, and the single `Path` parameter. Send no body.

For completeness, the accepted body is the empty object.

(a) Field table — there are no body fields.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | No request body is read. |

(b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12):

```json

  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "RetrieveVideoStreamUrlRequestBody",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

(c) TypeScript interface:

```typescript

```

(d) Rust struct mirror:

#### Successful Response

Status `200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is the primary URL object with the metadata envelope merged under the `stream` key.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `google_drive_file_identifier` | string | The validated identifier echoed back to the caller. |
| `stream_url` | string | Convenience alias equal to `download_url`. |
| `download_url` | string | Direct Google Drive download URL: `https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=<id>`. |
| `preview_url` | string | Embeddable Google Drive preview URL: `https://drive.google.com/file/d/<id>/preview`. |
| `stream` | object | Metadata envelope (see nested fields). |
| `stream.urls.download` | string | Same as top-level `download_url`. |
| `stream.urls.preview` | string | Same as top-level `preview_url`. |
| `stream.content_type` | string | MIME type derived from the document's `video_name`/`file_name` extension (e.g. `video/mp4`, `video/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/quicktime`, `video/x-matroska`, `video/x-msvideo`), defaulting to `application/octet-stream`. |
| `stream.expires_at_epoch_seconds` | integer | Epoch second at which the minted URL bundle is considered expired (`issued_at + 3600`, saturating). |
| `stream.validity_window_seconds` | integer | Constant `3600` (one hour). |
