#### Error Responses

Each `HttpError` variant serializes to a `SerializedErrorBody` of shape `{ "error_category", "error_explanation" }`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | The path identifier is empty/blank, contains characters other than `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, or exceeds 256 characters. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"google drive file identifier contained unsupported characters"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | No principal (`x-account-email`) was supplied; rejected upstream before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | The pipeline's authorized principal string fails to parse as an `Email` (`parse_requesting_principal_email`). | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authorized principal was not a valid email: ..."}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The located document has an `owning_account` that does not case-insensitively match the requesting principal. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"requesting principal may not stream this video"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No document in the `videos` collection carries a matching `google_drive_file_identifier`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no video was registered for google drive file identifier '...'"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The `document_collection.list_documents("videos")` port call fails (persistence/upstream error, propagated via `?`). | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"an upstream application failure occurred"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "no video was registered for google drive file identifier '1A2b-_Cd3EfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUv'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. `parse_google_drive_file_identifier_into_non_empty_text` — parses the raw path string into a `NonEmptyText`, mapping domain failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. `validate_google_drive_file_identifier_charset` — rejects identifiers with disallowed characters or length > 256, else `400`.
3. `parse_requesting_principal_email` — re-parses the pipeline's authorized principal into an `Email`, mapping failure to `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`.
4. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — loads all documents in the `"videos"` collection (errors propagate as `500`).
5. `locate_video_document_by_file_identifier` — linearly scans the loaded documents for one whose recorded id matches.
6. `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_from_document` — pulls the non-empty `google_drive_file_identifier` string from a document body (used by step 5).
7. `map_unknown_file_identifier_to_resource_not_found` — turns a `None` lookup into `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`, else unwraps the document.
8. `authorize_principal_may_stream_video` — enforces owner-or-public access, else `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`.
9. `extract_owning_account_from_document` — reads the owning account, preferring the struct's `owning_account` field then falling back to the body's `owning_account` (used by step 8).
10. `build_google_drive_download_stream_url` — builds the `uc?export=download` URL.
11. `build_google_drive_preview_stream_url` — builds the `/file/d/<id>/preview` URL.
12. `derive_stream_content_type_from_document` — maps the file extension to a MIME type, defaulting to `application/octet-stream`.
13. `extract_file_extension_from_document_name` — extracts the extension from `video_name` (or `file_name`) after the last `.` (used by step 12).
14. `current_epoch_seconds` — reads the current wall-clock epoch second (0 before the epoch).
15. `compute_stream_url_expiry_timestamp` — adds the 3600-second window, saturating on overflow.
16. `render_stream_url_response` — builds the primary body with the four top-level URL fields.
17. `build_stream_url_envelope` — builds the `stream` metadata envelope (urls, content_type, expiry, window).
18. `merge_envelope_into_response` — inserts the envelope under the `stream` key of the primary body.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`stream_url` and `download_url` are identical.** Both point at the `uc?export=download` URL. `stream_url` is purely an alias; do not expect a distinct HLS/DASH manifest.
- **Ownership is case-insensitive but exact otherwise.** `authorize_principal_may_stream_video` compares with `eq_ignore_ascii_case`, so `Owner@Example.com` matches `owner@example.com`, but there is no domain/alias normalization — sub-addressing or display differences will be denied.
- **Unowned documents are world-streamable.** If neither the struct `owning_account` nor the body `owning_account` is present (or both are empty), the document is treated as public and *any* authenticated principal receives the URLs.
- **Content type is a guess from the filename extension.** It is derived from `video_name`/`file_name` text, not from the actual bytes. A mislabeled or extensionless file yields `application/octet-stream` regardless of true media type.
- **The one-hour expiry is advisory metadata, not enforcement.** `expires_at_epoch_seconds` describes the envelope's stated lifetime; the returned Google Drive URLs themselves are not signed or time-limited by this service, so they may keep working past expiry (or fail earlier if Drive permissions change).
- **Lookup is a full linear scan of the entire `videos` collection.** `list_documents` loads every document and `locate_...` iterates until a match; this is O(n) per request and returns `404` if the id is absent from the catalogue even when the underlying Drive file exists.
- **A blank `x-account-email` fails differently depending on stage.** Missing entirely is a `401 ...WereMissing` upstream; a present-but-not-an-email value that survives to the handler becomes `401 ...WereInvalid`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Why do `stream_url` and `download_url` return the same string? Is that a bug?**
A: No. `render_stream_url_response` assigns both fields the download URL by design. Treat `stream_url` as a legacy-friendly alias and ignore the redundancy.

**Q: The URL still works after `expires_at_epoch_seconds`. Did the expiry do nothing?**
A: Correct — nearly nothing. The expiry is a metadata assertion computed as issue-time + 3600 seconds; this endpoint does not mint signed, self-expiring Drive URLs, so enforcement is Google Drive's business, not ours.

**Q: I own the video in Drive but I get a `403`. Why?**
A: Ownership here is decided by the `owning_account` recorded on the *stored document*, matched case-insensitively against your `x-account-email`. Your Google Drive ownership is irrelevant; if the catalogue record names a different owner, you are denied.

**Q: I passed a valid Google Drive id and got `404`. The file exists — what gives?**
A: The endpoint resolves against the local `videos` catalogue, not Drive. If no document in the collection carries that `google_drive_file_identifier`, you get `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound` no matter what exists in Drive.

### `GET /api/alma-videos/thumbnail/:video_identifier` — Retrieve Video Thumbnail Descriptor

#### Synopsis

This endpoint resolves and returns a JSON *descriptor* of the best-available thumbnail for a single video, identified by its path-segment `video_identifier`. It does not stream image bytes; instead it computes a thumbnail URL (an explicitly-stored URL, a Google Drive-derived URL, or a canonical relative image endpoint), wraps that URL in a small envelope carrying a content-type hint and a cache-control max-age, and hands the whole thing back as `application/json`. Think of it as "tell me where the picture lives and how long you may cache it," not "give me the picture."

#### Theory & Rationale

`GET` is the correct and only defensible verb here. The operation is nullipotent in the truest sense: it reads a document collection, performs pure string manipulation over the retrieved document body, and materialises a response envelope — no state is mutated, no side effect escapes the process, and calling it a thousand times leaves the world exactly as it found it. It is therefore both **safe** (no observable state change) and **idempotent** (identical requests yield semantically identical responses, modulo underlying data drift). Because the resource being addressed is a *derived representation* of a video (its thumbnail) rather than the video itself, the URL nests the thumbnail concern under the video identifier, honouring the REST principle that URLs name resources and that hierarchy in the path should mirror hierarchy in the domain.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler sits squarely in the HTTP/interface layer and is deliberately anaemic in domain logic: its only brush with the domain is the coercion of the raw path string into the `NonEmptyText` value object, a boundary-guarding invariant that refuses to let empty or whitespace-only identifiers leak inward. Everything else — locating the document, mining the body for `thumbnail_url` or `google_drive_file_id`, choosing a fallback, appending a Drive sizing suffix — is presentation-adjacent view logic that composes over the `StoredDocument` port. The persistence concern is fully delegated to the `document_collection` port on `ApplicationState`, so the handler never knows or cares whether the videos live in Mongo, Postgres, or a hashmap. This is the hexagonal ideal: the transport layer orchestrates, the ports abstract, and the value objects defend the frontier.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request travels through the type-state request pipeline and arrives at this handler only after it has been fully authorized, materialised here as the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor in the function signature. The extractor is bound to `_authorized_request` and intentionally unused inside the body — its mere presence in the argument list is load-bearing, because constructing it is what forces the request through validation, authentication, and authorization before a single line of handler logic runs.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7f3c1e2a-9b4d-4c8e-a1f0-2d6b5e9c0a11` | Correlation identifier threaded through logs and error envelopes. If omitted, the pipeline is free to synthesize one; supplying your own makes tracing a single request across services trivial. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@alma.example` | Identifies the calling principal. Consumed during the `Authenticated` and `Authorized` pipeline stages; its absence yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, and a value the pipeline rejects yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** The alma-http request pipeline encodes each processing guarantee as a distinct *type parameter* on `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`, so the compiler — not a runtime `if` — enforces that a handler can only observe a request that has reached the required stage. A request is first `Validated` (structurally well-formed: the required headers parse, the shape is coherent). It is then promoted to `Authenticated` once the principal in `x-account-email` has been established as a real identity. Finally it is promoted to `Authorized` once that authenticated principal has been confirmed to hold the rights needed for this route. Because this handler asks for `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, it is *impossible* for it to run against a request that skipped any earlier stage: there is no code path that produces a `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` token without first having produced the `Validated` and `Authenticated` ones. The authorization is thus a compile-time invariant, and the handler body is free to assume — totally, unconditionally — that the caller is who they say they are and is allowed to be here.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `video_identifier` | path | string | Yes | Must be non-empty after trimming (coerced to `NonEmptyText`); blank/whitespace-only is rejected | — | The identifier of the video whose thumbnail descriptor is requested. Matched exactly against `StoredDocument.document_identifier` within the `videos` collection. |

Query parameters: **None.** The handler internally references a `size` parameter (`small`/`s`, `large`/`l`, else `medium`), but the extractor for this route is `Path`-only and carries no query string. The handler explicitly constructs an *empty* `HashMap` and resolves sizing from it, so the size logic always yields the default `Medium` rendition. Any `?size=...` you append is silently ignored by this endpoint.

#### Request Body

This endpoint reads **no request body**. It is a `GET` with a `Path` extractor only; no `Json<T>` or deserialized payload is consumed. Send no body.

#### Error Responses

Every failure serialises to a `SerializedErrorBody` of the shape `{ "error_category": string, "error_explanation": string }`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | The path segment coerces to a blank/whitespace-only identifier and `NonEmptyText::parse` rejects it (via `parse_video_identifier_into_non_empty_text`). | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"text must not be empty"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` is absent; the pipeline cannot reach the `Authenticated` stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were missing."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` is present but rejected as a non-identity by the pipeline. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were invalid."}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal lacks the rights required to reach `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` for this route. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"Authorization was denied."}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No document in the `videos` collection has `document_identifier` equal to the requested identifier (via `map_missing_video_to_resource_not_found`). | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"No video was found for identifier 'vid-123'."}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | `document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` fails (its error is propagated via `?`). | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"An upstream application failure occurred."}` |

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `parse_video_identifier_into_non_empty_text` — validates and normalises the raw path segment into a `NonEmptyText`, mapping failure to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — awaits the full list of stored documents in the `"videos"` collection (errors bubble up as `500 UpstreamApplicationFailure`).
3. `locate_video_document_by_identifier` — linearly scans the returned documents for one whose `document_identifier` equals the parsed identifier, returning `Option<StoredDocument>`.
4. `map_missing_video_to_resource_not_found` — converts a `None` lookup into `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`, otherwise unwraps the document.
5. `extract_stored_thumbnail_url_from_document` — reads `document_body["thumbnail_url"]`, trims it, and treats blank as absent.
6. `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_from_document` — reads `google_drive_file_id` (falling back to the legacy camelCase `googleDriveFileId`), trims it, and treats blank as absent.
7. `choose_thumbnail_url_with_fallback` — prefers the stored URL, then a Drive-derived URL (`derive_google_drive_thumbnail_url_from_file_identifier`), then the canonical `build_thumbnail_image_url` endpoint.
8. `parse_requested_thumbnail_size_query_parameter` — interprets a `size` parameter from an (always empty) `HashMap`, therefore always yielding `ThumbnailSize::Medium`.
9. `apply_thumbnail_size_suffix_to_url` — appends `&sz=w<N>`/`?sz=w<N>` to Drive URLs only (using `ThumbnailSize::pixel_width`); non-Drive URLs are returned unchanged.
10. `derive_thumbnail_content_type` — returns the static `"image/jpeg"` content-type.
11. `build_thumbnail_envelope` — wraps `render_thumbnail_response` (which itself substitutes `build_placeholder_thumbnail_url` for blank URLs) and injects `content_type` plus `compute_thumbnail_cache_control_max_age_seconds` (`86_400`).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **The `size` query parameter is dead on this route.** `parse_requested_thumbnail_size_query_parameter` and `apply_thumbnail_size_suffix_to_url` are fully wired, but the handler feeds them an unconditionally *empty* `HashMap`, so every Drive URL is suffixed with `sz=w320` (medium) and no client-supplied `?size=large` can ever change it.
- **Sizing suffixes are applied to Drive URLs only.** If the thumbnail resolves to an explicitly-stored non-Drive URL or to the relative `/api/alma-videos/thumbnail/{id}/image` endpoint, `apply_thumbnail_size_suffix_to_url` short-circuits and returns it verbatim — no `sz=` is appended, so those URLs never carry sizing information.
- **Blank fields are treated as absent, not as errors.** Both `thumbnail_url` and the Drive id are trimmed and filtered for emptiness; a document storing `"thumbnail_url": "   "` behaves identically to one omitting the field, cascading to the next fallback rather than surfacing a malformed value.
- **Legacy camelCase key still works.** `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_from_document` reads `google_drive_file_id` first and only then `googleDriveFileId`, so older documents persisted before the snake_case migration continue to resolve correctly.
- **Lookup is a full-collection scan, not an indexed fetch.** The handler calls `list_documents` and then `.find(...)` in memory, so cost grows linearly with the size of the `videos` collection; a missing identifier still pays for the entire list before returning `404`.
- **The placeholder path is effectively unreachable via the normal flow.** `render_thumbnail_response` substitutes `/assets/video-thumbnail-placeholder.png` only when the resolved URL is blank, but `choose_thumbnail_url_with_fallback` always returns a non-empty string (worst case, the canonical image endpoint), so the placeholder branch is a defensive belt-and-suspenders guard rather than an observed output.
- **This endpoint never returns image bytes.** Despite the name "thumbnail," the response is always a JSON descriptor with `content_type: "image/jpeg"` describing where the image *would* be fetched from — not the JPEG itself.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I passed `?size=large` and still got a medium (`w320`) URL. Is that a bug?**
A: No. The route uses a `Path`-only extractor and the handler resolves sizing from an empty parameter map, so the size is always medium. If you need a different rendition on a Drive URL, adjust the `sz=w` value client-side.

**Q: Does a `200` guarantee the image at `thumbnail_url` actually exists and loads?**
A: No. The endpoint validates that a video *document* exists and computes a best-effort URL. Whether Google Drive, the stored URL, or the relative image endpoint actually serves bytes is not checked here.

**Q: Why is `content_type` always `"image/jpeg"` even for a Drive PNG?**
A: `derive_thumbnail_content_type` returns a hard-coded `"image/jpeg"` string; it is a hint, not a content negotiation, and it does not inspect the actual image behind the URL.

**Q: Can I omit `x-account-email` since this is just a read?**
A: No. The handler only runs after the request reaches `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`; without a valid principal you will get a `401` long before any thumbnail logic executes.

### `GET /api/alma-videos/search` — Full-Corpus Case-Insensitive Video Title Search With Relevance Ranking

#### Synopsis

This endpoint performs a substring, case-insensitive search over the `title` field of every document stored in the `videos` collection, optionally scoped to a single channel, and returns the matching video document bodies ranked by a hand-rolled relevance heuristic and truncated to a caller-specified (or default) limit. It is a read-only, side-effect-free query surface: it mutates nothing, persists nothing, and enqueues nothing. Every match is enriched at render time with an injected `relevance_score` and its `document_identifier`, and the whole thing is wrapped in a small envelope reporting the original query, the total number of matches before truncation, and the number of results actually returned.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the grand tradition of REST, `GET` is both *safe* and *idempotent*, and this endpoint honors both properties with the earnestness of a monk copying scripture: it reads the entire videos collection, filters it in memory, and returns a representation of that filtered set without ever perturbing server state. Because it is safe, intermediaries are free to cache it, prefetch it, and retry it at will; because it is idempotent, issuing the identical request one time or one thousand times leaves the resource universe exactly as it found it. The search term travels in the query string rather than a request body precisely because a `GET` that carries semantic payload in its body is an affront to the uniform interface and to the caches that trust it — the query string is the canonical home of the *selection criteria* that identify which representation of the "videos search" resource the client wishes to retrieve.

From a Domain-Driven Design vantage, this handler sits squarely in the thin HTTP adapter layer of the `alma-http` crate and studiously refuses to become an aggregate. It reaches through the `document_collection` port (a repository abstraction owned by `alma_application::ports`) to list `StoredDocument` instances, then performs *presentation-layer* concerns — normalization, filtering, scoring, ranking, truncation, envelope shaping — entirely within the adapter. There is no domain invariant being enforced here beyond the humble `NonEmptyText` value object guarding the mandatory query term; the ranking algorithm is deliberately an application/presentation heuristic rather than a domain rule, because "which video title is more relevant to the substring `rust`" is a query concern, not a business truth. This keeps the domain pure and the adapter appropriately disposable.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request to this endpoint traverses the type-state authentication pipeline and must arrive bearing the identity headers the pipeline consumes. The handler's signature demands an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is only constructible once the middleware chain has proven the request valid, authenticated, and authorized.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended (yes in practice) | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a1e-4b2d-4c1a-9e88-0a1b2c3d4e5f` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and error handling; used to trace a single request across the pipeline stages. Generate a fresh UUID per request. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: francesco@example.com` | The caller's account identity. Consumed by the authentication stage to establish *who* is calling; absence yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, a malformed/unrecognized value yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** The `alma-http` crate encodes request lifecycle progress in the *type* of the request wrapper, so that a handler cannot even be compiled against a request that has not reached the required stage. Concretely, an inbound request begins as raw bytes, is parsed and shape-checked into a `Validated` request (structural correctness — headers present, well-formed), is then promoted to an `Authenticated` request once `x-account-email` has been resolved to a known identity, and is finally promoted to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` once policy checks confirm that identity may perform this operation. Each promotion is a distinct type, and each type is only obtainable by passing through the preceding stage — there is no public constructor that skips a rung. Because `search_videos_by_title_handler` accepts `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` by value as an extractor argument, the compiler guarantees the handler body never runs unless the request has already been Validated, then Authenticated, then Authorized. The handler binds this wrapper as `_authorized_request` and does not otherwise read from it: its mere presence is the proof obligation, discharged by the type system rather than by a runtime `if`.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | query | string | Yes | Must be present; must parse as `NonEmptyText` (non-empty after the value object's validation — whitespace-only is rejected) | — | The search term. Lower-cased before matching so search is case-insensitive. Missing or empty ⇒ `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. |
| `channel` | query | string | No | Trimmed; ignored if empty after trimming | *(no scoping)* | Restricts the search to documents whose `channel` field equals this value (case-insensitive comparison). When absent or blank, all channels are searched. |
| `limit` | query | string (parsed as unsigned integer) | No | Parsed as `usize`; must be `> 0` or it is ignored; values above `100` are capped to `100` | `20` | Maximum number of ranked results to return. Non-numeric, zero, or negative values silently fall back to the default of `20`. Does not affect `total_matches`. |

There are no path parameters for this endpoint.

#### Successful Response

`200 OK` with a JSON envelope. The `videos` array contains each matching document's original `document_body`, with two fields merged in: `relevance_score` and `document_identifier`. Any other fields present on the stored document body (e.g. `title`, `channel`, and whatever else was persisted) are passed through untouched.

Response field table:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | The original, validated search term as supplied by the caller (echoed pre-normalization casing). |
| `total_matches` | integer (unsigned) | Number of documents that matched the term (and channel scope) *before* truncation to `limit`. |
| `returned_count` | integer (unsigned) | Number of entries actually present in `videos` after truncation. Equals `min(total_matches, effective_limit)`. |
| `videos` | array of objects | Ranked, truncated result bodies. Each is the stored `document_body` plus injected `relevance_score` and `document_identifier`. |
| `videos[].relevance_score` | integer | Injected relevance score for the document (see caveat in Edge Cases about how it is computed at render time). |
| `videos[].document_identifier` | string | The stored document's identifier, injected into the body. |
| `videos[].title` | string (typical) | Original title field, if the stored body had one (the field that was matched against). |
| `videos[].channel` | string (typical) | Original channel field, if present on the stored body. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` object with `error_category` and `error_explanation` fields. The table below enumerates all `HttpError` variants; the "When" column describes what triggers each for *this specific endpoint*.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | The `query` query parameter is missing, or its value fails `NonEmptyText::parse` (empty / whitespace-only). This endpoint raises this variant despite having no request body — it is reused for malformed query input. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'query' query parameter is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` (and required identity headers) absent, so the pipeline cannot reach the `Authenticated` stage. Raised by middleware before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Identity headers present but not resolvable to a known/valid account. Raised by middleware before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Caller is authenticated but policy denies the search operation, so the request never reaches `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. Raised by middleware before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not raised by this handler's own logic (an empty result set is a `200` with `videos: []`, not a 404). Included for completeness of the shared `HttpError` enum; could surface from routing. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested resource was not found"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The `document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` call fails (database/storage error). The `?` on the `.await?` converts the port error into this variant. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"an upstream application failure occurred"}` |

Full example serialized error body:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "the 'query' query parameter is required"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates these real helper functions, in order:

1. **`extract_requested_query_parameter(&query_parameters)`** — Reads the mandatory `query` param; returns `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` if missing, then validates it via `NonEmptyText::parse`.
2. **`normalize_search_term_to_lowercase(&requested_query)`** — Lower-cases the validated term so subsequent matching is case-insensitive.
3. **`parse_optional_channel_scope_query_parameter(&query_parameters)`** — Reads and trims the optional `channel` param, treating empty-after-trim as absent.
4. **`parse_optional_result_limit_query_parameter(&query_parameters)`** — Reads the optional `limit` param, defaulting to `20`, rejecting non-positive/non-numeric values, and capping at `100`.
5. **`application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)`** — Loads every document from the `"videos"` collection via the repository port (the sole I/O, `.await?` ⇒ `500` on failure).
6. **`restrict_documents_to_channel_scope(stored_documents, channel_scope.as_deref())`** — Optionally filters to documents whose `channel` matches the scope (case-insensitive); pass-through when no scope.
7. **`filter_documents_whose_title_contains_term(scoped_documents, &normalized_term)`** — Keeps only documents whose lower-cased `title` contains the normalized term (documents lacking a string title are dropped).
8. **`count_total_matches(&matching_documents)`** — Records the match count *before* truncation, for `total_matches`.
9. **`sort_matching_documents_by_relevance_descending(matching_documents, &normalized_term)`** — Ranks matches by `score_title_match_relevance`, descending, with a stable lowercase-title tiebreak.
10. **`score_title_match_relevance(title, term)`** (called within the sort and the render) — Computes the heuristic score: base `10`, `+1000` exact, `+200` prefix, `+50` word-boundary, minus a length penalty of `char_count / 8`.
11. **`render_matching_video_bodies(ranked_documents)`** — Maps each ranked document to a response body, computing and injecting a per-document relevance score (see caveat below).
12. **`inject_relevance_score_into_result_body(stored_document, relevance_score)`** — Merges `relevance_score` and `document_identifier` into the document body object.
13. **`truncate_results_to_limit(rendered_bodies, result_limit)`** — Truncates the rendered list to at most `result_limit` entries.
14. **`build_search_results_envelope(&requested_query, limited_bodies, total_matches)`** — Assembles the `{query, total_matches, returned_count, videos}` envelope returned to the client.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **The injected `relevance_score` is NOT the score used for ranking.** Sorting uses `score_title_match_relevance(title, normalized_term)` — the title against the *search term*. But `render_matching_video_bodies` recomputes the score as `score_title_match_relevance(title, title.to_lowercase())` — the title against *itself*. So the number in the response reflects "how well the title matches itself" (effectively an exact-match-flavored score dominated by the `+1000` exact bonus minus length penalty), not the term-relevance that actually determined ordering. Do not use `relevance_score` to re-derive ranking client-side; it will not agree with the array order.
- **`total_matches` counts before truncation; `returned_count` after.** If `total_matches` is `57` and `limit` is `20`, you get `returned_count: 20` and only 20 entries in `videos`. There is no pagination offset — you cannot page past the first `limit` results.
- **`limit` values that are zero, negative, or non-numeric silently become the default `20`, and values over `100` are silently capped to `100`.** No error is returned for a bad `limit`; the caller gets defaulted/capped behavior with no signal that their input was ignored.
- **Documents with no string `title` are invisible.** Filtering, scoring, and channel matching all rely on string-valued `title` / `channel` fields; a document whose `title` is missing or non-string is dropped from results, and one whose `channel` is missing is excluded whenever a channel scope is supplied.
- **This loads the ENTIRE videos collection into memory on every request.** `list_documents` fetches all documents and all filtering/scoring/sorting happens in application memory. There is no index-backed search; cost grows linearly with collection size on every call.
- **`channel` scoping is exact-equality (case-insensitive), not substring.** Unlike the title match (substring `contains`), the channel filter requires the whole channel string to equal the scope. `channel=sci` will not match a channel named `science`.
- **The `query` echoed back preserves original casing, but matching is lower-cased.** The envelope's `query` field returns what you sent (e.g. `"RuSt"`), while the actual matching used `"rust"`. Do not assume the echoed value reflects how matching was performed.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I searched and got `200` with an empty `videos` array and `total_matches: 0`. Isn't that supposed to be a `404`?**
A: No. An empty result set is a successful query over an existing collection resource. The absence of matches is data, not a missing resource. You get `200`, `total_matches: 0`, `returned_count: 0`, `videos: []`. The `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound` variant exists in the shared enum but this handler does not emit it for empty searches.

**Q: Why did my `relevance_score` values not line up with the order of the results?**
A: Because they measure different things. The ordering was computed against your search term; the number attached to each result was computed against the title itself. This is a real behavior of the current code, not a documentation typo. Trust the array order, ignore the number for ranking purposes.

**Q: Can I send the search term in a JSON request body instead of the query string?**
A: No. This is a `GET` endpoint and the handler never reads a body — it reads only `Query<HashMap<String, String>>`. Any body you send is ignored, and omitting the `query` query parameter yields `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` (yes, that variant name, even though the problem is a missing query parameter and not a body).

### `POST /api/alma-videos/registry/sync` — Reconcile the Video Registry Against the Raw Videos Collection

#### Synopsis

This endpoint reconciles the lightweight `video_registry` collection with the heavier `videos` collection, discovering videos that lack a matching registry entry and materialising fresh registry entries for them. It simultaneously counts registry entries that point at videos which no longer exist (orphans) without deleting them, and returns a compact numeric summary describing how far the registry had drifted and what corrective action was taken. It is the mutating half of a "scan and heal" workflow: it reads both collections, writes the missing index entries, and reports.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the parlance of Representational State Transfer, this is a `POST` — and it must be, for it is neither safe nor idempotent. It is not safe because it inserts new documents into the `video_registry` collection as an intended and observable side effect; a `GET` promising to synchronise anything would be a lie told to every intermediary cache between the client and the origin. It is not idempotent in the strict HTTP sense either: although a second invocation immediately following a first will (assuming the underlying collections are unchanged) discover zero missing videos and therefore insert nothing, each freshly minted registry entry is stamped with a newly generated `registry-{uuid}` identifier, so the operation is best understood as convergent-but-not-referentially-stable rather than mathematically idempotent. Because a reconciliation is fundamentally an action performed against a resource collection rather than the replacement of a single named resource, `POST` against the `/sync` sub-resource — rather than `PUT` against `/registry` — is the semantically honest verb.

Within a Domain-Driven Design topology, this handler sits squarely at the application boundary: it orchestrates two `DocumentCollectionPort` reads, a set of pure in-memory domain computations (set differencing between the two collections keyed on the Google Drive file identifier), and a sequence of writes back through the same port. The handler itself owns no persistence logic and no HTTP-framework knowledge beyond its extractors; every meaningful decision is delegated to small, individually testable free functions. This is the classic hexagonal arrangement — the transport adapter (axum) and the storage adapter (the document collection port) meet only through the application service that this function embodies, and the "registry" concept is treated as a derived read-model projected from the authoritative `videos` aggregate.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the type-state request pipeline before the handler body executes. The handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is the compile-time proof that authentication and authorization both succeeded; the value is bound to `_authorized_request` and deliberately left unused, but its mere presence forces the pipeline to run to completion.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: francesco@example.com` | Identifies the calling account. Consumed by the pipeline to drive the `Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized` transition. Absence surfaces as `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; a malformed or unrecognised value surfaces as `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 6b1c0e2a-9f4d-4a1a-8c2e-2b7f9d0a1c33` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces for this request. Not load-bearing for auth, but strongly advised so a given sync run can be located in the observability stack. |
| `Content-Type` | No | `Content-Type: application/json` | This endpoint reads **no** request body, so a content type is not required. Sending one is harmless and ignored. |

**The type-state pipeline (verbatim explanation).** The request is modelled as `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`, where `Stage` is a phantom marker advancing through three states. First, `Validated`: the raw request has been shape-checked (headers present and well-formed) and lifted into the pipeline. Second, `Authenticated`: the credentials carried by `x-account-email` have been resolved to a known principal — if the header is missing the pipeline halts with `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, and if it is present but cannot be resolved it halts with `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Third, `Authorized`: the authenticated principal has been checked against the policy governing this route — failure halts with `AuthorizationWasDenied`. Only a request that has reached the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` state can be extracted into this handler, so the handler body is statically guaranteed to run against a fully validated, authenticated, and authorized request; there is no imperative auth check inside the function because the types have already discharged that obligation.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint takes no path segments beyond the fixed literal `/api/alma-videos/registry/sync` and reads no query string parameters.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

#### Request Body

This endpoint reads **no request body**. The handler signature contains only the `State` extractor and the authorized-request extractor; there is no `Json<T>` body extractor, and no field of any request payload is read anywhere in the handler or its helper functions. Any body sent by the client is silently ignored.

**(a) Field table**

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns `200 OK` with a JSON object produced by `render_synchronization_summary`. It contains exactly four integer fields.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `videosScanned` | integer (i64) | Total videos considered scanned during the run. Computed as the max of a registry-derived floor figure (`determine_scanned_video_total`, floored at 6 for an empty registry) and `persisted_entry_count + registered_entry_count`. |
| `channelsScanned` | integer (i64) | Count of distinct, non-blank `channelName` values found across existing registry documents (`compute_channels_scanned_total`). |
| `videosAdded` | integer (i64) | Number of new registry entries materialised for videos that had no matching registry entry (`compute_videos_added_during_sync`). |
| `staleEntriesDetected` | integer (i64) | Number of registry entries whose backing Google Drive file id is no longer present in the videos collection. These are counted only, **not** deleted by this endpoint (`count_stale_registry_entries_to_prune`). |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialised as an `HttpError` into a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The table below enumerates every `HttpError` variant and describes when it can arise for **this** endpoint specifically.

| Status | error_category | When (for this endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Not reachable through the body path here (no body is parsed), but retained for parity; would only appear if pipeline-level shape validation rejected the request framing. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the request body was malformed"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The `x-account-email` header is absent, so the pipeline cannot advance past `Validated` into `Authenticated`. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` is present but does not resolve to a known principal. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal is not permitted to run a registry synchronisation, so the pipeline halts at the `Authorized` transition. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not raised by this handler's own logic (it operates on whole collections, not a named resource); listed for completeness. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested resource was not found"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any of the `list_documents` reads on `video_registry`/`videos`, or any `insert_document` write during `insert_newly_discovered_registry_entries`, fails at the document collection port and propagates via `?`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"an upstream application failure occurred"}` |

**Full SerializedErrorBody example**

```json

  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "an upstream application failure occurred"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler calls the following real helper functions, in this order:

1. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEO_REGISTRY_COLLECTION_NAME)` — reads all documents from the `video_registry` collection (`?`-propagates failures as `UpstreamApplicationFailure`).
2. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — reads all documents from the `videos` collection.
3. `compute_registered_entry_count(&registry_documents)` — returns the number of documents already in the registry (`registry_documents.len()`).
4. `determine_scanned_video_total(registered_entry_count)` — derives a "videos scanned" figure, applying a floor of `6` when the registry is empty, otherwise passing the count through.
5. `collect_distinct_channels_from_registry(&registry_documents)` — collects distinct, non-blank `channelName` values from registry documents in first-seen order.
6. `extract_channel_name_from_registry_document(...)` — helper used above; reads `channelName` as a non-empty string, else `None`.
7. `compute_channels_scanned_total(&distinct_channels)` — the count of distinct channels.
8. `identify_videos_absent_from_registry(&video_documents, &registry_documents)` — set-difference: videos whose Google Drive file id is not present in any registry entry.
9. `build_registry_entry_from_video_document(video_document, generate_registry_entry_identifier())` — for each missing video, mints a new `StoredDocument` copying `googleDriveFileId`, `channelName` (default `"uncategorized"`), `videoTitle`/`title` (default `"Untitled video"`), plus `sourceVideoIdentifier` and `discoveredBySync: true`.
10. `generate_registry_entry_identifier()` — produces `registry-{uuid_v4}`.
11. `compute_videos_added_during_sync(&new_entries)` — the count of newly built entries.
12. `identify_registry_entries_absent_from_videos_collection(&registry_documents, &video_documents)` — set-difference: registry entries whose file id is missing from videos (or which have no file id at all) are orphans.
13. `extract_google_drive_file_identifier_from_document(...)` — helper reading `googleDriveFileId` or legacy `googleDriveFileIdentifier`, non-empty.
14. `extract_document_identifier_as_str(...)` — helper borrowing a document's identifier for the orphan list.
15. `count_stale_registry_entries_to_prune(&orphaned_identifiers)` — the count of orphaned entries (counted, not deleted).
16. `insert_newly_discovered_registry_entries(document_collection, new_entries)` — inserts each new entry into `video_registry` and returns the successfully inserted count (`?`-propagates failures).
17. `render_synchronization_summary(videos_scanned, channels_scanned, videos_added, entries_pruned)` — shapes the four-field JSON response; `videos_scanned` is `scanned_video_total.max(persisted_entry_count + registered_entry_count)`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Orphans are detected, never deleted.** `staleEntriesDetected` counts registry entries whose backing video is gone, but this handler makes no delete calls; a separate prune step is implied by the summary but not performed here.
- **`videosScanned` is a derived, partly synthetic figure.** For an empty registry it is floored at `6` even though zero real videos were indexed, then reconciled via `max(...)` against `persisted + registered`. Do not treat it as an exact count of physical video documents.
- **New entry identifiers are non-deterministic.** Each materialised entry gets a fresh `registry-{uuid}`, so re-running the sync after external changes never reproduces the same identifiers — the operation converges in effect but is not referentially idempotent.
- **Dual key spelling for the Drive id.** Matching tolerates both `googleDriveFileId` (primary) and `googleDriveFileIdentifier` (legacy). A newly built entry, however, always writes the canonical `googleDriveFileId`.
- **Videos without a Drive id are skipped entirely.** In `identify_videos_absent_from_registry`, a video lacking a non-empty file id returns `false` and is never indexed; conversely a *registry* entry lacking a file id is always treated as orphaned.
- **Blank channel names are ignored for counting but defaulted on write.** `channelsScanned` skips blank/whitespace `channelName`s, yet a new entry built from a video missing `channelName` is stamped `"uncategorized"`.
- **Inserts are sequential and non-transactional at this layer.** `insert_newly_discovered_registry_entries` loops and awaits one insert at a time; a failure mid-loop propagates as `UpstreamApplicationFailure`, potentially leaving some entries already persisted.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Does this endpoint delete the stale/orphaned registry entries it reports?**
A: No. It counts them into `staleEntriesDetected` and moves on. Deletion is somebody else's job.

**Q: Is it safe to call twice in a row?**
A: Yes, in the sense that a second immediate run should add nothing new. No, in the sense that it is not idempotent: fresh UUID identifiers would be minted for anything it does find, so do not build retry logic that assumes byte-identical outcomes.

**Q: Why does `videosScanned` sometimes read `6` when I have fewer than six videos?**
A: Because `determine_scanned_video_total` applies a floor of `6` for an empty registry so a brand-new registry reports a "sensible" number, and the final value is a `max(...)` of that against the real inserted-plus-existing count. It is a reported figure, not a physical census.

### `POST /api/alma-videos/upload` — Register (Upload) a Video Document

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts a JSON descriptor of a video the caller wishes to register, validates the declared file name, extension, and byte size against server-side rules, and persists a freshly-minted video document into the `videos` document collection. It does **not** accept the video bytes themselves — despite the name "upload" — but rather records metadata about a video (optionally already staged in Google Drive) under the authenticated principal's ownership. On success it returns a JSON confirmation object echoing the normalized file metadata plus a server-derived ISO-8601 upload timestamp.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the strictest reading of REST semantics, `POST` is the appropriate verb here precisely because this operation is neither safe nor idempotent: each invocation with an identical body manufactures a brand-new document identifier (a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()`) and inserts a distinct row into the `videos` collection, so replaying the request N times yields N documents. This is the canonical "append a subordinate resource to a collection" pattern for which `POST` was designed; a `PUT` would have implied caller-supplied idempotency keys and last-writer-wins overwrite semantics that this handler deliberately does not provide. The endpoint is therefore unsafe (it mutates server state) and non-idempotent (retries multiply the effect), and any client-side retry logic must account for this by treating a failed-but-possibly-applied request as ambiguous.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, this handler sits squarely in the HTTP adapter layer (the `alma-http` crate), acting as a thin anti-corruption boundary between untyped external JSON (`serde_json::Value`) and the domain's validated value objects (`Email`, `NonEmptyText`). It performs input validation and orchestration but delegates the actual write to the `DocumentCollectionPort` — a port in the hexagonal-architecture sense — so the handler never speaks directly to a database driver. The "video document" is treated as a document-shaped aggregate keyed by an opaque identifier and stamped with an `owningAccount`; the handler enriches the caller's payload with derived fields (`fileSizeLabel`, `kind`, `owningAccount`) before persistence, reflecting the principle that the domain, not the client, owns the canonical shape of stored state.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

The handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is a **type-state** proof that the request has already traversed the full authentication and authorization pipeline before this code runs. The authenticated identity is retrieved via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()`, and that string is subsequently re-parsed into a domain `Email`.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `owner@example.com` | The principal's identity. Consumed by the pipeline to produce the authenticated/authorized principal; this handler reads it back via `authorized_principal()` and re-parses it as an `Email`. If it is not a valid email, the handler returns `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` (annotated `principal`). |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `3f1c9b0e-7a2d-4c3e-9f11-2b6d5a8c4e77` | Correlation identifier for tracing and log correlation across the pipeline stages. Not read by the handler body directly but threaded through the request pipeline for observability. |

**Type-state pipeline (`Validated → Authenticated → Authorized`).** The `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>` wrapper encodes, in Rust's type system, which stages a request has cleared. A request is first parsed and shape-checked into a `Validated` state; it is then resolved against the identity backing store to become `Authenticated` (a real principal is now attached); finally it is checked against access-control policy to become `Authorized` (`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`). Because this handler's parameter type is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, it is a compile-time impossibility for the handler to execute against a request that has not passed all three stages — the axum extractor machinery will reject the request with the appropriate `401`/`403` long before this function body is entered. The handler therefore never re-implements auth logic; it merely consumes the already-proven principal.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and reads the following fields by name. There is no strongly-typed request struct; every field is looked up dynamically.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fileName` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; must be non-empty (`NonEmptyText`); must end in a recognized video extension (`.mp4`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.avi`, `.m4v`, case-insensitive). | — | The declared name of the video file, including its extension. |
| `fileSize` | integer \| numeric string | Yes | Must be a JSON number **or** a numeric string parseable as `i64`; must be `>= 0`; must be `<= 5368709120` (5 GiB). | — | The declared size of the video in bytes. Front-ends frequently serialize this as a string; both forms are accepted. |
| `channelName` | string | No | If present, trimmed; if non-blank, parsed as `NonEmptyText`. | The owning account's email address | The channel under which to register the video. Blank/whitespace-only/absent values fall back to the owning account email. |
| `googleDriveFileId` | string | No | If present and non-blank (after trim), used as the Drive identifier. Accepts either `googleDriveFileId` or `google_drive_file_id`; `googleDriveFileId` is checked first. | absent (field omitted from stored doc) | Identifier of an already-staged file in Google Drive. Only added to the persisted document when non-blank. |
| `google_drive_file_id` | string | No | snake_case alias of the above; consulted only if `googleDriveFileId` is absent. | absent | See `googleDriveFileId`. |

Any additional fields present in the body are ignored.

**(d) Rust struct mirror**

This is a documentation mirror only; the handler actually reads an untyped `serde_json::Value`. The equivalent strongly-typed shape would be:

```rust
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct UploadVideoDocumentRequestMirror {
    /// Required. Parsed into `NonEmptyText`; must carry a recognized video extension.
    file_name: String,

    channel_name: Option<String>,
    /// Optional. Preferred camelCase Google Drive id.
    #[serde(default)]
    google_drive_file_id_camel: Option<String>, // "googleDriveFileId"
    /// Optional. snake_case alias, consulted only if camelCase absent.
    #[serde(default, rename = "google_drive_file_id")]
    google_drive_file_id_snake: Option<String>,
}
```

#### Successful Response

Status: `200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is the confirmation object assembled by `render_upload_confirmation`, augmented with `uploadedAt`.

**Response field table**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fileName` | string | Echo of the validated file name. |
| `fileSize` | string | The declared byte count, rendered as a **string** (via `.to_string()`), not a number. |
| `fileSizeLabel` | string | Human-friendly size label (e.g. `15.00 MB`), computed with binary (1024) divisors and 2 decimal places above bytes. |
| `channelName` | string | The resolved channel name (may be the owning account email if `channelName` was blank/absent). |
| `message` | string | Constant success message: `"Video uploaded and registry updated successfully"`. |
| `uploadedAt` | string | Server-derived ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the upload event, e.g. `2026-07-07T12:34:56Z`. |

**JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)**

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "UploadVideoDocumentResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["fileName", "fileSize", "fileSizeLabel", "channelName", "message", "uploadedAt"],
  "properties": {
    "fileName": { "type": "string" },
    "fileSize": { "type": "string" },
    "fileSizeLabel": { "type": "string" },
    "channelName": { "type": "string" },
    "message": { "type": "string" },
    "uploadedAt": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

**Realistic 200 example**

```json
{
  "fileName": "lecture-01.mp4",
  "fileSize": "15728640",
  "fileSizeLabel": "15.00 MB",
  "channelName": "Physics 101",
  "message": "Video uploaded and registry updated successfully",
  "uploadedAt": "2026-07-07T12:34:56Z"
}
```

Note carefully: the response's `fileSize` is a **string** even though the request accepts a number, and the confirmation does **not** include the generated document identifier, the `googleDriveFileId`, the `owningAccount`, or the `kind` field — those are persisted but not echoed.

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Body is not valid JSON; `fileName` missing/not a string/empty; `fileName` lacks a recognized video extension; `fileSize` missing/non-numeric/negative/over 5 GiB; the authenticated principal is not a valid `Email`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"The 'fileName' field is required and must be a string."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The `x-account-email` header (credential) is absent — rejected by the pipeline before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were missing."}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Supplied credential does not resolve to a known/valid principal — rejected by the pipeline before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"Authentication credentials were invalid."}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Authenticated principal lacks permission to reach this route — rejected by the pipeline before the handler runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"Authorization was denied."}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not produced by this handler's own logic (there is no lookup); reserved by the shared error taxonomy. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"The requested resource was not found."}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The `document_collection.insert_document` call into the `videos` collection fails (persistence/port error propagated via `?`). | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"An upstream application failure occurred."}` |

**Full example error body**

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "The declared file size (6442450944 bytes) exceeds the maximum of 5368709120 bytes."
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `parse_owning_account_email_from_principal` — Re-parses the authorized principal string into a validated `Email`; maps failure to `400` annotated `principal`.
2. `extract_uploaded_file_name_from_body` — Reads the required `fileName` string and parses it into a `NonEmptyText`.
3. `validate_uploaded_file_extension_is_video` — Lowercases the file name and confirms its extension is one of the six recognized video containers.
4. `extract_declared_file_size_bytes_from_body` — Reads `fileSize` from a JSON number or numeric string into an `i64` and rejects negatives.
5. `validate_declared_file_size_within_limit` — Rejects sizes exceeding the 5 GiB (`5368709120`-byte) ceiling.
6. `extract_target_channel_name_from_body` — Reads/trims optional `channelName`, falling back to the owning account email when blank/absent.
7. `extract_optional_google_drive_file_identifier_from_body` — Reads an optional Drive id under either `googleDriveFileId` or `google_drive_file_id`, ignoring blanks.
8. `generate_uploaded_video_identifier` — Produces a fresh UUID v4 string as the document identifier.
9. `build_uploaded_video_document_body` — Assembles the persisted JSON body (`fileName`, `fileSize`, `fileSizeLabel`, `channelName`, `owningAccount`, `kind: "video"`).
10. (inline) — Conditionally injects `googleDriveFileId` into the document body when a Drive id was supplied.
11. `format_declared_file_size_as_string` — (called from step 9) Renders the byte count as a human-friendly label using binary units.
12. `assemble_stored_video_document` — Wraps the identifier, owning account, and body into a `StoredDocument`.
13. `persist_uploaded_video_document` — Calls `DocumentCollectionPort::insert_document(VIDEOS_COLLECTION_NAME, ...)`; propagates port failures as `500`.
14. `render_upload_confirmation` — Builds the confirmation JSON echoing normalized metadata and the constant success message.
15. `derive_upload_timestamp_iso8601` → `format_unix_seconds_as_iso8601` → `civil_date_from_days` — Derives the current UTC time as an ISO-8601 string (Howard Hinnant's civil-from-days algorithm) and stamps it onto `uploadedAt`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **No bytes are uploaded.** Despite the route name `/upload`, this endpoint registers *metadata* only. The actual video content must already exist elsewhere (e.g. Google Drive); this call never touches file bytes.
- **`fileSize` is a string on the way out.** The request accepts a number or numeric string, but `render_upload_confirmation` calls `.to_string()`, so the response `fileSize` is always a JSON string. Clients round-tripping the value must not assume the type is preserved.
- **`channelName` silently defaults to your email.** A blank, whitespace-only, or missing `channelName` does not error — it is silently replaced by the owning account email. If you expected a validation error for an empty channel, you will instead get a document filed under your email address as the channel.
- **Google Drive id spelling precedence.** If both `googleDriveFileId` and `google_drive_file_id` are supplied, the camelCase key wins (it is checked first). Blank Drive ids are dropped entirely and the field is omitted from the stored document rather than stored as empty.
- **Every call creates a new document.** The identifier is a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` on each request; there is no de-duplication. Retrying an ambiguous request will create duplicate video documents.
- **The confirmation hides most persisted state.** The generated document identifier, `owningAccount`, `kind`, and `googleDriveFileId` are stored but never returned. There is no way to learn the new document's id from this response alone.
- **The principal is re-validated as an email.** If the pipeline authorized a principal that does not parse as an `Email`, the handler still returns `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` (annotated `principal`) — an authorization success can still yield a body-shaped error here.
- **Extension check is anchored to the last dot.** `validate_uploaded_file_extension_is_video` inspects only the substring after the final `.` and requires the name to contain a `.`; a name like `movie.mp4.txt` would be rejected (extension `txt`), and `noextension` is rejected outright.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I POSTed the same body twice and now I have two videos. Is that a bug?**
A: No. This endpoint is non-idempotent by design; each call mints a new UUID and inserts a new document. If you need at-most-once semantics, deduplicate on the client or before you call it.

**Q: Where do I put the actual video file?**
A: Not here. This endpoint records metadata only. Stage the bytes in Google Drive (or wherever your storage lives) and pass its identifier via `googleDriveFileId`. The endpoint never reads a multipart body or file stream.

**Q: Why is `fileSize` a number in my request but a string in the response?**
A: Because `render_upload_confirmation` stringifies it with `.to_string()`. The stored document keeps it as an integer; only the HTTP confirmation coerces it to a string. Yes, this is asymmetric. No, it will not be normalized for you.

---

### `GET /api/alma-videos/test-access` — Verify Video Access & Enumerate Readable Videos

#### Synopsis

This read-only endpoint answers the question "which stored ALMA videos can the currently authenticated principal actually reach, and is the video catalogue healthy enough to stream?" It lists every document in the `videos` collection, narrows the set to documents owned by the calling principal (plus globally-shared, owner-less documents), renders each survivor into a compact summary object, and folds an integrity report (documents missing a Google Drive file identifier) into the same envelope. When no real documents survive the filter, it deterministically substitutes a three-item seed catalogue so the front-end always has something to render during first-run and demo scenarios.

#### Theory & Rationale

In strict REST terms this is a `GET`, and therefore both **safe** and **idempotent**: invoking it any number of times produces no observable server-side state mutation — it opens a read transaction against the document store, computes a projection, and returns. Because the response is a *computed view* rather than the canonical representation of a single addressable resource, the path (`/api/alma-videos/test-access`) is best read as a diagnostic/collection-verification resource rather than an entity resource; there is no `id` to `PUT` to, no body to `POST`, and no ETag ceremony to observe. The endpoint's safety guarantee is real but shallow: it does not write, yet its output is *not* referentially stable across calls, because the seed-fallback branch and the principal-scoped filter both make the body a function of (collection contents, calling identity, first-run emptiness) rather than of the URL alone. Cache it at your peril.

Within a Domain-Driven Design layering, this handler is squarely an **application/interface-adapter** concern rather than a domain one. The only true domain object it touches is `alma_domain::value_objects::Email`, which it uses as a validated value object to reject malformed principals at the boundary. Everything else — the readability predicate ("owned by me, or owner-less"), the drive-identifier alias resolution, the seed catalogue, the `status: "ok" | "degraded"` health label — is presentation-and-authorization glue that belongs to the HTTP adapter and is deliberately kept out of the domain core. The persistence boundary is respected through the `UnitOfWork` / `document_collection` ports; the handler never speaks to a concrete database, only to the injected `ApplicationState` port surface, so the same handler compiles against any `UnitOfWork` implementation.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This handler is only reachable *after* the request has traversed the full type-state pipeline and arrived as `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. That type is the compiler-enforced proof that authentication and authorization already succeeded before a single line of handler code ran.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: scientist@alma.org` | Carries the calling principal's email. It becomes `authorized_request.authorized_principal()`, is re-parsed here via `Email::parse`, and scopes the readable video set. A missing/blank value fails earlier in the pipeline (`AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`); a syntactically invalid value that somehow reaches the handler is rejected as `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a10-4b2e-4c8a-9d5e-2b1f0a6c8e44` | Correlation identifier surfaced as `authorized_request.correlation_identifier()`. This handler reads it (`let _ = (accessible_count, authorized_request.correlation_identifier());`) purely to bind it into the correlation log; it never affects the response body. If absent, the pipeline typically synthesizes one upstream. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated → Authenticated → Authorized`).** The alma-http pipeline models request lifecycle as distinct *type-states*, each a marker type parameterizing `HttpRequestInPipeline<S>`:

- **`RequestHasBeenValidated`** — the raw request has passed structural validation (well-formed headers, extractable shape). No identity is asserted yet.
- **`RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`** — a principal has been established from credentials (here, the `x-account-email` header). The request now *knows who it is*.
- **`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`** — the authenticated principal has been checked against the policy for this route and permitted. Only this final state exposes `.authorized_principal()`.

Because this handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the Rust type system makes it *impossible* to invoke the handler with an unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request — the router would fail to compile or the extractor would short-circuit with the appropriate `HttpError` long before the handler body executes. Authorization is thus not something this handler does; it is a precondition the handler's *type* requires.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The route `/api/alma-videos/test-access` has no path segments and the handler reads no query string.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` request and the handler reads **no request body whatsoever**. It extracts only `State(application_state)` and the authorized-request type-state; there is no `Json<...>` extractor in the signature. Any body sent by the client is ignored.

(a) Field table — there are no request body fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | None. No request body is read. |

#### Successful Response

**HTTP 200 OK**, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is a `serde_json::Value` envelope assembled by `assemble_access_verification_response`. Note the deliberate duplication: `videos` and `filesInFolder` are identical arrays (the latter is a legacy/compatibility alias).

Response field table:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string (`"ok"` \| `"degraded"`) | `"ok"` when there are zero verification errors; `"degraded"` when at least one stored video is missing a Google Drive file identifier. |
| `errors` | array of object | One entry per document that failed integrity verification. Empty array when healthy. |
| `errors[].code` | string | Always `"missing_google_drive_file_identifier"` for the current implementation. |
| `errors[].documentIdentifier` | string | The `document_identifier` of the offending stored video. |
| `errors[].message` | string | Human-readable explanation of the integrity failure. |
| `folder` | object | Descriptor for the synthetic root videos folder. |
| `folder.name` | string | Always `"ALMA Videos Root"`. |
| `folder.videoCount` | integer | Count of rendered videos (post-filter, post-seed-fallback). |
| `videos` | array of object | The accessible, rendered video summaries (or the seed catalogue when empty). |
| `videos[].id` | string | The document identifier (or seed id such as `drive_file_0001`). |
| `videos[].name` | string | Display name: first non-blank of `name`/`title`/`displayName`, else the document identifier. |
| `videos[].googleDriveFileId` | string | Resolved Drive file id (first non-blank of `googleDriveFileId`/`google_drive_file_id`/`driveFileId`), or `""` when absent. |
| `videos[].owningAccount` | string \| null | Owning account email, or `null` for owner-less/shared videos (and always `null` for seeds). |
| `videos[].hasStreamableSource` | boolean | `true` when a non-empty Drive file id was resolved. |
| `filesInFolder` | array of object | Exact duplicate of `videos` (compatibility alias). |
