### `GET /api/preprocessing-stream` — Describe the OCR Preprocessing Stream

#### Synopsis

Returns a stage-by-stage progress snapshot of the caller's most-relevant OCR *preprocessing* job — the deskew → denoise → binarize → segment pipeline that runs before optical character recognition proper. The handler selects a single preprocessing job document out of the shared `ocr_jobs` document collection (preferring one owned by the authenticated principal), reads its embedded `preprocessing` progress counters, and derives which stage is currently executing, how far along that stage is as a percentage, which stages have finished, any warnings emitted, and whether the job is ready to hand off to OCR. When no preprocessing job exists at all, it responds `200 OK` with a "nothing in progress" placebo body rather than a `404`.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is, in the purest Fielding-ian sense, a *safe* and *idempotent* read. It is a `GET`, it mutates nothing, it acquires no locks that outlive the request, and invoking it a thousand times in a row yields the same representation as invoking it once (modulo the underlying job advancing on its own). The resource being represented is the abstract notion of "the preprocessing stream" — note the response's self-describing `"streaming_available": true`, `"transport": "server sent events"`, `"resource": "preprocessing"` triplet — even though, in the current implementation, the endpoint returns a one-shot JSON *description* of that stream rather than an actual `text/event-stream`. The description is the resource; the transport is metadata about how a future client might subscribe. This is deliberate: the URL names a long-lived conceptual entity, and `GET` returns its current projection.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, the handler sits squarely in the *application/HTTP boundary layer* of the `ocr` bounded context. It owns no persistence logic of its own; it leans on the `document_collection` port (`list_documents`) and the `UnitOfWork` generic to reach the `ocr_jobs` collection, then performs pure, in-memory *derivation* — the raw persisted `preprocessing` counters are the ubiquitous-language fact, and the stages, percentages, and readiness flags are *derived read-model projections* computed at request time. Nothing is written back. The type-state pipeline (`HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`) guarantees at *compile time* that the handler body can only ever run for a request that has already been validated, authenticated, and authorized, so the handler is free to speak exclusively in domain nouns and never re-checks credentials.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: alice@example.com` | Identifies the authenticated principal. Becomes `authorized_request.authorized_principal()`, which drives job selection: jobs owned by this email are preferred over all others. Absent/blank ⇒ `401`. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7f3c1e42-9b0a-4d5e-8c21-2a6b0f9d1234` | Correlation identifier. Echoed back verbatim in the response as `correlation_identifier`. If omitted, the pipeline supplies/derives one; supplying your own makes cross-service tracing far easier. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated → Authenticated → Authorized`).** Every request to this endpoint is threaded through a compile-time state machine before your handler code is ever reached. The extractor in the signature is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — the generic type parameter *is* the proof. The stages are:

1. **Validated** — the raw inbound request is parsed and structurally checked (well-formed headers, decodable body if any). A failure here surfaces as `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. **Authenticated** — the identity headers (notably `x-account-email`) are resolved into a concrete principal. Missing credentials ⇒ `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; malformed/rejected credentials ⇒ `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`.
3. **Authorized** — the authenticated principal is checked against the policy governing this route. Denial ⇒ `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`.

Because the handler accepts only the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` marker, it is *impossible* to invoke it with a request that skipped a stage — the code would not compile. Consequently the handler body contains zero inline auth checks; it trusts the type. The authorized principal is extracted once via `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` and the correlation id via `authorized_request.correlation_identifier()`.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

The endpoint takes no path segments beyond the literal route and reads no query-string parameters. In particular, there is **no** `job_identifier` query parameter — the job is selected server-side (see the Internal Processing Pipeline). Any query string you append is silently ignored.

#### Request Body

This endpoint is a `GET` and reads **no request body whatsoever**. The handler signature contains no `Json<T>` request-body extractor; it takes only `State<…>` and the authorized-request marker. Do not send a body; if you do, it is ignored.

(a) Field table — there are no request fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| _(none)_ | — | — | — | — | This endpoint reads no request body. |

(b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the (empty) request body:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma.example/schemas/describe-preprocessing-stream-request.json",
  "title": "DescribePreprocessingStreamRequest",
  "description": "This GET endpoint accepts no request body.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

(c) TypeScript interface for the (empty) request body:

```typescript
// GET /api/preprocessing-stream takes no request body.
export interface DescribePreprocessingStreamRequest {}
```

(d) Rust struct mirror for the (empty) request body:

```rust
/// GET /api/preprocessing-stream takes no request body.
/// The handler only extracts `State<..>` and
/// `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
```

#### Request Examples

```bash

curl -sS -X GET 'https://api.alma.example/api/preprocessing-stream' \
  -H 'x-account-email: alice@example.com' \
  -H 'x-request-id: 7f3c1e42-9b0a-4d5e-8c21-2a6b0f9d1234'
```

```bash
# HTTPie
http GET 'https://api.alma.example/api/preprocessing-stream' \
  'x-account-email:alice@example.com' \
  'x-request-id:7f3c1e42-9b0a-4d5e-8c21-2a6b0f9d1234'
```

```javascript
// fetch
const response = await fetch("https://api.alma.example/api/preprocessing-stream", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    "x-account-email": "alice@example.com",
    "x-request-id": "7f3c1e42-9b0a-4d5e-8c21-2a6b0f9d1234",
  },
});
const body = await response.json();
console.log(body.current_stage, body.stage_completion_percentage);
```

#### Successful Response

`200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is a single JSON object. Its shape depends on whether a preprocessing job was found.

**When a job is found**, the object is assembled from `DescribePreprocessingStreamResponsePayload::into_json()` and then augmented with six additional fields inserted directly by the handler:

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `streaming_available` | boolean | Yes | Constant `true`. Advertises that a stream conceptually exists. |
| `transport` | string | Yes | Constant `"server sent events"`. Names the intended transport. |
| `resource` | string | Yes | Constant `"preprocessing"`. Names the resource. |
| `job_identifier` | string \| null | Yes | The selected job's identifier; `null` in the no-job branch. |
| `owning_account` | string \| null | Yes (found branch) | The `owning_account` of the selected job document; may be `null` if the stored document has no owner. |
| `current_stage` | string \| null | Yes | Slug of the stage currently executing: `deskew`, `denoise`, `binarize`, `segment`, or `completed`. `null` in the no-job branch. |
| `stage_completion_percentage` | integer (0–100) | Yes | How far the *current* stage is through its pages, clamped to `[0,100]`. `0` when `pages_total` is 0 or no job. |
| `stages` | array of objects | Yes | One descriptor per processing stage (deskew, denoise, binarize, segment). Empty array in the no-job branch. |
| `stages[].stage` | string | — | The stage slug. |
| `stages[].pages_completed` | integer | — | Pages that have cleared this stage (clamped to `pages_total` when `pages_total > 0`). |
| `stages[].pages_total` | integer | — | Total pages in the job (`pages_total`). |
| `stages[].is_finished` | boolean | — | `true` iff `pages_total > 0` and `pages_completed >= pages_total`. |
| `pages_deskewed` | integer | Yes (found branch) | Clamped deskew count. |
| `pages_denoised` | integer | Yes (found branch) | Clamped denoise count. |
| `completed_stages` | array of string | Yes (found branch) | Slugs of stages whose `pages_completed >= pages_total`. |
| `warnings` | array of string | Yes (found branch) | Non-empty warning strings, re-validated through `NonEmptyText`. |
| `remaining_stage_count` | integer (0–4) | Yes (found branch) | Number of the four processing stages not yet finished. |
| `is_ready_for_ocr` | boolean | Yes (found branch) | `true` iff the derived current stage is `completed`. |
| `correlation_identifier` | string | Yes (found branch) | The request's correlation id (from `x-request-id`). |
| `message` | string | Only in no-job branch | `"no preprocessing job is currently in progress"`. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized through `HttpError` into a uniform `SerializedErrorBody` of `{error_category, error_explanation}`. The table lists every `HttpError` variant and precisely when it can arise *for this endpoint*.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Not produced on the normal path. The `parse_..._job_identifier` helper *can* emit this variant, but the handler calls it via `select_..._identifier`, which swallows the `Result` with `.ok()`; a malformed candidate identifier yields `None` (→ no-job `200`), not a `400`. Reachable only if the pipeline itself rejects a malformed request earlier. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"a preprocessing job identifier is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The `x-account-email` / auth headers are absent, so the request never reaches the `Authenticated` state. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Credentials are present but rejected during the `Authenticated` stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal fails the policy check for this route during the `Authorized` stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Raised by `load_..._job_record_..._transactional_unit` when the *selected* identifier is not found in the fetched documents. In practice near-unreachable, because the identifier was chosen from those same documents; a `404` implies a race/mutation between selection and load. Note: a completely empty collection yields `200` (no-job branch), **not** `404`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no preprocessing job could be located for identifier 'job-42_a'"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Raised by `query_..._current_progress` when the selected job document's body has **no `preprocessing` section**. Also propagated (`?`) if `document_collection.list_documents(...)` fails. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"the preprocessing progress query failed: the job record does not contain a preprocessing section"}` |

One full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "the preprocessing progress query failed: the job record does not contain a preprocessing section"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler body executes the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` — extracts the authenticated account email from the type-state-proven request.
2. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(OCR_JOBS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — awaits all stored documents in the `"ocr_jobs"` collection; an error here propagates as `500 UpstreamApplicationFailure` via `?`.
3. `select_preprocessing_stream_job_identifier(&stored_documents, &authenticated_account)` — picks the job to describe: prefers documents owned by the principal, else the whole set; within the pool takes the one with the highest `preprocessing.pages_total` (ties broken by identifier). Returns `None` ⇒ handler short-circuits with the no-job `200`.
4. `load_preprocessing_stream_job_record_within_transactional_unit(&stored_documents, &job_identifier)` — finds the matching `StoredDocument` and materializes a `PersistedPreprocessingJobRecord`; missing ⇒ `404`.
5. `query_preprocessing_stream_job_current_progress(&job_record)` — reads the `preprocessing` section's page counters and `warnings`; absent section ⇒ `500`.
6. `derive_preprocessing_stream_job_current_stage(&progress_snapshot)` — walks deskew→denoise→binarize→segment→completed to find the first unfinished stage.
7. `compute_preprocessing_stream_job_stage_completion_percentage(&progress_snapshot)` — computes `(pages_completed * 100 / pages_total)`, clamped to `0..=100`.
8. `build_preprocessing_stream_job_stage_descriptors(&progress_snapshot)` — builds the four `stages[]` descriptors with per-stage `pages_completed`, `pages_total`, `is_finished`.
9. `count_preprocessing_stream_job_pages_deskewed(&progress_snapshot)` — clamped deskew page count.
10. `count_preprocessing_stream_job_pages_denoised(&progress_snapshot)` — clamped denoise page count.
11. `list_preprocessing_stream_job_completed_stages(&progress_snapshot)` — collects the stages whose count `>= pages_total`.
12. `collect_preprocessing_stream_job_stage_warnings(&progress_snapshot)` — re-validates warning strings through `NonEmptyText::parse`, dropping any that fail.
13. `estimate_preprocessing_stream_job_remaining_stage_count(&progress_snapshot)` — `4 - completed_processing_stages` (saturating).
14. `determine_preprocessing_stream_job_is_ready_for_ocr(&progress_snapshot)` — `true` iff the current stage is `completed`.
15. `assemble_describe_preprocessing_stream_response_payload(...)` — packs job id, owner, current stage slug, percentage, and descriptors into the payload struct.
16. `response_payload.into_json()` then manual `response_object.insert(...)` calls — serializes the payload and grafts on `pages_deskewed`, `pages_denoised`, `completed_stages`, `warnings`, `remaining_stage_count`, `is_ready_for_ocr`, and `correlation_identifier` (from `authorized_request.correlation_identifier()`).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Empty collection returns `200`, not `404`.** If `ocr_jobs` has no documents, `select_...` returns `None` and the handler emits the no-job body with `job_identifier: null`. Clients must handle `null` for `job_identifier`/`current_stage` and an empty `stages` array.
- **You cannot pick which job you get.** There is no `job_identifier` query parameter. Selection is heuristic: your own jobs are preferred, and the "most recent" is *approximated* by the largest `pages_total` — a small job of yours can be shadowed by... nothing, but a large job with a spurious `pages_total` would win within a pool. If you own no jobs, you may be shown *another account's* job (the fallback pool is all documents).
- **`pages_total == 0` degrades everything.** With zero pages, `current_stage` is forced to `deskew`, `stage_completion_percentage` is `0`, every `is_finished` is `false`, `completed_stages` is empty, and `remaining_stage_count` is `4` — even if the counters are non-zero. Also, in the "found" branch, `pages_deskewed`/`pages_denoised` are returned *unclamped* when `pages_total == 0`.
- **Counters are clamped, so `pages_completed` can silently mask overshoot.** If a stage reports more pages than `pages_total`, the response clamps it to `pages_total`; the raw over-count is never surfaced.
- **Missing `preprocessing` section is a 500, not a 404.** A job document that exists but lacks `preprocessing` is treated as an upstream failure (`UpstreamApplicationFailure`), whereas a truly missing document is a `404`. These are different failure modes for arguably-similar client-visible situations.
- **Warnings are double-filtered.** Blank/whitespace warnings are dropped once when read (`query_...`) and again when re-parsed through `NonEmptyText` (`collect_...`). Non-string array entries are ignored entirely. The `warnings` you get back are a strict subset of what's stored.
- **The `completed` slug never appears in `stages[]`.** Only the four *processing* stages are emitted as descriptors; `completed` can appear only as `current_stage`. Reconcile job completion via `is_ready_for_ocr`, not by scanning `stages[]` for `"completed"`.
- **`correlation_identifier` is only in the found branch.** The no-job `200` body omits it (and `owning_account`, `warnings`, etc.). Do not assume every `200` carries the correlation id.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: It's called a "stream" and the body says `"transport": "server sent events"` — why did I get a plain JSON object instead of an SSE stream?**
A: Because it returns a *description* of the stream, not the stream. The `streaming_available`/`transport` fields are advertising metadata about a conceptual SSE channel; the handler itself is an ordinary `GET` returning `Json<Value>`. Poll it if you want updates.

**Q: How do I request the progress of a specific job by id?**
A: You don't. There is no path or query parameter for a job id. The server selects one job for you (your own, largest `pages_total`, ties broken by identifier). If you need per-job addressing, that is a different endpoint that does not exist here.

**Q: I sent a request body / query string and it was ignored. Is that a bug?**
A: No. This is a `GET` with no body extractor and no query parameters. Anything you attach is discarded by design. The only inputs that matter are the `x-account-email` (selection) and `x-request-id` (echoed) headers.

### `POST /api/ocr-retry` — Retry a Failed, Errored, or Cancelled OCR Job

#### Synopsis

This endpoint re-dispatches an optical-character-recognition (OCR) job that previously reached a terminal-but-recoverable state — specifically `failed`, `errored`, or `cancelled`/`canceled` — by loading the persisted job record, verifying it is genuinely retryable, incrementing its retry attempt counter, re-issuing the recognition request against the *same* source artifact (optionally scoped to the pages that previously failed), and persisting the new retry metadata. It computes and returns an exponential backoff delay so the caller knows how long to wait before polling for results, and records an audit entry describing the accepted retry. The endpoint is transactional, account-scoped, and idempotent only in the loosest sense: each successful call increments the attempt counter and therefore mutates state.

#### Theory & Rationale

From the vantage point of REST semantics, `POST /api/ocr-retry` is a *command* rather than a *query*: it is neither safe (it mutates the persisted OCR job record's `status`, `retry_attempt_number`, and `active_handle`) nor idempotent (two identical requests produce two distinct attempt numbers, two distinct handles, and two distinct backoff delays). We deliberately do **not** model this as `PUT /api/ocr-jobs/{id}` — although a case could be made for representing a retry as a state transition on the job resource — because the operation is a verb-shaped side-effecting instruction ("retry this job now"), not the idempotent replacement of a representation. The `POST`-to-a-command-collection idiom (`/api/ocr-retry`) is the honest HTTP mapping of an intent that cannot be replayed without consequence, and it keeps the retry-dispatch concern out of the generic job-representation surface.

Within a Domain-Driven Design layering, this handler sits squarely in the HTTP adapter (the `crates/http` boundary) and does no domain reasoning of its own beyond orchestration. It delegates persistence to the `document_collection` port, delegates the actual recognition work to the `artificial_intelligence_adapter` port, and confines the only genuine invariants it owns — "which statuses are retryable" and "how many attempts are permitted" — to small, individually-tested helper functions. The `PersistedOcrJobIdentifier` newtype is the archetypal DDD move: by wrapping a validated `String` in a type that can only be constructed through `parse_retry_ocr_job_identifier`, the code makes it *structurally impossible* to pass an unvalidated identifier deeper into the pipeline, pushing a runtime concern up into the type system where the compiler enforces it for free.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Authentication and authorization are enforced *before* the handler body executes, by virtue of the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor in the handler signature. If the type-state extractor fails to construct, the handler is never entered and the appropriate 401/403 error is returned by the pipeline machinery.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended (effectively required) | `x-request-id: 6f1c2a9e-3b7d-4c81-9f0a-2e5d8b4c1a77` | Correlation identifier threaded through the request pipeline and echoed into logs/audit. Supply a fresh UUID per request; if omitted, correlation across the dispatch/persist/audit stages is lost. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@example.com` | Identifies the calling account. Drives authentication (who you are) and authorization (whether you may touch this OCR job). Absent or empty → `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`. Malformed → `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Present-but-not-permitted → `AuthorizationWasDenied`. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | The body is parsed by axum's `Json<Value>` extractor; a non-JSON or unparseable body yields `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The alma-http request pipeline models the security lifecycle of a request as a sequence of *type states*, each a distinct marker type that a request can only be tagged with once the corresponding stage has succeeded:

1. **Validated** — the raw request has been structurally validated (headers present and well-formed, body extractable). Only a `Validated` request is eligible to be authenticated.
2. **Authenticated** — the `x-account-email` credential has been verified and resolved to a known account. A request cannot become `Authenticated` unless it was first `Validated`; the transition consumes the earlier state.
3. **Authorized** — the authenticated account has been checked against the policy governing this operation and found permitted. Only an `Authorized` request can be handed to a handler that demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`.

Because this handler's signature demands `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`, the compiler guarantees that no code path can reach the handler body without having traversed *all three* stages in order. There is no `if authenticated { ... }` check inside the handler because there cannot be an unauthenticated request inside the handler — the state is proven by construction. The `_authorized_request` binding is intentionally unused (prefixed with `_`): its mere presence in the signature is the enforcement mechanism.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint takes no path segments beyond the fixed `/api/ocr-retry` and reads no query-string parameters. All input arrives in the JSON request body.

#### Request Body

The handler extracts the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then reads exactly one field directly. Every other field consulted by the pipeline is read from the *persisted* OCR job record (loaded from the `ocr_jobs` collection), **not** from the request body. The table below lists only what the handler reads from the *request body*.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_identifier` | `string` | Yes | Trimmed; must be non-empty after trimming; length after trimming must be `<= 256` characters | — | The identifier of the OCR job to retry. Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped before use. Missing field, non-string value, empty-after-trim, or over-256-characters each yield `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. |

Any additional fields present in the request body are silently ignored — only `job_identifier` is consulted.

#### Successful Response

**Status:** `200 OK` · **Body:** `application/json`

The response is produced by `RetryOcrJobResponsePayload::into_json`, so the wire field names differ slightly from the internal struct: the internal `job_status` field is serialized under the key `status`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `job_identifier` | `string` | The validated (trimmed) identifier of the retried job. |
| `retry_attempt_number` | `integer` (u32) | The attempt number this retry represents. `1` for a job that had never been retried; otherwise the previously-stored count plus one. |
| `backoff_delay_seconds` | `integer` (u64) | Exponential backoff before the retry effectively begins: `2^(attempt-1) * 2` seconds, capped at `300`. So attempt 1 → 2s, attempt 2 → 4s, attempt 3 → 8s, attempt 4 → 16s, attempt 5 → 32s. |
| `status` | `string` | Always `"retried"` on success (derived from the presence of a recorded audit action; `"unknown"` is only reachable if the audit action were empty, which it never is on this path). |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The table lists every `HttpError` variant, whether it can arise on *this* endpoint, and when.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `job_identifier` missing / not a string / empty after trim / over 256 chars; OR the loaded job is not in a retryable status; OR the job has exhausted its 5 permitted attempts; OR the persisted record is missing its `source_storage_key`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'job_identifier' field is required"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` absent/empty — request never reaches the handler body (blocked at the Authenticated stage of the pipeline). | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| `401` | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` present but malformed / unresolvable to a known account — blocked at the Authenticated stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| `403` | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Authenticated account is not permitted to retry this OCR job — blocked at the Authorized stage of the pipeline before the handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| `404` | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No OCR job exists under the given identifier at load time; OR the record vanished between load and `replace_document` (the replace reported the record did not exist). | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no ocr job exists under the identifier 'ocr-job-2026-07-07-abc123'"}` |
| `500` | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The `artificial_intelligence_adapter.generate_completion` dispatch returned an `ApplicationError`; OR the `document_collection` fetch/replace propagated an error. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"failed to dispatch the ocr retry: <adapter error>"}` |

**Full SerializedErrorBody example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "an ocr job in status 'completed' cannot be retried"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. **`parse_retry_ocr_job_identifier(raw)`** — trims the raw identifier, rejects empty / whitespace-only / over-256-char values, and wraps the survivor in the `PersistedOcrJobIdentifier` newtype.
2. **`application_state.document_collection.fetch_document(OCR_JOBS_COLLECTION_NAME, id)`** — loads the stored document (if any) for the job from the `"ocr_jobs"` collection.
3. **`load_ocr_job_record_from_stored_document(doc, id)`** — converts the optional stored document into a `PersistedOcrJobRecord`, mapping absence to a 404 `RequestedResourceWasNotFound`.
4. **`validate_ocr_job_is_in_retryable_state(record)`** — reads `status`, lowercases it, and permits only `failed` / `errored` / `cancelled` / `canceled`; anything else → 400.
5. **`compute_ocr_job_next_retry_attempt_number(record)`** — reads the stored `retry_attempt_number` (defaulting to 0) and returns it saturating-plus-one.
6. **`reject_ocr_job_retry_when_maximum_attempts_exhausted(next, 5)`** — rejects with 400 if the prospective attempt number exceeds `MAXIMUM_OCR_JOB_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` (5).
7. **`resolve_ocr_job_retry_source_descriptor(record)`** — reads `source_storage_key` (required → 400 if absent) and `source_content_type` (defaults to `"application/pdf"`).
8. **`build_ocr_job_retry_processing_request(record, source, next)`** — assembles the `OcrJobProcessingRequest`, including the deduped/sorted failed page indices via **`collect_ocr_job_previously_failed_page_indices(record)`**.
9. **`describe_ocr_job_retry_prompt(request)`** — builds the natural-language prompt (`NonEmptyText`) describing the retry, listing specific pages or "all pages", with a constant fallback.
10. **`application_state.artificial_intelligence_adapter.generate_completion(prompt)`** — dispatches the retry to the AI adapter.
11. **`interpret_ocr_job_retry_dispatch_outcome(outcome, id, next)`** — on success builds a handle via **`build_ocr_job_retry_handle`** (`"{id}::retry::{n}"`); on error maps to 500 via **`map_ocr_job_retry_dispatch_error_to_http_error`**.
12. **`update_ocr_job_record_retry_metadata(record, next, handle)`** — clones the body and sets `status="retried"`, `retry_attempt_number`, and `active_handle`, preserving all other fields.
13. **`application_state.document_collection.replace_document(OCR_JOBS_COLLECTION_NAME, updated)`** — persists the updated document; a `false` return (record vanished) yields 404 via **`map_ocr_job_not_found_error_to_http_error`**.
14. **`compute_ocr_job_retry_backoff_delay_seconds(next)`** — computes `2 * 2^(n-1)` capped at 300 seconds.
15. **`record_ocr_job_retry_audit_entry(id, next)`** — builds the `OcrJobAuditEntry` with action `ocr_job_retry_attempt_{n}_accepted`.
16. **`assemble_retry_ocr_job_response_payload(id, next, backoff, audit)`** — assembles the `RetryOcrJobResponsePayload`, deriving `status` from the (non-empty) audit action; `into_json` serializes it to the wire.

Supporting shared helper: **`read_string_field(body, name)`** — reads a string field from a JSON object, returning `None` when missing or non-string.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Attempt-counter monotonicity is per-call, not per-outcome.** Because the counter is incremented and persisted on *every* successful dispatch, calling this endpoint 5 times on a genuinely stuck job will burn all attempts and thereafter return 400 `RequestBodyWasMalformed` ("exhausted its 5 permitted retry attempts"), even though nothing about the underlying source changed. The maximum is checked against the *prospective* number (`next > 5`), so the 6th prospective attempt is the one that is rejected.
- **The wire status key is `status`, not `job_status`.** The internal struct field is `job_status`, but `into_json` renames it to `status`. Clients that key off `job_status` in the response will always see `undefined`.
- **`source_content_type` silently defaults to `application/pdf`.** If the persisted record lacks a `source_content_type`, the retry proceeds as if the source were a PDF. A stored image job missing that field will be described to the AI adapter as a PDF, which may be wrong but will not error.
- **A missing `source_storage_key` surfaces as a 400, not a 500.** Even though this is a data-integrity problem with the *stored* record (not the caller's request), the handler maps it to `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. The `error_explanation` ("the ocr job record is missing its 'source_storage_key'") is the only hint that the fault is server-side data, not client input.
- **The AI dispatch result is discarded.** `interpret_ocr_job_retry_dispatch_outcome` matches `Ok(_generated_completion)` and throws the completion away, synthesizing a *deterministic* handle `"{id}::retry::{n}"` instead. The handle is not derived from anything the adapter returned, so two retries at the same attempt number would collide — but the attempt number is monotonic, so in practice they don't.
- **Non-object bodies survive metadata update but write nothing.** `update_ocr_job_record_retry_metadata` only mutates the body if `as_object_mut()` succeeds; if the stored `job_body` is not a JSON object, the status/attempt/handle updates are silently skipped and the unchanged body is written back. (In practice job bodies are always objects.)
- **Backoff is advisory only.** The `backoff_delay_seconds` value is computed and returned but the handler does not itself sleep or schedule anything; honoring the delay is entirely the caller's responsibility. The AI dispatch has *already happened* by the time the delay is reported.
- **`cancelled` and `canceled` are both accepted.** The retryable-state check matches both British and American spellings, so a job stored under either normalization is eligible.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Is this endpoint idempotent? Can I safely retry the retry?**
A: No. Each successful call increments and persists the attempt counter, mints a new handle, sets `status` to `retried`, and returns a larger backoff. Replaying the same request body five times will exhaust the job's attempts and then return 400. If you need at-most-once semantics, deduplicate on your side using `x-request-id`.

**Q: The job is `completed` and I want to run OCR again anyway. Why do I get a 400?**
A: Because a `completed` job is, by definition, not in a retryable state. Only `failed`, `errored`, `cancelled`, or `canceled` jobs are eligible. To reprocess a completed job, create a fresh job via `POST /api/ocr` rather than retrying an old one.

**Q: I sent `jobId` / `id` / `jobIdentifier` and got "the 'job_identifier' field is required." Why?**
A: The handler reads exactly the snake_case key `job_identifier` and nothing else. Camel-case, kebab-case, or alternate names are ignored, which leaves the required field effectively missing. Send `job_identifier`.

**Q: My retry returned 200 but `backoff_delay_seconds` is 300 — did something go wrong?**
A: No; 300 is simply the configured ceiling (`OCR_JOB_RETRY_MAXIMUM_BACKOFF_SECONDS`). For normal attempt numbers 1–5 you will see 2/4/8/16/32, so 300 would only appear for attempt numbers far beyond the permitted maximum — which the attempt-exhaustion check prevents you from reaching on this endpoint anyway.

---

### `POST /api/cleanup-tmp` — Run Cleanup of Temporary OCR Artifacts

#### Synopsis

This endpoint executes a maintenance sweep over the OCR jobs collection, enumerating every temporary artifact (rasterized page images, staging manifests, and any other transient family) that has aged beyond a fixed 24-hour retention window, deleting those artifacts from the backing object store, and purging any OCR job records whose entire artifact set was reclaimed. It reports the number of keys deleted, the total number of bytes reclaimed, and a per-key list of any deletions that failed. Although the endpoint is a `POST` and the handler contains logic for a configurable scope, retention threshold, and confirmation token, in its current wiring it accepts **no request body whatsoever** — the scope, retention window, and confirmation token are all hardcoded inside the handler.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a strict REST standpoint, this is a maintenance action that mutates server-side state by destroying resources, and therefore it correctly declines to masquerade as a safe verb. It is exposed as `POST`, not `DELETE`, because it does not target a single addressable resource identified by the request URI; instead it performs a sweeping, criteria-driven bulk purge whose affected set is computed at runtime from the retention policy. `POST` is neither safe nor idempotent in the general case, and this operation embraces both of those disclaimers: it is not safe (it deletes objects and job records), and while a *second* invocation moments later would typically find nothing left to delete and thus return `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound` rather than repeating the deletions, the observable response differs between the first and subsequent calls, so the operation cannot be advertised as idempotent. Put another way: the endpoint is a *command* in the CQRS sense — it expresses an intent to reconcile the persisted world with a retention policy — rather than a *query*, and its return value is a receipt of what was reconciled, not a representation of a resource.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, the transport handler is a thin application-service adapter sitting at the edge of the hexagon. The genuinely interesting logic — deciding which artifacts are eligible, tallying reclaimed bytes, partitioning successes from failures, and identifying orphaned job aggregates — is expressed as a battery of small, pure, individually-testable helper functions that operate over plain data (`StoredDocument`, `StorageObjectKey`, `TemporaryFileRetentionThreshold`) and never touch I/O. The handler orchestrates those pure computations and then, and only then, reaches through the `document_collection` port to enact deletions. This keeps the retention *policy* (a domain concern) cleanly separated from the persistence *mechanism* (an infrastructure concern), which is precisely where DDD wants the seam to fall.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

Every request traverses the type-state authentication pipeline before the handler body runs. The handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which is only constructible after the request has successfully passed through validation, authentication, and authorization. Inside the body the handler calls `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` and `authorized_request.correlation_identifier()` to bind (but, in the current implementation, not further act upon) the caller's identity and correlation id.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 3f9a2c1e-8b7d-4e6a-9f01-2c3d4e5f6a7b` | Correlation identifier surfaced to the handler via `correlation_identifier()`. Used for tracing a single cleanup run across logs. If omitted, the pipeline supplies/derives a correlation value; supplying your own makes the run traceable end-to-end. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: ops@alma.example` | Identifies the calling principal. Consumed by the authentication stage to move the request from `Validated` to `Authenticated`, and by the authorization stage to reach `Authorized`, after which `authorized_principal()` yields it. Missing or empty leads to `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; malformed/unrecognized leads to `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`; recognized-but-not-permitted leads to `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`), verbatim explanation.** The request is modeled as a value `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>` whose *type parameter* encodes exactly how far it has progressed through the middleware chain, so that illegal states are unrepresentable at compile time. First it enters the **`Validated`** stage: the raw HTTP envelope is parsed and its structural invariants (well-formed headers, decodable metadata) are checked; a request that fails here never advances. Next it is promoted to the **`Authenticated`** stage: the `x-account-email` credential is read and resolved to a known principal — failure to present credentials yields `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, and presenting credentials that cannot be validated yields `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Finally it is promoted to the **`Authorized`** stage: the authenticated principal is checked against the policy governing this route — a principal lacking permission yields `AuthorizationWasDenied`. Only a value of type `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` can be passed to this handler; because the compiler refuses to construct that type by any path other than the full `Validated → Authenticated → Authorized` progression, the handler body is statically guaranteed to run only for fully-authorized requests, and the accessors `authorized_principal()` and `correlation_identifier()` are available precisely because the `Authorized` marker guarantees the underlying data is present.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

**This endpoint reads no request body.** The handler's signature contains exactly two extractors — `State(application_state)` and `authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — and there is no `Json<T>` or other body extractor. Every operational input is hardcoded inside the handler body:

- the cleanup scope is fixed to `"all"` (`TemporaryFileCleanupScope::AllTemporaryArtifacts`);
- the retention threshold is fixed to `24` hours;
- the confirmation token is fixed to the literal `"CONFIRM_CLEANUP"`.

Consequently there are **no request-body fields the handler reads**. Any JSON payload you send is ignored entirely. For completeness, the accepted request body schema is the empty object:

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| _(none)_ | — | — | — | — | The handler reads no request body fields. Any body is discarded. |

```json
  "type": "object",
  "description": "This endpoint reads no request body. No properties are consumed.",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Raised internally by the pure helpers, not by parsing a client body: if an OCR job document carries a `temporary_artifacts` entry that is missing its `kind`, missing a numeric `age_hours`, or missing its `object_key`. (The hardcoded scope `"all"`, retention `24`, and token also route through validators that would raise this on bad values, but those values are fixed and valid.) | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"temporary artifact in job 'job-42' is missing its kind"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The `x-account-email` credential was absent; the pipeline could not reach the `Authenticated` stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Credentials were present but could not be validated into a known principal. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal is not permitted to run cleanup. Also produced internally by `validate_run_cleanup_temporary_files_confirmation_token` if the token does not equal `"CONFIRM_CLEANUP"` — but the token is hardcoded to that exact value, so in practice this variant reflects the authorization stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"the confirmation token did not match the required value"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Two paths: (a) `reject_run_cleanup_when_no_deletable_keys_present` — no artifacts matched the scope and retention window; (b) `map_temporary_file_deletion_error_to_http_error` when *every* deletion failed and the first failure was an `ObjectKeyWasNotFound`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no temporary artifacts matched the requested scope and retention window"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Raised when *every* deletion failed and the first failure was a `DeletionWasRejected` from the storage adapter; also propagated from `list_documents` / `delete_document` port calls on the collection. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"storage rejected deletion of 's3/tmp/x': disk full"}` |

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "no temporary artifacts matched the requested scope and retention window"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. `parse_run_cleanup_temporary_files_target_scope("all")` — parses the hardcoded scope string into `TemporaryFileCleanupScope::AllTemporaryArtifacts`.
2. `compute_run_cleanup_temporary_files_retention_threshold(24)` — validates the hardcoded 24-hour retention window (rejects 0 and anything above `24 * 365`).
3. `validate_run_cleanup_temporary_files_confirmation_token("CONFIRM_CLEANUP")` — parses the token as `NonEmptyText` and requires it to equal `"CONFIRM_CLEANUP"`, else denies.
4. `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` / `authorized_request.correlation_identifier()` — bind the caller identity and correlation id (currently held but not further acted upon).
5. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(OCR_JOBS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — loads every document from the `"ocr_jobs"` collection.
6. `enumerate_deletable_temporary_ocr_artifact_keys(...)` — walks each job's `temporary_artifacts` array and collects keys whose `kind` is in scope and whose `age_hours` exceeds the threshold.
7. `reject_run_cleanup_when_no_deletable_keys_present(...)` — returns `404` if the deletable-key list is empty.
8. `execute_temporary_file_batch_deletion(...)` — maps each key through the storage-adapter deletion model, preserving order.
9. `sum_temporary_file_deletion_reclaimed_bytes(...)` — totals the bytes of the `Ok` outcomes.
10. `partition_temporary_file_deletion_outcomes(...)` — splits outcomes into successful keys and (key, error) failures.
11. `map_temporary_file_deletion_error_to_http_error(...)` — invoked only when *no* deletions succeeded, mapping the first failure to `404` or `500`.
12. `count_temporary_file_deletion_successes(...)` — counts the successfully-deleted keys.
13. `purge_orphaned_ocr_job_records_within_transactional_unit(...)` — computes the identifiers of jobs whose every artifact was deleted (so no orphaned metadata remains).
14. `application_state.document_collection.delete_document(OCR_JOBS_COLLECTION_NAME, id)` — deletes each orphaned job document (looped).
15. `record_run_cleanup_temporary_files_audit_entry(...)` — builds an audit entry (held in `_audit_entry`, not returned).
16. `build_temporary_file_cleanup_failure_descriptors(...)` — converts (key, error) failures into caller-facing descriptors.
17. `assemble_run_cleanup_temporary_files_response_payload(...)` → `.into_json()` — assembles and serializes the final `200` envelope.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **No request body is read.** Despite being a `POST`, the handler has no body extractor. Sending `{"scope":"staging","retention_hours":1}` changes nothing — scope is always `"all"`, retention is always `24`.
- **Second call typically 404s.** Because the first run deletes matching artifacts, an immediate re-run finds no deletable keys and returns `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`, not `200`. The operation is not idempotent in its observable response.
- **`missing:`-prefixed keys are simulated not-found.** The storage adapter model treats any object key starting with `missing:` as `ObjectKeyWasNotFound`. These become entries in the `failures` array on partial success, or the source of a `404` when *all* deletions fail.
- **All-or-nothing failure mapping.** A hard `404`/`500` is only raised when `successful_keys` is empty; if even one deletion succeeds, failures are reported inline in `failures` and the overall status is `200`. Partial failure is a success envelope, not an error.
- **Malformed artifact metadata surfaces as 400.** Missing `kind`, non-numeric/missing `age_hours`, or missing `object_key` inside any job's `temporary_artifacts` raises `RequestBodyWasMalformed` — confusingly named, since there is no client body; it reflects malformed *stored* data.
- **`size_bytes` is optional and defaults to 0.** An artifact lacking `size_bytes` is still deletable but contributes zero to `reclaimed_bytes`, so the reported reclaimed total can understate reality.
- **Orphan purge uses strict "all deleted".** A job is only purged when *every* one of its artifacts' `object_key`s is in the deleted set; a job with even one surviving or non-in-scope artifact key is left in place. Jobs with an empty `temporary_artifacts` array are never purged.
- **`age_hours` is compared strictly greater-than.** An artifact exactly `24` hours old is *not* deletable; it must be `> 24`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: How do I clean up only staging manifests, or use a 1-hour retention?**
A: You cannot, via this endpoint as wired. The scope (`"all"`), retention (`24`), and token (`"CONFIRM_CLEANUP"`) are hardcoded literals in the handler body. The types support configurability; the route does not.

**Q: Do I need to send the `CONFIRM_CLEANUP` token in the body?**
A: No. There is no body. The confirmation token is validated against a hardcoded literal that already equals `"CONFIRM_CLEANUP"`, so the check always passes. It exists as a guardrail in the code, not as a client-supplied gate.

**Q: If some deletions fail, did the request fail?**
A: Not necessarily. If at least one key was deleted, you get `200` with the failed keys listed under `failures`. You only get a `404`/`500` when zero deletions succeeded. Always inspect `failures` even on `200`.

### `POST /api/preprocessing-stream` — Run an OCR Preprocessing Stream Job

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts a reference to a previously-stored source document together with an ordered list of preprocessing stages, validates the requested pipeline, opens a streaming channel on the Artificial Intelligence adapter, persists a deterministic job record inside the transactional unit of work, writes an audit-bearing job document into the `ocr_jobs` collection, and returns a job identifier plus a subscription URL the caller can poll for streamed events. It is the write-side companion to the `GET /api/preprocessing-stream` description endpoint that shares the same path. The handler is registered by the `#[route(method = "POST", path = "/api/preprocessing-stream")]` attribute on `run_preprocessing_stream_handler` and is wired into the OCR router via `.post(run_preprocessing_stream_handler::<TransactionalUnitOfWork>)`.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a strict REST perspective this endpoint is a `POST` because it *creates* a resource — a preprocessing job — as a side effect that the caller does not name in advance; the server mints the identity (`preprocessing-job::<normalized-reference>`), which is the textbook justification for choosing `POST` over `PUT`. It is therefore neither safe nor, in the general HTTP sense, guaranteed idempotent: every accepted invocation is intended to open a fresh streaming channel and record a new audit entry. That said, this particular implementation derives the job identifier deterministically from the (normalized, lowercased, whitespace-collapsed) source document reference rather than from a random token or the transient channel handle, which means repeated calls with the same source reference will re-persist the *same* logical job identifier — a pragmatic, quasi-idempotent-at-the-identity-layer compromise that keeps the operation total and testable even though the collection write itself is not deduplicated.

In Domain-Driven Design terms the handler sits squarely in the HTTP/interface layer and orchestrates rather than computes: it parses and validates the incoming wire representation into a small, pure, in-file domain vocabulary (`PreprocessingStreamJobStage`, `StoredDocumentDescriptor`, `PreprocessingTargetResolution`, `PreprocessingStreamJobProcessingRequest`), delegates persistence to the injected `UnitOfWork` and `document_collection` ports, and reduces the resulting aggregate back down to a lean response payload. The preprocessing-stream vocabulary is deliberately *local* to this file — none of its types are shared ports — so that each of the fifteen numbered helper functions stays synchronous, pure, and unit-testable without threading the whole `ApplicationState` through it. This is a conscious anti-corruption boundary: the messy JSON of the wire never leaks past step 2, and the transactional machinery never leaks into the pure validators.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a12-5b6e-4d0a-9c21-2e8f1b4a6d55` | Correlation identifier. Surfaced via `authorized_request.correlation_identifier()` and persisted verbatim into the stored job document as `correlation_identifier`. Echoed through the type-state pipeline for tracing. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: owner@example.com` | Authenticated principal. Surfaced via `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` and stored as the `owning_account` of the created job document. Absence or invalidity is rejected before the handler body ever runs. |

The handler receives an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. This is a *type-state* extractor: the request cannot syntactically reach this handler until it has already transited three compile-time-enforced stages. First, `Validated` — the raw request is structurally checked (required headers present and well-formed); a failure here yields `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed` or `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`. Second, `Authenticated` — the `x-account-email` principal is resolved and proven; a failure here yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Third, `Authorized` — the authenticated principal is checked for permission to perform this operation; a failure here yields `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. Only a value of the terminal type `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` can be constructed as an argument, so the compiler itself guarantees that no unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request can execute a single line of the handler body. The pipeline is `Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`, and each arrow is an irreversible, type-level promotion.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

The handler extracts the raw body as an untyped `Json<Value>` and reads the following fields by name. There is no `#[derive(Deserialize)]` struct; every field is read defensively with `.get(...)` and typed accessors, so missing fields fall back to defaults rather than causing a deserialization failure.

##### (a) Field table

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_document_identifier` | string | Yes | Must be non-empty after `NonEmptyText::parse` (rejects blank/whitespace-only). Must match the `document_identifier` of a document already stored in the `ocr_jobs` collection. | `""` (empty, which then fails validation) | Reference to the stored source document to preprocess. Read at `submitted_body.get("source_document_identifier").and_then(Value::as_str)`. |
| `requested_stages` | array of string | Yes (effectively) | Each element must be a known canonical stage name: `deskew`, `denoise`, `contrast_normalization`, `binary_threshold`, `layout_segmentation`, `text_recognition`. Names are trimmed and lowercased before matching. The list must be non-empty and strictly monotonically increasing by ordering rank (no duplicates, no out-of-order stages). | `[]` (empty, which then fails the non-empty check) | Ordered list of preprocessing stages to enqueue. Non-string array entries are silently filtered out before parsing. |
| `target_dots_per_inch` | integer (unsigned) | No | Must fall within the inclusive range `[72, 1200]`. | `300` | Target output resolution in DPI. Read via `Value::as_u64` and cast to `u32`. Validated but not otherwise threaded into the response (bound to `_target_resolution`). |

##### (b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)

```json

  "type": "object",

  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "source_document_identifier": {
      "type": "string",

    },

```

##### (c) TypeScript interface

```typescript
type PreprocessingStageName =
  | "deskew"
  | "denoise"
  | "contrast_normalization"
  | "binary_threshold"
  | "layout_segmentation"
  | "text_recognition";

interface RunPreprocessingStreamRequest {
  /** Non-empty reference to a document stored in the ocr_jobs collection. */
  source_document_identifier: string;
  /** Ordered, strictly-increasing list of preprocessing stages. */
  requested_stages: PreprocessingStageName[];
  /** Target output resolution in DPI, inclusive range [72, 1200]. Defaults to 300. */
  target_dots_per_inch?: number;
}
```

##### (d) Rust struct mirror

The live handler reads an untyped `serde_json::Value`. The following struct is an equivalent typed mirror of the fields it actually reads:

```rust
use serde::Deserialize;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct RunPreprocessingStreamRequest {
    /// Non-empty reference to a document stored in the `ocr_jobs` collection.
    pub source_document_identifier: String,

    /// Ordered, strictly-increasing list of canonical stage names.
    pub requested_stages: Vec<String>,

    /// Target output resolution in DPI; validated to [72, 1200]. Defaults to 300.
    #[serde(default = "default_target_dots_per_inch")]
    pub target_dots_per_inch: u32,
}

fn default_target_dots_per_inch() -> u32 {
    300
}
```

#### Successful Response

On success the handler returns `200 OK` with a JSON body produced by `RunPreprocessingStreamResponsePayload::into_json()`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `job_identifier` | string | Deterministic identifier for the created job, of the form `preprocessing-job::<normalized-reference>`, where the reference is trimmed, ASCII-lowercased, and has whitespace replaced by `-`. |
| `subscription_url` | string | Relative URL to subscribe to streamed job events. Derived from the job identifier by replacing `::` with `/`, of the form `/api/preprocessing-stream/<encoded-id>/events`. |
| `total_stage_count` | integer | Count of successfully requested and validated preprocessing stages. |

```json
  "type": "object",

  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
```

```json
  "subscription_url": "/api/preprocessing-stream/preprocessing-job/scan-001/events",
  "total_stage_count": 3
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is emitted as an `HttpError` variant and serialized to a `SerializedErrorBody` of shape `{ "error_category", "error_explanation" }`. The rows below reflect the conditions that can actually arise for *this* endpoint.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Blank/invalid `source_document_identifier`; unknown stage name; empty stage list; out-of-order or duplicate stages; `target_dots_per_inch` outside `[72, 1200]`; source document reported unsupported by the backend. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"unknown preprocessing stage: teleport"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` (or required auth header) absent — rejected by the type-state pipeline before the handler body runs. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Supplied credentials present but not resolvable to a valid principal — rejected at the `Authenticated` stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Authenticated principal lacks permission to run preprocessing jobs — rejected at the `Authorized` stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | No stored document in the `ocr_jobs` collection matches `source_document_identifier`. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no stored document matches reference 'scan-001'"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | AI adapter channel capacity exhausted; backend temporarily unavailable; unit-of-work refuses to persist a job without an open channel; underlying `list_documents`/`insert_document` port failure. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"preprocessing backend is temporarily unavailable"}` |

##### Full SerializedErrorBody example

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestedResourceWasNotFound",
  "error_explanation": "no stored document matches reference 'scan-001'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `parse_run_preprocessing_stream_document_reference(...)` — Parses the raw `source_document_identifier` into a `NonEmptyText`; rejects blanks with `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. `extract_raw_stage_names(&submitted_body)` — Pulls `requested_stages` from the body, keeping only string entries, into a `Vec<String>`.
3. `parse_run_preprocessing_stream_requested_stages(...)` — Maps each raw wire name to a `PreprocessingStreamJobStage`; unknown names raise `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
4. `reject_run_preprocessing_stream_when_stage_list_empty(...)` — Fails with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if no stages were requested.
5. `validate_run_preprocessing_stream_stage_sequence_is_ordered(...)` — Ensures each stage's ordering rank is strictly greater than the previous, rejecting duplicates and out-of-order lists.
6. `validate_run_preprocessing_stream_requested_target_dots_per_inch(...)` — Validates DPI against the inclusive range `[72, 1200]`, returning a `PreprocessingTargetResolution`.
7. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(OCR_JOBS_COLLECTION_NAME)` — Loads all stored documents from the `ocr_jobs` collection (awaited port call).
8. `DocumentCollection::from_slice(&stored_documents)` — Wraps the fetched slice in a lightweight, pure lookup view.
9. `resolve_run_preprocessing_stream_source_descriptor(...)` — Finds the matching document by identifier and extracts its `media_type` (defaulting to `application/octet-stream`); `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` if absent.
10. `build_run_preprocessing_stream_processing_request(...)` — Assembles a `PreprocessingStreamJobProcessingRequest` with the source id and canonical ordered stage names.
11. `open_preprocessing_stream_channel_on_artificial_intelligence_adapter(...)` — Opens a channel on the AI adapter (capacity/availability/empty-source checks), returning a `PreprocessingStreamJobChannelHandle`.
12. `generate_preprocessing_stream_job_identifier(...)` — Derives the deterministic `preprocessing-job::<normalized-reference>` identifier from the source reference.
13. `persist_preprocessing_stream_job_record_within_transactional_unit(...)` — Persists the job within the transactional unit of work; fails with `UpstreamApplicationFailure` if the channel token is blank.
14. `record_run_preprocessing_stream_creation_audit_entry(...)` — Builds an audit entry capturing the recorded stage count and canonical stage names.
15. `build_stored_job_document(...)` — Constructs the `StoredDocument` (job body, principal, correlation id) that is then inserted via `insert_document(OCR_JOBS_COLLECTION_NAME, ...)`.
16. `compute_preprocessing_stream_total_stage_count(...)` — Counts the validated stages for the response.
17. `derive_preprocessing_stream_job_subscription_url(...)` — Builds the `/events` subscription URL from the job identifier, with a total, non-empty fallback.
18. `assemble_run_preprocessing_stream_response_payload(...)` — Reduces the identifier, subscription URL, and stage count into the final response payload, then `.into_json()`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- The job identifier is derived *only* from the normalized source document reference — not from the channel handle or a random token — so two calls with `source_document_identifier: "Scan File"` and `source_document_identifier: "scan file"` both collapse to `preprocessing-job::scan-file` and will overwrite/duplicate at the collection layer. There is no dedup guard on the `insert_document` write.
- `target_dots_per_inch` is validated but then discarded — it is bound to `_target_resolution` and never influences the processing request, the channel, the persisted document, or the response. Sending a valid DPI has no observable effect beyond passing validation.
- Missing required fields do not cause a JSON deserialization error, because the body is read as an untyped `Value` with `.get(...)` and `unwrap_or_default()`. A missing `source_document_identifier` becomes `""` and then fails at `NonEmptyText::parse` as `RequestBodyWasMalformed`; a missing `requested_stages` becomes `[]` and fails the empty-list check.
- Stage validation demands *strictly increasing* ordering rank. Duplicate stages (e.g. `["deskew", "deskew"]`) are rejected as `RequestBodyWasMalformed`, not silently deduplicated. There is no way to run the same stage twice.
- The `ArtificialIntelligenceAdapter` is hardcoded in the handler with `available_channel_capacity: 32` and `backend_is_available: true`. In practice the capacity error only triggers if more than 32 stages are enqueued — impossible given only six distinct stages exist — and the backend-unavailable path is effectively unreachable from this call site despite being fully implemented and tested.
- Non-string entries inside `requested_stages` (numbers, nulls, objects) are silently filtered out by `extract_raw_stage_names` rather than rejected. An array of `[123, "deskew"]` is treated as `["deskew"]`, which can mask malformed client payloads.
- The `subscription_url` in the response is a *relative* path (`/api/preprocessing-stream/...`), not an absolute URL. Clients must prepend their own scheme+host.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I set `target_dots_per_inch` to 600 and nothing in the response changed. Bug?**
A: Working as written. The value is validated against `[72, 1200]` and then intentionally dropped (`_target_resolution`). It gates admission; it does not travel.

**Q: Is this endpoint idempotent? Can I safely retry?**
A: Not in the HTTP sense. The identifier is deterministic, so retries reuse the same `job_identifier`, but each accepted call still opens a channel and performs an unguarded `insert_document`. Retry at your own duplication risk.

**Q: Where does the actual streamed event data come from — the `subscription_url` returns nothing.**
A: This handler only creates the job and hands you a URL string. It does not stream events itself; it returns a *relative path* to a separate `/events` subscription surface. The channel opened here is against an in-file placeholder AI adapter, not a live stream.

### `POST /api/changelog` — Append a Changelog Entry

#### Synopsis

Appends exactly one immutable entry to the changelog collection (`changelog_entries`). The handler ingests a free-form JSON object, exhaustively parses and validates each field into a strongly typed changelog aggregate, guards against reusing an already-recorded semantic version, persists the aggregate through the document-collection port, and returns an acknowledgement payload describing the newly created entry (including a server-computed word count of the body markdown). The method is `POST`, the path is `/api/changelog`, and both are taken verbatim from the `#[route(method = "POST", path = "/api/changelog")]` attribute on `append_changelog_entry_handler`.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is the canonical "append to a log" operation, and it is therefore modelled as a non-idempotent, non-safe `POST` rather than a `PUT`. Every successful invocation mints a brand-new, server-side `entry_identifier` (a fresh UUID v4) and captures a fresh creation timestamp, which means that submitting byte-for-byte identical request bodies twice would, in the absence of any other guard, produce two distinct resources. Because the resource identifier is allocated by the server and not supplied by the client, the correct REST verb is unambiguously `POST` — the client is asking the collection to create a subordinate resource whose URI it cannot itself predict. There is deliberately no idempotency key; the only thing standing between a caller and a duplicate is the semantic-version uniqueness guard, which is a domain invariant and not an HTTP-level idempotency mechanism.

In Domain-Driven Design terms, `ChangelogEntryAggregate` is the aggregate root of the changelog bounded context, and the handler is the application-service seam that translates an untyped transport representation (`serde_json::Value`) into that aggregate through a battery of pure parsing functions. The newtypes — `SemanticVersionString`, `ChangelogCategoryLabel`, `ChangelogEntryIdentifier`, `ChangelogEntryTimestamp`, `ChangelogEntryWordCount` — exist so that the validation logic traffics in meaningful domain vocabulary rather than bare `String`s, keeping the parse-don't-validate discipline honest and unit-testable. Persistence is delegated to the `DocumentCollectionPort` abstraction (a hexagonal port), so the handler never speaks to a concrete database; it merely constructs a `StoredDocument` and hands it to whatever adapter the `ApplicationState` was wired with.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This route resolves the `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` extractor, which reads two headers before the handler body ever runs.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: author@example.com` | The authenticated principal. If absent → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`. If present but not valid UTF-8 text, or not parseable as an email → `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Also used as the default `author_email` when the request body omits one. |
| `x-request-id` | No | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a2e-1b6d-4e21-9f0a-5c2d8e1a4b90` | Correlation identifier for tracing. When absent it defaults to the literal string `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"`. It is never empty by the time validation runs, so it cannot fail validation in practice. |

Verbatim explanation of the type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`): the extractor in `pipeline/extractor.rs` builds the request through a compile-time state machine encoded in the `PipelineStage` phantom type of `HttpRequestInPipeline`. It first calls `HttpRequestInPipeline::originate(correlation_identifier)` to produce a `RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated`. It then calls `.validate()`, which rejects an empty correlation identifier with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` and otherwise yields a `RequestHasBeenValidated`. Next it calls `.authenticate(parsed_authenticated_principal)` — where the principal is the `x-account-email` header run through the `email_string_prism()` optic — producing a `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated` that now carries `Some(Email)`. Finally it calls `.authorize()`, which returns `AuthorizationWasDenied` if no principal is present and otherwise yields the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` value the handler receives. Because each stage is a distinct type and the transition methods are only implemented on the preceding stage, it is impossible to construct a `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` without having passed through validation and authentication first — the compiler enforces the ordering. Inside the handler, `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` therefore always returns a valid `&Email`.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The route `/api/changelog` has no path segments to bind and the handler reads no query string.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

#### Request Body

The body is extracted as an untyped `Json<Value>` and then each field is pulled out individually. The handler reads exactly the following fields.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | Must be present and a JSON string (`require_string_field`); must parse as `NonEmptyText` (non-blank after the domain's rules). | — | Human-readable title of the changelog entry. |
| `body` | string | Yes | Must be present and a JSON string; must parse as `NonEmptyText`. | — | Markdown body of the entry. Its whitespace-delimited token count is echoed back as `body_word_count`. |
| `version` | string | Yes | Must be present and a JSON string; trimmed; must be exactly three dot-separated components; each of `major`, `minor`, `patch` must parse as a `u64` (non-negative integer). Re-canonicalized to `"{major}.{minor}.{patch}"`. Must not already exist in the collection. | — | Semantic version `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` this entry documents. |
| `category` | string | Yes | Must be present and a JSON string; trimmed and lowercased; must be one of `added`, `changed`, `deprecated`, `removed`, `fixed`, `security`. | — | Keep-a-Changelog style category label. |
| `author_email` | string | No | If present must be a JSON string that parses as a domain `Email`. | The `x-account-email` authenticated principal. | Attribution for the entry; also becomes the stored document's `owning_account`. |
| `tags` | string[] | No | Read as an optional array; non-string elements are silently dropped; each element is trimmed and lowercased; blanks are skipped; duplicates removed case-insensitively; each surviving tag must parse as `NonEmptyText`. | `[]` (empty) | Optional free-form labels. |

Any field name not listed above is ignored entirely.
