#### Error Responses

Every variant is defined in `crates/http/src/error.rs`; the `error_category` values below are exactly what `category_label()` emits, and the body is always `{ "error_category", "error_explanation" }`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `title`/`body`/`version`/`category` missing or not a string; blank title/body; malformed version (not 3 components, or a component not a `u64`, or empty); invalid `author_email`; unknown `category`; a tag that fails `NonEmptyText`; **or** a duplicate `version` already exists (mapped from `DuplicateVersion`). | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"semantic version must have exactly three dot-separated components but found 2"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | The `x-account-email` header is absent (raised by the extractor before the handler runs). | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"the 'x-account-email' header was absent"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | `x-account-email` is not valid text, or does not parse into a valid email address. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the account header did not parse into a valid email address"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | No authenticated principal present at the authorization stage of the type-state pipeline. In normal operation this is unreachable for this route because a missing/invalid principal is already caught as a 401; it exists as a defense-in-depth invariant. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Not produced by this handler directly. It can only arise if an `ApplicationError::RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` surfaces from the collection port during listing/insertion and is mapped via `From<ApplicationError>`. Documented for completeness. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | The duplicate-version guard fails to list existing entries, or the insert fails (`PersistenceFailed`), or any other non-classified `ApplicationError` bubbles up. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"failed to persist changelog entry: connection refused"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "a changelog entry already exists for semantic version '1.2.3'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler body calls these real helper functions, in order:

1. `require_string_field(&submitted_body, "title")` — pulls `title` out of the JSON `Value` as a `String` or errors 400 if missing/non-string.
2. `parse_changelog_entry_title_from_request(...)` — parses the raw title into a `NonEmptyText`, mapping domain errors to 400.
3. `require_string_field(&submitted_body, "body")` then `parse_changelog_entry_body_markdown(...)` — same treatment for the markdown body.
4. `require_string_field(&submitted_body, "version")` then `parse_changelog_semantic_version_string(...)` — trims, splits on `.`, requires 3 components, parses each as `u64`, and canonicalizes.
5. Inline: reads optional `author_email` from the body, defaulting to `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()` when absent.
6. `parse_changelog_entry_author_email(...)` — parses the resolved author string into a domain `Email`.
7. `require_string_field(&submitted_body, "category")` then `validate_changelog_entry_category_label(...)` — trims/lowercases and matches against the fixed vocabulary.
8. `extract_optional_string_array_field(&submitted_body, "tags")` then `normalize_changelog_entry_tag_collection(...)` — collects string elements, trims/lowercases, skips blanks, dedupes, and parses each as `NonEmptyText`.
9. `guard_against_duplicate_changelog_version(document_collection, &semantic_version)` — calls `list_documents(CHANGELOG_COLLECTION_NAME)` and `detect_duplicate_changelog_version(...)`; errors if the version already exists (400) or listing fails (500).
10. `generate_changelog_entry_identifier()` — mints a fresh UUID v4.
11. `capture_changelog_entry_creation_timestamp()` — reads `SystemTime::now()` as epoch milliseconds (falls back to `0` if the clock is before the epoch).
12. `assemble_changelog_entry_aggregate(...)` — combines all validated parts into a `ChangelogEntryAggregate`.
13. `persist_changelog_entry_within_transaction(document_collection, &changelog_entry)` — via `build_stored_document_for_changelog_entry(...)`, builds the `StoredDocument` and calls `insert_document(...)`; maps failures through `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error(...)`.
14. `serialize_persisted_changelog_entry_to_response(...)` — via `count_words_in_changelog_body_markdown(...)`, assembles the acknowledgement payload returned to the client.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`created_at_epoch_ms` is a string, not a number.** In both the stored document and the response, the timestamp is serialized via `.to_string()`. Clients must not assume a JSON number.
- **The duplicate-version guard is racy.** It lists-then-inserts without a transactional uniqueness constraint. Two concurrent requests for the same `version` can both pass the guard and both persist, yielding duplicate versions despite the check. There is no `UnitOfWork`-backed atomicity around the guard and insert.
- **A duplicate version returns 400, not 409.** `DuplicateVersion` is mapped onto `RequestBodyWasMalformed`, so callers looking for `409 Conflict` will never see it.
- **`author_email` silently defaults to the caller's identity.** Omitting it is not an error; the `x-account-email` principal is used and also becomes the stored document's `owning_account`.
- **Tags are aggressively mangled.** Non-string array elements are dropped without error, tags are lowercased and trimmed, blanks are skipped, and duplicates are removed case-insensitively — so `["Feature","feature","API"]` becomes `["feature","api"]`. The response echoes the mangled form, not your input.
- **Version is re-canonicalized.** Leading zeros or surrounding whitespace are normalized: `" 01.02.03 "` becomes `"1.2.3"`. Duplicate detection compares against the canonical form.
- **Unknown body fields are ignored, not rejected.** The handler reads only the fields it knows; extra keys pass through silently.
- **`x-request-id` cannot fail.** A missing correlation id defaults to `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"`, which is non-empty, so the `.validate()` empty-check never trips for this route.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I supply my own `document_identifier`?**
A: No. The identifier is a server-minted UUID v4 from `generate_changelog_entry_identifier()`. Anything you send under that key is ignored; the handler never reads it.

**Q: Why did my perfectly valid `"2.0"` version get rejected?**
A: Because semantic versions here require *exactly three* dot-separated components. `"2.0"` has two, so you get `400 request_body_was_malformed` explaining it "found 2". Send `"2.0.0"`.

**Q: I posted the same entry twice and got two entries. Is the endpoint idempotent?**
A: No. `POST` is neither safe nor idempotent here, and there is no idempotency key. The only uniqueness enforced is on `version` — and even that is a best-effort, non-atomic list-then-check, so under concurrency you may still get duplicates.

---

### `POST /api/docs/create` — Create a Documentation Page

Accepts a JSON payload describing a new documentation page (title and markdown body at minimum), validates every field into a self-contained domain vocabulary, derives a URL-safe slug from the title, extracts a heading outline (table of contents) from the markdown, guards against a duplicate slug already living in the `documentation_pages` collection, and persists the assembled page aggregate through the generic `DocumentCollectionPort`. On success it returns a `200 OK` with a structured JSON envelope describing the freshly-minted page, including a synthetic `webViewLink`. This endpoint sits behind the full type-state request pipeline and therefore requires an already-authorized principal to reach the handler body at all.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the strictest reading of REST, minting a brand-new resource whose identity the server chooses is the archetypal `POST` operation: it is neither *safe* (it mutates server state by inserting a document) nor *idempotent* (two identical requests will each attempt to create a page, and the second is only stopped by the deterministic slug-conflict guard — the identity itself, a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()`, is regenerated on every call). This is precisely why the handler is mounted with `post(...)` rather than `put(...)`: the client does not, and cannot, dictate the resulting resource URI, so a `PUT`-to-a-known-location contract would be a category error. The slug-uniqueness check gives the operation a veneer of *conditional* idempotency at the business-key level, but you should not lean on it as a concurrency primitive — it is a read-then-write with no locking.

Viewed through a Domain-Driven Design lens, this endpoint is a thin transport-layer *application service*. The handler file deliberately owns a coherent, file-local ubiquitous language — `DocumentationPageAggregate`, `DocumentationPageSlug`, `DocumentationSectionPath`, `DocumentationAudienceKind`, `DocumentationPageIdentifier`, `DocumentationPageTimestamp`, `DocumentationHeadingOutlineNode` — because the upstream plan referenced shared domain types that do not (yet) exist as crate-level exports. Rather than persisting a loose bag of `serde_json::Value` fields, the handler funnels raw JSON through a battery of `parse_*`/`validate_*` functions that each return a validated newtype, assembles them into a single aggregate root, and only then serializes that aggregate down into the generic `StoredDocument` shape the persistence port understands. The transport boundary (`HttpError`) and the domain boundary (`NonEmptyText`, `Email`) are kept scrupulously separate, and every domain rejection is translated into a `RequestBodyWasMalformed` at the edge.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a2e-1d44-4b0a-9c11-8e2f6a1b5d90` | Becomes the request's `correlation_identifier`. The pipeline's `validate()` stage rejects an empty/whitespace-only value with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` ("the correlation identifier was empty"). Propagated for tracing; not read inside this handler's body. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: dev@example.com` | Identifies the calling principal. It is parsed into an `Email` and threaded through the pipeline to become the `authorized_principal()`. If no principal survives to the authorization stage, `authorize()` fails with `AuthorizationWasDenied`. In this handler the principal also serves as the default `authorEmail` when the body omits one. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** Reaching this handler is impossible unless the request has already climbed the entire compile-time-enforced ladder, because the handler's second extractor is typed `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — a phantom-typed wrapper that can *only* be constructed by successfully completing every prior stage. The lifecycle is:

1. **`RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated`** — created via `HttpRequestInPipeline::originate(correlation_identifier)` from the incoming `x-request-id`. It carries `declared_principal: None`.
2. **`RequestHasBeenValidated`** — produced by `.validate()`, which errors with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if the correlation identifier is blank. This is the *validated* rung.
3. **`RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`** — produced by `.authenticate(authenticated_principal: Email)`, which stamps the request with `Some(principal)`. This is the *authenticated* rung.
4. **`RequestHasBeenAuthorized`** — produced by `.authorize()`, which pattern-matches on the principal: `Some(_)` advances the request; `None` returns `AuthorizationWasDenied` ("no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"). This is the *authorized* rung, and the only stage that exposes `correlation_identifier()` and `authorized_principal()`.

Because each transition consumes `self` and returns a differently-parameterized type, there is no way to call `authorized_principal()` on a merely-validated request, and no way to inject a `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` value without having genuinely passed authorization. The types *are* the access-control proof.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

#### Request Body

The handler extracts `Json(submitted_body): Json<Value>` and then reads named fields out of the raw JSON object by hand. The markdown body is accepted under any of three aliases; several fields are optional with defaults. The following table enumerates every field the handler actually reads.

(a) **Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | Must be present and a JSON string; must parse as `NonEmptyText` (non-blank after trimming); must yield a non-empty slug after alphanumeric normalization. | — | Human-readable page title. Also the sole source of the derived `slug`. |
| `bodyMarkdown` | string | Yes* | Must be a non-blank string. *Required only as one of the three body aliases. Must parse as `NonEmptyText`. | — | The markdown source of the page. First alias checked. |
| `body` | string | Yes* | Same as `bodyMarkdown`. Used only if `bodyMarkdown` is absent/blank. | — | Second accepted alias for the markdown body. |
| `content` | string | Yes* | Same as `bodyMarkdown`. Used only if `bodyMarkdown` and `body` are absent/blank. | — | Third accepted alias for the markdown body. At least one of the three body aliases must supply a non-blank string. |
| `sectionPath` | string | No | Split on `/`; segments trimmed and empties dropped; must produce ≥1 segment; each segment may contain only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. | `"general"` | `/`-delimited navigation path locating the page in the docs tree. |
| `audience` | string | No | Case-insensitive, trimmed. Accepted: `end_user`/`end-user`/`user` → EndUser; `developer`/`dev` → Developer; `administrator`/`admin` → Administrator. Anything else is rejected. | `"end_user"` | Intended reader of the page. |
| `authorEmail` | string | No | If present and non-blank, must parse as a valid `Email`. | Authorized principal (`x-account-email`) | Attributed author; also stored as the document's `owning_account`. |

Note: any additional JSON fields in the body are silently ignored — the handler reads only the keys above.

```json
    },

        "end_user", "end-user", "user",
        "developer", "dev",

      "default": "end_user",
      "description": "Intended reader; case-insensitive; aliases accepted."

    }
  },

  "anyOf": [
    { "required": ["bodyMarkdown"] },

    { "required": ["content"] }
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` into a `SerializedErrorBody` with exactly two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `title` missing/not a string; all three body aliases missing/blank; title/body fail `NonEmptyText::parse`; title produces an empty slug; `sectionPath` has zero segments or an illegal segment; `authorEmail` fails `Email::parse`; unknown `audience`; **and** a conflicting slug already exists (mapped from `ConflictingSlugAlreadyExists`). | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"required field 'title' is missing or not a string"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | Raised earlier in the pipeline when authentication credentials are absent before the request is authenticated. Not produced inside this handler's body, but reachable on the path to it. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | Raised earlier in the pipeline when supplied credentials cannot be validated into a principal. Not produced inside this handler's body. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | The pipeline's `authorize()` finds no principal (`declared_principal == None`), or an `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` surfaces from persistence. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | Mapped from `ApplicationError::RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` / `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` bubbling out of the collection port during `list_documents` or `insert_document`. Not directly raised by this handler's own logic. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"the requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | `list_documents` fails (via `?` → `From<ApplicationError>`), or the insert is rejected (`PersistenceBackendRejectedWrite` mapped to `UpstreamApplicationFailure`), or any other `ApplicationError`. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"failed to persist documentation page: connection reset"}` |

**Full SerializedErrorBody example**

```json
{
  "error_category": "request_body_was_malformed",
  "error_explanation": "a documentation page with slug 'getting-started' already exists"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler `create_documentation_page_handler` invokes these real helpers, in order:

1. `read_required_string_field(&submitted_body, "title")` — pull `title` as a string or 400.
2. `read_body_markdown_field(&submitted_body)` — try `bodyMarkdown` → `body` → `content`; first non-blank wins, else 400.
3. `read_optional_string_field(&submitted_body, "sectionPath")` — optional string, blank treated as absent; defaults to `"general"`.
4. `read_optional_string_field(&submitted_body, "audience")` — optional string; defaults to `"end_user"`.
5. `read_optional_string_field(&submitted_body, "authorEmail")` — optional string; defaults to the authorized principal via `authorized_request.authorized_principal().as_str()`.
6. `parse_documentation_page_title(raw_title)` — validate into `NonEmptyText` or 400.
7. `parse_documentation_page_body_markdown(raw_body_markdown)` — validate into `NonEmptyText` or 400.
8. `derive_documentation_page_slug_from_title(&page_title)` — lowercase-alphanumeric slug with `-` separators; empty slug → 400.
9. `parse_documentation_page_section_path(raw_section_path)` — split/trim/validate segments (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) or 400.
10. `parse_documentation_page_author_email(raw_author_email)` — validate into `Email` or 400.
11. `validate_documentation_page_audience_kind(raw_audience)` — map alias to `DocumentationAudienceKind` or 400.
12. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(DOCUMENTATION_COLLECTION_NAME).await?` — read existing docs (errors map to 4xx/500 via `From<ApplicationError>`).
13. `guard_against_conflicting_documentation_page_slug(&existing_documents, &page_slug)` — scan stored `slug` fields; duplicate → `ConflictingSlugAlreadyExists` → 400.
14. `generate_documentation_page_identifier()` — fresh UUID v4.
15. `capture_documentation_page_creation_timestamp()` — epoch millis (0 on clock error).
16. `extract_documentation_page_heading_outline(&page_body_markdown)` — parse `#`..`######` headings, skipping fenced code blocks; internally calls `build_heading_anchor`.
17. `assemble_documentation_page_aggregate(...)` — bundle all validated parts into `DocumentationPageAggregate`.
18. `persist_documentation_page_within_transaction::<TransactionalUnitOfWork>(...)` — serialize via `serialize_documentation_page_body` into a `StoredDocument` and `insert_document`; failures → `PersistenceBackendRejectedWrite`.
19. `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error(...)` — translate collection errors to `HttpError` (conflict → 400, write failure → 500).
20. `serialize_created_documentation_page_to_response(&documentation_page)` — build the `200` JSON envelope, including the synthetic `webViewLink`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`headingCount` counts every `#`..`######` heading, code-fence-aware.** Headings inside triple-backtick fences are skipped, and a line of bare hashes with no text (e.g. `###`) is not counted. A markdown body with zero headings yields `headingCount: 0` and an empty `headingOutline`.
- **The slug is derived solely from `title`, and a symbol-only title is fatal.** A title like `"!!!"` parses fine as `NonEmptyText` (it is non-blank) but produces an empty slug, which triggers `RequestBodyWasMalformed` ("documentation page title produced an empty slug"). Two different titles that normalize to the same slug (e.g. `"Hello World"` and `"hello, world"`) will collide on the uniqueness guard.
- **`createdAtEpochMillis` is a string, not a number.** It is serialized via `.to_string()`, so JSON consumers must parse it back to an integer. Additionally, if the system clock is before the Unix epoch, the timestamp silently defaults to `0` rather than erroring.
- **The slug-conflict guard is a non-atomic read-then-write.** It lists all documents and scans in memory before inserting. Two concurrent creates with the same slug can both pass the guard and both insert — there is no locking or unique-index enforcement at this layer.
- **`webViewLink` is synthetic and points at Google Docs.** It is `https://docs.google.com/document/d/{uuid}/edit` built from a locally-generated UUID; it is not a real Google Docs document and will 404 if opened. The page is stored in the internal `documentation_pages` collection, not in Google Docs.
- **`authorEmail` defaults to the authorized principal but is validated independently.** If the client sends a garbage `authorEmail`, the request is rejected even though a perfectly valid principal exists in the header — the fallback only applies when the field is absent or blank.
- **Body alias precedence is fixed: `bodyMarkdown` > `body` > `content`.** If more than one is present, only the first non-blank in that order is used; the others are ignored. `sectionPath` normalization also silently drops empty segments, so `"a//b/"` becomes `"a/b"`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I set the page `id` myself by sending it in the body?**
A: No. The identifier is generated server-side with `Uuid::new_v4()` regardless of any `id` you send. Extra fields in the body are ignored.

**Q: Why did I get a `200 OK` from a `create` endpoint instead of `201 Created`?**
A: Because the handler returns `Ok(Json(...))`, which axum renders as `200 OK`. This endpoint does not set a `201` status or a `Location` header, despite creating a resource. Do not rely on the status code to distinguish creation from retrieval.

**Q: I sent the same request twice and got a 400 the second time — is that a bug?**
A: No, that is the slug-conflict guard working as designed. The first request created a page with a given slug; the second request derives the identical slug from the identical title and is rejected with `request_body_was_malformed` ("a documentation page with slug '...' already exists"). This endpoint is not idempotent, but it is slug-deduplicated on a best-effort basis.

**Q: My `audience` was `"Admin"` — why did it work?**
A: Audience matching is case-insensitive and trimmed, and `admin`/`administrator` are both aliases for `Administrator`. The canonical value stored and returned is `"administrator"`.

---

### `GET /api/docs/page` — Fetch a Single Rendered Documentation Page

This endpoint retrieves exactly one documentation page from the `documentation_pages` collection by its slug identifier, selects a revision snapshot (the latest by default or a caller-nominated one), and returns a fully assembled read-model containing rendered HTML, an extracted table of contents, a breadcrumb trail, an estimated reading time, and in-section sibling navigation. It is a pure read operation: nothing is mutated, no view counter is persisted, and the response is derived entirely on-the-fly from the stored document body and the query parameters supplied by the caller. Think of it as the "reader view" behind a documentation site: you hand it a slug, it hands you everything a rendering front-end needs to paint a page.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of REST, `GET /api/docs/page` is the archetypal **safe** and **idempotent** resource read. It is *safe* because invoking it produces no observable state transition on the server — there is deliberately no persisted "view count", "last accessed" write, or audit mutation; the `access_marker` field you will see in the response is a synthetic, in-memory string derived from the request correlation identifier and never written anywhere. It is *idempotent* because issuing the identical request an arbitrary number of times yields the identical representation (modulo concurrent edits to the underlying document, which are outside this handler's control). Because it is safe and idempotent, it is legitimately cacheable, retriable on transport failure, and prefetchable by a documentation front-end without fear of side effects. The endpoint models a *representation of a resource* rather than an RPC verb; the resource is "the documentation page identified by this slug, at this revision", and the many derived fields (`rendered_html`, `table_of_contents`, `breadcrumb_trail`, `sibling_pages`) are presentation projections computed at read time, not first-class stored entities.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, this handler lives squarely in the **HTTP/interface layer** and functions as a read-side query composer. It leans on the `document_collection` port (an application-layer abstraction over persistence) via `fetch_document` and `list_documents`, and it uses the domain value object `NonEmptyText` to enforce the invariant that a slug and a markdown body must be non-empty at their respective boundaries. Note carefully what is *absent*: there is no aggregate mutation, no unit-of-work commit, and no domain command. The presentation logic — markdown-to-HTML rendering, slugified anchors, humanized breadcrumb labels, reading-time heuristics — is intentionally kept in the interface layer because it is concern of *how the page is displayed*, not *what the page fundamentally is*. This keeps the domain and application layers blissfully ignorant of HTML, ATX headings, and the assumption that humans read 200 words per minute.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This endpoint is gated by the type-state request pipeline and executes only once the request has reached the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` stage. The handler itself performs **no per-resource authorization check** beyond the existence of an authorized principal established upstream; any authenticated, authorized caller may read any documentation page (the `owning_account` on a page is returned for information but is not used to restrict access in this handler).

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a2e-1b6d-4c8a-9e21-0f5d6a7b8c90` | Becomes the request **correlation identifier**. Validated upstream: an empty/whitespace-only value fails validation with `400 request_body_was_malformed` ("the correlation identifier was empty"). This handler reuses it verbatim to synthesize the `access_marker` (`documentation-view:<correlation>`), falling back to `documentation-view:uncorrelated` if empty. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: reader@example.com` | The declared principal. Parsed into a domain `Email` and installed during the authentication stage; its presence is what makes authorization succeed. Missing/invalid credentials fail upstream with `401`; a missing principal at the authorization stage yields `403 authorization_was_denied`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The request is modeled by `HttpRequestInPipeline<PipelineStage>`, a struct whose *stage* is encoded as a compile-time phantom type. A request begins life as `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated>` via `originate(correlation_identifier)`. Calling `.validate()` checks that the correlation identifier (sourced from `x-request-id`) is non-empty and, on success, returns a `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>` — the only way to obtain that type. Calling `.authenticate(email)` on a *validated* request installs the `x-account-email` principal and yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthenticated>`. Calling `.authorize()` on an *authenticated* request verifies a principal is actually present (returning `403 AuthorizationWasDenied` if not) and yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. This last type is precisely what this handler demands as its extractor (`_authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`). Because each stage transition is the *sole* constructor of the next stage's type, it is statically impossible to invoke this handler with an unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request: the code simply would not compile. The handler thus receives an ironclad compile-time proof that validation, authentication, and authorization all completed, and it only ever *reads* from the authorized request (via `correlation_identifier()`), never re-checking what the type already guarantees.

#### Path & Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | query | string | Yes* | Trimmed; must be non-empty after trimming (`NonEmptyText`). | — | The documentation page slug to fetch. Primary key of the lookup. |
| `slug` | query | string | Yes* | Trimmed; must be non-empty after trimming (`NonEmptyText`). | — | Fallback name for the slug. Used **only** if `identifier` is absent. |
| `revision` | query | string | No | Case-insensitive `latest`, or a base-10 integer `>= 1`. `0`, negatives, and non-numerics are rejected. | `latest` (i.e. highest `revision_number`) | Selects which stored revision snapshot to return. Empty string or `latest` behaves as "no selection" (latest wins). |

\* Exactly one of `identifier` or `slug` must be supplied. `identifier` takes precedence; if both are absent the request is rejected with `400 request_body_was_malformed` ("the 'identifier' query parameter is required").

#### Request Body

**This endpoint reads no request body.** It is a `GET` request; all input arrives via query parameters and headers. Any body sent is ignored by the handler. For completeness, the accepted body shape is the empty object:

| — | — | — | (no request body) | — | This `GET` endpoint reads no body; supply parameters via the query string. |

```javascript
const params = new URLSearchParams({
  identifier: "getting-started",
  revision: "latest",
});

const response = await fetch(
  `https://api.alma.example/api/docs/page?${params.toString()}`,
  {
    method: "GET",
    headers: {
      "x-request-id": "7f3c9a2e-1b6d-4c8a-9e21-0f5d6a7b8c90",
      "x-account-email": "reader@example.com",
    },
  },
);

if (!response.ok) {
  const error = await response.json(); // { error_category, error_explanation }
  throw new Error(`${error.error_category}: ${error.error_explanation}`);
}

const page = await response.json();
console.log(page.page_title, page.estimated_reading_minutes);
```

#### Successful Response

`200 OK` with a JSON object assembled by `serialize_fetched_documentation_page_to_response`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `page_slug` | string | The stored document's `document_identifier`. |
| `page_title` | string | The `title` from the document body, or the slug if no title is stored. |
| `owning_account` | string \| null | The `owning_account` on the stored document (informational; not access-controlling here). |
| `selected_revision_number` | integer (u64) | The `revision_number` of the selected snapshot, or `1` if the snapshot carries none. |
| `rendered_html` | string | HTML rendered from the revision's markdown body (headings, unordered lists, paragraphs; HTML-escaped). |
| `table_of_contents` | array of objects | One entry per ATX heading: `{ heading_level, heading_text, anchor_identifier }`. |
| `breadcrumb_trail` | array of objects | Per section-path segment: `{ segment_label, segment_slug, cumulative_path, depth_index }`. Empty if no `section_path`. |
| `estimated_reading_minutes` | integer (u32) | Alphanumeric word count / 200, rounded up, floored at 1. |
| `sibling_pages` | array of objects | Other pages in the same section: `{ page_slug, page_title, ordering_index }`, sorted by `ordering_index` then title. |
| `access_marker` | string | Synthetic view marker `documentation-view:<correlation>` (or `documentation-view:uncorrelated`). Not persisted. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized by `HttpError::into_response` as `{ "error_category": ..., "error_explanation": ... }` with the matching status code.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | `identifier`/`slug` missing; slug empty after trim (invalid `NonEmptyText`); `revision` is `0`, negative, or non-numeric/non-`latest`. Also raised upstream when `x-request-id` correlation is empty. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the 'identifier' query parameter is required"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | Raised upstream when no `x-account-email` credential is presented. Never raised inside this handler. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was provided"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | Raised upstream when `x-account-email` is present but not a valid `Email`. Never raised inside this handler. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the supplied credential was not a valid email"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | Raised at the pipeline authorization stage if no principal is present. This handler applies no additional per-page authorization. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | No page exists under the slug; OR the requested `revision` does not exist (including `revision != 1` on a page with no revision history); OR the page has no selectable revisions. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"no documentation page exists under the identifier 'getting-started'"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | The `document_collection` port fails (`fetch_document`/`list_documents`); OR the stored revision is missing its markdown body; OR the stored markdown is not a valid `NonEmptyText`. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"the stored documentation page revision is missing its markdown body"}` |

Full example error body:

```json
{
  "error_category": "requested_resource_was_not_found",
  "error_explanation": "revision 9 does not exist for this documentation page"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

1. **`parse_documentation_page_slug_from_query`** — reads `identifier` (falling back to `slug`), trims it, and parses it into a `NonEmptyText`; `400` if missing or empty.
2. **`parse_optional_documentation_page_revision_query`** — normalizes the optional `revision`: `None`/empty/`latest` → `None`; a positive integer → `Some(u32)`; `0` or non-numeric → `400`.
3. **`document_collection.fetch_document(DOCUMENTATION_COLLECTION_NAME, slug)`** — loads the stored page from the `documentation_pages` collection via the application port.
4. **`map_missing_documentation_page_to_not_found_error`** — converts a `None` lookup result into a `404` mentioning the slug.
5. **`select_documentation_page_revision`** — picks the revision snapshot: if a `revisions` array exists, finds the requested number or the max; otherwise treats the whole body as the sole revision (and `404`s if a revision other than `1` was asked for).
6. **`extract_documentation_page_markdown_body`** — pulls the markdown from `body_markdown` / `markdown` / `content` and parses it as `NonEmptyText`; `500` if absent or empty.
7. **`render_documentation_page_markdown_to_html`** — a dependency-free renderer for ATX headings, `- `/`* ` unordered lists, and paragraphs, HTML-escaping all text first.
8. **`extract_documentation_page_table_of_contents`** (with **`slugify_documentation_anchor`**) — collects one TOC entry per heading, each with a URL-safe anchor.
9. **`extract_documentation_section_path`** — reads the page's `section_path` (string array or `/`-delimited string) into ordered segments.
10. **`resolve_documentation_page_breadcrumb_trail`** (with **`humanize_section_segment`** / **`capitalize_first_letter`**) — builds cumulative breadcrumb entries with humanized labels.
11. **`compute_documentation_page_estimated_reading_minutes`** — counts alphanumeric words, divides by 200 words/minute rounded up, floored at 1.
12. **`document_collection.list_documents(DOCUMENTATION_COLLECTION_NAME)`** — loads all pages for sibling discovery.
13. **`summarize_sibling_documentation_pages`** (with **`summarize_single_documentation_page`**) — filters to same-section pages excluding the current one, summarizes, and sorts by `ordering_index` then title.
14. **`capture_documentation_page_access_timestamp`** — derives the non-persisted `access_marker` from the request correlation identifier.
15. **`serialize_fetched_documentation_page_to_response`** — assembles the final JSON object returned to the caller.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **`identifier` beats `slug`.** If both query parameters are present, `identifier` is used and `slug` is silently ignored. Supplying only `slug` works; supplying neither is a `400`.
- **`revision` semantics on a history-less page.** A page whose body has no `revisions` array is treated as a single implicit revision. Requesting `revision=1` returns the whole body; requesting any other number is a `404`, not a fallback to the latest.
- **`revision=latest` vs `revision=0`.** The literal `latest` (any case), an empty value, or omitting `revision` all mean "highest `revision_number`". But `revision=0` is an explicit `400` — zero is not a valid revision.
- **404 is overloaded.** A `404` can mean either "no such page" or "the page exists but that revision does not". Read `error_explanation` to disambiguate; the status code alone is ambiguous.
- **Missing markdown is a 500, not a 404.** If the page is found but its selected revision has no `body_markdown`/`markdown`/`content`, or the markdown is empty, that is treated as an upstream/data-integrity failure (`500 upstream_application_failure`), because a stored page is expected to always carry a body.
- **The renderer is intentionally minimal.** Only ATX headings (`#`..`######` followed by a space), `- `/`* ` unordered list items, and paragraphs are recognized. No bold, italics, links, code fences, ordered lists, or tables — those pass through as escaped paragraph text. `#NoSpace` is not a heading.
- **`access_marker` is not a timestamp and is never stored.** Despite the function name, it is a string derived from the correlation id (`documentation-view:<x-request-id>`), used only in the response. This endpoint records nothing server-side.
- **Sibling discovery loads the whole collection.** Sibling navigation calls `list_documents` over the entire `documentation_pages` collection and filters in memory by exact `section_path` equality; a page with an empty section path only lists other empty-section-path pages as siblings.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I POST to `/api/docs/page` to create or update a page?**
A: No. This route is registered as `GET` only. Creation lives at `POST /api/docs/create`. Sending a body here does nothing; the body is not read.

**Q: Why did I get a 404 when the page clearly exists?**
A: Almost certainly your `revision` parameter points at a revision that does not exist — or you asked for a revision other than `1` on a page that has no revision history. The `error_explanation` will say "revision N does not exist". Drop the parameter (or use `latest`) to get the current version.

**Q: Does viewing a page increment a view counter or update "last accessed"?**
A: No. The endpoint is safe and idempotent by design. The `access_marker` in the response looks like telemetry but is a purely synthetic, request-scoped string that is never persisted anywhere.

---

### `GET /api/changelog` — List Changelog Entries (Version-Grouped, Paginated, Filterable-in-Theory)

#### Synopsis

This endpoint returns the application's changelog: a collection of release notes drawn from the `changelog_entries` document collection, projected into a version-grouped, deterministically-sorted, page-bounded JSON payload. It is a read-only listing operation that fetches every stored changelog document, filters and sorts them through a battery of pure helper functions, and groups the resulting page by semantic version. As currently wired, the route exposes no query-string extractor, so all filter, sort, and pagination parameters resolve to their validated defaults (newest-first, page size 20, no filters, no cursor) — but the parsing machinery is fully present and unit-tested, awaiting a future `Query` extractor.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the grand cathedral of RESTful resource semantics, `GET /api/changelog` is a paragon of the *safe* and *idempotent* verb. It is **safe** because it mutates nothing — no side effect escapes the request, no document is written, no state is perturbed; the caller may invoke it a thousand times and the universe remains exactly as indifferent as before. It is **idempotent** because the response is a pure function of the persisted collection at the moment of reading: identical inputs (which, given the absent query extractor, are *always* identical) yield identical outputs modulo whatever the underlying document collection happens to contain. This makes the endpoint eminently cacheable, eminently retryable, and eminently boring — which is precisely the compliment REST intends to pay it.

From a Domain-Driven Design standpoint, this handler sits squarely within the `docs` bounded context of the `alma-http` crate, acting as a thin *application-layer orchestrator* that delegates the actual domain reasoning to a constellation of local value objects — `SemanticVersion`, `ChangelogPageSize`, `ChangelogCategoryLabel`, `SemanticVersionRange`, `ChangelogPaginationCursor` — each of which encapsulates a small, ferociously well-defined invariant. The handler itself owns no business rules; it merely marshals validated inputs into a `ChangelogEntriesQuerySpecification`, hands that specification and the raw `DocumentCollection` to a sequence of synchronously-testable pure functions, and serializes the result. This deliberate segregation of the impure (async I/O against the document collection) from the pure (parsing, filtering, sorting, grouping, projection) is the entire architectural point: the interesting logic never touches the network.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This handler's signature requires an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which means the request must have already traversed the full type-state authentication and authorization pipeline before the handler body ever executes.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 3f9a1c2e-8b7d-4e6f-9a01-2c3d4e5f6a7b` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and error surfaces; propagated across the pipeline for tracing a single request end-to-end. Absent one, the platform typically synthesizes one. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: francesco@example.com` | Identifies the calling account. Consumed during the pipeline's authentication stage to establish *who* is calling; its absence yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, and a malformed/unrecognized value yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The `alma-http` request lifecycle is encoded in Rust's type system as a progression of marker states carried by `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`. A request begins in the **Validated** state once its structural preconditions (well-formed headers, parseable envelope) are satisfied. It is then promoted to **Authenticated** once the identity headers — chiefly `x-account-email` — are resolved to a known account; failure here short-circuits with a `401`. Finally it is promoted to **Authorized** once the authenticated principal is confirmed to hold the permissions required for the operation; failure here short-circuits with a `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. Because this handler accepts *only* `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, it is statically impossible to invoke the handler body with a request that has not completed all three stages — the compiler itself enforces that no unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request can reach the changelog-listing logic. The `_authorized_request` parameter is bound but intentionally unused inside the body; its sole purpose is to serve as compile-time proof that the pipeline completed.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The route registers `GET /api/changelog` with no path segments beyond the literal and no `Query` extractor. Note, however, that the handler *internally* threads a full suite of would-be query parameters through its validation helpers, all currently fed `None` and therefore resolving to defaults:

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | (query, not wired) | integer offset | No | Must parse as non-negative `usize`; blank/absent treated as none | `null` (offset 0) | Opaque forward-only pagination cursor; a non-negative offset into the sorted result set. |
| `pageSize` | (query, not wired) | integer | No | Must be `> 0`; clamped to `[1, 100]`; blank/absent → default | `20` | Number of entries per page. |
| `category` | (query, not wired) | string | No | Non-blank after trim; max 120 chars; compared case-insensitively | none | Category label filter (e.g. `Bug Fixes`). |
| `from` | (query, not wired) | semver string | No | Parseable semver; if both bounds set, `from <= to` | none | Inclusive lower version bound. |
| `to` | (query, not wired) | semver string | No | Parseable semver; if both bounds set, `from <= to` | none | Inclusive upper version bound. |
| `sort` | (query, not wired) | string enum | No | One of `newest`/`newest_first`/`desc`/`descending` or `oldest`/`oldest_first`/`asc`/`ascending` | `newest` | Sort order by version. |

#### Request Body

This is a `GET` endpoint and reads **no request body**. The handler takes only `State` and the authorized-pipeline marker; no `Json<...>` extractor is present. Callers must not send a body; any body is ignored.

#### Successful Response

`200 OK` with `Content-Type: application/json`. The body is produced by `ListChangelogEntriesResponseBody::into_json`.

**Response field table**:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `releases` | array of objects | Entries grouped by their release version, in the query's sort order (default newest-first). Empty array when nothing matches. |
| `releases[].version` | string | Display version string of the grouping (e.g. `"3.0.0"`). |
| `releases[].date` | string | Release date carried from the first entry in the grouping (raw stored string, e.g. `"2026-03-01"`). |
| `releases[].entries` | array of objects | Summarized changelog entries within this version grouping. |
| `releases[].entries[].id` | string | Entry identifier (from the stored document's `id` field). |
| `releases[].entries[].category` | string | Entry category (e.g. `"Bug Fixes"`). |
| `releases[].entries[].title` | string | Entry title. |
| `releases[].entries[].description` | string | Entry description. |
| `releases[].entries[].severity` | string | Entry severity (e.g. `"Minor"`). |
| `releases[].entries[].breaking` | boolean | Whether the entry is a breaking change. |
| `totalCount` | integer | Total entries matching the query *before* pagination. |
| `nextCursor` | integer or null | Offset for the next page, present only when the returned page was full; `null` when the result set is exhausted. |

#### Error Responses

Every variant of `HttpError` is enumerated below with the concrete circumstances under which *this* endpoint would emit it. All errors serialize to a `SerializedErrorBody` shape of `{error_category, error_explanation}`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Only reachable if/when the query extractor is wired: a bad `cursor` (`"nope"`), `pageSize` of `0` or non-numeric, over-long/blank category, un-parseable `from`/`to` semver, inverted version range, or unrecognized `sort` value. With the current no-extractor wiring, defaults are used and this cannot fire. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"page size must be greater than zero"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The request never reaches the handler: `x-account-email` (or equivalent identity header) absent, so the pipeline cannot promote to Authenticated. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Identity header present but not resolvable to a known account during the Authenticated stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Authenticated principal lacks permission for the changelog-listing operation; pipeline refuses promotion to Authorized. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Mapped from `DocumentCollectionError::RequestedCollectionWasEmpty` via `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error` ("no changelog entries are available"). Note: the handler's *own* empty path returns `200` with an empty `releases` array; this 404 arises only if the collection layer itself signals emptiness as an error. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no changelog entries are available"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | A stored changelog document is malformed — missing/blank `version`, missing/blank `id`, or an unparseable semantic version — surfaced as `DocumentCollectionError::DocumentBodyWasMalformed` and mapped to a 500. Also produced by any failure of the underlying `document_collection.list_documents(...)` call propagated via `?`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"stored changelog document was malformed: changelog entry is missing its version"}` |

**Full `SerializedErrorBody` example**:

```json
{
  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "stored changelog document was malformed: changelog entry is missing its version"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler orchestrates the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `parse_changelog_pagination_cursor(None)` — parses the (currently `None`) raw cursor into an optional non-negative offset; rejects non-numeric text with `RequestBodyWasMalformed`.
2. `parse_changelog_pagination_page_size(None)` — resolves page size, defaulting to 20, rejecting `0`/non-numeric and clamping to `[1, 100]`.
3. `parse_optional_changelog_category_filter(None)` — parses an optional category label (trimmed, non-blank, ≤120 chars, lowercased for matching).
4. `parse_optional_changelog_version_range_filter(None, None)` — parses optional `from`/`to` bounds via `parse_optional_semantic_version_bound`; rejects inverted ranges.
5. `validate_changelog_entries_sort_order(None)` — maps a sort string to `NewestFirst`/`OldestFirst`, defaulting to `NewestFirst`.
6. `build_changelog_entries_query_specification(...)` — assembles all validated inputs into a single `ChangelogEntriesQuerySpecification`.
7. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(CHANGELOG_COLLECTION_NAME)` — the sole async I/O: fetches all stored documents from the `"changelog_entries"` collection (errors propagate via `?`).
8. `DocumentCollection::from_stored_documents(...)` — wraps the raw documents in a pure, testable collection type.
9. `count_total_matching_changelog_entries(&collection, &query)` — projects, filters, and counts all matching entries (pre-pagination), mapping collection errors via `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error`.
10. `build_empty_changelog_entries_list_response(total_count)` — short-circuit path returning an empty `releases` list with `200` when `total_count == 0`.
11. `load_changelog_entries_page(&collection, &query)` — sorts + filters, then slices the page from `start_offset` to `end_offset` (`saturating_add`, clamped to length).
12. `compute_next_changelog_pagination_cursor(&loaded_entries, page_size)` — emits a next-cursor offset only when the page was full; `None` on a short (exhausted) page.
13. `group_changelog_entries_by_semantic_version(loaded_entries)` — groups entries by `version_display`, preserving encounter order.
14. `serialize_changelog_entries_list_to_response(...)` — packs groupings, total, and next cursor into `ListChangelogEntriesResponseBody`, then `.into_json()` for the wire.

Supporting pure helpers invoked transitively: `project_stored_document_to_entry`, `extract_string_field`, `extract_boolean_field`, `entry_satisfies_query`, `collect_sorted_matching_entries`, and `summarize_changelog_entry_for_list_item`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Empty result returns 200, not 404.** When `total_count == 0`, the handler returns `build_empty_changelog_entries_list_response` with a `200` and `releases: []`. The `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound` only arises from the collection layer explicitly signaling `RequestedCollectionWasEmpty` — a distinct code path from the handler's own empty branch.
- **Filters/pagination are inert today.** The route wires no `Query` extractor, so every parsing helper receives `None`. You will always get newest-first, page size 20, no filters, no cursor — regardless of any query string you append. The validation logic exists and is unit-tested but is not reachable from HTTP yet.
- **A single malformed stored document poisons the whole request.** `collect_sorted_matching_entries` projects every document eagerly; the first document with a missing/blank `id`, missing/blank `version`, or unparseable semver returns `DocumentBodyWasMalformed`, which becomes a `500`. One bad row fails the entire listing.
- **`totalCount` and the page are computed via two independent sorts.** `count_total_matching_changelog_entries` and `load_changelog_entries_page` each independently call `collect_sorted_matching_entries` over the full collection — the collection is projected, filtered, and sorted twice per request. Correct, but O(2·n·log n).
- **Semantic version leniency causes silent equivalence.** `SemanticVersion::parse` treats `"1"`, `"v1"`, and `"1.0.0"` as equal (missing components default to 0) and strips a leading `v`. Two entries whose display strings differ (`"1"` vs `"1.0.0"`) parse equal for sorting/filtering but remain *separate groupings* because grouping keys on the raw `version_display` string, not the parsed `SemanticVersion`.
- **`nextCursor` is a naive offset, not a stable token.** `compute_next_changelog_pagination_cursor` returns `loaded_entries.len()` as the offset only on a full page. Since the offset indexes into a freshly re-sorted list on the next request, concurrent inserts/deletes into the collection can shift entries under the cursor (classic offset-pagination drift).
- **`date` comes from the first entry in each grouping.** `group_changelog_entries_by_semantic_version` sets the grouping's `release_date` from whichever entry created the grouping; entries in the same version with differing `date` values silently keep only the first.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I appended `?category=Bug%20Fixes&pageSize=5` and nothing changed. Bug?**
A: Working as wired. There is no `Query` extractor on this route, so your query string is parsed by no one and discarded by everyone. The defaults win. The `parse_optional_changelog_category_filter` helper is real, tested, and waiting patiently to be given something to do.

**Q: Why does an empty changelog sometimes return 200 and other times 404?**
A: The handler's own empty branch returns `200` with `releases: []`. A `404` only appears if the underlying document collection reports `RequestedCollectionWasEmpty` as an error, which is a different failure surface. In practice, for this endpoint, expect `200` with an empty array.

**Q: Do I need to send a request body or a `Content-Type`?**
A: No. It is a `GET`. Send `x-account-email` (and, kindly, `x-request-id`), send no body, and set `Accept: application/json` if you enjoy being explicit. Any body you send is ignored with the serene indifference of a safe, idempotent verb.

### `GET /api/docs` — List Documentation Pages (Flat List + Section Navigation Tree)

#### Synopsis

Returns the full catalogue of documentation pages persisted in the `documentation_pages` document collection, reconstructed from their stored JSON bodies, filtered, sorted, paginated, and shaped into two parallel views: a flat `documentation_pages` array of compact per-page summaries and a hierarchical `section_tree` of top-level section navigation nodes. The endpoint additionally reports a pre-pagination `total_count`, an opaque forward-only `next_cursor`, and the `sort_order` that was actually applied. Although the handler contains a complete, battle-tested query-specification parsing pipeline (section-path filter, audience-kind filter, free-text search, page size, pagination cursor, sort order), the current wired signature feeds every one of those parsers a hard-coded `None`, so in practice the endpoint always returns the default view: every page, no filter, no search, title-ascending, page size 20, no cursor offset.

#### Theory & Rationale

This is a textbook read-only collection resource under a plural, noun-keyed path (`/api/docs`), exposed via the only HTTP verb whose contract promises both **safety** (the server state is not mutated as a consequence of the request) and **idempotency** (issuing the request N times yields the same server state as issuing it once). Because it is safe, the response is a legitimate cache target, is freely retriable by clients and intermediaries, and can be prefetched without moral hazard; because it is idempotent, a nervous client behind a flaky proxy may replay it with impunity. The response deliberately projects a *read model* — `DocumentationPageListItemSummary` and `DocumentationSectionTreeNode` are shaped for the consumer, not for the persistence layer — rather than leaking the raw `StoredDocument` shape, honouring the CQRS instinct that queries deserve their own tailored projections.

Within the Domain-Driven Design layering of `alma-http`, this handler is a thin orchestration seam: it holds no business rules of its own beyond input validation and projection. The genuinely interesting logic lives in a fleet of small, owned newtypes (`DocumentationSectionPath`, `DocumentationAudienceKind`, `DocumentationPageSize`, `DocumentationPagesPaginationCursor`, `DocumentationPagesSortOrder`) and pure, synchronous helper functions that operate over `&[StoredDocument]` and `&[DocumentationPageAggregate]`. This is a conscious "functional core, imperative shell" arrangement: the async, side-effecting shell fetches the raw document list exactly once through the `document_collection` port, and every subsequent act of filtering, sorting, paging, tree-building and shaping is a pure function that never touches a `UnitOfWork` and is therefore trivially unit-testable without a database. The persistence boundary is reached through the application-layer `DocumentCollectionPort` abstraction, keeping the HTTP layer blissfully ignorant of whether documents live in Postgres, an in-memory fake, or a filing cabinet.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

The handler's second extractor is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. The presence of this type-state marker means the request cannot even reach the handler body until it has traversed the full authentication-and-authorization pipeline; the handler itself performs no auth logic — it merely *demands the proof*, encoded in the type, that the pipeline already ran to completion.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended (effectively required for correlation) | `x-request-id: 3f9a2c7e-1b44-4c0e-9c2a-77e5d0f11abc` | Client-supplied opaque correlation identifier echoed into logs/traces for this request. Consumed during the `Validated` stage of the pipeline. Absence does not, by itself, produce a domain error at this handler, but you lose end-to-end traceability. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: docs.reader@example.com` | Identifies the calling account. This is the credential the pipeline uses to move from `Validated` to `Authenticated`. If it is missing you get `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; if it is present but does not resolve to a real, valid account you get `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Authorization for the docs-read capability is then checked to reach `Authorized`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** Requests are threaded through `HttpRequestInPipeline<Stage>`, where `Stage` is a zero-sized marker type that encodes, *in the type system*, exactly how far the request has progressed. The transitions are strictly ordered and each is fallible:

1. **`Validated`** — the raw HTTP envelope is parsed and structurally checked (well-formed headers such as `x-request-id`, decodable body if any). Structural failure short-circuits to `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`. A request that survives this stage carries `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>`.
2. **`Authenticated`** — the `x-account-email` credential is resolved to a concrete account identity. A missing credential yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; a present-but-bogus credential yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. Success upgrades the marker to `RequestHasBeenAuthenticated`.
3. **`Authorized`** — the authenticated identity is checked against the capability required to read documentation. Denial yields `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`. Success upgrades the marker to `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`.

Because `list_documentation_pages_handler` accepts `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` and nothing weaker, it is a compile-time impossibility to route an un-validated, un-authenticated, or un-authorized request into this handler. The proof obligation is discharged by the type, not by a runtime `if`.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

Note for the exhaustive reader: the source file defines a complete query-parsing subsystem — `section_path`, `audience`, `search`, `page_size`, `cursor`, and `sort` were all clearly *intended* as query parameters, and their parsers (`parse_optional_documentation_section_path_filter`, `parse_optional_documentation_audience_kind_filter`, `parse_optional_documentation_pages_search_term`, `parse_documentation_pages_pagination_page_size`, `parse_documentation_pages_pagination_cursor`, `validate_documentation_pages_sort_order`) are fully implemented and tested. However, the wired handler signature has **no** `Query<…>` extractor; every parser is invoked with `None`. Consequently, no query parameter is read off the wire today. Any query string you append is silently ignored.

#### Request Body

This endpoint reads **no request body**. It is a `GET` with no `Json<…>` extractor; the only extractors are `State(ApplicationState)` and the authorized-request marker. Sending a body has no effect on the response.

(a) Field table — there are no body fields.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| _(none)_ | — | — | — | — | This endpoint reads no request body. |

(b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) — the empty-object schema for "no body":

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma.example/schemas/list-documentation-pages-request.json",
  "title": "ListDocumentationPagesRequestBody",
  "description": "This endpoint reads no request body.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

(c) TypeScript interface:

```typescript

export type ListDocumentationPagesRequestBody = Record<string, never>;
```

(d) Rust struct mirror:

```rust
/// This endpoint reads no request body.
/// The handler's only extractors are `State(ApplicationState<_>)` and
/// `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ListDocumentationPagesRequestBody;
```


#### Successful Response

**Status:** `200 OK`. **Content-Type:** `application/json`. Body is a JSON object assembled by `serialize_documentation_pages_list_to_response`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `documentation_pages` | array of object | Flat list of the current page of matching documentation pages (post-filter, post-sort, post-pagination). |
| `documentation_pages[].page_identifier` | string | The stored document's identifier. |
| `documentation_pages[].title` | string | Page title (`"Untitled"` when the stored body omits `title`). |
| `documentation_pages[].section_path` | string | Normalized slash-separated section path (`"uncategorized"` when missing/blank). |
| `documentation_pages[].audience` | string | One of `"end-user"`, `"administrator"`, `"developer"` (defaults to `"end-user"` when the stored value is missing/unrecognized). |
| `documentation_pages[].body_excerpt` | string | Whitespace-collapsed excerpt of the body, truncated to 160 characters with a trailing `…` when longer. |
| `documentation_pages[].last_updated_epoch_seconds` | integer (i64) | Last-updated timestamp in epoch seconds (`0` when missing). |
| `section_tree` | array of object | Top-level section navigation nodes, in first-seen order across the loaded page. |
| `section_tree[].section_segment` | string | The top-level section segment (first path component). |
| `section_tree[].contained_page_count` | integer | Number of loaded pages whose top segment equals this node. |
| `section_tree[].child_section_segments` | array of string | Distinct second-level segments observed under this top segment, in first-seen order. |
| `total_count` | integer | Total number of pages matching the filters **before** pagination is applied. |
| `next_cursor` | string \| null | Opaque forward-only cursor (a stringified offset) when the returned page was full; `null` when the page was short or empty (end of results). |
| `sort_order` | string | The applied sort order: `"title-asc"`, `"title-desc"`, or `"recently-updated"`. |

**Response JSON Schema (draft 2020-12):**

```json
  "title": "ListDocumentationPagesResponseBody",
```

#### Error Responses

Errors are rendered from the `HttpError` enum into a `SerializedErrorBody` `{ error_category, error_explanation }`. The table below enumerates every `HttpError` variant and states precisely when it can occur **for this endpoint**.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Structurally, this is reachable only via the `Validated` stage of the pipeline (malformed envelope). The handler's own parsers *can* raise it, but every parser is fed `None`, so no parser-originated 400 occurs on the wired path today. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"documentation section path filter must not be empty"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` (or the required credential) absent — pipeline cannot reach `Authenticated`. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Credential present but does not resolve to a valid account. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Authenticated identity lacks the capability to read documentation — pipeline cannot reach `Authorized`. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not emitted by this handler. A collection listing returns an empty array, not a 404, when there is nothing to list. (Listed here for completeness of the `HttpError` surface.) | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested resource was not found"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The `document_collection.list_documents(...)` call fails, or a stored document is corrupt (not a JSON object) via `StoredDocumentWasCorrupt`, or the store is unavailable via `UnderlyingStoreUnavailable`. Both collection errors are mapped here by `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"documentation page 'doc_bad' is corrupt: document body is not a JSON object"}` |

**Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:**

```json
{
  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "documentation store unavailable: connection timed out"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler executes the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `parse_optional_documentation_section_path_filter(None)` — parses an optional section-path filter; called with `None`, yields `None`.
2. `parse_optional_documentation_audience_kind_filter(None)` — parses an optional audience filter; called with `None`, yields `None`.
3. `parse_optional_documentation_pages_search_term(None)` — parses an optional free-text search term into `NonEmptyText`; called with `None`, yields `None`.
4. `parse_documentation_pages_pagination_page_size(None)` — parses the page size (1..=100); called with `None`, returns the default of 20.
5. `parse_documentation_pages_pagination_cursor(None)` — parses the opaque offset cursor; called with `None`, yields `None`.
6. `validate_documentation_pages_sort_order(None)` — validates the sort order; called with `None`, defaults to `TitleAscending`.
7. `build_documentation_pages_query_specification(...)` — assembles the six validated inputs into a single `DocumentationPagesQuerySpecification`.
8. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(DOCUMENTATION_COLLECTION_NAME)` — the sole async, side-effecting call; fetches every `StoredDocument` from the `"documentation_pages"` collection.
9. `load_documentation_pages_page(&stored_documents, &spec)` — reconstructs each document (`reconstruct_documentation_page_aggregate`, which internally calls `build_body_excerpt`), then `filter_and_sort_documentation_pages` (which calls `documentation_page_matches_filters`), then applies `skip(offset).take(limit)`.
10. `count_total_matching_documentation_pages(&stored_documents, &spec)` — recounts the matches ignoring the pagination window, producing `total_count`.
11. `assemble_documentation_pages_section_tree(&loaded_pages)` — builds the top-level `section_tree` nodes (via `documentation_page_top_level_segment`).
12. `summarize_documentation_page_for_list_item(...)` — mapped over the loaded pages to produce the flat list summaries.
13. `compute_next_documentation_pages_pagination_cursor(&loaded_pages, page_size)` — returns a cursor only when the page was full and non-empty.
14. `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error(...)` — maps `DocumentCollectionError` variants to `HttpError::UpstreamApplicationFailure` (applied to the results of steps 9 and 10).
15. `serialize_documentation_pages_list_to_response(...)` — serializes the tree, summaries, total, cursor, and applied sort order into the final `Value` payload returned as `Json`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Query parameters are silently ignored.** Every parser is invoked with `None`; there is no `Query<…>` extractor on the wired signature. `?section=guides&sort=recent&page_size=5` changes nothing. This is the single most surprising behaviour and the one most likely to burn an integrator.
- **Pagination is computed but effectively inert.** Because the cursor is always `None` and page size always 20, only the first 20 matches are ever returned, and `next_cursor` will be non-null only when there are at least 20 pages — yet there is no wired way to *send* that cursor back, so the second page is currently unreachable through this endpoint alone.
- **A single corrupt document poisons the whole response.** `load_documentation_pages_page` and `count_total_matching_documentation_pages` iterate and call `reconstruct_documentation_page_aggregate`, which returns `StoredDocumentWasCorrupt` if any document body is not a JSON object. That error maps to `500 UpstreamApplicationFailure`, so one malformed row fails the entire listing rather than being skipped.
- **Lossy field defaults hide data problems.** Missing `title` becomes `"Untitled"`, missing/blank `section_path` becomes `"uncategorized"`, unknown/missing `audience` becomes `"end-user"`, missing `last_updated_epoch_seconds` becomes `0`. A page can therefore appear perfectly valid in the response while its stored body was substantially incomplete.
- **`section_tree` reflects only the loaded page, not all matches.** The tree is built from `loaded_pages` (post-pagination), whereas `total_count` is computed over all matches. The counts in `section_tree[].contained_page_count` can thus be smaller than the true totals for those sections.
- **Sorting is case-insensitive for titles but the excerpt drives search, not the full body.** Title sorts lowercase both sides; the (currently unreachable) search predicate matches against `title + section_path + body_excerpt` — the truncated 160-char excerpt — so a term appearing only deep in a long body would not match even if search were wired.
- **`audience` on output is always canonical.** Regardless of the stored spelling (`admin`, `dev`, `user`, etc.), the response emits only the canonical `end-user` / `administrator` / `developer` strings via `DocumentationAudienceKind::as_str`.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I passed `?sort=recently-updated&audience=developer` and nothing changed. Is the sort broken?**
A: The sort is not broken; it is simply never given your input. The handler reads no query string. You are receiving the hard-coded default view (all pages, title-ascending, size 20). File a ticket to wire the `Query` extractor if you need it.

**Q: Why is `next_cursor` sometimes a string and sometimes `null` — shouldn't a cursor be a number?**
A: On the wire it is a stringified offset (`"20"`) so it can remain opaque and evolve without breaking clients; `null` signals "no more results" (the returned page was short or empty). Treat it as an opaque token, not an integer to do arithmetic on.

**Q: One of my documentation pages is missing from the response entirely — no error, just gone. Where did it go?**
A: If it were *corrupt* (body not a JSON object) you would get a `500`, not a silent drop. A silent absence means it fell outside the first page of 20 title-ascending results, or its `section_path` normalized somewhere you did not expect. It is present in `total_count`; it is just beyond the current, unreachable-second-page window.
