### `GET /api/doc-technical` — Retrieve the technical (OpenAPI) documentation for the HTTP API component

#### Synopsis

This endpoint returns a rendered, AI-summarized technical documentation document for the HTTP API itself. It reads the documentation artifact metadata from the `documentation_pages` document collection, fetches the raw OpenAPI source from the storage adapter, parses and catalogs the endpoints, asks the AI adapter for a natural-language summary, and returns a single JSON object describing the whole thing. Despite the machinery inside, the request surface is intentionally minimal: an authorized `GET` with the required identity header and nothing else.

#### Theory & Rationale

From a strict REST standpoint this is the archetypal safe, idempotent, cacheable read. `GET /api/doc-technical` mutates nothing, holds no side effects that the caller can observe, and — modulo the non-deterministic AI summarization step and whatever the latest stored artifact happens to be — may be replayed an unbounded number of times with the same observable class of result. It is nullipotent in the strict HTTP sense (the safe-method contract) even if the summarization text may drift between calls; the resource being read is conceptually the "technical documentation of the HTTP API component," and the endpoint is merely a projection of that resource into a transport-friendly envelope. One could, and an operator may, layer an HTTP cache in front of it.

Within a Domain-Driven Design topology this handler sits squarely in the outermost adapter ring: it is an HTTP inbound adapter that orchestrates three outbound ports — the document collection port (metadata), the storage port (raw bytes), and the artificial-intelligence port (summary generation) — without itself owning any domain logic. The genuinely interesting design decision is that the pure transformation core (identifier parsing, version resolution, OpenAPI extraction, rendering, serialization) is factored into a battery of small, generic-free, synchronously-testable helper functions, while the handler retains only the async I/O choreography. This is the classic "functional core, imperative shell" arrangement, and it is why the endpoint reads almost like a pipeline transcript rather than a monolith.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: analyst@example.com` | The authenticated principal. Must be present and must parse as a valid email via `email_string_prism`. Absent → `401 authentication_credentials_were_missing`. Non-ASCII/opaque bytes or a non-email value → `401 authentication_credentials_were_invalid`. |
| `x-request-id` | No | `x-request-id: 7f3c9d2a-2b1e-4c88-9a6e-1f0b2c3d4e5f` | Correlation identifier threaded through the pipeline. Optional at the wire level: if omitted it defaults to the literal string `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"`. Only that non-empty default (or a supplied non-empty value) survives the `validate()` stage. |

Verbatim explanation of the type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`): the handler does not accept a raw request. It accepts `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, a phantom-typed wrapper whose type parameter encodes which pipeline stages have already been discharged. Extraction happens in the `FromRequestParts` implementation, which runs a strictly-ordered state machine:

1. The `x-request-id` header is read (or defaulted), producing a fresh `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasNotYetBeenValidated>` via `originate(...)`.
2. `.validate()` is called: it rejects an empty correlation identifier with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` and otherwise yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>`.
3. The `x-account-email` header is read; if missing it becomes `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, if it is not valid text it becomes `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`, and if it does not parse into an email via the prism it becomes `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`.
4. `.authenticate(principal)` attaches the parsed `Email` and yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthenticated>`.
5. `.authorize()` confirms a principal is present (it always is at this point) and yields `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`; a missing principal would produce `AuthorizationWasDenied`.

Because each stage consumes `self` and returns the next stage's type, it is impossible — at compile time — for a handler to observe a request that has skipped validation, authentication, or authorization. The handler binds `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` (into `_requesting_principal`), which is guaranteed to be a valid `Email`. This endpoint does not further scope the principal: any successfully authorized caller may read the document.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The route is a fixed literal `/api/doc-technical` with no path segments and the handler reads no query string. Any query parameters supplied by the client are ignored entirely.

#### Request Body

This endpoint has **no request body**. It is a `GET` and the handler takes no body extractor whatsoever. Critically, even the values that *look* like they would come from a request — the component identifier, the API version, and the output format — are **hardcoded inside the handler**, not read from the caller:

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (none) | — | — | — | — | No caller-supplied body fields are read. The component is fixed to `"http-api"`, the version to `None` (latest), and the format to `"markdown"`. |

For completeness, the internal (non-wire, non-caller-controlled) inputs the pipeline parses are: component identifier `"http-api"`, api version `None`, output format `"markdown"`. These are passed to `parse_technical_documentation_request_inputs(...)` as literals.

#### Error Responses

Every `HttpError` variant serializes to a `SerializedErrorBody` of shape `{ "error_category": ..., "error_explanation": ... }`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `request_body_was_malformed` | Effectively unreachable via the wire for this endpoint's inputs (component/version/format are hardcoded valid literals). Can only arise if the `validate()` stage sees an empty correlation identifier, or via `ApplicationError::DomainInvariantViolated` bubbling from a port. | `{"error_category":"request_body_was_malformed","error_explanation":"the correlation identifier was empty"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_missing` | The `x-account-email` header is absent. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_missing","error_explanation":"the 'x-account-email' header was absent"}` |
| 401 | `authentication_credentials_were_invalid` | The `x-account-email` header is not valid text, or does not parse into a valid email address. | `{"error_category":"authentication_credentials_were_invalid","error_explanation":"the account header did not parse into a valid email address"}` |
| 403 | `authorization_was_denied` | No authenticated principal at the authorization stage (defensive; not normally reachable once authentication succeeds), or an `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` propagated from a port. | `{"error_category":"authorization_was_denied","error_explanation":"no authenticated principal was present at the authorization stage"}` |
| 404 | `requested_resource_was_not_found` | No documentation artifact exists for component `http-api`; the requested version cannot be matched; or the referenced storage object is missing/empty. | `{"error_category":"requested_resource_was_not_found","error_explanation":"no technical documentation was found for component 'http-api'"}` |
| 500 | `upstream_application_failure` | The document-collection `list_documents` call fails; the artifact is malformed (missing `version` or `storage_object_key`); the storage object is not valid UTF-8; the source is not valid JSON / not an object / lacks `paths`; or the AI adapter fails to generate a summary. | `{"error_category":"upstream_application_failure","error_explanation":"technical documentation source was not valid json: expected value at line 1 column 1"}` |

One full serialized error body example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "requested_resource_was_not_found",
  "error_explanation": "no technical documentation was found for component 'http-api'"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The real functions this handler invokes, in order:

1. `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` — retrieves the guaranteed-present authenticated `Email` (bound but otherwise unused for scoping).
2. `parse_technical_documentation_request_inputs("http-api", None, Some("markdown"))` — bundles the three sub-parsers below into a `TechnicalDocumentationRequestInputs`.
   - `parse_technical_documentation_component_identifier(...)` — trims, rejects empty/illegal chars, lowercases the slug.
   - `parse_optional_technical_documentation_api_version(...)` — strips a leading `v`, validates 2–3 numeric dotted segments, or returns `None`.
   - `validate_technical_documentation_output_format(...)` — maps `markdown`/`md` → Markdown, `json` → Json, `openapi`/`oas` → OpenApi.
3. `application_state.document_collection.list_documents(DOCUMENTATION_COLLECTION_NAME)` — fetches all stored documents from the `documentation_pages` collection (async port call).
4. `load_technical_documentation_artifact(&stored_documents, &component, version)` — filters by `component_slug`, selects the requested or latest version, extracts `version`, `storage_object_key`, and `title`.
   - `select_latest_documentation_candidate(...)` — picks the highest semantic version when no version is requested.
   - `parse_semantic_version_ordering_key(...)` — turns a version string into a comparable `(major, minor, patch)` tuple.
5. `map_missing_technical_documentation_to_not_found_error(...)` — converts an `ArtifactMissing` into a `404`.
6. `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error(...)` — converts other collection errors (malformed → 500, unavailable → 500).
7. `read_storage_object_bytes(storage_adapter, &object_key)` — async fetch of the blob via `StoragePort::fetch_blob`, returning `Option<Vec<u8>>`.
8. `load_technical_documentation_source_from_storage(fetched_object, &artifact)` — unwraps the bytes, decodes UTF-8, rejects empty content.
9. `map_storage_adapter_error_to_http_error(...)` — object-missing → 404, unavailable → 500.
10. `parse_technical_documentation_openapi_schema(&raw_source)` — parses JSON, requires an object root with a `paths` key.
11. `extract_technical_documentation_endpoint_catalog(&openapi_schema)` — walks `paths`, keeps the seven known HTTP methods, resolves summaries, sorts by path then method.
12. `request_ai_summary_text(ai_adapter, &artifact, &catalog)` — builds the prompt and calls `ArtificialIntelligencePort::generate_completion`.
    - `build_technical_documentation_summary_prompt(...)` — assembles the developer-audience prompt from the catalog.
    - `NonEmptyText::parse(...)` — guards the prompt is non-empty before dispatch.
13. `summarize_technical_documentation_with_artificial_intelligence(completion_text, &catalog)` — trims the completion and falls back to a count sentence when blank.
14. `map_artificial_intelligence_adapter_error_to_http_error(...)` — AI generation failure → 500.
15. `render_technical_documentation_to_requested_format(&artifact, catalog.clone(), format)` — renders Markdown (a `# title` + method/path/summary table) for this endpoint.
    - `render_endpoint_catalog_as_markdown(...)` — the Markdown table builder (with a "No endpoints documented." branch).
16. `serialize_technical_documentation_to_response(rendered_payload, summary, catalog)` — assembles the final `document` object returned as `Json`.
    - `endpoint_descriptor_to_json(...)` — maps each descriptor into `{method, path, summary}`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **The caller controls nothing about the content.** Component (`"http-api"`), version (`None` → latest), and format (`"markdown"`) are hardcoded literals inside the handler. Sending a body, query string, or different `Accept` header changes nothing.
- **Version resolution is lossy.** `parse_semantic_version_ordering_key` maps any non-numeric segment (and any absent segment) to `0`, so `"v2.foo"` orders as `(2,0,0)` and an artifact with no `version` orders as `(0,0,0)` rather than being rejected. Latest-selection can therefore silently prefer a well-formed lower version over a malformed higher one.
- **Empty storage object is a 404, not a 500.** `load_technical_documentation_source_from_storage` treats whitespace-only or empty bytes as `ObjectMissing`, which maps to `requested_resource_was_not_found` — even though the object physically exists.
- **A blank AI response never errors.** If `generate_completion` returns empty/whitespace text, the summary silently becomes `"This component exposes N endpoint(s)."`; only an actual adapter *error* surfaces as `500`.
- **`paths` must be present, but a non-object `paths` yields an empty catalog rather than an error.** `parse_technical_documentation_openapi_schema` only checks that a `paths` key exists; `extract_technical_documentation_endpoint_catalog` then returns an empty `Vec` if `paths` is not an object, producing a valid `200` with `endpoint_count: 0`.
- **Non-standard HTTP methods and OpenAPI extension keys are dropped.** Only `get/put/post/delete/patch/head/options` survive; keys like `x-ignored`, `parameters`, or `trace` under a path item are skipped.
- **`x-request-id` is effectively always non-empty.** Because it defaults to `"unassigned-correlation-identifier"` when absent, the `validate()` empty-correlation `400` branch is essentially unreachable from the wire for this endpoint.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I request a different component or a specific version via query params?**
A: No. The handler ignores everything and asks for `http-api` at the latest version, rendered as markdown. The parsing machinery for component, version, and format exists and is fully tested, but this route feeds it constants.

**Q: Is this endpoint safe to cache?**
A: It is a safe, idempotent `GET`, so HTTP-cache-wise, yes. Be aware the `summary` field is AI-generated and may differ between cache misses, and `rendered`/`endpoints` reflect whatever the latest stored artifact happens to be.

**Q: I got a 404 but I can see the documentation artifact in the collection. Why?**
A: Most likely the referenced `storage_object_key` points at a missing or empty blob, which is mapped to `requested_resource_was_not_found`. Alternatively the artifact's `component_slug` does not equal `http-api`, so it is filtered out before selection.

### `GET /api/documentation` — Retrieve User Documentation (Canonical Landing Page)

#### Synopsis

`GET /api/documentation` returns the canonical, human-facing user-guide page for the ALMA platform, always resolving to the hard-coded landing topic `getting-started` in the default locale `en`. The endpoint self-heals on a fresh install by seeding a default documentation page into the `documentation_pages` collection if it is absent, then hydrates that page into a rich JSON envelope containing rendered HTML, extracted FAQ entries, related topics, an estimated reading time, and a helpfulness prompt. It accepts no request body, no path parameters, and no query parameters — every input is fixed by the handler itself.

#### Theory & Rationale

This is a textbook `GET`: safe and idempotent in the strict HTTP sense that a caller may invoke it arbitrarily many times without any *caller-observable* mutation of resource state. There is, admittedly, a subtle wrinkle worth savoring — the handler performs a one-time, conditional seeding write (`ensure_default_documentation_page_is_seeded`) on an empty collection. This does not violate `GET` safety in spirit, because the write is idempotent (it only inserts when the target document is absent) and produces no observable difference to the client after the first successful call: the response for the seeded page is identical to the response the client would have received had the page pre-existed. The method is therefore both *safe* (no meaningful side effect the client would care about) and *idempotent* (N calls collapse to the same terminal state).

In Domain-Driven Design terms, this handler sits squarely in the `docs` bounded context and treats a `DocumentationPageAggregate` as its aggregate root, hydrated from a persistence-agnostic `DocumentCollectionPort`. Note the deliberate architectural honesty embedded in the source: the upstream plan referenced domain types (`DocumentationPageSlug`, `UserDocumentationLocale`) that *do not exist* in `alma_domain`, so the handler models them as small, well-behaved local newtypes rather than polluting the shared domain crate with speculative types. This is a defensible anti-corruption choice: the HTTP layer owns its own view-model value objects, keeps its helpers pure and testable, and does not force premature abstraction onto the domain. The `NonEmptyText` domain value object is reused where a genuine domain invariant (non-emptiness) applies.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This handler's signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, which means the request must have traversed the entire type-state authentication pipeline before the handler body is ever entered. The extractor itself performs the authentication and authorization work; if any stage fails, the handler is never invoked and the corresponding `HttpError` is returned.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 7f3c9a2e-1b44-4d8e-9c21-4e0f5a6b7c88` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs/traces; used to stitch the request across the Validated → Authenticated → Authorized stages. If omitted, the pipeline typically synthesizes one. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: researcher@example.org` | The caller's account identity. Consumed during the Authenticated stage to establish *who* is calling; its absence yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`, and a malformed/unrecognized value yields `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated → Authenticated → Authorized`), verbatim in spirit:**

The ALMA HTTP layer encodes request lifecycle as *types*, not as runtime booleans. A raw request first becomes `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenValidated>` once its shape and headers pass structural validation (**Validated** — malformed input at this boundary surfaces as `400 RequestBodyWasMalformed`). It is then promoted to `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthenticated>` once the identity headers (notably `x-account-email`) are resolved to a known account (**Authenticated** — missing or invalid credentials surface as `401`). Finally it is promoted to `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` once policy checks confirm the authenticated principal is permitted to perform *this* operation (**Authorized** — a denied policy surfaces as `403 AuthorizationWasDenied`). Because the handler's parameter is typed `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, it is *statically impossible* to reach the handler body without having passed all three stages: the compiler enforces the security posture. There is no way to "forget" to authenticate, because an unauthenticated request simply does not typecheck into this function.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The handler declares no path segments and no query extractor. Both the topic slug and the locale are fixed internally: the slug is always `getting-started` (`DEFAULT_USER_DOCUMENTATION_TOPIC_SLUG`) and the locale is always `en` (`DEFAULT_USER_DOCUMENTATION_LOCALE`). Any query string a client appends to the URL is silently ignored.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. This endpoint reads no path or query parameters. |

#### Request Body

This endpoint reads **no request body**. The handler function accepts only `State(application_state)` and the authorized-request type-state extractor; there is no `Json<...>` body extractor in its signature. Any payload sent by the client is ignored. The three internal parsing helpers (`parse_user_documentation_topic_slug`, `parse_optional_user_documentation_locale`, `parse_optional_user_documentation_search_term`) are all invoked with hard-coded constants and `None`, never with client-supplied values.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | None. No request body is deserialized. |

```javascript
  },
```

```json
}
```

#### Error Responses

Every ALMA `HttpError` variant serializes to a `SerializedErrorBody` shaped `{error_category, error_explanation}`. The table below documents each variant and the specific circumstances under which *this* endpoint can produce it.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | Emitted by the internal parsing helpers if their inputs are invalid. In practice, this route feeds the helpers hard-coded valid constants (`getting-started`, `None` locale, `None` search), so a 400 is effectively unreachable via normal use — but the variant exists in the code path. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"documentation topic slug must not be empty"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | The pipeline could not find identity credentials (e.g. `x-account-email` absent) before reaching the `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Credentials were present but did not resolve to a valid/known account during the Authenticated stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | The authenticated principal failed the policy check for this operation during the Authorized stage. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | The requested-locale page is missing AND the default-locale fallback also yields no page (`map_missing_user_documentation_to_not_found_error`), or `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error` translates a `NotFound`. Rare here because the page is seeded first. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"no documentation page exists for topic 'getting-started'"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any collection port failure surfaces as `Upstream` and is mapped here — e.g. seeding insert fails, `fetch_document`/`list_documents` errors, or a stored document is missing its `body_markdown` field. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"stored documentation 'getting-started::en' is missing its body_markdown field"}` |

One full serialized error body example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "UpstreamApplicationFailure",
  "error_explanation": "stored documentation 'getting-started::en' is missing its body_markdown field"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler executes the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `parse_user_documentation_topic_slug(DEFAULT_USER_DOCUMENTATION_TOPIC_SLUG)` — validates and normalizes the hard-coded slug `getting-started` into a `DocumentationPageSlug` (lowercase kebab-case, non-empty, no leading/trailing hyphen).
2. `parse_optional_user_documentation_locale(None)` — resolves the locale; with `None` it defaults to `en` and validates it is exactly two ASCII lowercase letters.
3. `parse_optional_user_documentation_search_term(None)` — resolves an optional search term; with `None` it yields `None` (no filtering).
4. `ensure_default_documentation_page_is_seeded(...)` — idempotently inserts the default `getting-started::en` page (title `Getting Started`, seed markdown) into `documentation_pages` only if it is absent.
5. `load_user_documentation_page_for_locale(...)` — composes the `slug::locale` identifier and `fetch_document`s it; assembles a `DocumentationPageAggregate` if found, else returns `NotFound`.
6. `fall_back_to_default_locale_user_documentation(...)` — invoked only if the requested-locale load returns `NotFound`; retries the load against the default locale `en`.
7. `map_missing_user_documentation_to_not_found_error(...)` — converts a final missing page into a `404 RequestedResourceWasNotFound`.
8. `render_user_documentation_markdown_to_html(...)` — renders the markdown body to a minimal, HTML-escaped fragment (`#/##/###` headings and `<p>` paragraphs).
9. `extract_user_documentation_frequently_asked_questions(...)` — scans the body for `Q:`/`A:` line pairs and builds `UserDocumentationFaqEntry` records.
10. `find_related_user_documentation_topics(...)` — `list_documents`s the collection, excludes the current page, optionally filters by search term, and returns related topics sorted by slug.
11. `compute_user_documentation_estimated_reading_minutes(...)` — counts whitespace-delimited words and divides by 200 wpm (ceiling), clamped to a minimum of 1.
12. `build_user_documentation_helpfulness_prompt(...)` — builds a 1–5 rating prompt string embedding the page title.
13. `serialize_user_documentation_to_response(...)` — assembles the final JSON envelope, calling `capture_user_documentation_access_timestamp()` internally to stamp `accessed_at_epoch_seconds`.

Supporting helpers invoked transitively: `compose_documentation_document_identifier`, `assemble_documentation_page_from_stored_document`, `derive_documentation_title_from_slug`, `escape_documentation_html`, `map_application_error_to_document_collection_error`, `map_document_collection_error_to_http_error`, and `capture_user_documentation_access_timestamp`.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Inputs are hard-coded, not client-driven.** Despite the parsing helpers accepting slugs, locales, and search terms, this route always uses `getting-started`, `en`, and no search term. Clients cannot change the served page via this endpoint; the parameterized helpers exist for reuse/testing.
- **A `GET` that can write.** `ensure_default_documentation_page_is_seeded` performs an insert on an empty collection. It is idempotent and only fires when the document is absent, but strictly speaking the first-ever call to this "safe" `GET` mutates persistence.
- **`body_markdown` is mandatory in storage.** If a stored documentation document lacks a `body_markdown` string field, assembly fails with `DocumentCollectionError::Upstream`, surfacing as a `500 UpstreamApplicationFailure` — not a 404.
- **HTML rendering is intentionally minimal and blank-line-lossy.** Only `#`, `##`, `###` headings and single-line paragraphs are rendered; empty lines are dropped, and there are no lists, links, bold, or code blocks. `Q:`/`A:` lines are rendered as ordinary `<p>` paragraphs even though they are *also* extracted separately into `frequently_asked_questions`.
- **Reading time is never zero.** `compute_user_documentation_estimated_reading_minutes` uses `div_ceil` then `.max(1)`, so even a one-word page reports `estimated_reading_minutes: 1`.
- **Related-topic titles fall back to `"Documentation"`.** Any related page with an empty/missing `title` is surfaced with the literal title `"Documentation"`, and related topics are always sorted ascending by slug.
- **Dangling FAQ questions are silently dropped.** A `Q:` line with no following `A:` line (or with an empty question/answer) produces no FAQ entry.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I request a different documentation topic or locale via query string, e.g. `?topic=projects&locale=fr`?**
A: No. The handler ignores the query string entirely and always resolves `getting-started` / `en`. Your carefully crafted query parameters will be admired by no one and read by nothing.

**Q: Why does a `GET` need to be authenticated and authorized if it just returns docs?**
A: Because the handler's parameter type is `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the compiler refuses to let an un-authorized request reach it. The documentation may be mundane; the type-state discipline is not.

**Q: The response includes `related_topics`, but mine is always empty. Is it broken?**
A: No. `related_topics` lists *other* pages in the `documentation_pages` collection. On a fresh install only the seeded `getting-started::en` page exists, and the current page is excluded from its own related list, so the array is legitimately empty until more pages are created.

### `POST /api/assess-policy-answer` — Assess a Free-Text Policy Answer

#### Synopsis

This endpoint accepts a free-text policy `question`, a candidate `answer`, and an optional `grading_rubric`, then dispatches a composed natural-language prompt to the configured Artificial Intelligence adapter to grade the answer. It returns a structured verdict comprising a numeric `score`, the effective `maximum_score`, a boolean `passed` flag, and a paragraph of qualitative `feedback`. All grading is performed by the upstream language model; the handler's own responsibility is validation, prompt composition, extraction of the score and feedback from the free-form completion, clamping, and pass/fail classification.

#### Theory & Rationale

At the level of REST semantics this is a `POST` and, despite its superficial resemblance to a read, it is neither safe nor idempotent — and it is honest about that. Although the endpoint mutates no server-side persisted state (it writes nothing to any collection; note that `collections.rs` for this category defines only `study_type_templates`, `drafting_templates`, and `corrections`, none of which this handler touches), it delegates to a non-deterministic language-model completion whose output can vary across otherwise-identical requests. Modelling it as `POST` is therefore correct on two independent grounds: first, the operation is a controller-style action ("assess this answer") rather than the retrieval of an addressable resource, and there is no natural URI whose representation this call would return; second, because the underlying computation is non-idempotent, exposing it under a safe verb such as `GET` would be a category error that would invite intermediaries to cache or prefetch a response that has no stable identity. The request body carries the entire input, which is the idiomatic shape for an RPC-flavoured action expressed over HTTP.

In Domain-Driven Design terms the handler is a thin application-layer coordinator sitting squarely at the HTTP boundary. It performs no domain persistence and owns no aggregate; its single point of contact with the domain is the `NonEmptyText` value object, whose smart constructor (`NonEmptyText::parse`) enforces the invariant that the assembled prompt is never empty before it crosses into the `ArtificialIntelligencePort` abstraction. The port itself is the anti-corruption seam: the handler speaks only to `ArtificialIntelligencePort::generate_completion` and never to a concrete model vendor, so the grading capability can be swapped, faked in tests, or re-implemented without disturbing this file. Everything score-shaped — extraction, clamping, and the 60%-of-maximum pass threshold — lives as pure, individually unit-tested helper functions, keeping the business rule ("what counts as a pass") explicit and inspectable rather than buried inside a prompt or an external service.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Yes | `x-request-id: 7f3c2a10-9b4e-4d21-8c6a-0f1e2d3c4b5a` | Correlation identifier consumed at the very first pipeline stage. Used to tag logs and to echo request lineage across the type-state pipeline. Absence is treated as a malformed/unauthenticated request depending on the pipeline configuration. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: analyst@example.org` | The caller's account identity. It is the credential the pipeline reads to move a request from *Authenticated* to *Authorized*. A missing value surfaces as `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing`; a syntactically or semantically invalid value surfaces as `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid`; a valid identity that lacks permission for this route surfaces as `AuthorizationWasDenied`. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | The handler extracts the body via axum's `Json<Value>` extractor. A non-JSON or unparseable body is rejected before the handler body runs. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated` → `Authenticated` → `Authorized`).** The handler's second argument is `_authorized_request: HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. This is not a decorative parameter: it is a compile-time proof obligation. `HttpRequestInPipeline<S>` is generic over a marker state `S`, and Rust's type system will only construct a value whose state parameter is `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` after the request has traversed the full pipeline. Conceptually the request first becomes **Validated** — its transport-level shape (headers such as `x-request-id`, body decodability) has been checked. It then advances to **Authenticated** — the `x-account-email` credential has been read and recognised as a real identity. It finally advances to **Authorized** — that identity has been confirmed to hold permission for *this* endpoint. Because the handler demands the terminal `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` type, it is structurally impossible to invoke the handler's logic against an unvalidated, unauthenticated, or unauthorized request; any failure earlier in the chain short-circuits with the corresponding `HttpError` before a single line of assessment logic executes. The parameter is prefixed with an underscore because, once the proof exists, the handler needs nothing further from it.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. This endpoint reads no path segments and consults no query-string parameters. All input arrives in the JSON request body.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | None. |

#### Request Body

The handler deserializes the body into a permissive `serde_json::Value` and then reads named fields by hand. Unknown fields are silently ignored; only the four fields below are ever read.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `question` | string | **Yes** | Must be present and must be a JSON string. | — | The policy question being graded against. Rejected with `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if missing or not a string. |
| `answer` | string | **Yes** | Must be present, must be a JSON string, and must not be blank (empty or whitespace-only after trimming). Answers longer than 4000 Unicode scalar values are truncated (with a ` [...]` marker) before being embedded in the prompt — the full answer is still accepted; only the prompt copy is shortened. | — | The candidate free-text answer to assess. |
| `grading_rubric` | string | No | If present but not a string, or a string that is empty/whitespace-only after trimming, it collapses to "no rubric". When present and non-blank it is trimmed and injected into the prompt. | absent (no rubric section) | Optional grading criteria to steer the model's assessment. |
| `maximum_score` | integer | No | When present must be a JSON non-negative integer, must be greater than `0`, and must not exceed `100`. A `null` value is treated as absent. Non-integer/negative values, `0`, and values `> 100` are all rejected with `RequestBodyWasMalformed`. | `10` | The grading ceiling. Drives clamping of the extracted score and the pass threshold (60% of this value). |

#### Successful Response

Status: `200 OK`. Body is a JSON object built by `build_assessment_response_payload`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `score` | integer | The extracted-and-clamped score. Never exceeds `maximum_score`. `0` when no digit could be extracted from the completion. |
| `maximum_score` | integer | The effective grading ceiling used (the supplied `maximum_score`, or the default `10`). |
| `passed` | boolean | `true` when `score` reaches at least 60% of `maximum_score` (integer arithmetic: `score * 100 >= maximum_score * 60`). |
| `feedback` | string | Qualitative feedback. Prefers text after a `Feedback:` label in the completion; otherwise the whole trimmed completion; otherwise a neutral placeholder. |

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialized as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`.

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `question` missing/not-a-string; `answer` missing/not-a-string; `answer` blank; `maximum_score` not an integer, `0`, or `> 100`; the composed prompt fails `NonEmptyText::parse`. | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"the 'answer' field must not be blank"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | `x-account-email` (or required correlation credentials) absent — pipeline never reaches `RequestHasBeenAuthorized`. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | `x-account-email` present but not a recognisable/valid identity. | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Identity is authenticated but not permitted to call this route. | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | Not produced by this handler's own logic; surfaces only if routing/path resolution fails to match. | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"the requested resource was not found"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | The AI adapter's `generate_completion` returns an application error; mapped via `HttpError::from` inside `request_assessment_completion`. | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"the AI provider returned an error"}` |

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

In call order, the real helper functions this handler invokes:

1. `extract_required_question_field(&submitted_body)` — reads mandatory `question`; errors `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if missing or not a string.
2. `extract_required_answer_field(&submitted_body)` — reads mandatory `answer`; errors `RequestBodyWasMalformed` if missing or not a string.
3. `reject_blank_answer_submission(&supplied_answer)` — rejects answers that are empty or whitespace-only after trimming.
4. `extract_optional_grading_rubric_field(&submitted_body)` — reads optional `grading_rubric`; trims it and collapses missing/non-string/blank values to `None`.
5. `extract_optional_maximum_score_field(&submitted_body)` — reads optional `maximum_score`; defaults to `10`, treats `null` as absent, rejects `0`, `> 100`, and non-integers.
6. `truncate_oversized_answer_for_prompt(&supplied_answer, MAXIMUM_ANSWER_CHARACTERS_IN_PROMPT)` — caps the prompt copy of the answer at 4000 Unicode scalar values, appending ` [...]` on truncation.
7. `compose_policy_assessment_prompt(&supplied_question, &answer_for_prompt, grading_rubric.as_deref())` — assembles the two-line-response grading instruction, optionally embedding the rubric.
8. `parse_assessment_prompt_into_non_empty_text(combined_prompt)` — validates the prompt into a domain `NonEmptyText`, mapping failures via `map_domain_parse_failure_to_malformed_body`.
9. `request_assessment_completion(application_state.artificial_intelligence_adapter.as_ref(), &prompt_text).await` — forwards the prompt to the `ArtificialIntelligencePort` and lifts port errors into `HttpError` (500).
10. `extract_numeric_score_from_completion_text(&completion.produced_text)` — finds the first integer after a `Score` label (case-insensitive), falling back to the first integer anywhere; `.unwrap_or(0)` applied by the handler when `None`. Internally uses `first_integer_in`, which saturates at `u8::MAX`.
11. `clamp_extracted_score_to_maximum(raw_score, maximum_score)` — clamps the extracted score down to at most `maximum_score`.
12. `extract_qualitative_feedback_from_completion_text(&completion.produced_text)` — pulls text after a `Feedback:` label, else the whole trimmed completion, else a neutral placeholder.
13. `classify_answer_pass_or_fail(clamped_score, maximum_score)` — integer-arithmetic pass test at 60% of maximum; always `false` when `maximum_score == 0`.
14. `build_assessment_response_payload(clamped_score, maximum_score, has_passed, &qualitative_feedback)` — constructs the JSON response object.

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **A score of `0` can mean "the model produced no number".** When `extract_numeric_score_from_completion_text` finds no digits, the handler's `.unwrap_or(0)` yields `0`, which is indistinguishable in the response from a genuine grade of zero. Callers cannot tell a truly-failing answer from an unparseable completion.
- **The `Score` label match is a naive substring search.** `extract_numeric_score_from_completion_text` looks for the lowercase substring `"score"` anywhere, then reads the first integer after it. A completion like "This scores well, unlike the 3 alternatives..." can latch onto the wrong number. If the model happens to write feedback before the score, the wrong integer may win.
- **Clamping hides model overshoot but never underflow-corrects.** `clamp_extracted_score_to_maximum` only caps the high side. A model that returns a raw score above `maximum_score` is silently clamped to the ceiling; there is no floor beyond the natural `u8` non-negativity.
- **`maximum_score` accepts `null` but not `0`.** `null` is quietly treated as "absent" and yields the default of `10`, whereas an explicit `0` is a `400`. Sending `maximum_score: null` and omitting the field entirely behave identically.
- **Answer truncation is silent and affects only the prompt.** Answers over 4000 Unicode scalars are cut (with ` [...]`) before being embedded, but the response does not signal that truncation happened. The grade may reflect only the first 4000 characters of a very long answer.
- **`first_integer_in` saturates rather than errors.** A gigantic number in the completion (e.g. `99999`) becomes `u8::MAX` (255), which is then clamped to `maximum_score`. No malformed-completion error is raised for absurd numbers.
- **The pass threshold uses integer arithmetic and rounds by comparison, not division.** `passed` is `score*100 >= maximum_score*60`. For `maximum_score = 10`, a score of exactly `6` passes; `5` fails. There is no partial-credit rounding.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Is this endpoint idempotent, so I can safely retry on timeout?**
A: No. It calls a non-deterministic language model, so two identical requests may return different scores and feedback. Retrying is safe in the sense that nothing is persisted (this handler writes to no collection), but the result is not guaranteed to match a prior attempt.

**Q: Why is the second handler argument named `_authorized_request` and never used?**
A: Its value is not used, but its type is load-bearing. `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` is a compile-time proof that the request cleared Validated → Authenticated → Authorized. The underscore only tells the compiler you knowingly discard the value, not the guarantee.

**Q: Can I get the raw model completion or the exact prompt that was sent?**
A: No. The response contains only `score`, `maximum_score`, `passed`, and `feedback`. The composed prompt and the unparsed completion text are internal; `feedback` is the closest thing to the model's raw output, and even that is stripped of the `Feedback:` label and any preceding `Score:` line when the label is present.

### `POST /api/corrections` — Record a Submitted Textual Correction

#### Synopsis

This endpoint records a single textual correction: a pairing of the original wording, the corrected wording, and an optional free-form note explaining the change. The submitted pair is validated, normalised into domain value objects, assembled into a JSON document body, stamped with a server-side creation timestamp and a freshly minted UUID, and persisted into the `corrections` collection under the authenticated principal's account. On success it returns the generated document identifier together with a terse acknowledgement.

#### Theory & Rationale

In the vocabulary of HTTP verbs, `POST` is the correct and only defensible choice here: the operation is neither safe nor idempotent, and it fabricates a brand-new subordinate resource each time it is invoked. It is not safe because it mutates persistent state — a document is inserted into a collection. It is not idempotent because the handler mints a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` on every call and stamps a fresh wall-clock timestamp, meaning two byte-for-byte identical requests produce two distinct, independently addressable correction documents. There is deliberately no client-supplied identifier and no upsert semantics, so `PUT` would misrepresent the contract; the resource path `/api/corrections` names the *collection* into which a new member is appended, and the server alone is the authority on the member's name. This is the textbook shape of a resource-factory `POST`.

Viewed through a Domain-Driven Design lens, this handler sits squarely in the application/interface layer and is scrupulous about staying there. It performs transport-level parsing (pulling `original_text`, `corrected_text`, and `correction_note` out of an untyped `serde_json::Value`), then immediately hands the semantically meaningful strings to the domain via `NonEmptyText::parse`, which is the true guardian of the "text must not be empty" invariant. The principal — an `Email` value object surfaced by the type-state pipeline — becomes the `owning_account` of the stored document, thereby weaving authorization identity directly into the persisted aggregate. Persistence itself is delegated to the `DocumentCollectionPort`, an abstraction the handler depends upon but does not implement, honouring the dependency-inversion discipline that keeps the HTTP crate ignorant of any particular storage engine.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 3f9a2c7e-1b64-4c0a-9d21-5e8f0a1b2c3d` | Correlation identifier echoed through logs and traces. Used to stitch a single request across pipeline stages; if omitted the platform may synthesise one. |
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: editor@example.com` | The authenticated principal's email. This value is parsed into an `Email` value object and, once the request is `Authorized`, becomes the `owning_account` written onto the persisted correction document. Missing or malformed values cause the request to fail before the handler body runs. |

This handler never executes until the request has traversed the crate's type-state pipeline and arrived as an `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`. The type-state pipeline encodes each successive guarantee in the type system, so that a handler literally cannot be compiled against a request that has not cleared every prior gate:

- **Validated** — the raw inbound request has been shape-checked at the transport boundary (well-formed headers, decodable framing). A request that fails validation never advances and yields a `4xx` before any authentication is attempted.
- **Authenticated** — the principal has been established. Concretely, `x-account-email` has been parsed into an `Email` value object and the caller's identity is now known and trustworthy. Failure at this stage surfaces as `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` (nothing to authenticate) or `401 AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` (present but unusable).
- **Authorized** — the authenticated principal has been checked against the policy required for *this* operation. Only after this transition does the request materialise as `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, the exact type this handler's signature demands. The authorized principal is then retrieved via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()`, returning the `&Email` used as the owning account.

Because the state is carried in the generic type parameter, skipping a stage is not a runtime risk to be tested for — it is a compile error. The handler's mere existence with a `RequestHasBeenAuthorized` parameter is a static proof that authentication and authorization have already succeeded by the time line 33 executes.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None. The endpoint accepts neither path segments beyond the literal `/api/corrections` nor any query-string parameters. All input arrives in the request body.

#### Request Body

The handler reads the body as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then extracts individual fields by name. The following table enumerates every field the handler actually inspects.

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `original_text` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; must be non-empty per `NonEmptyText::parse` (rejects empty/whitespace-only); must differ (after trimming) from `corrected_text` | — | The original wording being corrected. |
| `corrected_text` | string | Yes | Must be a JSON string; must be non-empty per `NonEmptyText::parse`; must differ (after trimming) from `original_text` | — | The replacement wording. |
| `correction_note` | string \| null | No | If a string, it is trimmed; a missing field, JSON `null`, a non-string value, or an empty-after-trim string all collapse to no note | `null` | Optional free-form explanation of the change. Stored as `null` when absent or meaningless. |

Any additional fields present in the JSON object are silently ignored — the handler only ever reads the three keys above.

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma.example/schemas/create-correction-request.json",
  "title": "CreateCorrectionRequest",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "original_text": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "The original wording being corrected."
    },
    "corrected_text": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "The replacement wording."
    },
    "correction_note": {
      "type": ["string", "null"],
      "description": "Optional free-form explanation of the change."
    }
  },
  "required": ["original_text", "corrected_text"],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

TypeScript interface:

```typescript
interface CreateCorrectionRequest {
  /** The original wording being corrected. Must be a non-empty string. */
  original_text: string;
  /** The replacement wording. Must be a non-empty string and differ from original_text (trimmed). */
  corrected_text: string;
  /** Optional free-form explanation. Missing/null/empty-after-trim are all treated as "no note". */
  correction_note?: string | null;
}
```

Rust struct mirror (the handler itself reads a `serde_json::Value`; this struct reflects the fields it extracts):

```rust

/// The live handler parses these out of a `serde_json::Value` rather than
/// deserialising into a struct.

    original_text: String,

    /// Optional. Extracted by `extract_optional_correction_note_field`;
    /// missing / null / non-string / empty-after-trim all yield `None`.
    correction_note: Option<String>,
}
```

#### Successful Response

The handler returns `Json(build_correction_creation_response(&generated_identifier))`. Axum serialises this with a `200 OK` status.

| Field | Type | Always Present | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document_identifier` | string (UUID v4) | Yes | The server-generated identifier of the newly created correction document. |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Yes | A fixed confirmation string, always the literal `"correction created"`. |

Response JSON Schema (draft 2020-12):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma.example/schemas/create-correction-response.json",
  "title": "CreateCorrectionResponse",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "document_identifier": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "uuid",
      "description": "Server-generated UUID v4 for the created correction."
    },
    "acknowledgement": {
      "type": "string",
      "const": "correction created"
    }
  },
  "required": ["document_identifier", "acknowledgement"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

Realistic 200 example:

```json

  "acknowledgement": "correction created"
}
```

Note that the response does NOT echo back the stored fields (`original_text`, `corrected_text`, `correction_note`, `created_at`). Those are persisted into the document body but are not returned to the caller; only the identifier and acknowledgement come back.

#### Error Responses

Every error is serialised as a `SerializedErrorBody` with two fields: `error_category` and `error_explanation`. The variants reachable from this endpoint are:

| Status | error_category | When (for THIS endpoint) | Example body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `RequestBodyWasMalformed` | `original_text` missing or not a string; `corrected_text` missing or not a string; `original_text` equals `corrected_text` (trimmed); either value empty per `NonEmptyText::parse`; or an application-layer `DomainInvariantViolated` bubbling up from persistence | `{"error_category":"RequestBodyWasMalformed","error_explanation":"field 'original_text' is required"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing` | No principal could be established at the Authenticated stage (e.g. `x-account-email` absent) — fails before the handler body runs | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereMissing","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were missing"}` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid` | Credentials present but unusable (e.g. `x-account-email` fails to parse into an `Email`) — fails before the handler body runs | `{"error_category":"AuthenticationCredentialsWereInvalid","error_explanation":"authentication credentials were invalid"}` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationWasDenied` | Authenticated principal lacks the required policy at the Authorized stage, or the persistence layer returns `ApplicationError::AuthorizationWasDenied` | `{"error_category":"AuthorizationWasDenied","error_explanation":"authorization was denied"}` |
| 404 | `RequestedResourceWasNotFound` | The `DocumentCollectionPort` reports `RequestedProjectCouldNotBeLocated` or `RequestedResourceCouldNotBeLocated` during insertion | `{"error_category":"RequestedResourceWasNotFound","error_explanation":"requested resource could not be located"}` |
| 500 | `UpstreamApplicationFailure` | Any other `ApplicationError` from `insert_document` (e.g. `StorageAdapterFailure`) — a storage/infrastructure failure | `{"error_category":"UpstreamApplicationFailure","error_explanation":"storage adapter failure: boom"}` |

Full `SerializedErrorBody` example:

```json
{
  "error_category": "RequestBodyWasMalformed",
  "error_explanation": "'original_text' and 'corrected_text' must differ from one another"
}
```

#### Internal Processing Pipeline

The handler body invokes the following real helper functions, in order:

1. `extract_required_original_text_field(&submitted_body)` — pulls the mandatory `original_text` string; errors 400 if absent or non-string.
2. `extract_required_corrected_text_field(&submitted_body)` — pulls the mandatory `corrected_text` string; errors 400 if absent or non-string.
3. `extract_optional_correction_note_field(&submitted_body)` — pulls the optional, trimmed `correction_note`; missing/null/non-string/empty-after-trim all become `None`.
4. `reject_identical_original_and_corrected_text(&original, &corrected)` — errors 400 if the trimmed original and corrected text are equal.
5. `parse_original_text_into_non_empty_text(original)` — validates/normalises the original into a domain `NonEmptyText` (via `NonEmptyText::parse`).
6. `parse_corrected_text_into_non_empty_text(corrected)` — same, for the corrected text.
7. `generate_correction_document_identifier()` — mints a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` as the document id.
8. `resolve_owning_account_from_principal(authorized_request.authorized_principal())` — extracts the principal's email string to use as `owning_account`.
9. `current_creation_timestamp_iso8601()` — reads the system clock and produces an RFC-3339 UTC timestamp (falling back to epoch on a pre-epoch clock).
10. `assemble_correction_document_body(&original, &corrected, note, &created_at)` — builds the JSON document body with all four stored fields.
11. `build_correction_stored_document(id, owning_account, body)` — wraps the parts into a `StoredDocument`.
12. `persist_correction_document(collection, document)` — calls `insert_document(CORRECTIONS_COLLECTION_NAME, ...)` on the `DocumentCollectionPort`; maps application errors via `map_application_error_to_http_error`.
13. `build_correction_creation_response(&generated_identifier)` — builds the `{document_identifier, acknowledgement}` success payload.

Supporting pure helpers used transitively by the timestamp routine: `format_unix_seconds_as_iso8601`, `convert_days_since_epoch_to_calendar_date`, `is_gregorian_leap_year`, and `month_lengths_for_year` — a hand-rolled calendar because the HTTP crate carries no calendar dependency. Error mapping is handled by `map_domain_parse_failure_to_malformed_body` (domain parse errors → 400) and `map_application_error_to_http_error` (application errors → 400/403/404/500).

#### Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Not idempotent by design.** Every call generates a new UUID and a new timestamp, so posting the same body twice creates two distinct correction documents. There is no dedup and no upsert.
- **`correction_note` swallows garbage silently.** A non-string `correction_note` (number, array, object) does NOT error — it is coerced to `None` and stored as JSON `null`. Only `original_text`/`corrected_text` type-check strictly.
- **Whitespace-only "changes" are rejected.** The identical-text check runs on trimmed values, so `original_text = "  same  "` versus `corrected_text = "same"` is treated as a no-op and rejected with 400, even though the raw strings differ.
- **The response hides the stored data.** Callers get back only `document_identifier` and a fixed `acknowledgement`; `created_at` and the stored texts are never returned. To read them back you must fetch the document separately (e.g. via the sibling `GET /api/corrections`).
- **Timestamp is a bespoke, seconds-resolution UTC string.** `created_at` is derived by hand from Unix seconds, always ends in `Z`, has no sub-second precision, and always renders as UTC. A clock reporting a pre-epoch time silently yields `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` rather than erroring.
- **Owning account is taken from the principal, not the body.** You cannot create a correction "on behalf of" another account; `owning_account` is always the authenticated `x-account-email`. The body has no account field, and one would be ignored if supplied.
- **Extra body fields are ignored.** Because the body is read as a `Value` and probed key-by-key, unknown fields neither error nor get stored.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I supply my own `document_identifier` to make the call idempotent?**
A: No. The identifier is generated server-side with `Uuid::new_v4()` and there is no field to override it. If you POST twice, you get two documents. Deduplication, if you want it, is your problem.

**Q: The docs mention `created_at` — why isn't it in my 200 response?**
A: Because the success payload is exactly `{document_identifier, acknowledgement}` and nothing else. `created_at` is stored in the document body, not echoed. Fetch the document if you need it.

**Q: I sent `correction_note: 12345` and it didn't error. Is that a bug?**
A: No, that is the documented behaviour. Only `original_text` and `corrected_text` are strictly type-checked. A non-string `correction_note` is treated as "no note" and persisted as `null`. If you wanted a note, send a non-empty string.

### `POST /api/templates/drafting-templates` — Create a Drafting Template

#### Synopsis

Creates a single, brand-new *drafting template* — a reusable document skeleton comprising a mandatory human-facing name, a mandatory body of prose, an optional free-text description, and an optional set of placeholder tokens that are cross-validated against the body. The endpoint accepts a raw JSON object, transforms it through a rigorous field-extraction and domain-validation pipeline, mints a fresh UUID identifier, stamps the record with the authenticated principal as the owning account, and persists it into the `drafting_templates` document collection. On success it returns the freshly generated `document_identifier` together with a terse textual acknowledgement.

#### Theory & Rationale

This endpoint is, in the truest Fielding-ian sense of the word, a *creation* endpoint, and it uses the `POST` verb accordingly. `POST` is neither safe nor idempotent, and this handler exhibits both of those properties: every successful invocation manufactures a new server-side resource with a *new* server-minted UUID (see `generate_drafting_template_identifier`), which means that firing the identical request body twice will produce two distinct drafting templates with two distinct identifiers. There is no client-supplied idempotency key, no natural-key deduplication, and no conditional-request machinery — the endpoint is non-idempotent, and callers who retry after an ambiguous network failure must reconcile the possibility of duplicate creation themselves. Because the resource identifier is allocated by the server rather than dictated by the client, this is a canonical "POST to a collection" pattern rather than a "PUT to a known URI" pattern; the collection URI `/api/templates/drafting-templates` is the factory, and the response body carries the identifier of the newly created resource.

From a Domain-Driven Design vantage point, the handler is a textbook thin application-layer orchestrator that studiously refuses to let raw transport-layer primitives leak into the domain. The two mandatory text fields are not trusted as bare `String`s for one nanosecond longer than necessary; they are immediately coerced into the `NonEmptyText` value object (`parse_template_name_into_non_empty_text`, `parse_template_body_into_non_empty_text`), whose very type guarantees the non-blank invariant that the rest of the system is entitled to assume. Placeholder tokens are subjected to a genuine *cross-field* business invariant — every declared token must literally appear as a substring of the body — which is enforced in the handler (`validate_placeholder_tokens_present_in_body`) precisely because it is an application-level consistency rule rather than a single-value parse concern. Persistence is delegated through the `DocumentCollectionPort`, an outbound port in the hexagonal-architecture sense, so the handler remains blissfully ignorant of whether the backing store is MongoDB, Postgres, or a pile of index cards. The result is a handler that is verbose, ceremonious, and correct — exactly as the reader of this documentation deserves.

#### Authentication & Required Headers

This endpoint is mounted behind the type-state request pipeline and its handler signature demands `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>`, meaning the request must have already traversed the full authentication-and-authorization gauntlet before a single line of handler logic executes. The authenticated principal is extracted via `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` and becomes the `owning_account` stamped onto the persisted document.

| Header | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x-account-email` | Yes | `x-account-email: author@example.com` | The caller's account email. This is the identity that the pipeline validates and authenticates, and it is the value ultimately resolved into the template's `owning_account` via `resolve_owning_account_from_principal`. Missing or unparseable values are rejected by the pipeline *before* the handler runs. |
| `x-request-id` | Recommended | `x-request-id: 8f2b1c34-5d6e-47a8-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` | A client-supplied correlation identifier echoed through logs and tracing. Not strictly enforced by this handler, but strongly encouraged for observability and for tying a duplicate-creation retry back to its originating request. |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `Content-Type: application/json` | The body is parsed via axum's `Json<Value>` extractor; a non-JSON or absent content type will cause extraction to fail before the handler body executes. |

**The type-state pipeline (`Validated -> Authenticated -> Authorized`).** The alma-http request pipeline encodes authorization progress *in the type system* rather than in runtime flags, so that it is impossible to write a handler that forgets to authenticate. A raw request first enters a `Validated` state (structural/transport prerequisites — e.g. a well-formed `x-account-email` — are satisfied). It is then promoted to `Authenticated` once the principal's identity has been positively established. Finally it is promoted to `Authorized` once policy checks confirm the authenticated principal is permitted to perform this operation. Only a value of type `HttpRequestInPipeline<RequestHasBeenAuthorized>` — the terminal state — can be passed to this handler; the compiler literally refuses to construct the handler's arguments otherwise. Consequently, by the time `create_drafting_template_handler` runs, authentication and authorization are *statically guaranteed to have happened*, and the handler is free to call `authorized_request.authorized_principal()` and trust the result unconditionally.

#### Path & Query Parameters

None.

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | This endpoint declares no path segments beyond the static route and reads no query-string parameters whatsoever. |

#### Request Body

The body is extracted as an untyped `serde_json::Value` and then hand-destructured field by field. Any top-level JSON that is not an object will fail the individual `.get(...)` field lookups and surface as a `RequestBodyWasMalformed` error for the first missing mandatory field.

**(a) Field table**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `template_name` | string | Yes | Must be present; must be a JSON string; must parse as `NonEmptyText` (i.e. not blank/whitespace-only after domain parsing). | — | The human-facing name of the drafting template. Extracted by `extract_required_template_name_field`, then parsed by `parse_template_name_into_non_empty_text`. |
| `template_body` | string | Yes | Must be present; must be a JSON string; must parse as `NonEmptyText`. | — | The reusable body prose of the template. Extracted by `extract_required_template_body_field`, then parsed by `parse_template_body_into_non_empty_text`. This is the text against which all placeholder tokens are substring-checked. |
| `description` | string | No | If present and a string, it is `trim()`-ed; if the trimmed result is empty it is treated as *absent* (stored as JSON `null`). Non-string values are silently ignored (treated as absent). | `null` (absent) | An optional human-facing description. Extracted by `extract_optional_template_description_field`. |
| `placeholder_tokens` | array of strings | No | If present it must be a JSON array; `null` is treated as an empty array. Every entry must be a JSON string; each entry is `trim()`-ed; a blank/whitespace-only entry is rejected as malformed. Every surviving (trimmed) token must appear as a literal substring of `template_body`. | `[]` (empty array) | The set of placeholder tokens the template promises to contain. Extracted by `extract_optional_placeholder_token_list`, then cross-validated by `validate_placeholder_tokens_present_in_body`. |

Note: any additional/unknown fields in the submitted object are simply ignored — the handler only reads the four fields above. The persisted document additionally carries a server-injected constant field `template_kind` = `"drafting_template"` that the client neither supplies nor controls.

**(b) JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)**

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://alma.example/schemas/create-drafting-template-request.json",
  "title": "CreateDraftingTemplateRequest",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "required": ["template_name", "template_body"],
  "properties": {
    "template_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Human-facing name; must be non-blank after domain parsing."
    },
    "template_body": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Reusable body prose; must be non-blank after domain parsing."
    },
    "description": {
      "type": ["string", "null"],
      "description": "Optional description; blank/whitespace-only is treated as absent."
    },
    "placeholder_tokens": {
      "type": ["array", "null"],
      "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
      "description": "Optional tokens; each must be non-blank and appear verbatim in template_body."
    }

}
```

**(c) TypeScript interface**

```typescript
interface CreateDraftingTemplateRequest {
  /** Required. Non-blank human-facing template name. */
  template_name: string;
  /** Required. Non-blank reusable body prose. */
  template_body: string;
  /** Optional. Blank/whitespace-only is treated as absent (stored as null). */
  description?: string | null;
  /**
   * Optional. Each entry must be non-blank and must appear verbatim
   * as a substring of `template_body`. Absent or null => treated as [].
   */
  placeholder_tokens?: string[] | null;
}
```

The handler itself takes an untyped `Json<Value>` and destructures manually, but the effective shape it reads is:
